RBBB: Delayed conduction through the right bundle branch; ECG shows wide QRS (>120 ms) with RSR' ('M-shape') in V1–V2 and deep S in V6. Isolated RBBB is often benign; new RBBB in the context of PE or anterior MI carries prognostic significance; bifascicular block (RBBB + left axis) may progress to complete heart block.
RBC: Biconcave erythrocytes carrying haemoglobin to deliver oxygen to tissues; normal lifespan ~120 days, produced by EPO-stimulated erythropoiesis in bone marrow. RBC count is reduced in anaemia from blood loss, haemolysis, or impaired production; elevated in polycythaemia vera or physiologically at high altitude. RBC indices (MCV, MCH, MCHC) classify the type of anaemia.
RCM: Non-dilated cardiomyopathy with impaired ventricular filling from myocardial stiffness; causes include amyloidosis, sarcoidosis, haemochromatosis.
RDS: Surfactant-deficiency lung disease of preterm infants (hyaline membrane disease); onset within hours of birth with grunting, nasal flaring, subcostal recession, and cyanosis - risk inversely proportional to gestational age. Antenatal corticosteroids (betamethasone <34 weeks) reduce severity; exogenous surfactant therapy and respiratory support (CPAP or mechanical ventilation) are the cornerstones of treatment.
ROP: Disordered retinal vascularisation in preterm infants from abnormal VEGF signalling and oxygen exposure; risk proportional to prematurity and oxygen therapy duration. Ophthalmology screening begins at 4–6 weeks postnatal age or 31–32 weeks corrected gestational age; treated with laser photocoagulation or intravitreal anti-VEGF (bevacizumab) for threshold disease; untreated severe ROP causes retinal detachment and blindness.
ROSC: Restoration of a palpable pulse or measurable blood pressure after cardiac arrest. Post-resuscitation care includes targeted temperature management, early coronary angiography for suspected cardiac cause, haemodynamic optimisation, and neuroprognostication at ≥72 h; ROSC alone does not predict neurological outcome.
RR: Breaths per minute; normal adult range 12–20/min; one of the earliest and most sensitive indicators of clinical deterioration. Tachypnoea (>20/min) occurs with hypoxia, metabolic acidosis, pain, fever, and anxiety; NEWS and MEWS scoring systems assign high weight to RR because of its predictive value for adverse outcomes.

Ratio of disease incidence (or event probability) in an exposed group divided by that in an unexposed group; used in cohort studies. RR >1 indicates increased risk, RR <1 a protective effect; differs from the odds ratio (OR) used in case-control studies, though for rare outcomes RR ≈ OR.
RRT: Extracorporeal or peritoneal methods substituting for lost renal function; includes haemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis, and kidney transplantation for ESRD, and continuous/intermittent renal replacement in ICU for AKI. Indications: refractory hyperkalaemia, acidosis, fluid overload unresponsive to diuretics, or uraemic encephalopathy/pericarditis.
RSI: Technique for emergency intubation using simultaneous induction agent and neuromuscular blocker to minimise aspiration risk.
RSV: Commonest cause of bronchiolitis and viral pneumonia in infants; peak season winter–spring; most children infected by age 2. Management of bronchiolitis is supportive (oxygen, fluids); newer prevention options include nirsevimab monoclonal antibody (all infants) and maternal RSV vaccination; palivizumab remains an option for high-risk preterm infants or those with congenital heart disease.
RV: Thin-walled cardiac chamber pumping deoxygenated blood through the pulmonary circulation; sensitive to afterload increases (pulmonary hypertension, massive PE). RV failure causes elevated JVP, peripheral oedema, and hepatic congestion; assessed by echocardiography and BNP/NT-proBNP.
SABA: Short-acting reliever bronchodilator used for acute bronchospasm; salbutamol (salbutamol) is the most common AU example.
SAH: Bleeding into the subarachnoid space, classically presenting as a sudden thunderclap headache ('worst headache of my life') from a ruptured intracranial aneurysm. CT head is >95% sensitive within 6 h; LP showing xanthochromia if CT negative. Complications include rebleeding, vasospasm (delayed cerebral ischaemia), and hydrocephalus; aneurysm secured by endovascular coiling or surgical clipping.
SARS: Severe viral pneumonia caused by SARS-CoV-1; 2003 epidemic had 10% mortality and preceded SARS-CoV-2/COVID-19.
SBI: Bacteraemia, UTI, meningitis, or pneumonia in febrile infants, especially those <3 months; risk stratification uses Rochester/Philadelphia/PECARN criteria to guide investigation and empirical antibiotics (ampicillin + gentamicin). Comprehensive sepsis workup (FBC, CRP, blood culture, urine MCS, ± LP) is indicated in febrile young infants regardless of clinical appearance.
SBP: Bacterial infection of ascitic fluid in cirrhosis without an identifiable intra-abdominal source; diagnosed by ascitic fluid PMN ≥250/µL; most common organisms are E. coli and Klebsiella. Treated with IV ceftriaxone + IV albumin (reduces hepatorenal syndrome risk); long-term norfloxacin prophylaxis after the first episode.

Peak arterial pressure during ventricular systole; normal <120 mmHg. Note: the target depends on context - the Heart Foundation advises <140 mmHg for most treated adults and <120 mmHg where high cardiovascular risk makes intensive lowering tolerable, against a MAP target of ≥65 mmHg in septic shock; measured by sphygmomanometer or invasive arterial line.
SC: Injection into the subcutaneous fat layer; common sites are the abdomen, thigh, and upper arm. Used for insulin, LMWH, some biologics, and palliative medications; slower and more sustained absorption than IM, making it suitable for continuous infusions via a syringe driver.
SDH: Blood collection between the dura and arachnoid mater, often from bridging vein tear; acute SDH is a neurosurgical emergency.
SGA: Birth weight or fetal size below the 10th centile for gestational age.
SGLT2: Proximal tubule transporter; SGLT2 inhibitors (empagliflozin, dapagliflozin, canagliflozin) block renal glucose reabsorption, causing glucosuria and modest glucose lowering. Cardiorenal benefits are independent of glycaemia: reduce HF hospitalisation (HFpEF and HFrEF), slow CKD progression, and lower CV mortality. Adverse effects: genital mycotic infection; euglycaemic ketoacidosis, so withhold before surgery or during acute illness; volume depletion; Fournier gangrene, rare.
SIADH: Euvolaemic hyponatraemia (low serum osmolality, inappropriately concentrated urine >100 mOsm/kg) from excessive ADH secretion; causes include SCLC, CNS disease (meningitis, SAH), pulmonary disease, and drugs (SSRIs, carbamazepine, cyclophosphamide). Managed with fluid restriction; vasopressin receptor antagonists (tolvaptan) or demeclocycline for severe/refractory cases; correct sodium slowly to avoid osmotic demyelination.
SIDS: Unexplained sudden death of an apparently healthy infant <1 year, unresolved after thorough case investigation including autopsy; incidence peaks at 2–4 months. Risk is significantly reduced by supine sleeping ('back to sleep'), firm flat sleep surface, smoke-free environment, room-sharing without bed-sharing, and breastfeeding.
SIRS: Non-specific inflammatory response defined by ≥2 of: temperature <36°C or >38°C, HR >90, RR >20 or pCO₂ <32 mmHg, WBC <4 or >12 ×10⁹/L or >10% bands. SIRS is not specific for infection; replaced by SOFA-based Sepsis-3 definition (2016) for sepsis diagnosis - qSOFA (GCS <15, RR ≥22, SBP ≤100) is the preferred bedside screen outside the ICU.
SJS: Severe immune-mediated mucocutaneous drug reaction with epidermal detachment <10% BSA; commoner triggers: allopurinol, aromatic anticonvulsants (carbamazepine, phenytoin), sulfonamides, NSAIDs. Presents with prodromal fever, mucous membrane involvement (oral, ocular, genital), and target lesions with positive Nikolsky sign; stop causative drug immediately; manage in specialist burns unit.
SLE: Multisystem autoimmune disease with ANA positivity; 2019 ACR/EULAR criteria include malar rash, discoid lesions, serositis, nephritis, cytopenias, anti-dsDNA, and anti-Sm antibodies. Hydroxychloroquine is background therapy; corticosteroids manage flares; mycophenolate or azathioprine for organ-threatening disease such as lupus nephritis.
SNRI: Antidepressants blocking serotonin and noradrenaline reuptake (venlafaxine, duloxetine, desvenlafaxine); effective for depression, GAD, social anxiety, PTSD, and pain syndromes - duloxetine is approved for diabetic neuropathy and fibromyalgia. Discontinuation syndrome (dizziness, 'brain zaps', irritability) common - taper gradually.
SOFA: ICU score measuring organ dysfunction across six systems (respiratory, renal, hepatic, cardiovascular, haematologic, neurologic); used to define sepsis.
SPECT: Nuclear imaging technique using gamma-emitting isotopes to create 3-D functional images; used in cardiac perfusion and brain studies.
SS: Serotonergic excess from drug combination (SSRI+MAOI, tramadol+SSRI etc.); Criteria: Hunter criteria - clonus, agitation, hyperthermia, diaphoresis. Mx: cease the serotonergic agent; supportive care with benzodiazepines and active cooling; cyproheptadine in severe cases.
SSEPs: Electrophysiological measure of somatosensory pathway integrity; used intraoperatively to monitor spinal cord function.
SSI: Infection occurring at a surgical incision within 30 days of the procedure; classified as superficial, deep, or organ/space.
SSRI: Antidepressants blocking the presynaptic serotonin transporter, increasing synaptic 5-HT; first-line for depression, GAD, panic disorder, OCD, and PTSD (e.g. sertraline, escitalopram, fluoxetine). Onset 2–4 weeks; common side effects include initial nausea, sexual dysfunction, and insomnia; risk of serotonin syndrome if combined with MAOIs or tramadol.
STD: Older term now largely replaced by 'STI' (sexually transmitted infection) to emphasise that many infections are asymptomatic and still transmissible; same clinical entities. Refers to infections acquired through sexual contact including chlamydia, gonorrhoea, syphilis, herpes, HPV, and HIV.
STEMI: Acute MI with ST-segment elevation or new LBBB on ECG from complete coronary occlusion; requires emergent reperfusion - primary PCI (door-to-balloon ≤90 min) or thrombolysis if PCI unavailable within 120 min. Mx: dual antiplatelet therapy with aspirin and a P2Y12 inhibitor; anticoagulation; high-intensity statin; beta-blocker; ACE inhibitor.
STI: Infection transmitted primarily through sexual contact; includes chlamydia (commonest bacterial STI), gonorrhoea, syphilis, HSV, HPV, and HIV - many are asymptomatic. Annual screening of sexually active young people and high-risk groups is recommended; contact tracing and partner notification are integral to management.
SVC: Large vein returning blood from the upper body to the right atrium; SVC syndrome occurs from extrinsic compression.
SVD: Unassisted vaginal birth occurring without instrumental or operative intervention.
SVT: Narrow-complex tachycardia originating above the bundle of His; most commonly AVNRT or AVRT via accessory pathway. Acutely terminated by vagal manoeuvres (Valsalva) or IV adenosine; long-term management with catheter ablation (highly curative) or rate-controlling agents for recurrent symptomatic episodes.
SpO2: Non-invasive estimate of arterial oxygen saturation measured by pulse oximetry.
T1DM: Autoimmune destruction of pancreatic β-cells causing absolute insulin deficiency; associated with HLA-DR3/DR4 and positive anti-GAD/islet cell antibodies; C-peptide is low or absent. Presents in childhood or young adults, often as DKA; requires lifelong insulin replacement.
T2DM: Insulin resistance with progressive β-cell dysfunction; strongly associated with obesity and adult onset; managed with lifestyle modification then stepwise pharmacotherapy (metformin → SGLT2-i, GLP-1 RA, DPP-4i, or insulin). Intensive glycaemic and cardiovascular risk-factor control reduces microvascular and macrovascular complications.
TAA: Dilatation of the thoracic aorta; associated with Marfan syndrome, bicuspid aortic valve, and hypertension.
TB: Chronic infection by Mycobacterium tuberculosis; classically pulmonary with productive cough, haemoptysis, weight loss, night sweats, and upper lobe cavitation. Transmitted by respiratory droplets; latent TB (IGRA/Mantoux positive, no disease) can reactivate with immunosuppression. Mx: 2 months rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol, then 4 months rifampicin and isoniazid, given under a state TB service; drug resistance (MDR-TB) requires second-line agents.
TBI: Brain injury from external mechanical force; severity stratified by GCS: mild (13–15, includes concussion), moderate (9–12), and severe (≤8, requiring intubation and ICP monitoring). CT head performed per NICE/Canadian CT Head criteria; complications include diffuse axonal injury, contusions, subdural and extradural haematomas, and raised ICP.
TCA: Older antidepressants (amitriptyline, nortriptyline, imipramine) now used primarily at sub-antidepressant doses for neuropathic pain, migraine prophylaxis, and insomnia; significant anticholinergic (dry mouth, urinary retention, constipation) and cardiac (QRS widening, QTc prolongation) toxicity in overdose. Narrow therapeutic window requires caution in patients at suicide risk.
TEE: US term for TOE - high-resolution cardiac ultrasound via an oesophageal probe.
TEN: Most severe end of the SJS spectrum with epidermal detachment >30% BSA; same triggers as SJS; SCORTEN score predicts mortality (up to 25–35%). Managed in a burns or intensive care unit with meticulous wound care, fluid resuscitation, nutritional support, ophthalmological care, and prevention of secondary infection; IVIG and ciclosporin used in some centres.
TFT: Panel assessing thyroid status: TSH alone as first-line screen (most sensitive); add free T4 if TSH is abnormal, plus free T3 if hyperthyroidism suspected. Raised TSH + low fT4 = primary hypothyroidism; suppressed TSH + high fT4/T3 = hyperthyroidism; subclinical disease has isolated TSH abnormality with normal free hormones.
TFTs: Panel of tests including TSH, free T4, and sometimes free T3 to assess thyroid function.
TGA: Aorta arises from RV and pulmonary artery from LV creating parallel circulations; presents with severe cyanosis at birth; prostaglandin E1 + balloon atrial septostomy → arterial switch operation.
Sudden-onset anterograde amnesia lasting hours in middle-aged adults; benign and self-limiting; thought to involve venous congestion or spreading depolarisation; low risk of stroke.
TIA: Transient focal neurological deficit from cerebral ischaemia resolving within 24 hours (usually <1 h) without infarction on imaging; 10–15% risk of stroke within 90 days, highest in the first 48 h. ABCD² score stratifies risk; requires urgent antiplatelet therapy, carotid imaging, cardiac monitoring, and vascular risk-factor management.
TIBC: Indirect measure of circulating transferrin; TIBC rises in iron deficiency (upregulated transferrin) and falls in anaemia of chronic disease and iron overload. Transferrin saturation (TSAT) = serum iron ÷ TIBC × 100; in iron deficiency: low ferritin, low iron, raised TIBC, TSAT <16%; in ACD: low iron, low-normal TIBC, normal-raised ferritin.
TIMI: Validated ACS risk score predicting 14-day death and ischaemic events; also used to assess STEMI reperfusion success.
TKI: Small-molecule drugs inhibiting specific tyrosine kinases by competing with ATP binding; imatinib (BCR-ABL, KIT, PDGFR) transformed CML from a fatal disease to a chronic condition managed orally. Subsequent generations overcome resistance mutations (dasatinib/nilotinib for CML; osimertinib for EGFR-mutant NSCLC); well tolerated but kinase domain mutations drive resistance.
TLCO: Transfer Factor for CO (same as DLCO; UK/AU terminology)
Measures alveolar gas transfer efficiency; reduced in emphysema and pulmonary fibrosis, raised in alveolar haemorrhage. DLCO in US sources.
TLS: Oncological emergency from massive tumour cell death releasing intracellular contents; triad of hyperuricaemia, hyperkalaemia, hyperphosphataemia → AKI; prevent with IV fluids and allopurinol/rasburicase.
TOE: High-resolution cardiac ultrasound via an oesophageal probe, used for endocarditis and valve assessment.
US equivalent term for TOE; same procedure - oesophageal ultrasound probe for cardiac imaging.
TORCH: Acronym for major congenital infections: Toxoplasmosis, Rubella, CMV, Herpes, and Other (syphilis, Zika, etc.).
TPN: Complete IV nutritional support via central venous catheter, providing carbohydrates, amino acids, lipids, electrolytes, vitamins, and trace elements; indicated when enteral nutrition is not feasible (short bowel, prolonged ileus, bowel obstruction). Complications: CLABSI, refeeding syndrome (hypophosphataemia on initiating nutrition after prolonged starvation), hepatic steatosis, and hyperglycaemia.
TR: Regurgitation across the tricuspid valve producing large v-waves in the JVP and a pulsatile liver; usually secondary (functional) from RV dilation due to pulmonary hypertension or left heart failure. Functional TR often improves with treatment of the underlying cause; severe primary TR from endocarditis or carcinoid syndrome may require valve repair or replacement.
TSAT: Percentage of transferrin bound with iron; elevated in haemochromatosis, low in iron deficiency anaemia.
TSH: Pituitary glycoprotein hormone that drives thyroid hormone synthesis and secretion; the most sensitive first-line screening test for thyroid dysfunction. Raised TSH indicates primary hypothyroidism; suppressed TSH indicates hyperthyroidism or exogenous thyroid hormone excess; measured with free T4 (and T3 if hyperthyroidism suspected) for complete assessment.
TTE: Standard non-invasive ultrasound of the heart performed through the chest wall.
TTP: ADAMTS13 deficiency (acquired or congenital) causing ultra-large VWF multimer accumulation → platelet microthrombi; presents with MAHA (schistocytes, elevated LDH), thrombocytopenia, and end-organ injury. Plasma exchange (therapeutic plasma exchange) is life-saving and must not be delayed; caplacizumab reduces time to platelet recovery; rituximab prevents relapse.
TURP: Endoscopic resection of prostatic tissue through the urethra under spinal or general anaesthesia; most effective surgical treatment for BPH causing significant LUTS refractory to medical therapy. Complications: TUR syndrome (dilutional hyponatraemia - now rare with bipolar TURP using saline), retrograde ejaculation (common), and urinary incontinence (<5%).
ToF: Cyanotic congenital heart disease comprising four defects: VSD, overriding aorta, RV outflow obstruction, and RV hypertrophy; boot-shaped heart on CXR. 'Tet spells' (hypercyanotic episodes) treated acutely with knee-chest position, oxygen, and morphine; definitive repair (VSD closure + RVOT relief) performed in infancy.
UA: Dipstick and microscopic examination of urine for infection, protein, blood, and other abnormalities.
UC: Chronic mucosal inflammation of the colon beginning at the rectum and extending proximally in a contiguous pattern; presents with bloody diarrhoea, urgency, and cramping. 5-ASA is first-line for mild–moderate disease; moderate–severe disease requires corticosteroids, immunomodulators, or biologics; long-standing UC carries increased colorectal cancer risk requiring surveillance colonoscopy.
UEC: Standard Australian biochemistry panel measuring renal function and electrolytes; equivalent to US Basic Metabolic Panel.
URI: Common viral infection of the nose, sinuses, and pharynx; most often caused by rhinovirus and self-limiting within 7–10 days. Managed with rest, hydration, and symptomatic relief (decongestants, antipyretics); antibiotics are not indicated for uncomplicated viral URI.
URTI: Viral infection of the upper airways - nose, sinuses, pharynx, and larynx - typically rhinovirus, coronavirus, or adenovirus; self-limiting within 7–10 days. Managed symptomatically; antibiotics only if bacterial superinfection is confirmed (e.g. group A strep pharyngitis, acute bacterial sinusitis).
USS: Diagnostic ultrasound - high-frequency sound waves imaging soft tissue and organs; no ionising radiation, so first-line in pregnancy.
UTI: Bacterial infection of the urinary tract, most commonly Escherichia coli, presenting with dysuria, frequency, urgency, and suprapubic pain. Uncomplicated lower UTI treated with a short course of nitrofurantoin or trimethoprim; pyelonephritis or complicated UTI requires longer or parenteral therapy guided by urine MCS.
V/Q: Nuclear medicine scan comparing ventilation and perfusion to detect pulmonary embolism.
VAP: Pneumonia developing >48 h after endotracheal intubation in mechanically ventilated patients; pathogenesis involves microaspiration of oropharyngeal secretions around the cuff. Prevented by the 'VAP bundle' (head-of-bed elevation 30–45°, daily sedation holds, oral chlorhexidine care, cuff pressure monitoring); associated with prolonged ICU stay and antibiotic resistance.
VBAC: Planned vaginal delivery in a woman with a prior uterine scar; carries small risk of uterine rupture.
VBG: Blood gas analysis on a venous sample; approximates arterial pH and bicarbonate, particularly useful in non-respiratory assessment.
VCUG: Fluoroscopic study of the bladder and urethra during voiding; used to diagnose vesicoureteric reflux in children.
VEP: Electrophysiological measure of visual pathway conduction; delayed in optic neuritis and demyelinating disease.
VF: Chaotic disorganised ventricular electrical activity producing no cardiac output - immediate cardiac arrest; commonest initial rhythm in witnessed out-of-hospital arrest. Each minute without defibrillation reduces survival ~10%; CPR buys time while defibrillator is prepared. After ROSC, ICD implanted for secondary prevention.
VRE: Enterococcus faecium (most commonly) harbouring VanA/VanB resistance genes conferring glycopeptide resistance; a major nosocomial pathogen causing UTI, BSI, and wound infections in immunocompromised or hospitalised patients. Treatment: linezolid or daptomycin; strict contact precautions and environmental decontamination are essential for outbreak control.
VSD: Commonest congenital heart defect; a deficiency in the interventricular septum produces a harsh holosystolic murmur and left-to-right shunt. Small defects may close spontaneously; large VSDs cause pulmonary overcirculation, heart failure, and Eisenmenger syndrome if untreated - surgical or catheter closure indicated for haemodynamic compromise.
VT: Wide-complex tachycardia arising from the ventricular myocardium; can degenerate to VF causing cardiac arrest. Haemodynamically unstable VT requires immediate synchronised DC cardioversion; stable VT treated with IV amiodarone or procainamide. Implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) for secondary prevention; catheter ablation for scar-mediated VT.
VTE: Umbrella term for DVT and pulmonary embolism; risk factors include immobility, malignancy, thrombophilia, surgery, oestrogen therapy, and pregnancy. Prophylaxis with LMWH or DOAC recommended in high-risk inpatients; therapeutic anticoagulation (DOAC preferred) for ≥3 months; extended therapy for unprovoked or high-risk VTE.
VZV: Herpesvirus causing varicella (primary) and herpes zoster (reactivation); treated with aciclovir.
WBC: Leucocytes mediating immune defence; normal count 4–11 ×10⁹/L. Differential count identifies the predominant subtype: neutrophilia (bacterial infection), lymphocytosis (viral infection), eosinophilia (allergy/parasites); neutropenia (ANC <0.5 ×10⁹/L) significantly increases infection risk and warrants reverse barrier nursing.
WPW: Ventricular pre-excitation via an accessory AV pathway; ECG shows short PR interval and delta wave at QRS onset. AF conducting rapidly down the accessory pathway (broad irregular tachycardia) risks degeneration to VF - AV nodal blockers (adenosine, beta-blockers, digoxin, verapamil) are contraindicated in this scenario. Definitive treatment is catheter ablation of the accessory pathway.
Wells: Pre-test probability score for DVT or PE; combined with D-dimer to guide imaging decisions.
XDR: Resistant to nearly all effective antibiotics; XDR-TB is resistant to isoniazid, rifampicin, fluoroquinolones, and injectables.
aPTT: Activated form of the PTT using a contact activator (kaolin or ellagic acid); measures the intrinsic and common coagulation pathways. Used to monitor unfractionated heparin (UFH) therapy; target 1.5–2.5× the control value (~60–100 s); prolonged aPTT with normal PT indicates intrinsic pathway factor deficiency or heparin effect.
albumin: Major serum protein synthesised by the liver; low levels indicate malnutrition, liver disease, or nephrotic syndrome.
aldosterone: Mineralocorticoid regulating sodium retention and potassium excretion; elevated in primary hyperaldosteronism (Conn syndrome).
ammonia: Nitrogenous waste elevated in hepatic encephalopathy and urea cycle disorders; guides lactulose and rifaximin therapy.
amylase: Enzyme elevated in pancreatitis and parotitis; less specific than lipase for pancreatic disease.
bDMARD: Biologically derived DMARD targeting specific immune mediators (e.g. TNF, IL-6); used in refractory RA and other autoimmune diseases.
bHCG: Subunit of hCG measured to confirm pregnancy, monitor ectopic pregnancy, and assess trophoblastic disease.
bilirubin: Breakdown product of haem; elevated in haemolysis (unconjugated) or cholestasis/hepatocellular disease (conjugated).
cortisol: Principal glucocorticoid; measured to diagnose Cushing syndrome (elevated) and adrenal insufficiency (low).
csDMARD: Traditional small-molecule DMARDs for rheumatoid arthritis; methotrexate is the anchor therapy.
eGFR: Calculated estimate of GFR from serum creatinine, age, and sex; used to stage chronic kidney disease.
ferritin: Iron storage protein; low in iron deficiency, elevated in haemochromatosis, inflammation, and haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis.
hCG: Hormone produced by the placenta; measured to confirm pregnancy and monitor trophoblastic disease.
lipase: Pancreatic enzyme elevated in acute pancreatitis; more specific than amylase for pancreatic injury.
mRS: Six-point functional disability scale from 0 (no symptoms) to 6 (death); primary outcome measure in stroke trials.
qSOFA: Bedside sepsis screening score using GCS <15, RR ≥22, and SBP ≤100; ≥2 points suggests sepsis risk.
renin: Enzyme released by the juxtaglomerular apparatus; initiates the RAAS cascade and is measured in the aldosterone-renin ratio.
tPA: Fibrinolytic agent that activates plasminogen to dissolve clots; used in ischaemic stroke, STEMI, and massive PE.
tsDMARD: Small-molecule DMARDs targeting specific intracellular pathways such as JAK kinases; used in RA and psoriatic arthritis.
urate: End product of purine metabolism; elevated in gout and tumour lysis syndrome.

Mx: DAPT (aspirin + P2Y12), heparin, β-blocker, ACE-i, statin. Ddx: aortic dissection, pericarditis, PE, oesophageal rupture/spasm, pneumothorax, costochondritis.

conditions.summary: Irregularly irregular rhythm without P waves. ↑stroke risk. CHA2DS2-VASc → anticoagulation (DOAC preferred unless valvular). Mx: Rate control (β-blocker / non-DHP CCB) or rhythm control (cardioversion, antiarrhythmics, ablation).

conditions.name: Atrial flutter
conditions.summary: Macroreentrant atrial tachyarrhythmia, classic sawtooth flutter waves (II, III, aVF). Often 2:1 block → regular ventricular rate ~150 bpm. Mx: Anticoagulation as for AFib; ablation highly effective (cavotricuspid isthmus).

conditions.name: Aortic stenosis
conditions.summary: Crescendo-decrescendo systolic murmur at RUSB radiating to carotids. Sx (triad): angina, syncope, HF. Ix: echo (valve area, mean gradient). Severe + symptomatic → SAVR or TAVR. Avoid afterload-↓ agents (ACE-i, nitrates) in critical AS.

conditions.name: Aortic regurgitation
conditions.summary: Decrescendo early-diastolic murmur at LSB. Wide pulse pressure, water-hammer pulse. Mx: Acute (endocarditis, dissection) → surgical emergency. Chronic → vasodilators, valve replacement when symptomatic or LV dysfunction.

conditions.name: Mitral stenosis
conditions.summary: Mid-diastolic rumble with opening snap, loud S1. Most often rheumatic. Sx: dyspnoea, AFib, haemoptysis. Mx: rate control, anticoagulation, percutaneous balloon valvuloplasty for suitable anatomy.

conditions.name: Mitral regurgitation
conditions.summary: Holosystolic murmur at apex radiating to axilla. Causes: MVP, IE, ischaemic, rheumatic. Mx: Acute MR (papillary muscle rupture) → cardiogenic shock, urgent surgery. Chronic → vasodilators, repair preferred over replacement.

conditions.name: Aortic aneurysm
conditions.summary: AAA: infrarenal (most common, 90%); ≥3 cm (dilated) or ≥1.5× normal diameter. Risk: male, age >65, smoking (strongest risk factor), HTN, family history, atherosclerosis, COPD, Marfan/Ehlers-Danlos (connective tissue). Screening (UK NHS): USS to all men aged 65 (one-time invitation). Ix: Surveillance: 3-4.4 cm → annual USS; 4.5-5.4 cm → 3-monthly. Rupture risk: ↑sharply when >5.5 cm. Mx: Ruptured AAA: sudden severe back/loin/abdominal pain + haemodynamic collapse → immediate surgical emergency (mortality 50% even with surgery, 80%+ without). Elective repair (≥5.5 cm men, ≥5.0 cm women; symptomatic/rapid growth): EVAR (endovascular - less morbidity, equivalent long-term) vs open repair (better long-term durability for anatomy unsuitable for EVAR). TAA: thoracic; associated with bicuspid aortic valve, Marfan, aortic dissection.

conditions.name: Aortic dissection
conditions.summary: Tear in aortic intima → blood enters media, creating false lumen. Predisposing: HTN (most important), atherosclerosis, bicuspid aortic valve, Marfan/Ehlers-Danlos/Turner, aortitis, coarctation, cocaine, pregnancy. Stanford: Type A (ascending aorta involved - most common, most dangerous) vs Type B (descending only, distal to left subclavian). DeBakey I-III. Sx: sudden severe tearing/ripping chest pain radiating to back (interscapular); pulse/BP differential (>20 mmHg between arms); aortic regurgitation (Type A); neurological deficit (stroke/paraplegia - coronary/vertebral artery involvement); limb ischaemia. Ix: CT angiography (rapid, gold standard); CXR (widened mediastinum); TOE (gold standard bedside/perioperative). Mx: immediate blood pressure control (IV labetalol/nitroprusside - target SBP 100-120 mmHg, HR <60); Type A: emergency surgery (replacement of ascending aorta ± root); Type B (uncomplicated): medical management (anti-impulse therapy); Type B (complicated - malperfusion, rupture): TEVAR (thoracic endovascular aortic repair).

conditions.name: Pericarditis
conditions.summary: Inflammation of pericardium. Sx: Sharp pleuritic chest pain better when leaning forward, friction rub, diffuse ST-elevation + PR-depression. Causes: viral, post-MI (Dressler), uraemic, autoimmune. Mx: NSAIDs + colchicine; steroids 2nd-line. Ddx: STEMI (diffuse vs focal ST changes), pleuritis, aortic dissection, PE, musculoskeletal chest pain.

conditions.name: Cardiac tamponade
conditions.summary: Life-threatening compression of heart by pericardial effusion → impaired filling → ↓CO. Beck's triad: hypotension + JVP elevation + muffled heart sounds. Pulsus paradoxus (exaggerated fall in SBP >10 mmHg on inspiration). Kussmaul sign absent (unlike constrictive pericarditis). Ix (ECG): sinus tachycardia, low voltage, electrical alternans (specific). Ix (CXR): enlarged globular heart. Ix (echo): diagnostic - effusion + right atrial/ventricular diastolic collapse, IVC plethora. Causes: malignancy, uraemia, pericarditis, aortic dissection type A, TB, trauma. Mx: pericardiocentesis (emergent) or surgical pericardial window; avoid diuretics, vasodilators, +ve pressure ventilation (all ↓preload → decompensation).

conditions.name: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
conditions.summary: Autosomal dominant (sarcomere mutations - MYH7, MYBPC3); asymmetric septal hypertrophy (most common - septal:posterior wall ratio >1.3:1); LVOT obstruction in 70% (Valsalva/standing → ↑obstruction; squatting/lying → ↓obstruction). Sx: exertional dyspnoea, angina, syncope (dynamic obstruction), palpitations, sudden cardiac death (young athletes - most common cause in <35 yr). Sx: jerky pulse, double apical impulse, systolic murmur (LVOT) - louder with Valsalva, SAM of mitral valve → mitral regurgitation. Ix (echo): LV wall ≥15 mm (or ≥13 mm with family history); SAM; LVOT gradient. Mx: beta-blockers/verapamil; disopyramide; ICD (high-risk: family SCD, VT, extreme LVH, LVOT gradient, unexplained syncope); septal reduction (myectomy or alcohol ablation) for drug-refractory obstruction; mavacamten (myosin inhibitor).

conditions.name: Endocarditis
conditions.summary: Infection of valvular endocardium (S. aureus, Strep viridans, enterococci). Modified Duke criteria. Sx: fever, new murmur, Janeway, Osler, Roth, splinter haemorrhages. Mx: Echo (TOE > TTE). 4-6 wk IV antibiotics; surgery for HF/abscess/large vegetations.

Ix (severity): CURB-65 / PSI. Vaccinate: pneumococcal, influenza. conditions.name: COPD

conditions.name: Bronchitis
conditions.summary: Self-limited tracheobronchial inflammation, usually viral. Ix: Productive cough lasting <3 wk; CXR clear. Mx: Antibiotics rarely indicated (consider in pertussis exposure or severe COPD overlap). Symptomatic Mx.

conditions.name: Bronchiolitis
conditions.summary: Viral lower respiratory tract infection causing inflammation/oedema of bronchioles → air-trapping/hyperinflation; predominantly <2 yr (peak 2-6 months). Aetiology: RSV (70-80%), rhinovirus, human metapneumovirus, adenovirus. Sx: 2-3 d prodrome (coryzal, low-grade fever) → tachypnoea, respiratory distress (subcostal/intercostal recession, nasal flaring, grunting), wheeze, fine inspiratory crackles (bilateral). Severe: apnoeas (especially premature/young infants), cyanosis, poor feeding (<50% usual intake), SpO₂ <92%. Risk: prematurity, CLD, CHD, immunosuppression. Ix: clinical. Mx: supportive (majority self-limiting); high-flow oxygen (SpO₂ <92% or signs of distress); high-flow humidified oxygen/HHFNC (↓work of breathing); NG/OG feeds/IV fluids (poor oral intake); NOT: bronchodilators (salbutamol), nebulised adrenaline, steroids, antibiotics, nebulised hypertonic saline (evidence equivocal); CPAP/intubation (severe); nirsevimab (RSV monoclonal antibody - now first-line seasonal immunisation for infants in many countries); palivizumab (high-risk only - monthly IM).

conditions.name: Tuberculosis
conditions.summary: M. tuberculosis infection. Sx: Latent (positive IGRA/TST, no Sx) vs active (cough >3 wk, fever, night sweats, weight loss). Ix: CXR/CT, AFB smear, NAAT, culture. Mx (active): RIPE 2 mo → RI 4 mo. Latent: isoniazid 9 mo or rifampicin/RIF-INH regimens.

conditions.name: Pulmonary hypertension
conditions.summary: Mean PAP ≥20 mmHg. WHO groups: 1 PAH; 2 LHF; 3 lung disease/hypoxia; 4 chronic thromboembolic; 5 multifactorial. Sx: dyspnoea, syncope, RHF. Echo screen, RHC confirms. Group 1 Mx: PDE5i, ERAs, prostacyclins.

conditions.name: ARDS
conditions.summary: Non-cardiogenic pulmonary oedema with bilateral infiltrates and hypoxaemia (Berlin: PaO2/FiO2 ≤300). Triggers: sepsis, pneumonia, aspiration, trauma. Lung-protective ventilation (Vt 6 mL/kg, plateau ≤30, PEEP), prone positioning. Ddx: cardiogenic pulmonary oedema (↑PCWP, ↑BNP - must exclude), bilateral pneumonia, diffuse alveolar haemorrhage.

conditions.name: Pneumothorax
conditions.summary: Air in pleural space. Spontaneous (tall thin males), traumatic, tension. Sx: sudden pleuritic pain, dyspnoea, hyperresonance, ↓breath sounds. Tension PTX → tracheal deviation, shock; needle decompression then chest tube. Small simple PTX: O2 ± observation. Ddx: pleuritis, PE, rib fracture, pneumonia, musculoskeletal chest pain (all can present with pleuritic pain).

conditions.name: Pleural effusion
conditions.summary: Accumulation of fluid in pleural space. Transudate (pleural protein <25 g/L; LDH <200 IU/L; Light criteria - protein effusion/serum <0.5, LDH effusion/serum <0.6, LDH effusion <2/3 upper limit normal): cardiac failure (most common), hepatic cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome, hypothyroidism, Meigs syndrome. Exudate (Light's criteria met): pneumonia (parapneumonic - most common exudate), malignancy (lung, breast, lymphoma, mesothelioma), TB, PE, autoimmune (RA, SLE, drug-induced), oesophageal rupture (high amylase + very low pH). Sx: pleuritic chest pain (inflammatory), dyspnoea (large). Sx: dullness to percussion, ↓breath sounds, ↓vocal resonance/fremitus at base; tracheal deviation (massive). Ix (CXR): costophrenic angle blunting (>200 mL), meniscus, massive (white-out). Ix: diagnostic aspiration (Light's criteria, protein, LDH, glucose, pH, cytology, culture, ADA - TB, amylase); USS-guided. Mx: treat cause; therapeutic aspiration (dyspnoea - ≤1.5 L/session); intercostal drain (exudate/parapneumonic); pleurodesis (recurrent malignant - talc slurry/bleomycin); indwelling pleural catheter (IPC - recurrent malignant, outpatient).

conditions.name: Sarcoidosis
conditions.summary: Multisystem non-caseating granulomas. Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy ± lung infiltrates. ↑ACE, hypercalcaemia. Sx: Lofgren (acute, good prognosis): erythema nodosum + bihilar adenopathy + arthralgia. Mx: observation, steroids if organ-threatening.

conditions.name: Cystic fibrosis
conditions.summary: AR; CFTR mutation (F508del most common); defective Cl⁻/water secretion → viscid secretions in respiratory, GI, reproductive tracts. Pulmonary: chronic infection (Staphylococcus aureus early, Pseudomonas aeruginosa later - biofilm), bronchiectasis, haemoptysis, pneumothorax, respiratory failure. GI: meconium ileus (neonates), exocrine pancreatic insufficiency (steatorrhoea, fat-soluble vitamin deficiency), CF-related diabetes, biliary cirrhosis, distal intestinal obstruction syndrome (DIOS). Reproductive: male infertility (bilateral absence vas deferens), female subfertility. Ix: sweat chloride >60 mmol/L; CFTR genotyping; NBS. FEV1 best predictor of survival. Mx: CFTR modulator therapy (ivacaftor, lumacaftor, elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor - Trikafta - for F508del, major advance); mucolytics (dornase alfa, hypertonic saline); physiotherapy; prophylactic antibiotics; pancreatic enzymes; transplant.

conditions.name: Lung cancer
conditions.summary: Most common cause of cancer death. NSCLC (85%): adenocarcinoma (most common - peripheral; women, non-smokers; EGFR/ALK/ROS1/KRAS mutations), squamous cell (central; smokers; PTHrP → hypercalcaemia; cavitates), large cell. SCLC (15%): central; most aggressive; almost all smokers; neuroendocrine features; paraneoplastic (SIADH, Cushing, Lambert-Eaton, LEMS, encephalitis); limited vs extensive stage. Risk: smoking (20× increased RR); radon gas; asbestos; occupational; COPD/pulmonary fibrosis; genetic. Sx: cough, haemoptysis, weight loss, dyspnoea, chest pain, hoarseness (RLN), dysphagia (mediastinal compression); Pancoast syndrome (superior sulcus tumour - Horner + arm pain + wasting); SVC obstruction; paraneoplastic. Ix: CT chest/abdomen/pelvis; PET-CT (staging); bronchoscopy ± biopsy; mediastinoscopy/EBUS (LN staging); MRI brain; liquid biopsy (ctDNA). Molecular testing (NSCLC): EGFR, ALK, ROS1, KRAS G12C, BRAF, MET, RET, NTRK, PD-L1. Mx: NSCLC stage I-II: surgery (lobectomy) ± adjuvant chemo/immuno; stage III: concurrent chemoRT + durvalumab; stage IV: targeted (osimertinib/EGFR, alectinib/ALK, sotorasib/KRAS G12C) or pembrolizumab (high PD-L1 ≥50%) or chemo + immuno; SCLC limited: concurrent cisplatin-etoposide + RT; extensive: carboplatin-etoposide + atezolizumab/durvalumab; prophylactic cranial irradiation.

conditions.name: Influenza
conditions.summary: Acute viral respiratory infection (A/B). Sx: Sudden fever, myalgia, cough, headache. Confirm with PCR/antigen. Oseltamivir within 48 h (ongoing benefit if hospitalised/high-risk). Mx: Annual vaccination cornerstone of prevention.

conditions.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis
conditions.summary: Insulin deficiency → hyperglycaemia, ketosis, AGMA. T1DM > T2DM. Sx: polyuria, vomiting, Kussmaul breathing, fruity breath. Mx: aggressive IV fluids, insulin infusion, K+ replacement (give once K<5.3), monitor for cerebral oedema in children. Ddx: HHS (↑↑glucose but no acidosis/ketones; elderly T2DM), alcoholic ketoacidosis (ketonaemia, low/normal glucose, less hyperglycaemia), starvation ketosis, lactic acidosis, salicylate toxicity.

conditions.name: Hyperthyroidism
conditions.summary: ↑Thyroid hormone. Causes: Graves (most common), toxic adenoma/MNG, thyroiditis. Sx: weight loss, palpitations, heat intolerance, tremor, AFib. ↓TSH ↑T4/T3. Mx: β-blocker, methimazole/PTU, radioiodine, surgery. Ddx: anxiety disorder, phaeochromocytoma (episodic hypertension/sweating), stimulant use, carcinoid syndrome, perimenopause (hot flushes ± palpitations).

conditions.name: Hypothyroidism
conditions.summary: ↓Thyroid hormone. Hashimoto most common (anti-TPO). Sx: fatigue, cold intolerance, weight gain, constipation, dry skin, bradycardia. ↑TSH ↓T4. Mx: levothyroxine; recheck TSH after 6 wk. Myxoedema coma → IV T4 + hydrocortisone.

conditions.name: Cushing syndrome
conditions.summary: Glucocorticoid excess. Exogenous (most common overall - iatrogenic/steroid use). Endogenous: ACTH-dependent (Cushing disease - pituitary adenoma, 70%; ectopic ACTH - SCLC, carcinoid); ACTH-independent (adrenal adenoma/carcinoma, micronodular dysplasia). Sx: central obesity, moon face, buffalo hump, purple striae, proximal myopathy, easy bruising, skin thinning, hirsutism, oligomenorrhoea, HTN, DM, osteoporosis, psychiatric (depression, psychosis). Ix: screen - 24-hr urinary free cortisol (×2), late-night salivary cortisol, overnight 1 mg dexamethasone suppression test (DST). Localise: plasma ACTH (if low → adrenal; if high → pituitary/ectopic); high-dose DST (8 mg - suppresses pituitary but not ectopic/adrenal); MRI pituitary; IPSS (inferior petrosal sinus sampling - differentiates pituitary from ectopic). Mx: resect primary cause; steroidogenesis inhibitors (metyrapone, ketoconazole) while awaiting surgery; adrenalectomy (adrenal cause or bilateral for ectopic); pituitary surgery (transsphenoidal).

conditions.name: Addison disease
conditions.summary: Primary adrenal insufficiency (autoimmune most common). ↓Cortisol AND ↓aldosterone. Sx: fatigue, weight loss, hyperpigmentation, hypotension, hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia. ACTH stim test. Mx: hydrocortisone + fludrocortisone. Stress dosing for illness/surgery. Ddx: septic shock (no hyperpigmentation; cortisol often elevated), CKD (hyponatraemia + hyperkalaemia), malignancy with cachexia, SIADH (hyponatraemia without hyperkalaemia), secondary adrenal insufficiency (pituitary cause; no hyperpigmentation, no aldosterone deficiency).

conditions.name: Pheochromocytoma
conditions.summary: Catecholamine-secreting adrenal medullary tumour. Sx: Classic triad: episodic headache, palpitations, sweating. ↑plasma/urinary metanephrines. Ix: CT/MRI ± MIBG. Mx: Surgery after α-blockade (phenoxybenzamine/doxazosin) ≥7 d, then β-blocker.

conditions.name: Hyperparathyroidism
conditions.summary: Primary HPT: autonomous PTH hypersecretion; solitary adenoma (85%), hyperplasia (10% - MEN1/MEN2A), carcinoma (<1%). Sx: Most common: asymptomatic hypercalcaemia on routine bloods (fracture/osteoporosis, nephrolithiasis more common presentations than classic 'bones, stones, moans'). Hypercalcaemia + inappropriately normal/↑PTH = primary HPT. ↑24-hr urinary calcium (distinguish from FHH which has hypocalciuria). Ix: Parathyroid scintigraphy (Sestamibi) or USS localisation. Mx: parathyroidectomy (symptomatic; Ca >0.25 mmol/L above ULN; age <50; osteoporosis; nephrolithiasis; ↓GFR <60%). Cinacalcet (calcimimetic - ↓PTH, ↓Ca²⁺; for inoperable/contraindicated). Secondary HPT: physiological response to chronic hypocalcaemia/vitamin D deficiency/CKD (↑PTH appropriately trying to correct). Mx: Tertiary HPT: autonomous PTH secretion developing in long-standing secondary HPT (renal failure/transplant) - parathyroidectomy needed.

conditions.name: Acromegaly
conditions.summary: GH hypersecretion (>95% from pituitary somatotroph adenoma). GH → ↑IGF-1 → tissue growth. Sx: insidious; enlargement of hands/feet (ring/shoe size change), coarsening of facial features (frontal bossing, macroglossia, prognathism), interdental spacing, skin thickening. Complications: T2DM, HTN, cardiomyopathy (main cause of death), sleep apnoea, colon polyps (↑CRC risk), carpal tunnel, arthropathy. Ix: ↑IGF-1 (best screening test); oral GTT fails to suppress GH <1 μg/L (normally GH suppressed). MRI pituitary: adenoma. Visual field testing (bitemporal hemianopia). Mx: surgery (transsphenoidal - first-line); somatostatin analogues (octreotide LAR, lanreotide - most effective medical Mx, also shrink tumour); pegvisomant (GH receptor antagonist - most potent IGF-1 normalisation); cabergoline; radiotherapy (adjunct).

conditions.name: Hypoglycaemia
conditions.summary: BG <3.9 mmol/L (<70 mg/dL). Whipple triad. Causes: insulin/sulfonylurea excess, alcohol, sepsis, adrenal/pituitary insufficiency, insulinoma. Conscious: PO carbs; impaired LOC: IV dextrose or IM glucagon.

conditions.name: Acute kidney injury
conditions.summary: Sudden ↓renal function. Ix: KDIGO: ↑Cr ≥0.3 in 48 h or ↑1.5× in 7 d. Pre-renal (volume depletion), intrinsic (ATN, GN, AIN), post-renal (obstruction). FENa <1% pre-renal, >2% ATN. Treat cause; dialysis indications: AEIOU. Sx: Ddx of intrinsic AKI: ATN (most common; ischaemic or nephrotoxic), acute interstitial nephritis (drug rash + eosinophiluria), glomerulonephritis (haematuria + proteinuria + casts), rhabdomyolysis (↑↑CK, pigmented casts), hepatorenal syndrome (severe cirrhosis + ascites).

kidney replacement therapy dialysis acute kidney injury indications

conditions.name: Chronic kidney disease
conditions.summary: Sustained eGFR <60 or albuminuria ≥3 mo. Most common: diabetes, hypertension. Mx: Slow progression: BP control (ACE-i/ARB), glycaemic control, SGLT2i, low-dose aspirin if ↑CV risk, smoking cessation. Plan vascular access at eGFR ~20.
utd: definition staging chronic kidney disease adults
overview management chronic kidney disease adults
chronic kidney disease mineral bone disorder management

conditions.name: Glomerulonephritis
conditions.summary: Glomerular inflammation. Ix: Nephritic: HTN, oligaemia, RBC casts, mild proteinuria. Causes: post-strep, IgA, ANCA, anti-GBM, lupus. Ix: complement, ANCA, anti-GBM, ANA, biopsy. Treat underlying cause.

conditions.name: Nephrotic syndrome
conditions.summary: Sx (triad): heavy proteinuria (>3.5 g/24 hr or urine PCR >300 mg/mmol), hypoalbuminaemia (<30 g/L), oedema. Fourth: hyperlipidaemia + lipiduria. Causes by age: children - minimal change disease (80%); adults - membranous nephropathy (most common in adults - primary: anti-PLA2R Ab; secondary: malignancy, hepatitis B, drugs like NSAIDs/gold), FSGS (second most common adults, especially African Americans/HIV/heroin), diabetic nephropathy, AL amyloidosis, membranoproliferative GN. Complications: thrombosis (renal vein thrombosis - membranous, nephrotic hypercoagulability), infection (↓IgG, loss of complement), ↑CVD risk. Ix: urine PCR/24-hr protein, serum albumin, renal biopsy (adult/atypical presentation), complement, ANA, anti-PLA2R, hepatitis/HIV screen, SPEP. Mx: underlying cause; oedema: loop diuretics; ACEi/ARB (↓proteinuria, renoprotective); anticoagulation (especially membranous + albumin <20); SGLT2i (↓proteinuria); specific: prednisolone (minimal change); rituximab/tacrolimus/cyclophosphamide (membranous/FSGS).
utd: general principles management nephrotic syndrome adults

conditions.name: Urinary tract infection
conditions.summary: E. coli most common. Sx: Cystitis: dysuria, frequency, urgency, suprapubic pain. Pyelonephritis: fever, flank pain, CVA tenderness. Uncomplicated cystitis: nitrofurantoin or trimethoprim-sulfa. Pyelonephritis: cipro or ceftriaxone. Ddx: urethritis/STI (chlamydia, gonorrhoea - urethral discharge, sexual history), vulvovaginitis, interstitial cystitis (chronic; sterile urine), prostatitis (perineal pain, boggy tender prostate), pelvic inflammatory disease.

acute complicated urinary tract infection pyelonephritis adults
recurrent simple cystitis in women prevention treatment

conditions.name: Pyelonephritis
conditions.summary: Upper UTI involving renal parenchyma. Sx: Fever, flank pain, CVA tenderness, pyuria + bacteriuria. Outpatient: cipro/levofloxacin if low resistance; otherwise ceftriaxone IV. Ix: CT if no improvement at 48-72 h (abscess, obstruction).
utd: acute complicated urinary tract infection pyelonephritis adults

conditions.name: Nephrolithiasis
conditions.summary: Renal/ureteric calculi. Calcium oxalate most common. Sx: severe colicky flank pain radiating to groin, haematuria. Non-contrast CT KUB is gold standard. Mx: NSAIDs, fluids, α-blocker (tamsulosin) for stones <10 mm in distal ureter; ESWL/URS/PCNL for large/refractory. Ddx: ruptured AAA (older patient, pulsatile mass - do not miss), pyelonephritis (fever, CVA tenderness, pyuria), ovarian torsion/cyst, appendicitis, MSK flank pain.
utd: prevention recurrent calcium kidney stones adults

conditions.name: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
conditions.summary: Nodular hyperplasia of periurethral (transitional zone) prostate → bladder outlet obstruction; >50% men >60 yr. Sx: obstructive (hesitancy, poor stream, terminal dribbling, incomplete emptying, overflow incontinence) and irritative (urgency, frequency, nocturia, urge incontinence) LUTS; risk of acute urinary retention (AUR). PSA: may be mildly elevated in BPH (≤10 ng/mL in absence of prostatitis/cancer). International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) - severity. Ix (US): residual volume, upper tract (hydronephrosis). Ix: clinical + flow rate (uroflowmetry); exclude prostate cancer (PSA + DRE). Mx: mild (IPSS <8): watchful waiting + lifestyle; moderate-severe: alpha-blockers (tamsulosin, alfuzosin - rapid onset; SE: retrograde ejaculation, orthostatic hypotension) ± 5-alpha reductase inhibitors (finasteride, dutasteride - shrinks prostate, reduces AUR, but delays response 3-6 months); combination (MTOPS trial); surgical: TURP (transurethral resection - gold standard surgical, suitable medium glands), holmium laser enucleation (HoLEP - large glands, ↓bleeding/complications).
utd: evaluation lower urinary tract symptoms men

conditions.name: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease
conditions.summary: Retrograde flow of gastric contents into oesophagus → mucosal injury/symptoms. Mechanisms: transient LOS relaxations (most common), ↓LOS tone (hiatal hernia), ↑intragastric pressure (obesity, pregnancy). Sx: heartburn (retrosternal burning), regurgitation, water brash; atypical: chronic cough, hoarseness, laryngitis, globus sensation, non-cardiac chest pain; nocturnal: aspiration, coughing. Complications: oesophagitis (LA classification A-D), stricture (peptic), Barrett oesophagus (columnar metaplasia - risk of adenocarcinoma; surveillance endoscopy). Ix: clinical; OGD (gold standard - if red flag symptoms: dysphagia, weight loss, progressive symptoms, ≥55 yr + new onset); 24-hr pH impedance monitoring (definitive test if atypical). Mx: lifestyle (weight loss, head of bed elevation, dietary modification, avoid triggers); alginate/antacids (symptomatic); PPI (omeprazole, lansoprazole - gold standard medical Mx; 4-8 wk; on-demand for mild); H2 blockers; Nissen fundoplication (surgical - for PPI failures/large hiatal hernia).

conditions.name: Peptic ulcer disease
conditions.summary: Mucosal defect extending through muscularis mucosae; stomach (gastric ulcer, GU) or duodenum (duodenal ulcer, DU). Causes: H. pylori (80% DU, 65% GU - eradication heals and prevents recurrence), NSAIDs/aspirin (impair mucosal prostaglandins → ↓mucus/bicarbonate), gastric acid hypersecretion (ZES), idiopathic. Sx: epigastric pain (burning/gnawing); DU: pain relieved by food, worse 2-3 hr after eating, wakes from sleep; GU: pain precipitated by food (worse postprandially), weight loss. Complications: bleeding (haematemesis/melaena - most common; Forrest classification for endoscopic stigmata), perforation (peritonitis, pneumoperitoneum), obstruction (pyloric stenosis), penetration (into pancreas - back pain). Ix: OGD (gold standard - biopsy GU for malignancy + H. pylori); H. pylori testing (urea breath test, stool antigen test - most accurate non-invasive). Mx: PPI; H. pylori eradication (PAC - PPI + amoxicillin + clarithromycin × 7-14 d; or quadruple if clarithromycin-resistant); stop NSAIDs; endoscopic haemostasis (adrenaline injection + thermal/clip) for bleeding ulcer; surgery (laparoscopic) for perforation.
utd: peptic ulcer disease clinical manifestations diagnosis
approach acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding adults

conditions.name: Crohn disease
conditions.summary: Transmural inflammation, skip lesions, anywhere mouth-anus (terminal ileum classic). Sx: chronic abdominal pain, non-bloody diarrhoea, weight loss, perianal disease. Mx: 5-ASA, steroids for flares, immunomodulators (azathioprine/MTX), biologics (anti-TNF).

management mild moderate crohn disease adults
management severe fulminant crohn disease adults

conditions.name: Ulcerative colitis
conditions.summary: Mucosal inflammation, continuous from rectum proximally. Sx: bloody diarrhoea, urgency, tenesmus. Toxic megacolon, ↑colorectal cancer risk. Mx: 5-ASA, steroids for flares, biologics for refractory. Colectomy curative.
utd: clinical manifestations diagnosis ulcerative colitis adults

conditions.name: Diverticulitis
conditions.summary: Inflammation of colonic diverticula (sigmoid most common). Sx: LLQ pain, fever, leucocytosis. CT confirms ± abscess. Mx: Uncomplicated: oral abx (metronidazole + cipro/Augmentin); complicated: IV abx, drainage, surgery. Ix: Avoid colonoscopy in acute phase.

conditions.name: Appendicitis
conditions.summary: Obstruction of appendiceal lumen → inflammation. Sx: Periumbilical → RLQ pain, anorexia, vomiting. McBurney point tenderness, Rovsing, psoas, obturator signs. Ix: CT (US in pregnancy/children). Mx: Appendicectomy; abx alternative in selected uncomplicated cases. Ddx: mesenteric adenitis, Meckel diverticulitis, ovarian torsion, ectopic pregnancy, PID, renal colic, Crohn ileitis, right-sided diverticulitis.
utd: acute appendicitis adults clinical manifestations diagnosis

conditions.name: Cholecystitis
conditions.summary: Inflammation of gallbladder. Acute calculous (>90%): gallstone impacted in cystic duct → obstruction → distension + secondary infection (E. coli, Klebsiella, Enterococcus). Sx: RUQ pain (worse postprandially, worse with movement), fever, nausea; positive Murphy's sign (inspiratory arrest on deep palpation of RUQ). Acalculous cholecystitis (<10%): critically ill patients (ICU, burns, TPN, post-surgery). Jaundice suggests stone in CBD (Mirizzi syndrome) or Charcot's triad/cholangitis. Ix (US): gallstones, gallbladder wall thickening (>3 mm), pericholecystic fluid, tenderness on scan (sono-Murphy). ↑WBC, ↑CRP, ↑ALP. Complications: empyema, gangrenous cholecystitis, emphysematous cholecystitis (gas on AXR/CT - urgent), perforation, cholecystoenteric fistula/gallstone ileus. Mx: IV fluids, analgesia, antibiotics (co-amoxiclav or cephalosporin + metronidazole); laparoscopic cholecystectomy (early, within 1 wk - superior to delayed); percutaneous cholecystostomy for high-surgical-risk patients.
utd: acute cholecystitis pathogenesis clinical features diagnosis

conditions.name: Pancreatitis
conditions.summary: Acute: gallstones, alcohol most common; epigastric pain → back, nausea/vomiting, ↑lipase. Ix (severity): BISAP/Atlanta. Mx: aggressive IV fluids, analgesia, early enteral nutrition, treat cause. Avoid prophylactic abx unless infected necrosis. Ddx: perforated PUD (rigid abdomen, free air), cholecystitis, mesenteric ischaemia, inferior MI (↑troponin, ECG), bowel obstruction.

conditions.name: Cirrhosis
conditions.summary: End-stage chronic liver disease with fibrosis and nodular regeneration. Causes: alcohol, NAFLD, hep B/C. Sx: Decompensation: ascites, variceal bleed, hepatic encephalopathy, jaundice, HRS. Child-Pugh, MELD score for prognosis. Ix: Surveillance: HCC US q6mo.

conditions.name: Hepatitis B
conditions.summary: DNA virus, transmitted by blood/sex/perinatal. Acute: most clear; ~5% adults chronic. Chronic → cirrhosis, HCC. Ix: Serology: HBsAg, anti-HBs, HBcAg, anti-HBc IgM/IgG, HBeAg. Mx (chronic): tenofovir or entecavir. Mx: Vaccination is preventive.
utd: treatment chronic hepatitis b virus infection adults

conditions.name: Hepatitis C
conditions.summary: RNA virus, blood-borne. ~75% develop chronic infection → cirrhosis, HCC. Ix: Screen all adults at least once. Anti-HCV → confirm with HCV RNA. Mx: direct-acting antivirals (sofosbuvir, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir) - >95% cure.
utd: screening diagnosis hepatitis c virus infection adults
treatment chronic hepatitis c virus direct-acting antivirals

conditions.name: Bowel obstruction
conditions.summary: Failure of intestinal contents to pass. Small bowel obstruction (SBO): adhesions (most common in adults - post-surgical), hernias (especially femoral/inguinal in elderly), Crohn disease, malignancy, gallstone ileus, intussusception, volvulus. Sx: colicky central/periumbilical pain, vomiting (early/bilious in proximal), distension, absolute constipation/obstipation (no flatus or faeces - complete obstruction); high-pitched 'tinkling' bowel sounds. Large bowel obstruction (LBO): carcinoma (most common - sigmoid/left colon), sigmoid volvulus (elderly, constipated, psychiatric - 'coffee bean' on AXR), diverticular stricture, faecal impaction. AXR/CT: dilated loops of bowel (SBO >2.5 cm; LBO >6 cm; caecum >9-12 cm - 'rule of 9s'), absent gas beyond obstruction, 'string of pearls' sign. Closed-loop obstruction: strangulation risk - emergency. Mx: drip and suck (IV fluids, NG tube, catheter); adhesive SBO: trial of conservative (water-soluble contrast follow-through - Gastrografin - diagnostic and therapeutic); early surgery for strangulation/peritonitis; LBO: resection ± stoma; sigmoid volvulus: rigid sigmoidoscopy flatus tube.
utd: small bowel obstruction adults clinical features evaluation

conditions.name: HIV
conditions.summary: Retrovirus → CD4 depletion. Acute (flu-like), chronic asymptomatic, AIDS (CD4<200 or AIDS-defining illness). Screen all 13-64. Confirm with HIV-1/2 Ab + p24 + viral load. Mx: ART (e.g. bictegravir/TAF/FTC); maintain VL undetectable. PrEP for high-risk.

conditions.name: Sepsis
conditions.summary: Life-threatening organ dysfunction from dysregulated host response to infection (qSOFA / SOFA). Septic shock: vasopressors needed for MAP≥65 + lactate >2 despite resus. Mx (Hour-1 bundle): cultures, broad-spectrum abx, lactate, IV fluids 30 mL/kg, vasopressors. Ddx: non-infectious SIRS (pancreatitis, major trauma, burns), adrenal/Addisonian crisis (↑K, ↓Na, hypopigmentation history), anaphylaxis (urticaria, trigger exposure), cardiogenic shock (↑JVP, pulmonary oedema), DKA.

use of vasopressors and inotropes in adults with sepsis
investigation source of infection sepsis adults
sepsis in children definition diagnosis treatment

conditions.name: Meningitis
conditions.summary: Inflammation of meninges. Bacterial (S. pneumoniae, N. meningitidis), viral (enterovirus), fungal, TB. Sx (triad): fever, neck stiffness, AMS. CT before LP if focal deficits, papilloedema, immunocompromised. Mx (empiric): ceftriaxone + vancomycin + dexamethasone (+ amp if >50 y or immunocompromised). Ddx: SAH (thunderclap onset, xanthochromia), viral encephalitis (prominent AMS), brain abscess (focal deficits), migraine (no fever/meningism), septic shock.

treatment of bacterial meningitis caused by specific pathogens adults
bacterial meningitis in children older than one month treatment
aseptic meningitis adults clinical features diagnosis

conditions.name: Lyme disease
conditions.summary: Borrelia burgdorferi via Ixodes tick. Sx: Stage 1: erythema migrans (target rash). Stage 2: carditis (AV block), facial nerve palsy, meningitis. Stage 3: arthritis, neuroborreliosis. Mx (early): doxycycline; severe: ceftriaxone.

conditions.name: Malaria
conditions.summary: Protozoan infection; Plasmodium spp. transmitted by Anopheles mosquito. P. falciparum (most severe; Africa) - irregular fever, no dormant liver stage, cerebral malaria (coma, seizures), severe anaemia, ARDS, AKI, hypoglycaemia, blackwater fever (haemoglobinuria). P. vivax/P. ovale - 48-hr cycles (tertian fever), Schüffner dots, dormant hypnozoites (relapse). P. malariae - 72-hr quartan fever. Ix: blood smear (thick/thin × 3); RDT (rapid antigen). Mx: uncomplicated P. falciparum: artemisinin combination therapy (ACT - artemether-lumefantrine); severe: IV artesunate (superior to quinine); P. vivax/ovale: ACT or chloroquine (if sensitive) + primaquine (8-wk) for radical cure (hypnozoites); check G6PD first.

conditions.name: Mononucleosis
conditions.summary: EBV (or CMV). Sx (triad): fever, pharyngitis, lymphadenopathy. ± splenomegaly, hepatitis, atypical lymphocytes, +monospot. Mx: Avoid amoxicillin/ampicillin (rash). Avoid contact sports 4 wk (splenic rupture risk).

conditions.name: Stroke
conditions.summary: Acute neurologic deficit from infarction (~85%) or haemorrhage (~15%). Ix: Time is brain - non-contrast CT first. Mx: Ischaemic + within 4.5 h: tPA; within 24 h with LVO + favourable imaging: thrombectomy. BP <185/110 for tPA. Mx: Long-term 2° prevention: antiplatelet, statin, BP control. Ddx: Todd's paralysis (post-ictal), hypoglycaemia (always check BGL), migraine with aura, subdural haematoma, hypertensive encephalopathy, brain tumour, septic encephalopathy.
utd: initial assessment and management of acute stroke
intravenous thrombolytic therapy acute ischemic stroke
long-term antithrombotic therapy after ischemic stroke
spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage acute treatment prognosis

conditions.name: Migraine
conditions.summary: Recurrent moderate-severe unilateral throbbing headache 4-72 h, photo-/phonophobia, nausea ± aura. Triggers: hormones, stress, sleep, foods. Acute: triptans, NSAIDs, antiemetics. Prevention if frequent: β-blockers, topiramate, amitriptyline, CGRP antagonists. Ddx: tension headache (bilateral, band-like, no nausea), cluster headache (severe periorbital, autonomic features), SAH (sudden-onset worst-ever), meningitis (fever + meningism), idiopathic intracranial hypertension (obese women, papilloedema).
utd: acute treatment of migraine in adults
preventive treatment of episodic migraine in adults

conditions.name: Tension headache
conditions.summary: Most common headache type (prevalence 30-80%); episodic or chronic (≥15 d/month). Sx: Bilateral pressing/tightening (non-pulsating) pain; mild-moderate severity; not aggravated by physical activity; no/one associated symptom (nausea, photo, phono - not both photophobia AND phonophobia unlike migraine). Location: bilateral fronto-occipital ('band-like', 'hat band'), neck muscle tenderness. Typically 30 min to 7 hr. Ix: Diagnosis of exclusion (exclude secondary - SAH, meningitis, space-occupying lesion, GCA in >50 yr). ICHD-3 criteria. Sx: Chronic TTH (≥15 d/month >3 months) overlaps with MOH (medication overuse headache - up to 50%). Mx: acute: paracetamol, NSAIDs, aspirin (simple analgesia; avoid frequent use → MOH; limit to ≤10-15 d/month); triptans NOT effective for TTH. Ix: Preventive (chronic TTH): amitriptyline (most evidence - 25-75 mg nocte); stress management; physiotherapy; botulinum toxin (evidence limited for TTH, unlike migraine).

conditions.name: Cluster headache
conditions.summary: Most painful primary headache; attacks in 'clusters' (one attack daily × weeks/months, then remission). Male:female 3:1; peak 20-40 yr. Sx: Strict unilateral peri-orbital/temporal pain (15-180 min, 1-8 attacks/d); ipsilateral autonomic features: conjunctival injection, lacrimation, nasal congestion/rhinorrhoea, miosis/ptosis (Horner-like), eyelid oedema, facial flushing; restlessness/agitation during attack (unlike migraine - patient still). Nocturnal attacks common (wakes from sleep, hypothalamic involvement - circadian link). Episodic CH: clusters 6-12 wk separated by ≥1 month remission. Chronic CH: <1 month remission per year. Acute Mx: 100% O₂ (12-15 L/min × 15 min via non-rebreather - 78% effective); subcutaneous sumatriptan 6 mg (fastest acting triptan); nasal sumatriptan 20 mg/zolmitriptan 5 mg. Preventive Mx: verapamil (first-line, ECG monitoring - ↑PR); lithium; topiramate; suboccipital steroid injections; short transitional courses of oral prednisolone; neuromodulation (vagal nerve stimulation, SPG block); galcanezumab (CGRP antibody - US/EU-approved for episodic CH).

conditions.name: Parkinson disease
conditions.summary: Loss of dopaminergic neurons in substantia nigra. Sx: TRAP: tremor (rest, pill-rolling), rigidity (cogwheel), akinesia/bradykinesia, postural instability. Mx: levodopa-carbidopa (most effective; long-term dyskinesias), DA agonists, MAO-B inhibitors, anticholinergics for tremor.

conditions.name: Alzheimer disease
conditions.summary: Most common dementia. Progressive memory loss + executive dysfunction. β-amyloid plaques, neurofibrillary tau tangles. Ix: MMSE/MoCA, MRI for atrophy/exclude reversible causes. Mx: cholinesterase inhibitors (mild-mod), memantine (mod-severe); aducanumab/lecanemab in selected pts.

conditions.name: Multiple sclerosis
conditions.summary: Autoimmune CNS demyelination, dissemination in space and time. Sx: optic neuritis, INO, sensory/motor deficits, Lhermitte, Uhthoff. Ix (MRI): T2 hyperintense plaques. CSF: oligoclonal bands. Mx: steroids for relapses; DMTs (interferon, glatiramer, fingolimod, ocrelizumab) to ↓ relapse rate.

conditions.name: Epilepsy
conditions.summary: ≥2 unprovoked seizures or 1 with high recurrence risk. Focal (with/without impaired awareness, ± secondary generalisation) vs generalised. EEG, MRI brain. Mx: levetiracetam, lamotrigine (focal), valproate (generalised, avoid in pregnancy), surgery for refractory focal. Ddx: syncope (convulsive syncope mimics seizure; no post-ictal), psychogenic non-epileptic seizures (PNES), hypoglycaemia, TIA, parasomnias, movement disorder.

conditions.name: Bell palsy
conditions.summary: Acute unilateral LMN (lower motor neuron) facial nerve (CN VII) palsy; presumed HSV-1 reactivation + inflammatory oedema in facial canal. LMN pattern: complete unilateral facial weakness including forehead (differentiates from UMN - stroke, spares forehead). Sx: rapid onset (<72 hr); unilateral facial droop, inability to close eye (Bell phenomenon - eye rolls up), taste (anterior 2/3 tongue), hyperacusis, post-auricular pain. Ix: clinical; exclude UMN (stroke), Ramsay Hunt (herpetic vesicles in ear/palate → antivirals), Lyme (bilateral palsy), parotid tumour, sarcoidosis. Mx: oral prednisolone (started within 72 hr - key, shortens course, ↑complete recovery) ± aciclovir if severe; eye lubrication/patching (prevent corneal ulceration); most recover fully within 3-6 months.

conditions.name: Trigeminal neuralgia
conditions.summary: Severe paroxysmal unilateral facial pain in distribution of trigeminal nerve (V2/V3 most common, V1 rare). Lancinating, electric shock-like pain lasting seconds, triggered by light touch (eating, talking, brushing teeth, wind). Idiopathic (most: vascular compression of CN V at root entry zone) or secondary (MS - younger patients, bilateral; tumour; AVM). Ix: clinical (ICHD-3 criteria); MRI to exclude secondary cause. Mx: first-line - carbamazepine (reduces Na⁺ channel activity) or oxcarbazepine; lamotrigine, gabapentin (second-line); baclofen (adjunct). Surgical: microvascular decompression (MVD - curative if vascular compression confirmed), percutaneous radiofrequency rhizotomy, glycerol rhizolysis, stereotactic radiosurgery (Gamma Knife) for high-surgical-risk.

conditions.name: Subarachnoid haemorrhage
conditions.summary: Bleeding into subarachnoid space (between arachnoid and pia mater). Aetiology: ruptured intracranial aneurysm (85% - Berry aneurysm, most at Circle of Willis - PCOM, MCA, AComm), AVM, perimesencephalic SAH (non-aneurysmal - good prognosis). Sx: thunderclap headache ('worst headache of life' - instantaneous maximum intensity), meningism (neck stiffness, photophobia develops hours later), ± focal deficit, LOC, retinal haemorrhages (subhyaloid - Terson syndrome). Ix: CT head (non-contrast - hyperdense subarachnoid blood - sensitivity 98% within 12 h; drops to 85% at 24 h), LP (xanthochromia after 12 h - spectrophotometry - if CT negative but clinical suspicion high), CTA (aneurysm detection), DSA (gold standard for aneurysm). Mx: immediate - BP control (target <160 systolic), analgesia, nimodipine (oral - PREVENTS vasospasm - ↓ischaemic deficit/death - NOT to treat it; start within 96 h and continue 21 days), neurosurgical/neurointerventional review. Aneurysm: coiling (endovascular - preferred - ISAT trial) or clipping. Complications: re-bleeding (highest risk first 24 h), vasospasm (days 4–14 - DINDs - delayed ischaemic neurological deficit), hydrocephalus, hyponatraemia (SIADH or cerebral salt-wasting).

conditions.name: Iron deficiency anaemia
conditions.summary: Microcytic hypochromic anaemia. ↓ferritin, ↑TIBC, ↓transferrin sat. Causes: blood loss (menstrual, GI), poor intake, malabsorption (coeliac, IBD). Investigate GI source in adults. Mx: oral ferrous sulfate; IV iron if intolerant or severe.

conditions.name: Vitamin B12 deficiency
conditions.summary: Macrocytic anaemia + neuro Sx (subacute combined degeneration, neuropathy, dementia). Causes: pernicious anaemia, gastrectomy, ileal disease, vegan diet. ↓B12, ↑MMA, ↑homocysteine. Mx: IM B12 injections then maintenance.

conditions.name: Sickle cell disease
conditions.summary: Autosomal recessive; HbS (glutamate→valine, β-chain codon 6 - Glu6Val); HbSS (sickle cell anaemia) or compound heterozygotes (HbSC, HbS/β-thal). Polymerisation of deoxyHbS → sickling → haemolysis, vaso-occlusion. Complications: vaso-occlusive crisis (bone pain, dactylitis - 'hand-foot syndrome' in infants), acute chest syndrome (fever, chest pain, ↓SpO₂ - life-threatening, exchange transfusion), stroke, splenic sequestration (infant/child - acute splenic enlargement + anaemia), aplastic crisis (parvovirus B19), priapism, avascular necrosis, sickle retinopathy, nephropathy, skin ulcers, functional asplenia → encapsulated organism infection risk (pneumococcal, meningococcal, Hib). Ix: Hb electrophoresis/HPLC; solubility test. Mx: hydroxycarbamide (↑HbF - ↓crises, acute chest, transfusion requirement); transfusion (exchange for stroke/ACS); penicillin prophylaxis + vaccinations (functional asplenia); analgesia (opioids for crisis); voxelotor, crizanlizumab (newer agents); HSCT (curative); gene therapy.

conditions.name: Haemophilia
conditions.summary: X-linked recessive bleeding disorder. Haemophilia A (factor VIII deficiency, most common - 80%); Haemophilia B (factor IX deficiency - Christmas disease). Ix (severity): mild (factor >5%: surgery/major trauma bleeds), moderate (1-5%), severe (<1%: spontaneous bleeds). Sx: haemarthroses (target joints - knee, elbow, ankle → chronic synovitis → haemophilic arthropathy), haematomas (muscle, retroperitoneal - iliopsoas haematoma mimics appendicitis/hip pain), intracranial haemorrhage. Ix: ↑APTT, normal PT and bleeding time. Specific: low factor VIII (A) or IX (B) assay. Mx: recombinant factor concentrate (on-demand or prophylactic); DDAVP (desmopressin) for mild haemophilia A (↑VWF and FVIII); emicizumab (bispecific antibody bridging FIX/FX - subcutaneous, prevents bleeds in A with/without inhibitors); avoid aspirin/NSAIDs; gene therapy (maturing - long-term factor production).

conditions.name: Thalassaemia
conditions.summary: Inherited haemoglobin disorder; reduced/absent globin chain production → haemolytic anaemia, ineffective erythropoiesis. Beta-thalassaemia: β0 (absent β-chain) or β+ (reduced); homozygous → thalassaemia major (Cooley anaemia): severe haemolytic anaemia, transfusion-dependent from 6-24 months, splenomegaly, bone changes (chipmunk facies, frontal bossing - extramedullary haematopoiesis). Heterozygous (trait): mild hypochromic microcytic anaemia (Hb ~10-12 g/dL). Alpha-thalassaemia: 4 α-globin genes - 1 del (silent carrier), 2 del (α-thal trait), 3 del (HbH disease - moderate haemolytic anaemia), 4 del (Hb Bart's - hydrops fetalis, fatal). Ix: blood film (target cells, hypochromia, microcytosis); Hb electrophoresis (↑HbA2 in β-trait); HPLC; gene analysis. Mx: major: regular transfusions + iron chelation (desferrioxamine/deferasirox); hydroxycarbamide (↑HbF production); splenectomy; HSCT (curative); gene therapy (betibeglogene autologous gene addition, luspatercept).

conditions.name: Multiple myeloma
conditions.summary: Plasma cell malignancy (clonal IgG 50%, IgA 20%, light chain only - Bence Jones); M-protein in serum/urine. CRAB criteria (end-organ damage): hyperCalcaemia, Renal impairment, Anaemia (normocytic), Bone lesions (osteolytic - 'punched out' lesions, pathological fractures; NO osteoblastic activity → normal bone scan, ALP). Hyperviscosity (IgA/IgM). ↑ESR (rouleaux formation), ↑total protein, ↑globulin. Ix: SPEP (serum protein electrophoresis - M spike), serum free light chain assay, bone marrow biopsy (≥10% clonal plasma cells), whole-body low-dose CT/PET-CT (bone lesions). Ix (staging): R-ISS. Mx: transplant-eligible: VRd induction (bortezomib + lenalidomide + dexamethasone) → ASCT → lenalidomide maintenance; non-eligible: VRd or daratumumab-VRd; relapsed/refractory: carfilzomib, pomalidomide, daratumumab, belantamab mafodotin, CAR-T (idecabtagene/ciltacabtagene for ≥4 prior lines); bisphosphonates (bone protection); treat CRAB complications.

conditions.name: Breast cancer
conditions.summary: Most common cancer in women worldwide; lifetime risk ~12.5% (UK). Types: invasive ductal (NST - no special type, 75%); lobular (15% - bilateral, E-cadherin negative); DCIS (in situ, no invasion); Paget disease of nipple. Risk: BRCA1/2 (lifetime risk 65-87% - BRCA1 higher; also ↑ovarian cancer); family history, Klinefelter (males), HRT (combined oestrogen-progestogen), obesity (postmenopausal), alcohol, nulliparity, early menarche/late menopause, radiation, dense breast tissue. Molecular subtypes: Luminal A (ER+/PR+, HER2−, low Ki67 - best prognosis); Luminal B (ER+, HER2± high Ki67); HER2-enriched (HER2+ ER−); Triple-negative (TNBC - ER−/PR−/HER2−; BRCA associated; aggressive). Ix: NHS Breast Screening Programme (50-71 yr, mammography every 3 yr). Ix (staging): TNM. Sx: painless lump (most common), nipple discharge (bloody), skin changes (peau d'orange, dimpling, ulceration), lymphadenopathy. Mx: surgery (wide local excision/breast-conserving + sentinel LN biopsy or mastectomy + axillary clearance); radiotherapy (after BCS, reduces local recurrence); systemic: adjuvant chemotherapy (anthracycline + taxane), endocrine therapy (tamoxifen - premenopausal; aromatase inhibitor [letrozole/anastrozole/exemestane] - postmenopausal; 5-10 yr); anti-HER2 (trastuzumab, pertuzumab, T-DM1/T-DXd); CDK4/6 inhibitors (palbociclib, ribociclib - metastatic ER+/HER2−); PARP inhibitors (olaparib/talazoparib for BRCA+, metastatic TNBC); pembrolizumab (PD-1 - metastatic TNBC, high PD-L1).

conditions.name: Prostate cancer
conditions.summary: Most common male cancer in Western world; predominantly peripheral zone (adenocarcinoma); slowly progressive. Risk: age, Black ethnicity, family history (BRCA1/2, Lynch), testosterone. Sx: often asymptomatic (screen-detected); LUTS (local); bone pain/pathological fracture (metastatic - osteoblastic, ↑ALP, ↑PSA); haematuria, haematospermia, erectile dysfunction. PSA (prostate-specific antigen): screening controversial; PSA density, PSA velocity, free:total PSA ratio. DRE: hard, irregular, nodular prostate. Ix: multi-parametric MRI (mpMRI) → PI-RADS (3-5 = suspicious) → targeted/systematic biopsy (TRUS or transperineal); Gleason score (grade group 1-5); TNM staging; PSMA PET-CT (nodal/metastatic staging). Mx: localised: active surveillance (low-risk); radical prostatectomy (laparoscopic/robotic); external beam RT ± brachytherapy; locally advanced: RT + long-term androgen deprivation therapy (ADT, 2-3 yr); metastatic: ADT (LHRH agonist/antagonist - castration) + docetaxel or abiraterone/enzalutamide/apalutamide; castration-resistant: cabazitaxel, PARP inhibitors (olaparib - BRCA+), 177Lu-PSMA-617.

conditions.name: Colorectal cancer
conditions.summary: Third most common cancer globally; 95% adenocarcinoma. Pathways: chromosomal instability (APC → RAS → TP53 - Vogelstein sequence, 70%), microsatellite instability/MMR deficiency (Lynch syndrome/sporadic MLH1 methylation, ~15%), serrated pathway (BRAF). Risk: adenomatous polyps, IBD (especially pancolitis), family history, diet (processed/red meat), obesity, alcohol, smoking. Protective: aspirin, dietary fibre, NSAIDS. Ix: colonoscopy (gold standard); FIT (faecal immunochemical test - NHSBSP uses FIT → if positive → colonoscopy). Sx: right-sided (iron-deficiency anaemia, occult bleeding, palpable mass - ascending colon); left-sided (change in bowel habit, rectal bleeding, tenesmus, obstruction - descending/sigmoid). Ix (staging): TNM/Duke; CT chest/abdomen/pelvis (staging); TRUS/MRI rectum (rectal cancer staging - T-stage/CRM). Mx: colon: laparoscopic right/left hemicolectomy/anterior resection; rectal: low anterior resection (LAR) / abdominoperineal resection (APR) + neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (locally advanced); adjuvant FOLFOX/CAPOX (stage III); cetuximab (EGFR inhibitor - RAS WT); pembrolizumab (MSI-H/dMMR).

conditions.name: Rheumatoid arthritis
conditions.summary: Symmetric chronic polyarthritis, MCPs/PIPs/wrists; morning stiffness >1 h. Extra-articular: nodules, ILD, vasculitis, cardiac. RF, anti-CCP (more specific), ↑ESR/CRP. Mx: early MTX ± hydroxychloroquine/sulfasalazine; biologics (anti-TNF) if refractory. Ddx: SLE (ANA/anti-dsDNA; multisystem), psoriatic arthritis (DIP joints + skin/nail; asymmetric), reactive arthritis, viral arthritis (parvovirus B19; self-limiting), osteoarthritis (no systemic features, Heberden/Bouchard nodes).
utd: initial treatment of rheumatoid arthritis in adults
general principles and overview of management of rheumatoid arthritis
alternatives to methotrexate for the initial treatment of rheumatoid arthritis in adults

conditions.name: Osteoarthritis
conditions.summary: Cartilage wear → joint pain (worse with activity), stiffness <30 min, crepitus. Heberden/Bouchard nodes. X-ray: joint space narrowing, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis/cysts. Mx: weight loss, exercise, paracetamol, topical/oral NSAIDs, intra-articular steroid, joint replacement.

conditions.name: Systemic lupus erythematosus
conditions.summary: Multisystem autoimmune disease. Diverse Sx: malar rash, photosensitivity, serositis, arthritis, nephritis, cytopaenias, neuropsych. ANA highly sensitive; anti-dsDNA and anti-Sm specific. Lupus nephritis is major cause of mortality. Mx: hydroxychloroquine for all; immunosuppression for organ involvement. Ddx: rheumatoid arthritis (symmetric small joint; RF/anti-CCP; no nephritis/malar rash), mixed connective tissue disease (anti-U1RNP), drug-induced lupus (histone antibodies; resolves on stopping), viral arthritis (parvovirus B19, hep B/C), sarcoidosis.
utd: overview of the management and prognosis of systemic lupus erythematosus in adults

conditions.name: Gout
