conditions.summary: Monosodium urate crystal deposition. Acute: severe monoarthritis, often podagra (1st MTP). Synovial fluid: needle-shaped, negative birefringent crystals. Acute Mx: NSAIDs, colchicine, steroids. Chronic: allopurinol/febuxostat (don't start during flare; cover with prophylaxis). Ddx: septic arthritis (must exclude - aspirate joint; WBC >50k, organisms), pseudogout/CPPD (rhomboid positively birefringent crystals; knee/wrist), reactive arthritis, osteoarthritis flare.
utd: pharmacologic urate lowering therapy treatment of gout

conditions.name: Fibromyalgia
conditions.summary: Chronic widespread pain syndrome; central sensitisation (↑pain processing in CNS). ACR 2010/2011 diagnostic criteria: widespread pain index (WPI) + symptom severity scale (SSS - fatigue, unrefreshing sleep, cognitive symptoms; exclude other diagnoses). Female > male (7:1); peak 20-50 yr. Not inflammatory/degenerative - normal investigations (bloods, X-rays, biopsies normal). Key features: widespread musculoskeletal pain (>3 months), fatigue (severe, post-exertional malaise - CF-like), sleep disturbance (non-restorative), cognitive difficulties ('fibro fog'), anxiety/depression (common comorbid). Associations: prior trauma, infections (viral - glandular fever), poor sleep, hypothyroidism (exclude), IBS, chronic headache. Ix: clinical + exclusion of inflammatory/rheumatological causes. Mx: multidisciplinary approach essential; exercise (aerobic, graded - most effective, reduces pain/fatigue); CBT (pain catastrophising, sleep); medications: duloxetine (SNRI), pregabalin, amitriptyline (low-dose, sleep), tramadol (weak evidence); avoid opioids (evidence lacking, worse outcomes long-term); sleep hygiene; patient education.

conditions.name: Ankylosing spondylitis
conditions.summary: Chronic inflammatory arthropathy of axial skeleton (sacroiliac joints and spine); HLA-B27 (>90% HLA-B27 positive). Predominantly young males (18-35 yr). Sx: insidious onset inflammatory back pain (morning stiffness >1 hr, improves with exercise, worsens with rest - opposite of OA), buttock pain (alternating - SI joint), chest pain (costovertebral joints → ↓chest expansion <5 cm), peripheral arthritis (large joints), enthesitis (Achilles tendinopathy, plantar fasciitis). Extra-articular: anterior uveitis (most common, 25-40%), IBD, aortic regurgitation, apical pulmonary fibrosis, cardiac conduction disease. Progressive spinal fusion → 'bamboo spine' (X-ray) + 'question mark' posture. Ix: modified NY criteria (sacroiliitis on X-ray); ASAS criteria (axial SpA - MRI sacroiliitis before X-ray changes; HLA-B27 + features); MRI SI joints (bone marrow oedema - early). Mx: NSAIDs (first-line, daily continuous - anti-inflammatory + possibly slows disease); physiotherapy (critical - maintains flexibility); TNF inhibitors (adalimumab, etanercept, certolizumab - if inadequate NSAID response); IL-17 inhibitors (secukinumab, ixekizumab - may be preferred); no DMARDs (ineffective for axial disease).

conditions.name: Polymyalgia rheumatica
conditions.summary: Inflammatory condition; aching and morning stiffness (>45 min) of shoulder girdle, hip girdle, neck; >50 yr, peak 70s; 3× more common in women. Rapid response to steroids (diagnostic). ↑ESR/CRP; normocytic anaemia. Giant cell arteritis (GCA) overlap in 15-30% (check for headache, visual symptoms, jaw claudication - exam temporal arteries). Ix: US of shoulder/hip (subdeltoid bursitis, biceps tenosynovitis, trochanteric bursitis); PET-CT (large-vessel involvement). Ix: 2012 ACR/EULAR classification criteria (age ≥50, bilateral shoulder aching, ↑ESR/CRP + ≥4 points - morning stiffness, hip girdle pain, US findings, absence of RF/ACPA, absence of other diagnosis). Mx: prednisolone 15 mg/d (rapid dramatic improvement within 48-72 hr - diagnostic); slow taper over 1-2 yr; methotrexate (steroid-sparing if relapse/SE); tocilizumab.

conditions.name: Giant cell arteritis
conditions.summary: Large-vessel granulomatous vasculitis (aorta and branches, especially external carotid branches); >50 yr, peak 70-80 yr; females > males. Sx: new unilateral temporal headache (throbbing), jaw claudication (pathognomonic - pain on chewing), scalp tenderness (combing hair), visual symptoms (amaurosis fugax, diplopia, visual loss - anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy, AION), polymyalgia rheumatica (40-50% overlap). Sx: thickened, nodular, tender, pulseless temporal artery. ↑ESR (>50, often >100), ↑CRP, normocytic anaemia, ↑ALP. Temporal artery biopsy (TAB): gold standard - giant cells, intimal hyperplasia, granulomatous inflammation (false-negative if skip lesions - take ≥2 cm); do not delay treatment for biopsy. Mx: prednisolone (40-60 mg/d immediately - prevent blindness); 80 mg if visual symptoms; tocilizumab (IL-6 blocker - first approved adjunct to steroids, permits faster tapering, prevents relapse); aspirin (75 mg) for ischaemic complications.
utd: initial treatment of Giant cell arteritis

conditions.name: Psoriasis
conditions.summary: Chronic autoimmune skin disease. Plaque type most common: well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scale on extensor surfaces, scalp. Nail pitting. Associated psoriatic arthritis. Mx: topical steroids/vitamin D analogues, phototherapy, methotrexate, biologics (anti-TNF, anti-IL-17/23).
utd: clinical features and diagnosis of Psoriasis

conditions.name: Eczema
conditions.summary: Chronic relapsing pruritic eczematous dermatitis. Often part of atopy (asthma, allergic rhinitis). Flexural in adults, face/extensor in infants. Mx: emollients (cornerstone), topical steroids/calcineurin inhibitors, dupilumab for moderate-severe.
utd: clinical features and diagnosis of Eczema

conditions.name: Cellulitis
conditions.summary: Bacterial infection of dermis/subcutaneous tissue. Strep pyogenes most common; S. aureus (incl MRSA) in some. Sx: Erythema, warmth, tenderness, swelling, often unilateral lower limb. Mx: cephalexin/flucloxacillin; consider MRSA cover (clinda, doxy, TMP-SMX). Mark margins; review at 48 h. Ddx: necrotising fasciitis (disproportionate pain, crepitus, systemic toxicity - surgical emergency), DVT (can coexist; US if swollen leg), lipodermatosclerosis, stasis dermatitis, erysipelas (sharply demarcated).
utd: cellulitis and skin abscess clinical manifestations diagnosis
cellulitis and skin abscess in adults treatment

conditions.name: Erysipelas
conditions.summary: Superficial cellulitis with sharp demarcation, raised border, classically on face/legs. S. pyogenes. Mx: penicillin V or amoxicillin; cephalexin if penicillin-allergic with mild reaction.
utd: clinical features and diagnosis of Erysipelas

conditions.name: Melanoma
conditions.summary: Malignant tumour of melanocytes; most lethal skin cancer. Risk: UV, fair skin, familial (CDKN2A/BRAF mutations), multiple naevi, dysplastic naevi syndrome, xeroderma pigmentosum. ABCDE criteria: Asymmetry, Border irregularity, Colour variation, Diameter >6 mm, Evolving. Subtypes: superficial spreading (most common), nodular (fast-growing, uniform dark/amelanotic), lentigo maligna, acral lentiginous (palms, soles, subungual - darker skin). Breslow thickness key prognostic factor. Ix (staging): TNM → sentinel LN biopsy if >0.8 mm. Mx: wide excision; adjuvant immunotherapy (pembrolizumab, nivolumab) or targeted (BRAF/MEK inhibitors - vemurafenib/cobimetinib if BRAF V600E+) for stage III-IV.

conditions.name: Kawasaki disease
conditions.summary: Acute systemic vasculitis of childhood (predominantly <5 yr); unknown aetiology; Japanese/East Asian highest prevalence; leading cause of acquired heart disease in children in developed world. Diagnostic criteria: fever ≥5 d + ≥4 of 5 features (CRASH mnemonic: Conjunctival injection (bilateral, non-exudative), Rash (polymorphous, truncal), Adenopathy (cervical, >1.5 cm, usually single), Strawberry tongue/red lips/oropharyngeal erythema, Hands/Feet - erythema + oedema → desquamation). Incomplete Kawasaki: <4 features but echo shows coronary artery aneurysm (CAA) - treat. Ix (echo): CAA in 15-25% untreated (proximal LAD, RCA); giant aneurysm (>8 mm or Z-score ≥10) - risk thrombosis/MI. Mx: IVIG 2 g/kg (single dose, within 10 d - ↓CAA from 25% to 5%) + aspirin (high-dose anti-inflammatory → low-dose antiplatelet); IVIG-resistant: second IVIG or infliximab or steroids; anticoagulation for giant CAA.

conditions.name: Henoch-Schönlein purpura
conditions.summary: IgA-mediated small-vessel vasculitis, usually post-URTI in children. Sx (tetrad): palpable purpura on buttocks/legs, arthralgia, abdominal pain (intussusception), nephritis. Mx: Mostly self-limiting; supportive care. Sx: Steroids if severe abdominal pain or nephritis.
utd: diagnosis of Henoch-Schönlein purpura in children
treatment of Henoch-Schönlein purpura in children

conditions.name: Intussusception
conditions.summary: Telescoping of proximal bowel into distal segment; most common cause of intestinal obstruction in 3 months-2 years (peak 6-9 months). Ileocolic (ileum into colon) most common. Causes: often idiopathic (viral illness, ↑Peyer patches acting as lead point); lead points in older children/adults (Meckel diverticulum, polyp, lymphoma, Henoch-Schönlein purpura - bowel haematoma). Sx: intermittent colicky abdominal pain (child draws up knees, appears well between attacks), vomiting, current jelly stool (blood + mucus - late sign), palpable 'sausage-shaped' mass in RUQ. Ix (US): diagnostic - target/donut sign (concentric rings). Mx: non-surgical pneumatic/hydrostatic enema reduction (80-90% success if no peritonism or perforation); surgical reduction/resection if enema fails or peritonitis.

conditions.name: Pyloric stenosis
conditions.summary: Hypertrophy of pyloric muscle → gastric outlet obstruction; most common surgical cause of vomiting in infants. Male:female 4:1; first-born males; presents 2-8 weeks. Sx: projectile non-bilious vomiting (after each feed), hungry after vomiting ('hungry vomit'), visible gastric peristalsis, palpable 'olive' (firm pyloric mass in RUQ during feed). Metabolic: hypochloraemic hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis (loss of HCl from vomiting; ↑aldosterone → K⁺ loss). Ix (US): pyloric muscle thickness >3 mm, pyloric channel length >14-17 mm. Mx: correct electrolyte/fluid derangement first (saline → replace chloride; then potassium); Ramstedt pyloromyotomy (surgical - definitive, curative). Never operate until metabolic derangement corrected.

conditions.name: Croup
conditions.summary: Parainfluenza most common (6 mo-3 y). Sx: Barking cough, inspiratory stridor, hoarse voice, often viral prodrome. Steeple sign on CXR. Mx: corticosteroids (dexamethasone) for all; nebulised adrenaline if moderate-severe stridor.

conditions.name: Otitis media
conditions.summary: Middle ear infection. Acute OM common in children, often follows URTI. S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae. Bulging, erythematous TM with effusion. Mx: amoxicillin if severe, <2 y bilateral, otorrhoea; observation for mild cases >2 y. Watch for chronic OME and conductive hearing loss.
utd: diagnosis of Otitis media in children
treatment of Otitis media in children

conditions.name: Preeclampsia
conditions.summary: New HTN ≥20 wk + proteinuria or end-organ involvement. Sx: Severe features: BP ≥160/110, ↑Cr, ↑LFTs, thrombocytopenia, pulmonary oedema, neuro Sx. Mx: BP control (labetalol/hydralazine), MgSO4 for seizure prophylaxis, deliver at 37 wk (or earlier if severe). HELLP variant.

conditions.name: Eclampsia
conditions.summary: Generalised seizures in setting of preeclampsia. MgSO4 IV (load 4-6 g, then 1-2 g/h). Ix: Watch for Mg toxicity (loss of reflexes, respiratory depression - calcium gluconate antidote). Deliver promptly. BP control with labetalol/hydralazine.

conditions.name: Ectopic pregnancy
conditions.summary: Implantation outside uterine cavity; fallopian tube (95%, ampullary most common), ovarian, interstitial (cornual - higher mortality), heterotopic (IUP + ectopic simultaneously - especially post-IVF), abdominal/cervical. Risk: prior ectopic (×10), prior PID/tubal surgery, IUD, assisted reproduction, tubal ligation failure. Sx: triad - amenorrhoea (6-8 wk), vaginal bleeding (dark/spotting), pelvic pain (ipsilateral); may be asymptomatic. Rupture: severe acute abdominal pain, shoulder tip pain (diaphragmatic irritation by blood), haemodynamic instability → haemoperitoneum, collapse, death. hCG: positive at ≥25 IU/L; serial hCG rise <53% in 48 hr suggests non-viable/ectopic (normal IUP rises >66% in 48 hr). Ix: TVUSS (gestational sac location; empty uterus + adnexal mass + free fluid - heterogeneous → haemoperitoneum); hCG levels. Mx: haemodynamically unstable → emergency laparoscopic salpingectomy; stable + unruptured: expectant (falling hCG, <35 mm, hCG <1000), methotrexate (single-dose IM - no fetal cardiac activity; hCG <5000; no contraindications: breastfeeding, immunocompromise, renal failure, hepatic disease, ↓WBC) or surgical (laparoscopic salpingectomy or salpingotomy if contralateral tube damaged).

conditions.name: Endometriosis
conditions.summary: Endometrial-like tissue outside uterus (pelvic peritoneum, ovaries - endometrioma/'chocolate cyst', pouch of Douglas, bladder, bowel). Oestrogen-dependent; retrograde menstruation hypothesis (Sampson). Sx: dysmenorrhoea (severe, cyclical), deep dyspareunia, pelvic pain (chronic), dyschezia (painful defecation - posterior disease), dysuria, subfertility. Sx: fixed retroverted uterus, tenderness/nodularity in pouch of Douglas, endometrioma on USS. Ix: laparoscopy + biopsy (gold standard); USS/MRI (endometrioma, deep infiltrating endometriosis - recto-vaginal, bladder). CA-125 (may be elevated, not diagnostic). Ix (staging): AFS/ASRM I-IV (minimal-severe). Mx: analgesia (NSAIDs, paracetamol); hormonal suppression (COCP, progestins, LNG-IUS, GnRH agonists, danazol); surgery (laparoscopic excision - preferred, especially deep disease; salpingo-oophorectomy + hysterectomy for severe/postmenopausal); assisted reproduction for infertility.

conditions.name: Polycystic ovary syndrome
conditions.summary: Most common endocrine disorder in women of reproductive age (5-15%). Rotterdam criteria (2 of 3): oligo/anovulation, clinical/biochemical androgen excess, polycystic ovaries on USS (≥12 follicles or ovarian volume >10 mL in each ovary). Sx: irregular periods, hirsutism, acne, alopecia (androgen-mediated), infertility, obesity (50-60%). ↑LH:FSH (>2:1), ↑testosterone/androstenedione, ↑DHEA-S; ↑LH; oestrogen usually normal; ↑AMH (marker of follicle number). Associations: insulin resistance (50-70%), T2DM, metabolic syndrome, endometrial carcinoma (risk 3×, anovulation → unopposed oestrogen), OSA. Mx: lifestyle (weight loss, exercise - improves all features); menstrual regulation (COCP, progestins - prevents endometrial hyperplasia); insulin-sensitisers (metformin - off-licence, improves ovulation/metabolic); ovulation induction (letrozole/clomiphene, FSH injections); anti-androgens (spironolactone, cyproterone acetate); bariatric surgery.

conditions.name: Major depressive disorder
conditions.summary: ≥2 wk of depressed mood/anhedonia + ≥4 of SIGECAPS. Screen with PHQ-9. Mx: SSRI/SNRI 1st-line; CBT highly effective. Combine for severe. Reassess at 4-6 wk; switch class or augment if no response. Suicide risk assessment essential.

conditions.name: Generalized anxiety disorder
conditions.summary: Excessive uncontrollable worry ≥6 mo + ≥3 somatic Sx (restlessness, fatigue, ↓concentration, irritability, muscle tension, sleep disturbance). Mx: CBT and/or SSRI/SNRI (sertraline, escitalopram, venlafaxine). Buspirone alternative; avoid long-term benzodiazepines.

conditions.name: Bipolar disorder
conditions.summary: BP-I: ≥1 manic episode (≥7 d, requires hospitalisation, or psychosis). BP-II: hypomania + MDE. Mania: DIGFAST. Mx: lithium, valproate, atypical antipsychotics; lamotrigine for bipolar depression. Avoid antidepressant monotherapy (risk of mood switch).

conditions.name: Schizophrenia
conditions.summary: Psychotic disorder ≥6 mo with ≥2 of delusions, hallucinations, disorganised speech, disorganised behaviour, negative Sx (≥1 from first three). Mx: 2nd-generation antipsychotics 1st-line (risperidone, olanzapine, aripiprazole). Clozapine for treatment-resistant. Psychosocial Mx essential.

conditions.name: Post-traumatic stress disorder
conditions.summary: Develops after exposure to traumatic event (actual/threatened death, serious injury, sexual violence) - directly, witnessed, or indirect. Ix: Criteria (DSM-5): intrusion symptoms (flashbacks, nightmares, intrusive memories), avoidance (thoughts, reminders), negative alterations in cognition/mood (guilt, emotional numbing, detachment), hyperarousal (hypervigilance, exaggerated startle, sleep disturbance, irritability, reckless behaviour). Duration >1 month. Acute stress reaction: <4 wk. Complex PTSD (ICD-11): after prolonged/repeated trauma (childhood abuse, domestic violence) + emotion dysregulation + distorted self-perception + difficulties in relationships. Mx: trauma-focused CBT (TF-CBT - first-line) or EMDR (eye movement desensitisation and reprocessing - first-line equivalent); SSRI/SNRI (second-line, or for comorbid depression/anxiety); prazosin (nightmares); avoid benzodiazepines.

conditions.name: Obsessive-compulsive disorder
conditions.summary: Obsessions (recurrent, intrusive, unwanted thoughts/images/urges causing anxiety) + compulsions (repetitive behaviours/mental acts performed to reduce obsession-related anxiety - often recognised as excessive). Common themes: contamination (handwashing), harm, symmetry/checking, sexual/religious intrusive thoughts. Ego-dystonic (distressing, unwanted) - differentiates from OCD spectrum disorders. Impairment: >1 hr/day on obsessions/compulsions. Y-BOCS scale. Comorbid: depression (major), tics (Tourette overlap), BDD, anorexia. Mx: CBT with ERP (exposure and response prevention - first-line for mild-moderate); SSRI (first-line pharmacological - higher doses needed: fluoxetine 60-80 mg, sertraline 200 mg; ≥12 wk trial); combination CBT + SSRI; clomipramine (TCA, second-line, more SE); augmentation with antipsychotic (aripiprazole, risperidone) for partial responders.

conditions.name: Glaucoma
conditions.summary: Optic neuropathy with characteristic visual field loss. Usually ↑IOP (open-angle most common). Sx: Acute angle-closure: emergency - severe pain, red eye, fixed mid-dilated pupil, halos, nausea. Mx: topical agents (prostaglandins, β-blockers, α-agonists), laser, surgery.

conditions.name: Cataract
conditions.summary: Opacification of crystalline lens; leading cause of reversible blindness worldwide. Types: nuclear (most common - central, progressive myopia, 'second sight'); cortical (spokes); posterior subcapsular (PSC - worst effect on vision, steroid-associated, diabetic, radiation). Risk: age, smoking, UV, diabetes, steroids, trauma, congenital (TORCH infections - rubella classic; galactosaemia, metabolic). Congenital cataract → amblyopia risk (urgent surgery). Sx: gradual ↓visual acuity, glare (esp. night driving, oncoming headlights), diplopia (monocular), ↓colour vision. Ix: slit lamp; red reflex (absent). Mx: surgical: phacoemulsification (gold standard - ultrasound emulsification + IOL implantation); extracapsular (manual ECCE - large incision, limited world settings); posterior capsule opacification (PCO - 'after-cataract') post-op → YAG capsulotomy.

conditions.name: Macular degeneration
conditions.summary: Leading cause of irreversible central vision loss in >50 yr; drusen (lipid deposits under RPE) + RPE atrophy. Dry AMD (85%): slowly progressive drusen accumulation → geographic atrophy (RPE loss) → central scotoma; no approved treatment until recently (pegcetacoplan - complement C3 inhibitor for geographic atrophy). Wet (neovascular) AMD (15% but causes 90% of severe vision loss): choroidal neovascularisation (CNV) → exudate, haemorrhage, rapid vision loss; Amsler grid (central distortion/scotoma). Ix: fundoscopy (drusen, CNV membrane), OCT (subretinal fluid, CNV), FFA. Mx: wet AMD: anti-VEGF injections (ranibizumab, bevacizumab off-licence, aflibercept, faricimab - intravitreal; repeated injections; significantly ↑visual outcomes); photodynamic therapy (PDT, less used now). Risk reduction (dry AMD + wet): AREDS2 supplements (AREDS2: lutein/zeaxanthin + vitamin C/E + zinc/copper - ↓progression in intermediate/advanced AMD); smoking cessation; UV protection.

conditions.name: Sinusitis
conditions.summary: Most acute sinusitis is viral (resolves <10 d). Bacterial: Sx >10 d, double-worsening, severe Sx. Causes: S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae, M. catarrhalis. Mx: amoxicillin-clavulanate; symptomatic care. Watch for orbital cellulitis, intracranial extension.

conditions.name: Pharyngitis
conditions.summary: Viral most common; GAS in ~15-30% of children. Sx: Centor criteria (fever, tonsillar exudate, tender LN, no cough). Rapid antigen ± culture. Mx: Mx (GAS): penicillin V or amoxicillin (prevent rheumatic fever). Avoid amoxicillin if EBV suspected (rash).

conditions.name: Anaphylaxis
conditions.summary: Life-threatening systemic hypersensitivity reaction (IgE-mediated or non-immune). Triggers: foods (peanut, shellfish), drugs (penicillin, NSAIDs), insect stings, latex. Sx: urticaria, angioedema, bronchospasm, hypotension within minutes. Mx: IM adrenaline (adrenaline) 0.5 mg lateral thigh immediately; lie flat, IV fluids, antihistamine + steroid adjuncts. Biphasic reaction possible; observe ≥4 h. Prescribe EpiPen on discharge. Ddx: vasovagal syncope (no urticaria/bronchospasm), acute severe asthma (no urticaria/hypotension), angioedema without urticaria (hereditary/ACE-i), panic attack, carcinoid, phaeochromocytoma.

conditions.name: Angioedema
conditions.summary: Rapid deep-tissue swelling (dermis, submucosa), often perioral, periorbital, extremities. Allergic (histamine-mediated), hereditary (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency), or ACE-inhibitor-induced (bradykinin). Laryngeal involvement → airway emergency. Mx: Hereditary: icatibant or C1-inh concentrate for attacks; lanadelumab or tranexamic acid prophylaxis.

conditions.name: Urticaria
conditions.summary: Pruritic wheals (raised erythematous plaques) lasting <24 h each. Acute (<6 wk): most often allergic or viral. Chronic (>6 wk): often autoimmune or idiopathic. Dermographism common. Mx: non-sedating antihistamine (cetirizine, fexofenadine); omalizumab for chronic refractory; identify and avoid triggers.

conditions.name: Allergic rhinitis
conditions.summary: IgE-mediated nasal inflammation. Sx: sneezing, nasal discharge, congestion, nasal itch ± conjunctival Sx. Seasonal (pollens) or perennial (dust mite, pet dander, mould). Mx: intranasal corticosteroid (most effective), oral non-sedating antihistamine, LTRA; allergen immunotherapy for refractory.

conditions.name: Hyponatraemia
conditions.summary: Na⁺ <135 mmol/L; most common electrolyte disturbance. Classify: hypovolaemic (↓Na⁺ + ↓volume - GI losses, diuretics, Addison's; urine Na <20 = extrarenal, >20 = renal loss), euvolaemic (SIADH, hypothyroidism, glucocorticoid deficiency, psychogenic polydipsia), hypervolaemic (↓effective circulating volume - CCF, cirrhosis, nephrotic - urine Na <20). SIADH criteria: hypo-osmolar hyponatraemia, urine osmolality >100, urine Na >20, euvolaemia, normal thyroid/adrenal function. Sx: severity depends on rate of development: acute/rapid - cerebral oedema (nausea, headache, seizures, coma); chronic - often asymptomatic or subtle. Correct slowly if chronic (max 8-10 mmol/L/24 hr - avoid osmotic demyelination syndrome/central pontine myelinolysis). Mx: SIADH - fluid restriction; severe/symptomatic: hypertonic saline (3%) in ICU; vaptans (tolvaptan - AVP receptor antagonist); treat cause.
utd: overview of the treatment of hyponatremia in adults
pathophysiology and etiology of the syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion
diagnostic evaluation of adults with hyponatremia

conditions.name: Hypernatraemia
conditions.summary: Serum Na >145 mmol/L. Always reflects water deficit relative to sodium. Causes: insensible losses (fever, burns), DI, inadequate intake. Sx: thirst, lethargy, seizures. Mx: free water replacement (PO if alert, D5W or 0.45% NaCl IV); correct slowly ≤10 mmol/L/24 h. Identify and treat underlying cause (e.g. desmopressin for central DI).

conditions.name: Hypokalaemia
conditions.summary: K⁺ <3.5 mmol/L; serious at <3.0, life-threatening at <2.5 mmol/L. Causes: GI loss (vomiting - alkalosis + ↑aldosterone; diarrhoea - metabolic acidosis), renal loss (diuretics - most common, hyperaldosteronism, Cushing, Bartter/Gitelman, RTA I/II, hypomagnesaemia), shift into cells (insulin, β₂-agonists, alkalosis, hypokalaemic periodic paralysis). Sx: muscle weakness → rhabdomyolysis, paralytic ileus, polyuria (↓renal concentrating ability), palpitations. Ix (ECG): U waves (prominent), T-wave flattening/inversion, prolonged QU, ST depression, ↑PR, Vtach/VF risk. Mx: mild (>3.0): oral KCl; severe (<3.0 or symptomatic): IV KCl (max 20 mmol/hr via central line; max 40 mmol/hr only in extreme emergency with monitoring); correct magnesium (hypomagnesaemia → refractory hypokalaemia); treat cause.

conditions.name: Hyperkalaemia
conditions.summary: K⁺ >5.5 mmol/L; life-threatening arrhythmia risk at >6.5 mmol/L. Causes: ↓renal excretion (AKI, CKD, Addison's, RTA IV, ACEi/ARB, K-sparing diuretics, trimethoprim), ↑release from cells (acidosis, rhabdomyolysis, haemolysis, tissue necrosis, insulin deficiency), ↑intake (K supplements, diet). Ix: ECG changes (progressive): peaked T waves → PR prolongation → P wave flattening → wide QRS → sine wave → VF/asystole. Mx (by urgency): cardiac monitoring; calcium gluconate/chloride IV (membrane stabilisation - immediate, does not ↓K⁺); insulin + dextrose (shifts K⁺ into cells - 20-30 min); salbutamol nebulisation (shifts K⁺ - additive with insulin); sodium bicarbonate (acidosis); polystyrene sulfonate/patiromer/SZC (GI cation exchange - eliminates K⁺); dialysis (refractory/severe AKI); treat underlying cause.
utd: treatment and prevention of hyperkalemia in adults
causes and evaluation of hyperkalemia in adults

conditions.name: Hypocalcaemia
conditions.summary: Corrected Ca <2.1 mmol/L. Causes: hypoparathyroidism (post-thyroidectomy most common), vitamin D deficiency, CKD (↓1,25-OH-D3), hypomagnesaemia, pancreatitis, citrate toxicity. Sx: perioral tingling, Trousseau/Chvostek signs, tetany, QT prolongation, seizures. Mx: IV calcium gluconate (symptomatic); oral calcium + vitamin D (chronic).

conditions.name: Hypercalcaemia
conditions.summary: Corrected Ca²⁺ >2.65 mmol/L. Causes: hyperparathyroidism (most common outpatient - primary, 90% from adenoma, usually mild/asymptomatic), malignancy (most common inpatient - PTHrP from solid tumours, bony metastases, myeloma, lymphoma), vitamin D toxicity, sarcoidosis, granulomatous disease, FHH (familial hypocalciuric hypercalcaemia - benign, ↑PTH + low urine Ca), thiazides, milk-alkali, Addison. Sx (if severe/rapid): 'stones, bones, groans, moans' - renal stones (nephrolithiasis), bone pain/pathological fracture, constipation/nausea/vomiting/pancreatitis, depression/confusion/coma; polyuria/polydipsia (nephrogenic DI). Ix (ECG): short QTc. Mx: hydration (IV 0.9% NaCl - cornerstone); bisphosphonates (IV zoledronate/pamidronate - peak effect 48-72 hr, for malignancy/severe); calcitonin (rapid but tachyphylaxis); denosumab (malignant, refractory); treat cause; avoid thiazides.

conditions.name: Hypomagnesaemia
conditions.summary: Mg <0.7 mmol/L. Causes: malabsorption, alcohol, PPI long-term, loop/thiazide diuretics, diarrhoea, aminoglycosides. Sx: tremor, tetany, seizures, refractory hypokalaemia and hypocalcaemia. Mx: oral magnesium (mild); IV magnesium sulfate if severe or symptomatic.

conditions.name: Metabolic acidosis
conditions.summary: pH <7.35 with ↓HCO3. Ix: Calculate anion gap (Na − Cl − HCO3; normal 8–12). High-AG: MUDPILES (methanol, uraemia, DKA, propylene glycol/paracetamol, isoniazid/iron, lactic acidosis, ethylene glycol, salicylates). Sx: Normal-AG (hyperchloraemic): diarrhoea, RTA, saline excess. Compensation: ↓PaCO2 (Winter's formula: expected PaCO2 = 1.5×HCO3 + 8 ± 2). Treat underlying cause.
utd: causes and evaluation of Metabolic acidosis

conditions.name: Metabolic alkalosis
conditions.summary: pH >7.45 with ↑HCO3. Sx: Common causes: vomiting (chloride loss), diuretics, hypokalaemia, hyperaldosteronism, post-hypercapnia. Chloride-responsive (urine Cl <20): vomiting, diuretics - Mx: IV 0.9% NaCl. Chloride-resistant (urine Cl >20): hyperaldosteronism, Cushing - Mx: treat cause. Compensation: ↑PaCO2 (expected PaCO2 = 0.7×HCO3 + 21).
utd: causes and evaluation of Metabolic alkalosis

conditions.name: Respiratory acidosis
conditions.summary: pH <7.35 with ↑PaCO2 (hypoventilation). Acute: limited metabolic compensation (↑HCO3 by 1 per 10 mmHg ↑CO2); chronic: ↑HCO3 by 3.5 per 10 mmHg ↑CO2. Causes: COPD, neuromuscular disease, opioid/sedative overdose, obesity hypoventilation, tension PTX. Mx: address cause; ventilatory support if severe.
utd: causes and evaluation of Respiratory acidosis

conditions.name: Respiratory alkalosis
conditions.summary: pH >7.45 with ↓PaCO2 (hyperventilation). Compensation: ↓HCO3 (acute: 2 per 10 mmHg ↓CO2; chronic: 5 per 10 mmHg ↓CO2). Causes: anxiety, pain, fever, salicylate poisoning, high altitude, liver failure, pregnancy. Sx: perioral tingling, light-headedness. Mx: treat cause; paper-bag breathing only for anxiety-related.
utd: causes and evaluation of Respiratory alkalosis

conditions.name: Septic shock
conditions.summary: Sepsis + vasopressor requirement for MAP ≥65 + lactate >2 mmol/L despite fluid resus. Warm, high-output state (initially); distributive physiology. Most common cause of ICU mortality. Mx (Hour-1 bundle): broad-spectrum abx, 30 mL/kg IV crystalloid, cultures, lactate; vasopressors (noradrenaline 1st-line). Stress-dose hydrocortisone if refractory. Ddx: other shock types - cardiogenic (↑JVP, pulmonary oedema, ↓CO), hypovolaemic (clear source of volume loss), obstructive (tension PTX, tamponade), adrenal crisis, anaphylaxis.

conditions.name: Cardiogenic shock
conditions.summary: Cardiac pump failure → ↓CO, ↑PCWP, hypoperfusion. Causes: STEMI (most common), decompensated HF, acute VHD, myocarditis, arrhythmia. Sx: hypotension, pulmonary oedema, cool peripheries, ↑lactate. Mx: urgent revascularisation (STEMI); vasopressors (noradrenaline) ± inotrope (dobutamine); mechanical support (IABP, Impella) in selected pts. Avoid diuretics/vasodilators if hypotensive. Ddx: septic shock (warm peripheries, ↓SVR), obstructive shock (cardiac tamponade, tension PTX - ↑JVP, absent breath sounds), hypovolaemic shock, acute PE.

conditions.name: Obstructive shock
conditions.summary: Extracardiac obstruction to blood flow. Causes: tension pneumothorax (most common), cardiac tamponade, massive PE, constrictive pericarditis. Distended neck veins, hypotension, absent breath sounds (tension PTX). Immediate cause-specific intervention: needle decompression (tension PTX), pericardiocentesis (tamponade), thrombolysis (massive PE).

conditions.name: Dilated cardiomyopathy
conditions.summary: Most common cardiomyopathy; LV/biventricular dilatation + systolic dysfunction (↓EF). Causes: idiopathic (genetic - titin, lamin A/C, desmin mutations), post-viral (coxsackievirus, parvovirus B19, SARS-CoV-2), alcohol, peripartum, drug toxicity (anthracyclines, trastuzumab, cocaine), haemochromatosis, sarcoidosis, uraemic, autoimmune, thyrotoxicosis. Sx: HF (dyspnoea, orthopnoea), fatigue, palpitations, embolic events (LV thrombus), arrhythmias (VT, AF), SCD. Ix (echo): dilated LV, ↓EF, wall motion abnormality (global), ± LV thrombus. Ix (MRI): LGE pattern helps distinguish cause. Mx: HF with reduced EF (HFrEF) protocol (ACEi, beta-blocker, MRA, SGLT2i, diuretics); ICD (LVEF ≤35%); CRT (if LBBB + QRS >150 ms); anticoagulation if thrombus; heart transplant.
utd: dilated cardiomyopathy clinical manifestations diagnosis evaluation

conditions.name: Long QT syndrome
conditions.summary: Inherited ion channel disorder (K⁺/Na⁺/Ca²⁺); prolonged QTc (>450 ms men, >460 ms women) → risk of torsades de pointes (TdP) → syncope/SCD. Schwartz score. Types: LQT1 (KCNQ1 - loss of I_Ks; exercise/swimming trigger; broad-based T wave), LQT2 (KCNH2 - auditory triggers; notched T wave), LQT3 (SCN5A - sleep trigger; late peaked T wave). Drug-induced (acquired): class IA/III antiarrhythmics, antipsychotics, macrolides, fluoroquinolones, methadone - check CredibleMeds. Mx: avoid QT-prolonging drugs; avoid electrolyte imbalances; beta-blockers (first-line LQT1/2 - nadolol best); ICD for high-risk (syncope, prior cardiac arrest, LQT3); left cardiac sympathetic denervation (LCSD).
utd: acquired long QT syndrome causes treatment

conditions.name: Torsades de pointes
conditions.summary: Polymorphic VT with twisting QRS axis around isoelectric baseline; occurs on background of long QT. Triggered by bradycardia or pause. Can degenerate to VF. Mx: IV magnesium sulfate (2 g) 1st-line; temporary pacing or isoprenaline for bradycardia-dependent torsades. Remove QT-prolonging agents.

conditions.name: Rheumatic fever
conditions.summary: Post-GAS pharyngitis immune-mediated disease. Ix: Jones criteria: major (carditis, polyarthritis, chorea, erythema marginatum, subcutaneous nodules), minor (fever, ↑CRP/ESR, prolonged PR). Carditis → mitral (most common) or aortic valve disease long-term. Mx: Mx (acute): aspirin, steroids if carditis; secondary prophylaxis with penicillin to prevent recurrence.
utd: acute rheumatic fever clinical manifestations diagnosis

conditions.name: Infective endocarditis
conditions.summary: Infection of endocardium (valves, chordae, mural endocardium). Risk: native valve disease (regurgitation/stenosis/prolapse), prosthetic valve (highest risk - early <60 d: S. aureus/CoNS/Gram-negatives; late >60 d: similar to native valve), IVDU (tricuspid - S. aureus), structural CHD, intravascular devices (pacemaker leads, CIED). Mx: Organisms: S. aureus (most common overall - acute, high virulence, community/IVDU); viridans streptococci (S. sanguis, S. mutans - native valve, subacute, oral bacteraemia - dental procedures); CoNS (prosthetic valve, hospital); HACEK organisms; C. burnetii (Q fever); Enterococcus. Ix: Duke criteria (modified): 2 major, 1 major + 3 minor, or 5 minor = definite IE. Major: positive blood culture (typical organism ×2, or persistent positive); positive echocardiography (vegetation, abscess, dehiscence). Echocardiography: TOE (trans-oesophageal - gold standard; detects vegetations, perivalvular extension, abscess better than TTE). Complications: embolism (stroke - vegetation fragments; septic emboli), HF (regurgitation from valve destruction), abscess, mycotic aneurysm, metastatic infection. Mx: prolonged IV antibiotics (minimum 4-6 wk; empiric: amoxicillin + flucloxacillin + gentamicin; adjust for organism; MRSA: vancomycin ± rifampicin); surgery (HF due to valve dysfunction, uncontrolled infection, large vegetation with embolism risk, abscess, prosthetic valve IE).
utd: infective endocarditis antimicrobial therapy native valve

conditions.name: Cor pulmonale
conditions.summary: Right-heart failure from pulmonary hypertension due to lung or pulmonary vascular disease (COPD most common). Sx: dyspnoea, peripheral oedema, ↑JVP, tricuspid regurgitation. Ix (echo): dilated RV, elevated RVSP. Mx: treat underlying lung disease, O2 (COPD), diuretics for oedema; pulmonary vasodilators if PHT group 1.

conditions.name: Obstructive sleep apnoea
conditions.summary: Repeated upper airway obstruction during sleep → apnoeic episodes, oxygen desaturation, arousal. Risk: obesity (BMI>30), male, middle-aged, large neck circumference, retrognathia, tonsillar hypertrophy, alcohol. Sx: snoring, witnessed apnoeas, excessive daytime somnolence (Epworth Sleepiness Scale), morning headache, nocturia, cognitive impairment; affects driving. Associations: HTN (resistant), AF, stroke, depression, GORD. Ix: overnight polysomnography or home sleep study; AHI (apnoea-hypopnoea index) - mild 5-15, moderate 15-30, severe >30/hr. Mx: CPAP (gold standard for moderate-severe; ↓AHI, daytime somnolence, BP); weight loss; mandibular advancement device (mild-moderate); positional therapy; tonsillectomy/adenoidectomy (children); uvulopalatopharyngoplasty (UPPP, bariatric surgery selected).
utd: acute exacerbation of Obstructive sleep apnoea

conditions.name: Pulmonary fibrosis
conditions.summary: Chronic progressive fibrotic ILD of unknown cause. Affects older males, smokers. Sx: slowly progressive exertional dyspnoea, dry cough, finger clubbing, bibasal inspiratory Velcro crackles. Ix (HRCT): honeycombing ± traction bronchiectasis (UIP pattern). PFT: restrictive + ↓DLCO. Mx: antifibrotics (nintedanib/pirfenidone) slow progression; lung transplant for end-stage. No steroids (worsens outcomes).
utd: idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis clinical manifestations diagnosis

conditions.name: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis
conditions.summary: Immune-mediated lung disease (type III/IV hypersensitivity) from inhaled organic antigens. Common causes: thermophilic actinomycetes (farmer's lung - mouldy hay, bird fancier's lung - bird droppings/feathers, humidifier lung, mushroom worker's). Acute: 4-8 hr after exposure; fever, myalgia, cough, dyspnoea, bilateral crackles; resolves 24-72 hr. Subacute: insidious dyspnoea, weight loss. Chronic: progressive fibrosis (resembles UIP/NSIP) - honeycombing, traction bronchiectasis. Ix: BAL (lymphocytosis - CD8>CD4 in acute; CD4>CD8 in chronic); precipitins (IgG - exposure marker, not diagnostic); HRCT (ground-glass, mosaic attenuation, air-trapping); biopsy if uncertain. Mx: antigen avoidance (key); steroids (acute/subacute); antifibrotics if fibrotic progression.

conditions.name: Pulmonary oedema
conditions.summary: Fluid accumulation in pulmonary interstitium and alveoli. Sx: Cardiogenic (↑PCWP from HF): orthopnoea, pink frothy sputum, bilateral crackles, Kerley-B lines. Non-cardiogenic (ARDS, TRALI): ↑permeability without ↑PCWP. Acute cardiogenic Mx: sit upright, O2, IV furosemide, nitrates; BiPAP/CPAP (reduces intubation); IV morphine for dyspnoea.

conditions.name: Mesothelioma
conditions.summary: Malignancy of mesothelial cells (pleura most common, peritoneum, pericardium); almost exclusively caused by asbestos exposure (latency 20-50 yr). Sx: progressive dyspnoea, pleuritic chest pain, weight loss, haemoptysis; signs of pleural effusion; pleural thickening on imaging. CXR/CT: unilateral pleural effusion, pleural thickening (circumferential), pleural masses. Ix: CT-guided biopsy (pleural fluid cytology poor sensitivity); immunostains (calretinin+, WT1+, CK5/6+; CEA-, TTF1−, CD15−). Histological types: epithelioid (best prognosis), biphasic, sarcomatoid (worst). Ix (staging): TNM. Mx: palliative (poor prognosis - median survival 12-18 mo); first-line: nivolumab + ipilimumab (immunotherapy, OS benefit); chemotherapy (pemetrexed + cisplatin - modest benefit); surgical: pleurectomy/decortication (selected early cases). Compensation through industrial injury claims.
utd: malignant pleural mesothelioma clinical features diagnosis

conditions.name: Coeliac disease
conditions.summary: Autoimmune enteropathy triggered by dietary gluten (wheat, barley, rye) in genetically susceptible individuals (HLA-DQ2 [90%] or HLA-DQ8 [5%]); immune-mediated villous atrophy → malabsorption. Sx: GI - diarrhoea, steatorrhoea, weight loss, abdominal bloating/pain, mouth ulcers; extraintestinal - iron-deficiency anaemia (malabsorption - most common presentation in adults), osteoporosis (↓Ca²⁺ + vitamin D), dermatitis herpetiformis (IgA deposits on skin - pruritic vesicles on extensor surfaces - pathognomonic), ataxia (gluten ataxia), peripheral neuropathy; hyposplenia (↑encapsulated organism risk), associated autoimmune diseases (T1DM, thyroid disease). Ix: serology (anti-tTG IgA + total IgA - most sensitive; anti-EMA IgA - most specific; anti-DGP IgG if IgA deficient); duodenal biopsy (Marsh classification: 0-3c; villous atrophy + crypt hyperplasia + intraepithelial lymphocytes - Marsh 3). Mx: strict lifelong gluten-free diet (GFD) - only treatment; dietetic counselling; correct nutritional deficiencies (iron, B12, folate, Ca²⁺, vitamin D); DEXA scan; refractory coeliac (persistent villous atrophy despite GFD): steroids, immunosuppression; refractory type II → risk of enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma (EATL).

conditions.name: Irritable bowel syndrome
conditions.summary: Functional GI disorder. Sx: Rome IV: recurrent abdominal pain ≥1 d/wk for 3 mo, related to defecation or change in stool form/frequency. Subtypes: IBS-C, IBS-D, IBS-M. No structural pathology. Ix: Red flags (blood, weight loss, nocturnal, family history colorectal Ca, age >50) warrant investigation. Mx: diet (low-FODMAP), soluble fibre; IBS-D: loperamide, rifaximin, alosetron; IBS-C: laxatives, linaclotide; antispasmodics, low-dose TCA.
utd: clinical manifestations diagnosis irritable bowel syndrome adults

conditions.name: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease
conditions.summary: Most common liver disease in developed world; spectrum: hepatic steatosis → NASH (steatosis + inflammation + hepatocyte ballooning ± fibrosis) → cirrhosis → HCC. Risk: obesity, T2DM, metabolic syndrome, rapid weight loss, TPN. Sx: usually asymptomatic; fatigue, RUQ discomfort. LFTs: mild ↑ALT/AST (AST:ALT <1 in early; >1 in advanced fibrosis - unlike alcoholic hepatitis). Ix (US): bright liver (echogenic). Non-invasive fibrosis assessment: FIB-4 score, liver stiffness (Fibroscan). Ix: liver biopsy (NAS scoring - gold standard, but reserved for diagnostic uncertainty). Mx: weight loss (7-10% body weight - core); exercise; treat metabolic comorbidities; Vitamin E (non-diabetics with NASH on biopsy); resmetirom (THRβ agonist - first approved medication for NASH with fibrosis 2024); GLP-1 agonists; bariatric surgery.
utd: nonalcoholic fatty liver disease clinical features diagnosis

conditions.name: Non-alcoholic steatohepatitis
conditions.summary: Inflammatory subtype of NAFLD with hepatocyte ballooning, lobular inflammation, and fibrosis. Risk of progression to cirrhosis and HCC. Ix: liver biopsy (NAS score). Associated with obesity, T2DM, dyslipidaemia. Mx: weight loss (cornerstone), bariatric surgery for severe obesity, vitamin E, pioglitazone; antifibrotics in trials.

conditions.name: Primary biliary cholangitis
conditions.summary: Autoimmune destruction of small intrahepatic bile ducts; middle-aged women (10:1 F:M). Associations: Sjögren syndrome, autoimmune thyroid, RA, systemic sclerosis. Sx: pruritus (early), fatigue; later jaundice, xanthelasma, xanthomata. Cholestatic LFTs (↑ALP predominant). AMA (antimitochondrial antibody, M2 subtype) - >95% sensitivity, pathognomonic. ↑IgM. Ix (biopsy): bile duct destruction → granulomas → fibrosis → cirrhosis (staging I-IV, Ludwig/Batts-Ludwig). Ix: ↑ALP + AMA positive (biopsy not required). Mx: UDCA (13-15 mg/kg/day - first-line; ↓LFTs, ↓fibrosis progression, ↑transplant-free survival); obeticholic acid (if inadequate UDCA response); bezafibrate; cholestyramine/rifampicin for pruritus; transplant for decompensated cirrhosis.
utd: clinical manifestations diagnosis primary biliary cholangitis

conditions.name: Primary sclerosing cholangitis
conditions.summary: Progressive fibro-inflammatory cholangiopathy of intra/extrahepatic bile ducts; strong association with IBD (70-80% have UC; PSC-IBD). Cholestatic LFTs (↑ALP > ALT), pruritus, fatigue, jaundice. Ix: MRCP (gold standard - multifocal biliary strictures, 'beads-on-string' appearance); ERCP (therapeutic). pANCA positive (~80%). No effective medical therapy (UDCA does not improve survival). Complications: dominant stricture, cholangitis, cholangiocarcinoma (10-15% lifetime risk - surveillance with CA19-9 + MRCP), PSC-IBD (pancolitis, ↑colorectal cancer risk - annual colonoscopy), liver failure. Mx: liver transplant (definitive; recurs in ~20%); endoscopic dilation of dominant strictures.
utd: primary sclerosing cholangitis clinical manifestations diagnosis

conditions.name: Autoimmune hepatitis
conditions.summary: Autoimmune liver disease; two types: type 1 (ANA + SMA - anti-smooth muscle; adults; 80%); type 2 (anti-LKM1 - anti-liver-kidney microsomal antibody; children/young adults). Sx: fatigue, jaundice, acute hepatitis or incidental ↑LFTs; can present as acute liver failure. ↑ALT/AST (hepatitic pattern), ↑IgG. Ix (biopsy): interface hepatitis, plasma cell infiltrate, rosetting (pathological hallmark). Simplified/Rose criteria for diagnosis (autoantibodies, IgG, histology, viral exclusion). Mx: prednisolone ± azathioprine (induce and maintain remission in 80%); alternative: budesonide + azathioprine (less systemic SE); life-long maintenance often needed; transplant for acute liver failure or treatment failure.

conditions.name: Barrett oesophagus
conditions.summary: Columnar metaplasia of distal oesophagus from chronic GERD; ↑risk oesophageal adenocarcinoma (0.1-0.5%/yr in non-dysplastic). Ix: endoscopy + biopsy (specialised intestinal metaplasia). Screen long-duration GERD patients. Surveillance interval by dysplasia grade. Mx: PPI, endoscopic eradication therapy for dysplasia (RFA, EMR); oesophagectomy for high-grade refractory.

conditions.name: Achalasia
conditions.summary: Failure of lower oesophageal sphincter relaxation + absent peristalsis from loss of Myenteric plexus ganglion cells. Sx: progressive dysphagia (solids + liquids equally), regurgitation, weight loss, chest pain. Barium: bird-beak appearance. Manometry (gold standard): ↑LES pressure, absent peristalsis. Mx: Heller myotomy (most durable), peroral endoscopic myotomy (POEM), or pneumatic dilatation; botulinum toxin for poor surgical candidates.

conditions.name: Clostridioides difficile
conditions.summary: Toxin-producing anaerobe causing antibiotic-associated colitis. Risk: broad-spectrum abx (clindamycin, fluoroquinolones, cephalosporins), hospital exposure, age >65, PPI. Sx: watery diarrhoea ≥3/day, abdominal cramps, fever. Severe: WBC >15, ↑Cr. Ix: GDH + toxin EIA or PCR. Mx: first episode: metronidazole (mild) or fidaxomicin/oral vancomycin (moderate-severe); FMT for recurrent.
utd: clostridioides difficile clinical manifestations diagnosis adults

conditions.name: Ischaemic colitis
conditions.summary: Colon ischaemia from hypoperfusion (watershed areas: splenic flexure, rectosigmoid junction). Causes: atherosclerosis, low-flow states, vasospasm, embolism, post-aortic surgery. Sx: acute LLQ pain, bloody diarrhoea. CT: bowel wall thickening. Mostly self-limiting; Mx: bowel rest, IV fluids, abx; surgery for gangrene/perforation.

conditions.name: Syphilis
conditions.summary: STI caused by Treponema pallidum (spirochaete); resurgent globally. Stages: Primary (9-90 d after exposure): painless indurated ulcer (chancre) at inoculation site (genitalia, rectum, oropharynx) + regional lymphadenopathy; heals spontaneously. Secondary (6-12 wk after primary): systemic dissemination - maculopapular rash involving palms + soles (classic), condylomata lata, alopecia, hepatitis, meningitis, uveitis; Latent: asymptomatic (serology positive). Tertiary (10-30 yr): gummas (destructive granulomata); cardiovascular syphilis (aortitis - aortic root dilatation, AR, coronary ostial stenosis - saccular aneurysm of ascending aorta); neurosyphilis (meningovascular, general paresis, tabes dorsalis [posterior column degeneration - wide-based gait, lancinating pains, loss of vibration/proprioception, Argyll Robertson pupils - accommodate but not react to light, Charcot joints]). Congenital: SNHL, Hutchinson teeth, interstitial keratitis. Ix: serology - RPR/VDRL (non-treponemal, titres follow activity); TPHA/EIA (treponemal, qualitative - remain positive for life); dark field microscopy. Mx: benzathine penicillin G IM (primary/secondary/early latent: 2.4 MU single dose); late latent/tertiary: 3 doses weekly × 3; neurosyphilis: IV penicillin G 14 d. Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction (3-6 hr post first treatment - fever, rigors, hypotension - counsel patients; premedicate with paracetamol).

conditions.name: Gonorrhoea
conditions.summary: STI caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae (diplococci); second most common bacterial STI. Increasingly antimicrobial-resistant (multi-drug resistant gonorrhoea - major public health concern). Sx (males): urethral discharge (purulent), dysuria (more symptomatic than chlamydia). Sx (females): often asymptomatic or cervicitis (discharge, intermenstrual bleeding), ascending → PID; neonatal conjunctivitis (ophthalmia neonatorum - from vertical transmission; requires prophylaxis in high-prevalence settings). Disseminated gonococcal infection (DGI): 0.5-3% - bacteraemia → septic arthritis (purulent, typically mono/oligoarthritis), dermatitis (pustular lesions on extremities), tenosynovitis; endocarditis (rare). Ix: NAAT (first-catch urine/HVS/rectal/pharyngeal swab); culture + sensitivity (essential for antibiotic resistance testing when positive). Mx: ceftriaxone 1 g IM single dose (+ azithromycin if sensitivities unknown - now as single dose ceftriaxone per 2022 UK guidelines); dual therapy (ceftriaxone + doxycycline for concurrent chlamydia); partner notification; test of cure (TOC) at 2 wk if pharyngeal involvement or resistance concern.

conditions.name: Chlamydia
conditions.summary: Most common bacterial STI in UK/developed world; Chlamydia trachomatis serovars D-K. Often asymptomatic (70% women, 50% men). Sx (females): abnormal vaginal discharge, dysuria, intermenstrual/post-coital bleeding, pelvic pain (ascending → PID); Sx (males): urethral discharge, dysuria, epididymo-orchitis; Reactive arthritis (Reiter - urethritis + arthritis + conjunctivitis). Ix: NAAT (nucleic acid amplification test) - first-catch urine or vulvovaginal swab (self-taken); sensitivity >95%. Ocular chlamydia (trachoma - serovars A-C): leading cause of infectious blindness worldwide. Lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV - serovars L1-L3): tropical; genital ulcer → inguinal lymphadenopathy (buboes) → proctocolitis (MSM). Mx: doxycycline 100 mg BD × 7 d (first-line; cure rate 97%); azithromycin 1 g single dose (lower efficacy - use for pregnancy, intolerance); partner notification/treatment; test of cure (not routine, except pregnancy/LGV/rectal chlamydia); screen in ≤25 yr sexually active annually (NCSP - National Chlamydia Screening Programme).

conditions.name: COVID-19
conditions.summary: Coronavirus disease caused by SARS-CoV-2. Spectrum: asymptomatic to critical illness. Sx: fever, cough, anosmia, dyspnoea; severe: ARDS, cytokine storm, ↑D-dimer/ferritin, myocarditis. Ix: PCR/antigen. Mx (severe): dexamethasone (O2-dependent), remdesivir, IL-6 inhibitor, baricitinib; anticoagulation for VTE. Vaccination prevents severe disease. Long COVID: persistent symptoms >4 wk post-acute illness.

conditions.name: Septicaemia
conditions.summary: Presence of bacteria in blood. Bacteraemia: transient (procedures) or continuous (endovascular infection). Septicaemia (older term): bacteraemia causing clinical illness. Mx: Staphylococcus aureus bacteraemia requires 2-wk minimum IV antibiotics (endocarditis must be excluded by TOE); repeat blood cultures at 48–72 h to confirm clearance.

conditions.name: Guillain-Barré syndrome
conditions.summary: Acute immune-mediated polyneuropathy; often post-infectious (Campylobacter jejuni, CMV, EBV, COVID-19, influenza). Ascending flaccid paralysis (starts distal limbs), areflexia, ↓vibration/proprioception; pain (back/radicular - common); autonomic dysfunction (BP/HR instability, ileus, urinary retention). Peak weakness 4 wk. Respiratory failure in 25% → ICU. Miller Fisher variant: ophthalmoplegia + ataxia + areflexia (GQ1b IgG antibody). Ix: CSF (albuminocytological dissociation - ↑protein, normal WBC); NCS/EMG (demyelination - AIDP; axonal AMAN/AMSAN). Mx: IVIG (0.4 g/kg/d × 5 d) or plasma exchange (both equivalent, combination not better); corticosteroids not effective; supportive - respiratory monitoring, DVT prophylaxis, pain (gabapentin), early physio. Prognosis: 80% walk independently by 6 months; 5-10% severe disability.

conditions.name: Myasthenia gravis
conditions.summary: Autoimmune NMJ disorder; AChR antibodies (85%) or anti-MuSK (10%). Thymic abnormality: thymoma (10-15%), thymic hyperplasia. Sx: fatigable weakness (worse with use, improves with rest) - ptosis, diplopia (bulbar muscles early), dysarthria, dysphagia; proximal limbs, respiratory muscles. Myasthenic crisis: respiratory failure (triggered by infection, surgery, certain drugs). Ix: AChR/MuSK antibodies; Tensilon (edrophonium) test (now rarely used); ice pack test (ptosis); NCS: repetitive nerve stimulation - decremental response; single-fibre EMG (most sensitive). Mx: symptomatic - pyridostigmine (anticholinesterase); immunosuppression - prednisolone + azathioprine; thymectomy (improves outcomes even without thymoma in AChR+ generalised MG); IVIG or plasma exchange (acute exacerbation/myasthenic crisis); eculizumab, efgartigimod (newer targeted therapies).

conditions.name: Peripheral neuropathy
conditions.summary: Damage to peripheral nerves. Patterns: polyneuropathy (distal 'glove-stocking'), mononeuropathy, mononeuritis multiplex, radiculopathy. Causes: diabetes (most common), alcohol, B12 deficiency, uraemia, hypothyroidism, amyloid, paraneoplastic, hereditary (CMT). Ix: EMG/NCS. Mx: treat underlying cause; neuropathic pain: duloxetine, pregabalin, amitriptyline.

conditions.name: Carpal tunnel syndrome
conditions.summary: Compression of median nerve at wrist (carpal tunnel); most common peripheral entrapment neuropathy. Risk: female, pregnancy (2nd/3rd trimester), hypothyroidism, RA, diabetes, acromegaly, obesity, repetitive wrist use, wrist fractures (Colles), CRPS, amyloidosis. Sx: pain + tingling + numbness in lateral 3.5 digits (thumb, index, middle, lateral ring - median distribution); worse at night/waking, shaking relieves; thenar wasting (severe/chronic). Sx: Tinel sign (tapping wrist → tingling), Phalen sign (wrist flexion × 60 sec → sx); thenar atrophy; ↓2-point discrimination. Nerve conduction studies (NCS): ↓sensory and motor conduction velocity in median nerve (gold standard). Mx: conservative (mild/moderate): splint (night-time neutral position), corticosteroid injection (wrist); surgical: carpal tunnel decompression (open or endoscopic; highly effective, definitive - division of flexor retinaculum; indicated when symptoms severe, failed conservative, thenar wasting).
utd: acute treatment of Carpal tunnel syndrome
long-term management of Carpal tunnel syndrome

conditions.name: Normal pressure hydrocephalus
conditions.summary: Communicating hydrocephalus with normal or mildly elevated CSF pressure; cause of reversible dementia in elderly. Classic triad (Hakim's triad): gait apraxia (magnetic gait, 'walking on ice'), cognitive impairment (frontal predominant - executive dysfunction, apathy), urinary incontinence (often late). CT/Ix (MRI): ventriculomegaly disproportionate to cortical atrophy; corpus callosum thinning. CSF drainage test (large volume LP or extended lumbar drain): improvement in gait supports diagnosis. Ix: Evans index >0.3 + clinical triad. Mx: ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunt - most effective for gait; cognitive/bladder improve less reliably.
utd: acute treatment of Normal pressure hydrocephalus
long-term management of Normal pressure hydrocephalus

conditions.name: Subdural haematoma
conditions.summary: Collection of blood between dura and arachnoid from torn bridging veins. Acute SDH (<72 h): high-velocity trauma, usually young - biconvex on CT ONLY if arterial (epidural); subdural is crescent-shaped, crosses suture lines, concave inner border. Chronic SDH (>3 weeks): elderly, minor trauma (often forgotten), anticoagulants, alcohol - slow re-bleeding of initial haematoma → expanding hygroma. Sx: Acute - depressed consciousness, focal deficit, ipsilateral dilated pupil (uncal herniation), contralateral hemiplegia. Chronic - gradually worsening headache, cognitive decline, fluctuating consciousness, subtle focal signs. Ix: CT head (acute: hyperdense crescent; subacute: isodense - easily missed; chronic: hypodense). Mx: Acute large SDH (>10 mm, >5 mm midline shift, or deteriorating) - urgent craniotomy; Chronic - burr-hole drainage (recurrence common - ≤30%); dexamethasone (chronic - ↓recurrence); tranexamic acid in anticoagulated patients.

conditions.name: Extradural haematoma
conditions.summary: Arterial bleed between skull and dura (usually middle meningeal artery from temporal bone fracture). Classic presentation: lucid interval (brief LOC then recovery then rapid deterioration) - NOT always present (<30%). CT: biconvex (lenticular) hyperdense haematoma that does NOT cross suture lines (dura attached at sutures - distinguishes from SDH). Sx: ipsilateral fixed dilated pupil (CN III compression from uncal herniation), contralateral hemiplegia (Kernohan's notch - false localising sign). Associated: pterion fracture (thinnest skull - middle meningeal artery runs here). Mx: urgent surgical evacuation (craniotomy) - most time-critical haemorrhage (haematoma expanding at arterial pressure); excellent prognosis if treated before herniation. Temporal bone fracture + scalp haematoma over temporal/pterional region → high suspicion.

conditions.name: Vascular dementia
conditions.summary: Second most common dementia after Alzheimer. Stepwise or sudden cognitive decline after stroke(s) or from chronic cerebrovascular disease. Executive dysfunction often prominent early. Ix: lacunar infarcts, white-matter changes (Fazekas scale). Mx: No disease-specific Mx; secondary prevention: antiplatelet/anticoagulation, BP control, statin, glycaemic control.

conditions.name: Lewy body dementia
conditions.summary: Second most common degenerative dementia after AD; alpha-synuclein Lewy bodies in neocortex, limbic system. Core features: fluctuating cognition (attention/alertness), recurrent vivid visual hallucinations (well-formed, often people/animals), REM sleep behaviour disorder (precedes dementia), parkinsonism (spontaneous, often mild). Supportive: severe neuroleptic sensitivity (use of antipsychotics → acute worsening - AVOID conventional antipsychotics), autonomic dysfunction, repeated falls. DaTscan: reduced striatal dopamine transporter (differentiates from AD). Ix: ≥2 core features or 1 core + DaTscan abnormal. Mx: rivastigmine (ChEI) for cognitive; levodopa (caution) for motor; melatonin for RBD; avoid anticholinergics.
utd: acute treatment of Lewy body dementia
long-term management of Lewy body dementia

conditions.name: Essential tremor
conditions.summary: Most common movement disorder; bilateral postural/kinetic upper-limb tremor (handwriting, pouring), can involve head/voice. Family history in 50-70%. Worse with caffeine/anxiety, temporarily improved by alcohol. Mx: β-blocker (propranolol) or primidone 1st-line; topiramate, gabapentin; thalamotomy/focused ultrasound for severe refractory.

conditions.name: Huntington disease
conditions.summary: Autosomal dominant; CAG trinucleotide repeat expansion in HTT gene (huntingtin) on chromosome 4p; >36 repeats → disease (>40 fully penetrant); anticipation (↑repeats with each generation - paternal transmission). Mean age onset: 30-50 yr; inverse correlation with repeat length. Sx: triad - movement disorder (chorea - involuntary jerky, flowing movements; dystonia, rigidity; bradykinesia - late), cognitive decline (executive dysfunction, frontal dementia → dementia), psychiatric (depression most common, anxiety, OCD, psychosis, irritability, apathy, suicide risk × 5). Gait disturbance, weight loss (↑energy expenditure from chorea). HD-like conditions: HDL1 (PRNP - prion protein), HDL2 (JPH3), DRPLA, SCA17, FXTAS, neuroferritinopathy. Ix: genetic testing (CAG repeat count; predictive testing requires multidisciplinary counselling before result); Ix (MRI): caudate atrophy ('box-car' ventricles). Mx: no disease-modifying therapy (huntingtin-lowering - tominersen, antisense oligonucleotide, trial results mixed); chorea: tetrabenazine/deutetrabenazine (VMAT2 inhibitor), olanzapine; depression: SSRIs; irritability: atypical antipsychotics; MDT/palliative care; median survival 15-20 yr from onset.

conditions.name: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo
conditions.summary: Most common cause of vertigo; free-floating otoconia (canaliths) in semicircular canal. Brief intense vertigo with positional change (lying down, rolling over). Ix: Dix-Hallpike (upbeat-torsional nystagmus). Mx: canalith repositioning manoeuvre (Epley) - highly effective, often single treatment. May recur. Avoid labyrinthine sedatives (vestibular suppressants). Ddx: vestibular neuritis (prolonged vertigo, no hearing loss, recent viral illness), Ménière disease (episodic vertigo + tinnitus + hearing loss), posterior circulation stroke (direction-changing nystagmus, cerebellar signs - HINTS exam), acute labyrinthitis (hearing loss present), central vertigo (multiple sclerosis, tumour).
utd: diagnosis of Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo
acute treatment of Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo
long-term management of Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo

conditions.name: Osteoporosis
conditions.summary: ↓Bone mineral density (T-score ≤ −2.5 on DEXA); ↑fracture risk. Risk factors: age, female, oestrogen deficiency, steroid use, alcohol, smoking, ↓calcium/vitamin D, hypogonadism, RA. FRAX tool estimates 10-yr fracture probability. Mx: calcium + vitamin D; bisphosphonate (alendronate, risedronate) 1st-line; denosumab, teriparatide for severe/refractory; HRT in peri-menopausal women.

conditions.name: Osteomyelitis
conditions.summary: Infection of bone. Haematogenous: mainly children (metaphysis - rich blood supply, turbulent flow, sluggish, ideal for bacterial seeding); also vertebral osteomyelitis (Pott's disease if TB; most common adult form). Direct inoculation/contiguous spread: trauma, surgery, orthopaedic implants, chronic wounds (diabetic foot - Staphylococcus aureus most common in all forms; MRSA increasingly). Sx: bone pain, fever, swelling, erythema (acute); chronic: sinus tract, pathological fracture, amyloidosis (long-standing). Vertebral OM: back pain, fever, ↑CRP/ESR, blood cultures positive in 60%. Ix: MRI (modality of choice for soft tissue extent + early infection); bone biopsy + culture (before antibiotics if possible - essential for tailored therapy); bone scan (99mTc); PET-CT (chronic/PJI); ↑CRP, ↑ESR, ↑WBC. Mx: antibiotics (IV then oral guided by culture/sensitivities × 4-6 wk minimum; short-course OVIVA trial for selected - oral as effective as IV); surgical debridement (chronic/necrotic bone - sequestrectomy, chronic OM); implant removal (infected); hyperbaric oxygen (adjunct chronic).

conditions.name: Septic arthritis
conditions.summary: Medical emergency - bacterial infection of synovial joint → rapid cartilage destruction. Most common: S. aureus (all ages); Streptococcus (haematogenous); N. gonorrhoeae (young sexually active adults - most common cause in <40 yr); Gram-negative bacilli (elderly, immunocompromised, IVDU, neonates). Risk: prosthetic joint (most common presentation in elderly), IVDU, immunosuppression, rheumatoid arthritis, DM, skin infection, previous joint surgery. Haematogenous most common; direct inoculation (trauma, injection); adjacent osteomyelitis. Sx: hot, swollen, acutely painful joint (worst joint pain of patient's life), fever, ↓ROM, inability to weight-bear; joint effusion. Prosthetic joint infection (PJI): pain ± fever; acute (<3 months) vs delayed (3-24 months) vs late (>24 months). Ix: joint aspiration (urgent - WBC >50,000 cells/mm³ + >90% PMN strongly suggests; Gram stain + culture; glucose + lactate); blood cultures ×3; inflammatory markers. Mx: emergency IV antibiotics (empiric: flucloxacillin ± gentamicin; MRSA suspected: vancomycin; gonococcal: ceftriaxone) + daily joint aspiration or surgical washout (arthroscopic lavage; open washout for hip/prosthetic joint infections); DAIR (debridement antibiotics implant retention - early PJI).

conditions.name: Pseudogout
conditions.summary: Calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate crystal deposition in joints. Episodic acute arthritis (knees, wrists most common). Positive birefringent rhomboid crystals on joint fluid. Chondrocalcinosis on X-ray. Associated with hyperparathyroidism, haemochromatosis, hypomagnesaemia, hypothyroidism. Mx (acute): NSAIDs, colchicine, intra-articular steroids. Prophylaxis: colchicine.

conditions.name: Reactive arthritis
conditions.summary: Aseptic arthritis triggered by remote infection (GI: Salmonella, Campylobacter, Yersinia, Shigella; GU: Chlamydia trachomatis - most common STI-associated). HLA-B27 associated (up to 80%). Classic triad (Reiter's) - 'Can't see, can't pee, can't climb a tree': urethritis/cervicitis, conjunctivitis/anterior uveitis, arthritis (asymmetric, lower limb oligoarthritis). Additional: keratoderma blenorrhagica (psoriasiform rash - hands/soles), circinate balanitis, mouth ulcers, nail changes, sacroiliitis. Onset 1-6 wk post-infection. Ix: clinical + reactive serology; joint aspirate (exclude septic arthritis - sterile in reactive). Mx: NSAIDs (first-line); physiotherapy; sulphasalazine (chronic); doxycycline/azithromycin for chlamydial trigger; steroids (intra-articular).

conditions.name: Bursitis
conditions.summary: Inflammation of bursa (fluid-filled sac adjacent to joint). Prepatellar (housemaid's knee), olecranon (student's elbow), trochanteric (lateral hip pain), subdeltoid, retrocalcaneal. Causes: repetitive trauma, gout, septic (S. aureus). Ix: clinical; aspiration if septic bursitis suspected. Mx: rest, NSAIDs; aspiration ± steroid injection; IV antibiotics for septic bursitis.

conditions.name: Rhabdomyolysis
conditions.summary: Breakdown of skeletal muscle → release of myoglobin (nephrotoxic), CK, K⁺, phosphate. Causes: trauma/crush injury, prolonged immobility, seizures, severe exertion (exertional rhabdomyolysis - marathon running, military training), drugs (statins, alcohol, cocaine, amphetamines, ecstasy), heat stroke, hypothermia, metabolic (hypokalaemia, hyponatraemia, hypophosphataemia), toxins (snakebite), infections, NMS/malignant hyperthermia. Sx: myalgia, weakness, 'cola'-coloured urine (myoglobinuria - positive dipstick for blood but no RBCs on microscopy). ↑CK (>5× ULN, often >10,000 IU/L in severe), ↑myoglobin, ↑K⁺, ↑PO₄, ↑urate, ↑creatinine (AKI). Mx: aggressive IV fluid resuscitation (0.9% NaCl or LR - 1-2 L/hr; maintain UO >0.5 mL/kg/hr, target 200-300 mL/hr until myoglobin cleared); correct electrolytes; urine alkalinisation (bicarbonate - controversial); treat AKI; avoid nephrotoxins; dialysis if refractory AKI.

conditions.name: Marfan syndrome
conditions.summary: Autosomal dominant connective tissue disorder; FBN1 gene mutation (fibrillin-1 → ↓microfibrils → ↑TGF-β signalling → tissue fragility). Sx: cardiovascular (most serious) - aortic root dilation/dissection (risk of type A dissection - leading cause of death), mitral valve prolapse + MR, aortic regurgitation; skeletal - tall stature, arm span > height (>1.05:1), pectus excavatum/carinatum, scoliosis, pes planus, arachnodactyly (Steinberg thumb sign, Walker sign), dolichocephaly, high-arched palate, joint hypermobility; ocular - ectopia lentis (superotemporal lens dislocation - pathognomonic), myopia, retinal detachment, glaucoma. Ghent nosology (2010 revised criteria): aortic Z-score ≥2 + ectopia lentis = Marfan regardless of FBN1 status; or combination of systemic score + FBN1. Ix: echocardiography (aortic root dimension + Z-score); slit-lamp; FBN1 sequencing. Mx: annual echocardiography; beta-blockers (↓aortic dilation rate); losartan (ARB - ↓TGF-β, no proven superiority over beta-blocker); aortic root replacement (prophylactic: aortic diameter ≥5.0 cm, or rapid growth >0.5 cm/yr, family history dissection); avoid contact sports, competitive sport, extremes of exertion.

conditions.name: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
conditions.summary: Group of connective tissue disorders (CTDs); collagen synthesis/processing defects. 13 subtypes (2017 EDS Classification). Classic EDS (cEDS): COL5A1/2 - skin hyperextensibility, fragility, widened atrophic scars, joint hypermobility. Vascular EDS (vEDS): COL3A1 - catastrophic vascular/organ rupture (aorta, mesenteric, uterine), high mortality, thin translucent skin, minimal joint hypermobility; most dangerous. kyphoscoliotic EDS (kEDS): PLOD1/FKBP14 - scoliosis, muscle hypotonia. Hypermobile EDS (hEDS - most common ~80%, no identified gene - diagnosis requires clinical criteria): generalised joint hypermobility (Beighton score ≥5), systemic features (skin, pelvic floor), musculoskeletal complications (pain, dislocations, early OA). Marfanoid habitus ± overlapping. Associations: POTS/dysautonomia (very common in hEDS), mast cell activation syndrome (MCAS), chronic pain, fatigue (ME/CFS overlap). Ix: genetic testing (except hEDS - no known gene); Beighton score; clinical criteria. Mx: physiotherapy (joint stabilisation, muscle strengthening - cornerstone); pain management; avoid contact sports/extreme ROM; vEDS: celiprolol (↓arterial rupture risk); surveillance imaging (vEDS - CT/MRI vessels annually).

conditions.name: Turner syndrome
conditions.summary: 45,X karyotype (or mosaic). Short stature, primary amenorrhoea, streak gonads (infertility), webbed neck, wide-spaced nipples, cubitus valgus, coarctation of aorta, horseshoe kidney. ↑FSH/LH, ↓oestrogen. Mx: GH therapy for height; oestrogen replacement at 11-12 y (breast development + bone health); annual cardiac echo.

conditions.name: Klinefelter syndrome
conditions.summary: Most common sex chromosome aneuploidy (1 in 600-700 males); 47,XXY (80%) or mosaic 46,XY/47,XXY. Hypogonadism due to impaired Leydig/Sertoli cell function → ↓testosterone, ↑LH/FSH (hypergonadotrophic hypogonadism). Sx: tall stature (long legs), small firm testes (testicular atrophy - fibrosis), azoospermia (infertile - oligospermia in mosaic), ↓testosterone → poor secondary sexual characteristics (sparse facial/body hair, gynaecomastia, small phallus), ↑risk of autoimmune disease, metabolic syndrome, breast cancer (20× ↑risk vs males), language/learning difficulties (mild executive dysfunction, reading difficulty, shyness, low self-esteem). Ix: karyotype. Mx: testosterone replacement therapy (puberty → lifelong; ↑muscle mass, body hair, bone density, libido; ↑energy; ↓metabolic risks); fertility: TESE (testicular sperm extraction) + ICSI (50% success in obtaining sperm); treat gynaecomastia (mastectomy if severe); psychological support.

conditions.name: Down syndrome
conditions.summary: Most common chromosomal disorder (trisomy 21 in 95%). Sx: intellectual disability, flat facies, epicanthal folds, single palmar crease, atlantoaxial instability, congenital heart defects (AVSD most common), Hirschsprung, duodenal atresia, hypothyroidism, ↑risk acute leukaemia (ALL/AML), early-onset Alzheimer. Ix: Annual thyroid function; routine cardiac evaluation; occupational screening.

conditions.name: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia
conditions.summary: Group of autosomal recessive disorders of adrenal steroidogenesis; 21-hydroxylase deficiency (CYP21A2, 95%). Blocked cortisol synthesis → ↑ACTH → adrenal hyperplasia + shunting to androgen pathway. Classic CAH: salt-wasting (most severe - no aldosterone: neonatal adrenal crisis, hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia) or simple virilising (virilisation of female genitalia - ambiguous genitalia, ↑androgens). Non-classic (late-onset): milder androgen excess - hirsutism, oligomenorrhoea, acne, infertility (diagnosed later). Ix: ↑17-OHP (17-hydroxyprogesterone) - peak marker; Synacthen test (stimulated 17-OHP); genetic testing. Mx: glucocorticoid replacement (hydrocortisone in children - prevents over-treatment-related growth suppression; dexamethasone/prednisolone adults); mineralocorticoid (fludrocortisone) in salt-wasting; salt supplements in infancy; surgery for virilised females; prenatal Mx controversial.

conditions.name: Amyloidosis
conditions.summary: Extracellular deposition of misfolded amyloid fibrils in tissues. AL (light-chain; plasma cell dyscrasia): cardiac, renal, peripheral neuropathy, macroglossia. AA (secondary to chronic inflammation): renal most common. ATTR (transthyretin; wild-type or hereditary): cardiac amyloidosis (restrictive CMP), neuropathy. Ix: Congo red stain (apple-green birefringence). Mx: AL: anti-myeloma therapy; ATTR: tafamidis (cardiac); patisiran/inotersen (neuropathy).

conditions.name: Haemochromatosis
conditions.summary: Autosomal recessive; HFE gene (C282Y/H63D); ↑iron absorption → iron deposition in liver, pancreas, heart, joints, pituitary, skin. Predominantly males (>40 yr - menstrual loss protects females). Sx: fatigue, arthralgia (2nd/3rd MCP joints - pseudo-gout, chondrocalcinosis), hepatomegaly → cirrhosis, diabetes ('bronze diabetes'), skin pigmentation ('bronzing'), cardiomyopathy (DCM/restrictive), hypogonadism (testicular atrophy, amenorrhoea). ↑serum ferritin, ↑transferrin saturation (>45% - sensitive screening marker). Ix: genetic testing (HFE genotype); liver biopsy (hepatic iron index >1.9, Perl's stain) if diagnosis uncertain or staging fibrosis. Mx: venesection (weekly phlebotomy, each 500 mL removes ~250 mg iron; target ferritin 50-100 μg/L); desferrioxamine (chelation - when venesection not tolerated); avoid alcohol, vitamin C supplements.

conditions.name: Wilson disease
conditions.summary: Autosomal recessive; ATP7B mutation; defective copper transport → copper accumulation in liver, brain, cornea, kidney, heart. Presents 5-35 yr. Hepatic: hepatitis, cirrhosis, acute liver failure (Coombs-negative haemolytic anaemia + high bilirubin). Neurological: tremor, dysarthria, dysphagia, Parkinsonism-like, chorea, psychiatric symptoms. Ophthalmological: Kayser-Fleischer rings (copper in Descemet membrane - visible with slit lamp; present in >95% with neurological disease; absent in pure hepatic disease in ~50%). Ix: ↓serum caeruloplasmin (<0.2 g/L - not sensitive alone), ↑24-hr urinary copper (>0.6 μmol/24 hr; >1.6 μmol/24 hr post D-penicillamine challenge), liver copper (gold standard >250 μg/g dry weight); ATP7B sequencing. KF rings on slit lamp. Mx: chelation (D-penicillamine, trientine); zinc (maintenance - ↓GI copper absorption); liver transplant for liver failure.

conditions.name: Raynaud phenomenon
conditions.summary: Vasospasm of digital arteries/arterioles in response to cold/emotional stress → triphasic colour change: white (pallor - vasospasm), blue (cyanosis - deoxygenation), red (erythema - reperfusion). Primary (Raynaud disease): young women, bilateral, no underlying disease, normal nailfold capillaroscopy, no tissue damage. Secondary: connective tissue disease (systemic sclerosis, SLE, MCTD, polymyositis - screen for these), occupational (vibrating tools), drugs (beta-blockers, ergotamine, bleomycin), atherosclerosis, cryoglobulinaemia, thoracic outlet syndrome. Ix: history + nailfold capillaroscopy (abnormal capillaries → secondary); ANA; RF; anti-Scl-70/ACA. Mx: lifestyle (avoid cold, gloves, hand warmers); calcium channel blockers (nifedipine - first-line medical); GTN/prostaglandins (PGI2 - iloprost IV) for ischaemia; digital sympathectomy; avoid beta-blockers.

conditions.name: Scleroderma
conditions.summary: Autoimmune fibrosis + vasculopathy. Limited cutaneous (lcSSc/CREST: skin confined to distal extremities + face, Anti-centromere Ab): Calcinosis, Raynaud, oEsophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia; late PAH risk. Diffuse (dcSSc; anti-Scl-70/anti-topoisomerase I Ab): rapid skin fibrosis, ILD, renal crisis. Mx: No disease-modifying Mx; organ-based: CCB (Raynaud), PPI (reflux), ACE-i (renal crisis), PAH Mx, cyclophosphamide/mycophenolate (ILD).

conditions.name: Sjögren syndrome
conditions.summary: Autoimmune exocrinopathy. Keratoconjunctivitis sicca (dry eyes), xerostomia (dry mouth). 1° or 2° (with RA, SLE). ↑↑risk non-Hodgkin lymphoma (especially MALT). Anti-Ro (SSA) and anti-La (SSB). Ix: Schirmer test, minor salivary gland biopsy (focal lymphocytic sialadenitis). Extraglandular: arthritis, interstitial nephritis, peripheral neuropathy. Mx: ocular lubricants, pilocarpine; NSAIDs/hydroxychloroquine for systemic Sx.

conditions.name: Dermatomyositis
conditions.summary: Idiopathic inflammatory myopathy + characteristic skin changes; humoral immune-mediated (B-cell, CD4+, complement). Skin: heliotrope rash (periorbital violet discolouration), Gottron papules (violaceous papules over MCP/IP joints - pathognomonic), Gottron sign (erythema over extensor surfaces, elbows, knees), shawl sign (upper back), V-sign (upper chest), periungual erythema/dilated nailfold capillaries, calcinosis (in JDM). Sx: proximal weakness + skin changes; dysphagia, ILD. Amyopathic DM: skin changes without muscle weakness. Malignancy (up to 30%): screen especially ovarian, lung, GI, lymphoma. MSA: anti-Mi-2 (classic DM, good prognosis), anti-MDA5 (amyopathic + rapidly progressive ILD - poor prognosis), anti-NXP2 (calcinosis, malignancy), anti-TIF1γ (malignancy-associated). Ix: same as PM; biopsy shows perifascicular atrophy (specific). Mx: prednisolone + steroid-sparing; IVIG; rituximab; hydroxychloroquine (skin); sun protection; treat malignancy.

conditions.name: Polymyositis
conditions.summary: Idiopathic inflammatory myopathy (IIM); T-cell-mediated (CD8+ cytotoxic) endomysial inflammation. Sx: insidious proximal muscle weakness (shoulder/hip girdle); dysphagia (oesophageal involvement); minimal skin findings (unlike dermatomyositis). Complications: ILD (anti-Jo-1 antibody - anti-synthetase syndrome: fever, mechanic's hands, Raynaud, arthritis, ILD), cardiac (conduction abnormalities, cardiomyopathy), malignancy (less than DM). Ix: ↑CK (often markedly elevated); EMG (myopathic - short duration, low amplitude, polyphasic); MRI muscle (oedema - guides biopsy); biopsy (endomysial inflammation, CD8+ cells, necrosis - not perifascicular atrophy). Myositis-specific antibodies (MSA): anti-Jo-1, anti-Mi-2, anti-MDA5, anti-NXP2, anti-SAE, anti-SRP (IMNM). Mx: prednisolone ± steroid-sparing (methotrexate, azathioprine, mycophenolate); IVIG for severe/refractory; rituximab.

conditions.name: Polycythaemia vera
conditions.summary: Myeloproliferative neoplasm (MPN); JAK2 V617F mutation (>97%). Clonal ↑RBC mass + variable ↑WBC and platelets. Sx: ruddy complexion (plethora), headache, dizziness, visual disturbance, pruritus after bath/shower (aquagenic - ↑histamine), erythromelalgia (burning pain + erythema of extremities - esp. hands/feet), ↑risk thrombosis (Budd-Chiari, portal vein, stroke - characteristic sites), splenomegaly. ↑Hct, ↑Hb, ↑RBC, ↑WBC, ↑platelets; ↓EPO; JAK2 positive. Ix: WHO 2022 criteria (↑Hb/Hct + BM biopsy + JAK2 + ↓EPO). Mx: venesection (target Hct <0.45 - ↓thrombosis risk); aspirin 75 mg (all patients); cytoreduction (hydroxycarbamide - high-risk, elderly; ruxolitinib - JAK inhibitor for hydroxycarbamide-resistant/intolerant, or PV with pruritus); transformation: MF, blast phase AML (~10% at 20 yr).

conditions.name: Essential thrombocythaemia
conditions.summary: Myeloproliferative neoplasm; clonal ↑platelets. Driver mutations: JAK2 V617F (60%), CALR (25%), MPL (5%), triple-negative (10%). Sx: often asymptomatic (incidental finding); thrombosis (arterial: TIA/stroke, MI; venous: DVT, PE, hepatic/portal vein) or bleeding (paradoxically, at very high platelets >1000-1500 × 10⁹/L - acquired vWF deficiency); erythromelalgia; microvascular symptoms (headache, visual changes, paraesthesia).
