Platelets >450 × 10⁹/L + bone marrow biopsy + exclusion of reactive causes + driver mutation. Risk stratification (IPSET-thrombosis): low, intermediate, high. Mx: aspirin 75 mg (most patients); cytoreduction (hydroxycarbamide - high-risk; anagrelide - second-line; interferon-alpha - young, in pregnancy); ruxolitinib (refractory/intolerant).

conditions.name: Aplastic anaemia
conditions.summary: Pancytopenia with hypocellular bone marrow; destruction/suppression of haematopoietic stem cells. Causes: idiopathic (most - immune-mediated T-cell destruction of HSCs); drugs (chloramphenicol, sulfonamides, carbamazepine, NSAIDs), viral (EBV, parvovirus, hepatitis - hepatitis-associated aplastic anaemia), PNH (5-10% aplastic → PNH), Fanconi anaemia (AR, constitutional - chromosome fragility). Sx: anaemia, thrombocytopenia (petechiae, bleeding), neutropenia (infections). Severe aplastic anaemia (SAA): neutrophils <0.5, platelets <20, reticulocytes <20 × 10⁹/L; BM cellularity <25%. Ix: BM biopsy. Mx: young patient (<40 yr) with sibling donor → HSCT (curative); no donor or older: immunosuppression (anti-thymocyte globulin + ciclosporin + eltrombopag); supportive transfusions; G-CSF; treat PNH clone if present; avoid causative drugs.

conditions.name: Hereditary spherocytosis
conditions.summary: Most common inherited haemolytic anaemia in Northern Europeans; autosomal dominant (75%) or recessive. Mutations: ankyrin (most common, AD), band 3, spectrin, protein 4.2 (AR). Red cell membrane instability → spherocytes → splenic trapping/destruction (extravascular haemolysis). Sx: anaemia (variable), jaundice, splenomegaly; aplastic crises (parvovirus B19 - sudden severe anaemia); gallstones (pigmented - bilirubin gallstones, from chronic haemolysis). FBC: mild anaemia, ↑MCHC (>360 g/L), ↑RDW; blood film: spherocytes (no central pallor); ↑reticulocytes; ↑bilirubin (indirect), ↓haptoglobin; DAT (Coombs) negative (distinguishes from AIHA). EMA binding test (eosin-5'-maleimide) or osmotic fragility test; genetic confirmation. Mx: folate supplementation; transfusion (aplastic crisis, severe); splenectomy (severe disease - significantly reduces haemolysis; delayed until age 5-6+ to preserve immune function; pre-splenectomy vaccines: pneumococcal + meningococcal + Hib; lifelong penicillin V after splenectomy); gallstones: cholecystectomy.

conditions.name: G6PD deficiency
conditions.summary: X-linked recessive; G6PD mutation → ↓NADPH → ↓glutathione → oxidative haemolysis. Most common enzyme deficiency; prevalent in Africa, Mediterranean, SE Asia (malaria protection). Sx: usually asymptomatic; haemolytic anaemia precipitated by: oxidant drugs (primaquine, dapsone, rasburicase), infections (most common trigger), fava beans (G6PD Mediterranean), neonatal jaundice. Blood film during crisis: Heinz bodies (denatured Hb - bite cells after splenic removal). Ix: G6PD enzyme assay (may be falsely normal during acute haemolysis as reticulocytes have higher G6PD activity - retest when stable). Mx: avoid triggers; supportive transfusion if severe; folate supplementation; self-limiting episodes.

conditions.name: Ovarian cancer
conditions.summary: Most common gynaecological cancer causing death; 'silent killer'. Risk: BRCA1/2 mutation (lifetime risk up to 44%), Lynch syndrome, nulliparity, early menarche/late menopause, HRT, endometriosis; COCP is protective. Types: epithelial (90%) - serous (HG serous: TP53, BRCA, chromosomally unstable; most common and lethal), mucinous, endometrioid, clear cell; sex cord stromal (granulosa cell - oestrogen-producing, post-menopausal bleeding, Call-Exner bodies); germ cell (dysgerminoma, teratoma, yolk sac tumour - young women). Sx: vague (abdominal distension, bloating, urinary frequency, early satiety, weight loss, pelvic pressure); CA-125 ↑ (elevated in HG serous; less so in mucinous/early). Ix: USS (adnexal mass); CT (staging - FIGO I-IV); laparotomy + histology. Mx: optimal debulking surgery (cytoreduction) + platinum-taxane chemotherapy; PARP inhibitors (olaparib, niraparib - maintenance, especially BRCA-mutated); bevacizumab.

conditions.name: Cervical cancer
conditions.summary: Squamous cell carcinoma (70-80%) or adenocarcinoma (15-20%) of cervix; almost all caused by HPV (HPV 16, 18 responsible for ~70%). Risk: multiple sexual partners, early coitarche, immunosuppression, smoking (SCC), COCP (adenocarcinoma). Premalignant: CIN (cervical intraepithelial neoplasia) I-III → detected on cervical screening (smear/HPV testing). Sx: abnormal vaginal bleeding (post-coital, intermenstrual, post-menopausal), vaginal discharge; advanced: pelvic pain, haematuria, rectal bleeding, renal failure (ureteric obstruction). Ix: colposcopy + biopsy; staging MRI (local) + CT/PET (systemic). FIGO staging. Mx: CIN: surveillance (CIN I), LLETZ/LEEP (CIN II-III); microinvasive (stage IA1): LLETZ or cone; early invasive (IB-IIA): radical hysterectomy (Wertheim) vs. chemoradiotherapy (equiv. outcomes); locally advanced (IIB-IV): cisplatin-based chemoradiotherapy; bevacizumab + pembrolizumab (metastatic/recurrent).

conditions.name: Endometrial cancer
conditions.summary: Most common gynaecological cancer. Type 1 (endometrioid, oestrogen-driven; obese/anovulatory/HRT): presents early with postmenopausal bleeding. Type 2 (serous/clear cell; de novo): more aggressive. Ix: endometrial biopsy. FIGO staging (MRI). Mx: Mx (early): total hysterectomy + bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy ± pelvic LN dissection; adjuvant Mx based on stage; checkpoint inhibitors for MSI-H.

conditions.name: Renal cell carcinoma
conditions.summary: Clear cell RCC most common (>70%); VHL gene mutation. Classical triad (rare): haematuria, flank pain, palpable mass. More often: incidental renal mass on imaging. Paraneoplastic: polycythaemia, hypercalcaemia, Stauffer syndrome. Ix (staging): CT chest/abdomen/pelvis. Mx: partial/radical nephrectomy for localised; sunitinib/pazopanib or cabozantinib + nivolumab for metastatic; checkpoint inhibitors.

conditions.name: Bladder cancer
conditions.summary: Most common urological cancer (90% urothelial/transitional cell carcinoma, TCC); 10% squamous cell carcinoma (Schistosoma haematobium - Middle East, endemic areas; chronic irritation). Risk: smoking (most important modifiable - 50%), occupational carcinogens (aniline dyes, rubber/chemical industry), cyclophosphamide, radiation, chronic UTI. Sx: painless haematuria (macroscopic - classic; any in >50 yr → urgent investigation); dysuria, frequency (irritative). Ix: flexible cystoscopy + biopsy (gold standard); CT urogram (upper tract TCC, staging); urine cytology (high-grade/CIS); TURBT (staging + treatment of NMIBC). Ix (staging): non-muscle invasive (NMIBC - 75%: Ta/T1/CIS) vs muscle-invasive (MIBC: ≥T2). Mx: NMIBC: TURBT + intravesical BCG (high-risk T1/CIS - ↓recurrence/progression) or mitomycin C; MIBC: neoadjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy + radical cystectomy (or chemoradiation); advanced: pembrolizumab/atezolizumab (PD-1/L1 - second-line); enfortumab vedotin (nectin-4 ADC).

conditions.name: Thyroid storm
conditions.summary: Life-threatening thyroid hormone excess; precipitated by illness, surgery, radioiodine in undertreated hyperthyroid patient. Sx: extreme tachycardia, hyperthermia, hypertension, AMS (confusion, coma), vomiting, diarrhoea. Burch-Wartofsky score >45 diagnostic. Mx: propylthiouracil (PTU, blocks synthesis + T4→T3 conversion) → then iodine (Wolff-Chaikoff) after 1 h → β-blocker + corticosteroids + supportive care. ICU.

conditions.name: Myxoedema coma
conditions.summary: Life-threatening end-stage hypothyroidism; mortality 30–60%. Precipitants: cold exposure, infection, sedatives, surgery in undiagnosed hypothyroidism. Sx: extreme hypothermia (cardinal feature), bradycardia, hypotension, hypoventilation (CO2 retention), hyponatraemia, altered consciousness, macroglossia, non-pitting oedema, pleural/pericardial effusions. Mx: ICU; IV T4 (levothyroxine) ± T3 (liothyronine) - rapid T3 for severe cases; IV hydrocortisone (concurrent adrenal insufficiency until excluded); passive warming; supportive (ventilation, pressors).

conditions.name: Primary hyperaldosteronism
conditions.summary: Excess aldosterone from adrenal adenoma (Conn's, 35%) or bilateral adrenal hyperplasia (60%). Most common cause of secondary hypertension. Sx: HTN (often resistant), hypokalaemia (not always), metabolic alkalosis. Ix: aldosterone-to-renin ratio (>30 suggests PA). CT adrenals; adrenal vein sampling to lateralise. Mx: unilateral adenoma: laparoscopic adrenalectomy (curative). BAH: spironolactone/eplerenone.
utd: primary aldosteronism imaging adrenal vein sampling

conditions.name: Diabetes insipidus
conditions.summary: Deficient ADH action → polyuria (hypotonic, dilute urine) + polydipsia. Cranial DI: ADH deficiency (hypothalamic/posterior pituitary lesion - tumour [craniopharyngioma, germinoma], trauma, surgery, sarcoid, Langerhans cell histiocytosis, Wolfram syndrome, genetic, idiopathic). Nephrogenic DI: renal resistance to ADH (mutations in V2R/AQP2, lithium - most common drug cause, hypercalcaemia, hypokalaemia, chronic renal disease). Gestational DI: placental vasopressinase. Ix: urine osmolality <300 mOsm/kg + serum osmolality >295 + polyuria (>3 L/day). Fluid deprivation test: urine osmolality fails to rise above 300 with dehydration → DI confirmed; desmopressin (DDAVP) challenge: urine osmolality rises >50% = cranial DI; <50% = nephrogenic. Copeptin measurement increasingly used. Mx: cranial: desmopressin (DDAVP - intranasal/oral/SC; analogue of ADH; main treatment); nephrogenic: remove cause (stop lithium, correct Ca²⁺/K⁺), low-sodium/low-protein diet + thiazide (↓urine volume paradoxically - ↓ECF volume → ↑proximal reabsorption); amiloride (lithium-induced); NSAIDs (↑renal prostaglandin-mediated resistance to ADH).

conditions.name: Metabolic syndrome
conditions.summary: Cluster of cardiovascular risk factors. Ix: IDF criteria (≥3 of 5): central obesity (waist >94/80 cm M/F), ↑TG (>1.7 mmol/L), ↓HDL, ↑BP (≥130/85), ↑fasting glucose (≥5.6 mmol/L). Mx: Strongly associated with insulin resistance, T2DM, NAFLD, CVD, sleep apnoea. Mx: lifestyle modification (diet, exercise, weight loss); individualise pharmacotherapy for each component.

conditions.name: Carcinoid syndrome
conditions.summary: Carcinoid tumours (well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumours - NET G1/G2) - midgut origin (ileum most common) predominantly. Sx: Carcinoid syndrome (occurs when liver metastases bypass hepatic inactivation - serotonin, tachykinins reach systemic circulation): flushing (most common - episodic, triggered by alcohol/stress/exercise), diarrhoea (secretory, watery), bronchospasm (wheeze), right-sided valvular heart disease (carcinoid heart disease: tricuspid regurgitation + pulmonary stenosis - fibrous plaque deposition; sign of advanced disease, most common cause of death). ↑24-hr urinary 5-HIAA (serotonin metabolite). Mx: Octreotide scan (111In-DTPA octreotide) or DOTATATE PET-CT (somatostatin receptor imaging - tumour + metastases). Chromogranin A (tumour marker - ↑). Mx: somatostatin analogues (octreotide/lanreotide LAR - first-line, ↓symptoms, antiproliferative); surgery (resection of primary, cytoreductive debulking); PRRT (177Lu-DOTATATE - peptide receptor radionuclide therapy, ↑PFS); liver-directed therapy (embolisation, RFA for hepatic metastases); telotristat (tryptophan hydroxylase inhibitor - ↓5-HT synthesis, ↓diarrhoea).
utd: neuroendocrine tumors carcinoid syndrome clinical features diagnosis

conditions.name: Gestational diabetes
conditions.summary: Glucose intolerance first recognised in pregnancy (≠ pre-existing DM); affects 5-8% pregnancies; resolves after delivery in most. Risk: BMI>30, previous GDM, previous macrosomia (>4.5 kg), South Asian/Black/Middle Eastern ethnicity, first-degree relative with T2DM, PCOS. Pathophysiology: ↑pregnancy hormones (progesterone, oestrogen, hPL, cortisol, growth hormone) → insulin resistance + relative insulin deficiency. Complications - maternal: pre-eclampsia, CS, future T2DM (50% within 10 yr); fetal: macrosomia (shoulder dystocia, operative delivery), neonatal hypoglycaemia, preterm birth, stillbirth, IUGR (insulin-deficient GDM), shoulder dystocia. Ix: OGTT (75 g, 2-hr) at 24-28 wk (or earlier if risk); NICE criteria: fasting ≥5.6 mmol/L OR 2-hr ≥7.8 mmol/L = GDM. Mx: dietary modification + blood glucose monitoring (first-line); metformin or insulin (if targets not met - fasting <5.3 mmol/L; 1-hr PP <7.8 mmol/L); insulin preferred for macrosomia; induction ≥40+6 wk (or earlier for complications); annual OGTT/HbA1c post-delivery.

conditions.name: Placenta previa
conditions.summary: Placenta overlying internal cervical os. Complete vs marginal. Risk: prior uterine surgery (CS, curettage), multiple gestation, advanced maternal age, smoking. Presents with painless bright-red vaginal bleeding in 2nd-3rd trimester. Ix: US (transvaginal most accurate). Mx: no digital vaginal exam; CS delivery (elective at 36-37 wk if asymptomatic major praevia); emergency CS for haemorrhage.

conditions.name: Placental abruption
conditions.summary: Premature placental separation from uterine wall. Risk: hypertension (most common), trauma, cocaine, smoking, prior abruption, polyhydramnios. Sx: painful uterine bleeding, rigid tender abdomen, fetal distress; concealed haemorrhage possible. Complications: DIC, fetal hypoxia, preterm birth, maternal shock. Mx: stabilise mother; fetal monitoring; immediate delivery (CS if fetal compromise/severe abruption); DIC management.

conditions.name: Ovarian torsion
conditions.summary: Twisting of ovary (and often fallopian tube) on its pedicle → occlusion of blood supply → ischaemia → infarction. Most common with ovarian mass >5 cm (dermoid cyst most common; OHSS risk in IVF). Can occur in normal ovary (children, young adults). Sx: acute onset severe unilateral pelvic pain (often sudden, constant, may radiate to flank/thigh), nausea/vomiting, low-grade fever. Sx: unilateral tender adnexal mass. Doppler Ix (US): enlarged ovary ± mass, absent/reduced blood flow (Doppler can be misleading - flow present does not exclude torsion). Ix: high clinical suspicion; USS + Doppler; definitive: diagnostic laparoscopy. Mx: surgical emergency - laparoscopic detorsion (untwist - even if appears ischaemic/necrotic, oophoropexy or oophorectomy); ovarian cystectomy/oophorectomy if non-viable; fertility preservation prioritised in young women (detorsion without oophorectomy when possible); post-IVF OHSS → detorsion + oophoropexy (bilateral risk).

conditions.name: Uterine fibroids
conditions.summary: Benign smooth muscle tumours of uterus; most common pelvic tumour in women. Oestrogen-sensitive; multiple and vary in size/location: intramural (most common), submucosal (worst symptoms - heaviest bleeding), subserosal, pedunculated. Sx: heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB), dysmenorrhoea, bulk symptoms (urinary frequency, constipation, abdominal bloating), subfertility (submucosal), pelvic pressure. Asymptomatic in 50%. Ix (US): diagnostic (characteristic hypoechoic masses). Mx: medical: tranexamic acid, NSAIDs, COCP, LNG-IUS (less effective with large/multiple fibroids), GnRH agonists (↓fibroid size pre-operatively, temporary); ulipristal acetate (SPRM - liver toxicity concern); relugolix combination; surgical: myomectomy (wish to preserve fertility), hysterectomy (definitive); uterine artery embolisation (UAE - non-surgical, effective for HMB, avoid if considering pregnancy); HIFU (focused ultrasound).

conditions.name: Eating disorders
conditions.summary: Anorexia nervosa: restriction → ↓weight (BMI <17.5), intense fear of weight gain, body image distortion. Complications: amenorrhoea, osteoporosis, electrolyte abnormalities (hypokalaemia), lanugo, bradycardia, refeeding syndrome. Bulimia nervosa: binge-purge cycles; parotid enlargement, dental erosion, Russell sign, hypokalaemia/alkalosis. Mx (AN): structured re-feeding + psychotherapy (CBT/FBT); medical stabilisation; rarely admission. BN: CBT + SSRI (fluoxetine).

conditions.name: Alcohol use disorder
conditions.summary: Spectrum from harmful use to dependence. Dependence features: compulsive use, difficulty controlling, tolerance, withdrawal (CAGE/AUDIT questionnaires). Alcohol withdrawal syndrome: 6-24 hr post last drink - tremor, sweating, tachycardia, anxiety, nausea; 24-48 hr: seizures (tonic-clonic, single/brief - 'rum fits'); 48-72 hr: delirium tremens (DT) - confusion, hallucinations (visual/tactile - 'seeing things'), autonomic instability (hyperthermia, HTN, tachycardia), mortality 5-15% untreated. CIWA-Ar score (severity assessment). Wernicke's encephalopathy: triad - ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, confusion (classic triad present in only 10%); Ix (MRI): mammillary body/periaqueductal grey ↑T2/FLAIR. Mx: withdrawal: chlordiazepoxide/diazepam (reducing regimen, symptom-triggered) ± CIWA; prophylactic/therapeutic parenteral thiamine (Pabrinex IV - before/with glucose). Relapse prevention: acamprosate (↓craving), naltrexone (μ-opioid blocker, ↓reward), disulfiram (aldehyde dehydrogenase inhibitor, aversion therapy); CBT; 12-step programmes.

conditions.name: Opioid use disorder
conditions.summary: DSM-5: ≥2 criteria for opioid misuse pattern; craving, tolerance, withdrawal, role impairment. Overdose: respiratory depression, miosis, coma - Mx: naloxone (IM/IN/IV), repeat every 2-3 min. Sx: Withdrawal: lacrimation, diaphoresis, piloerection, diarrhoea, myalgia, insomnia (not life-threatening). MAT: buprenorphine/naloxone (Suboxone) 1st-line; methadone (supervised dispensing); naltrexone (after detox).

conditions.name: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
conditions.summary: Neurodevelopmental disorder. DSM-5: ≥6 inattentive OR hyperactive-impulsive symptoms, present before age 12, in ≥2 settings, >6 mo. Three subtypes: predominantly inattentive, hyperactive-impulsive, combined. Mx: stimulants 1st-line (methylphenidate, amphetamines); atomoxetine, guanfacine/clonidine as alternatives. Behavioural therapy; psychoeducation for family.

conditions.name: Rosacea
conditions.summary: Chronic inflammatory facial skin condition. Subtypes: erythematotelangiectatic (flushing, persistent central facial erythema, telangiectasia), papulopustular (acne-like papules/pustules on background erythema - DD: acne vulgaris, perioral dermatitis), phymatous (rhinophyma - sebaceous hyperplasia of nose), ocular (blepharitis, conjunctivitis). Triggers: alcohol, hot drinks, spicy food, sun, stress, temperature. Associated: Demodex mites, H. pylori (controversial). Mx: trigger avoidance; topical metronidazole/azelaic acid/ivermectin; oral doxycycline (low-dose anti-inflammatory); laser for telangiectasia; isotretinoin for phymatous/severe.

conditions.name: Tinea
conditions.summary: Dermatophyte fungal infection of skin/hair/nails. Tinea pedis (athlete's foot): interdigital maceration; tinea corporis (ringworm): annular pruritic scaly plaques; tinea capitis: scalp, lymphadenopathy, fluorescence under Wood lamp (Microsporum); tinea unguium (onychomycosis): nail dystrophy. Ix: KOH prep (hyphae). Mx: topical azole/terbinafine (body/feet); oral terbinafine (nails, scalp).
utd: clinical features and diagnosis of Tinea

conditions.name: Scabies
conditions.summary: Sarcoptes scabiei mite infestation. Intense pruritus, worse at night; burrows in finger webs, wrists, genitals, areolae; spares face (in adults). Crusted (Norwegian) scabies in immunocompromised: hyperkeratotic, highly infectious. Ix: dermatoscopy or skin scraping (mite/eggs/faeces). Mx: topical permethrin 5% (whole body, leave 8-12 h, repeat in 1 wk); oral ivermectin for crusted scabies; treat all household contacts simultaneously; wash clothing/bedding.
utd: clinical features and diagnosis of Scabies

conditions.name: Acne vulgaris
conditions.summary: Follicular hyperkeratosis + sebum overproduction + Cutibacterium acnes proliferation. Open (blackheads) and closed (whiteheads) comedones, inflammatory papules/pustules, nodules, cysts. Scarring risk with nodular/cystic acne. Mx: mild: topical retinoid ± BPO; moderate: add topical/oral antibiotic (limit duration, use BPO to reduce resistance); severe/scarring: isotretinoin (teratogenic, iPLEDGE in USA); COCP/spironolactone in females.
utd: clinical features and diagnosis of Acne vulgaris

conditions.name: Conjunctivitis
conditions.summary: Inflammation of conjunctiva. Bacterial (purulent discharge): S. aureus, S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae; Mx: topical antibiotics. Viral (watery discharge, often adenovirus): self-limiting, very contagious. Allergic (itching, watery, bilateral): antihistamine drops. Mx: Neonatal: gonococcal (erythromycin prophylaxis at birth) or chlamydial - systemic treatment required. Hyperacute purulent - gonococcal emergency.

conditions.name: Uveitis
conditions.summary: Inflammation of uveal tract (iris, ciliary body, choroid). Anterior uveitis (iritis - 75%): ciliary flush, irregular pupil, keratic precipitates, hypopyon, posterior synechiae. Posterior uveitis: vitritis, retinal/choroidal lesions, floaters, visual loss. Panuveitis: all segments. Causes: HLA-B27 (AS, reactive arthritis, IBD, psoriasis - unilateral recurrent anterior); sarcoidosis (bilateral, chronic, mutton-fat KPs); JIA (associated anterior uveitis - insidious, no redness, risk of band keratopathy, glaucoma, cataract); Behçet (posterior/panuveitis - risk of blindness); infectious (toxoplasma - most common cause of posterior uveitis worldwide; CMV; syphilis; TB; HSV; VZV); MS; idiopathic. Ix: slit-lamp examination; FBC, ESR/CRP, ANA, HLA-B27, ACE (sarcoidosis), syphilis serology, toxoplasma IgG/IgM, CXR, MRI brain (MS). Mx: topical steroids (anterior uveitis - first-line); cycloplegic (prevents posterior synechiae); systemic steroids (posterior/panuveitis, severe); immunosuppression (azathioprine, MMF, ciclosporin, biologic anti-TNF - refractory); treat infections.

conditions.name: Retinal detachment
conditions.summary: Separation of neurosensory retina from RPE. Rhegmatogenous (most common - retinal tear → fluid enters subretinal space): risk - myopia, previous cataract surgery, trauma, PVD (posterior vitreous detachment). Tractional: fibrovascular proliferation pulls retina (proliferative diabetic retinopathy). Exudative: subretinal fluid accumulation (tumour, VKH, choroidal effusion). Sx (rhegmatogenous): floaters (vitreous haemorrhage - 'cobwebs'), flashing lights (photopsia - traction on retina during PVD), curtain/shadow across visual field (detachment), reduced acuity (macula involved - 'macula-off' = emergency). USS B-scan (macula status if media opaque). Mx: immediate referral; pneumatic retinopexy (gas bubble + laser/cryotherapy - simple superior detachments); scleral buckle; vitrectomy ± gas/silicone oil tamponade (complex/inferior/macula-off). Macula-off: surgery within hours-days for best visual outcome.

conditions.name: Age-related hearing loss
conditions.summary: Bilateral symmetric high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss from cochlear hair cell degeneration; most common cause of hearing loss in elderly. Sx: Insidious onset; difficulty hearing high-pitched sounds and speech in noise. Audiogram: bilateral high-frequency sloping loss. Mx: hearing aids (most effective); cochlear implantation for severe-profound; tinnitus management as needed.

conditions.name: Supraventricular tachycardia
conditions.summary: Narrow-complex tachycardia (usually) from reentrant circuit above ventricles. AVNRT most common (dual AV nodal pathways); AVRT (accessory pathway, e.g. WPW). Sx: sudden-onset palpitations, chest tightness, presyncope. Ix: Vagal manoeuvres → adenosine IV (6 mg, then 12 mg) for diagnosis and Mx. Mx: Haemodynamically unstable: synchronised DC cardioversion. Long-term: ablation (curative); β-blocker or CCB for rate control.
utd: acute management paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia adults

conditions.name: Ventricular tachycardia
conditions.summary: Wide-complex tachycardia (QRS >120 ms) from ventricular origin. Monomorphic VT (structural heart disease - post-MI scar, DCM) vs polymorphic (long QT → torsades). Pulseless VT: defibrillation + CPR. Mx: Haemodynamically stable: IV amiodarone or procainamide; synchronised cardioversion. Sustained VT with structural heart disease: ICD implantation; catheter ablation for recurrent episodes.
utd: acute management sustained ventricular tachycardia adults
secondary prevention sudden cardiac death icd

conditions.name: Heart block
conditions.summary: Impaired AV conduction. 1st-degree: prolonged PR >200 ms - benign, no treatment. 2nd-degree Mobitz I (Wenckebach): progressive PR prolongation → dropped beat - usually benign; Mobitz II: sudden non-conducted P wave without PR change - risk of complete block, may need pacing. 3rd-degree (complete): no AV conduction, escape rhythm; causes: fibrosis, ischaemia, Lyme, sarcoid, drug toxicity. Mx: transcutaneous/transvenous pacing → permanent pacemaker.

conditions.name: Hypertensive emergency
conditions.summary: Severe HTN (usually >180/120) + acute end-organ damage (hypertensive encephalopathy, ICH, AKI, flash pulmonary oedema, aortic dissection, retinal haemorrhage). Sx: Distinguish from urgency (no end-organ damage). Mx: IV antihypertensives (labetalol, nicardipine, nitroprusside, clevidipine); MAP reduction ≤25% in first hour, then cautious further reduction. Specific targets per organ: dissection BP <120 systolic; ischaemic stroke: less aggressive reduction.

conditions.name: Myocarditis
conditions.summary: Inflammation of myocardium. Causes: viral (enterovirus, SARS-CoV-2, parvovirus B19, HHV-6), autoimmune (giant cell), drug hypersensitivity, sarcoidosis. Sx: chest pain (pericarditis-like), dyspnoea, palpitations; may present as DCM or acute HF. ↑Troponin, ECG changes (ST elevation mimicking MI). CMR gold standard. Mx: supportive; restrict exercise; treat HF (ACE-i, β-blocker); IVIG/steroids for giant cell; avoid NSAIDs in early phase.

conditions.name: Constrictive pericarditis
conditions.summary: Fibrous/calcified pericardium restricts cardiac filling. Causes: prior viral pericarditis (most common in West), TB (endemic areas), post-cardiac surgery/radiation. Sx: progressive right-heart failure (↑JVP with Kussmaul sign, oedema, ascites), preserved EF, rapid ventricular filling. Pericardial knock, equalised diastolic pressures on catheterisation. CT/CMR: pericardial thickening/calcification. Mx: pericardiectomy (definitive); diuretics temporising.

conditions.name: Syncope
conditions.summary: Transient LOC from global cerebral hypoperfusion, self-limiting with spontaneous recovery. Vasovagal (reflex/neurally-mediated): most common; prodrome of nausea/diaphoresis, triggered by prolonged standing/emotional stress. Orthostatic hypotension: ↓BP >20/10 mmHg on standing. Cardiac: arrhythmia (sudden onset, no prodrome), structural (AS, HCM, PE). Ix: ECG, orthostatic BP, echo if structural suspected; tilt-table test. Mx: vasovagal: avoid triggers, increased salt/fluids, β-blocker/fludrocortisone if refractory.

conditions.name: Coarctation of aorta
conditions.summary: Constriction of aorta, typically distal to left subclavian artery. Associated with bicuspid aortic valve, Turner syndrome. Sx: HTN in upper extremities, diminished/delayed femoral pulses, rib notching on CXR (collateral intercostal vessels). Adults may have hypertension as isolated finding. Ix: CT angiography. Mx: endovascular stenting (most common) or surgical repair. Complications of untreated: HF, stroke, aortic rupture, endocarditis.

conditions.name: Tetralogy of Fallot
conditions.summary: Most common cyanotic congenital heart disease. Four defects: VSD, overriding aorta, pulmonary stenosis (RVOT obstruction), RV hypertrophy. Sx: cyanosis (boot-shaped heart on CXR), 'tet spells' (hypercyanotic episodes - squat position relieves). Ix: echo. Mx: total surgical correction (VSD patch + RVOT relief), usually in first year; propranolol for tet spells; palliative BT shunt if needed.

conditions.name: Ventricular septal defect
conditions.summary: Most common congenital heart defect (overall); 4 types: perimembranous (most common, 80%), muscular, outlet/supracristal, inlet (AV canal type). Haemodynamics: L-to-R shunt (size-dependent) → LV/RV volume overload → pulmonary hypertension → Eisenmenger. Small VSD (restrictive): pansystolic murmur at LLSE (Maladie de Roger), loud, no haemodynamic compromise; may close spontaneously. Large VSD: soft/no murmur (large pressure equalisation), signs of HF, FTT in infants. Ix (echo): diagnostic. Mx: small: observation (most close spontaneously); large symptomatic: surgical or device closure; endocarditis prophylaxis (when applicable); treat HF.
utd: ventricular septal defect adults clinical management

conditions.name: Atrial septal defect
conditions.summary: Congenital shunt; three main types: ostium secundum (most common - central, ↑PFO); ostium primum (AV canal defect - associated with Down syndrome, primum ASD + cleft mitral/tricuspid valve); sinus venosus (posterior, associated with partial anomalous pulmonary venous drainage). Haemodynamics: L-to-R shunt → RV volume overload → pulmonary hypertension (late). Sx: often asymptomatic until adulthood; palpitations (AF/flutter), dyspnoea, paradoxical embolism, Eisenmenger (late). Sx: fixed split S2 (pathognomonic), soft ejection systolic murmur (pulmonary flow), mid-diastolic murmur (tricuspid flow). Ix (echo): diagnostic. Mx: closure (percutaneous device or surgical) if significant shunt or symptoms; anticoagulate if AF.
utd: atrial septal defect adults clinical management

conditions.name: Patent ductus arteriosus
conditions.summary: Failure of ductus arteriosus to close after birth; prematurity (PGE2 keeps open), congenital rubella, high altitude. Haemodynamics: L-to-R shunt (aorta → pulmonary artery) → LV volume overload → pulmonary hypertension → Eisenmenger (late). Sx: continuous 'machinery' murmur (Gibson murmur) at left infraclavicular area; bounding pulses, wide pulse pressure; FTT and recurrent chest infections in large PDA. In premature infants: respiratory distress, inability to wean from ventilator. Mx: premature: indometacin or ibuprofen (COX inhibitor - ↓PGE2; contraindicated if renal/haemorrhage concerns); catheter-based device closure (transcatheter - Amplatzer); surgical ligation; ductal-dependent CHD: keep open with prostaglandin E1 (PGE1).
utd: patent ductus arteriosus adults clinical features management

conditions.name: Venous insufficiency
conditions.summary: Failure of venous valves → chronic venous hypertension. Sx: varicose veins, leg oedema, lipodermatosclerosis, venous stasis dermatitis (medial gaiter), venous ulcers (medial malleolus, shallow, sloping edge). Duplex US for incompetent perforators/truncal reflux. Mx: compression stockings (cornerstone), leg elevation; endovenous ablation (EVLA/RFA) or sclerotherapy for truncal incompetence; ulcer management.

conditions.name: Bronchiectasis
conditions.summary: Irreversible bronchial dilatation from chronic airway infection/inflammation. Causes: post-infective (TB, pertussis), cystic fibrosis, ciliary dyskinesia, hypogammaglobulinaemia, ABPA. Sx: daily productive purulent cough, recurrent chest infections, haemoptysis. Ix (HRCT): signet-ring sign (airway diameter > adjacent artery). Mx: airway clearance (physiotherapy, hypertonic saline), bronchodilators, macrolide prophylaxis; IV antibiotics for exacerbations (Pseudomonas common); manage underlying cause.

conditions.name: Pertussis
conditions.summary: Bordetella pertussis. Catarrhal phase (1-2 wk, infectious, mild cough) → paroxysmal phase (2-6 wk): inspiratory 'whoop', post-tussive vomiting, apnoea in infants; lymphocytosis. Ix: nasopharyngeal PCR. Mx: azithromycin (shortens infectious period if given early; post-exposure prophylaxis for contacts). Vaccination (DTaP/Tdap) is primary prevention; maternal immunisation in 3rd trimester protects neonates.
utd: pertussis whooping cough clinical features diagnosis

conditions.name: Epiglottitis
conditions.summary: Life-threatening supraglottic inflammation, classically H. influenzae type b in unvaccinated children; now predominantly adults (streptococcal). Sx: Children: acute onset fever, drooling, dysphagia, tripod posture ('sniffing' position), muffled voice - do NOT examine throat, do NOT lay child flat. Adults: odynophagia, dysphagia, stridor. Thumb sign on lateral neck X-ray. Mx: secure airway (expert intubation/tracheostomy); ceftriaxone; dexamethasone to reduce oedema.

conditions.name: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency
conditions.summary: Autosomal co-dominant SERPINA1 mutations (ZZ most severe). Deficient AAT fails to inhibit neutrophil elastase → emphysema (panacinar, lower lobe). Liver disease from misfolded AAT polymer accumulation in hepatocytes → cirrhosis, HCC. Presents in young non-smoker with COPD, or unexplained liver disease. Ix: serum AAT level + phenotype (Pi typing). Mx: smoking cessation; COPD management; IV AAT augmentation therapy (slows FEV1 decline); liver transplant for end-stage liver disease.
utd: alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency clinical manifestations diagnosis

conditions.name: Lung abscess
conditions.summary: Necrotising pulmonary infection with pus-filled cavity. Causes: aspiration (most common - anaerobes; often in impaired consciousness/dental disease), secondary to pneumonia (S. aureus, Klebsiella), septic emboli (IVDU), post-obstructive (tumour). Sx: fever, weight loss, productive foul-smelling sputum, haemoptysis; air-fluid level on CXR/CT. Mx: prolonged antibiotics (amoxicillin-clavulanate 4-6 wk; clindamycin if anaerobic); postural drainage; surgery/bronchoscopy for refractory.

conditions.name: Prolactinoma
conditions.summary: Most common pituitary adenoma; benign. Microprolactinoma (<10 mm): amenorrhoea/galactorrhoea in women; hypogonadism (↓libido, ED) in men (often found late as macroprolactinoma). ↑Prolactin; rule out drugs (antipsychotics, metoclopramide, domperidone, opioids). Mx: dopamine agonists (cabergoline 1st-line, bromocriptine) normalise PRL and shrink tumour in most. Mx: Surgery (transsphenoidal) for dopamine-agonist resistance/intolerance; radiotherapy for residual.

conditions.name: Pituitary adenoma
conditions.summary: Benign pituitary tumour. Functional: prolactinoma (most common), GH-secreting (acromegaly), ACTH-secreting (Cushing's disease), TSH-secreting (rare). Non-functional ('null cell'): mass effects - headache, bitemporal hemianopia, hypopituitarism. Ix: MRI pituitary. Mx: functional - treat hormone excess; non-functional: surgery (transsphenoidal) if symptomatic/large; dopamine agonists for prolactinoma.

conditions.name: Multiple endocrine neoplasia
conditions.summary: MEN1 (3 Ps): Parathyroid (95%, hypercalcaemia), Pituitary (prolactinoma most common), Pancreatic NETs (gastrinoma, insulinoma). MEN2A: Medullary thyroid cancer (MTC), Phaeochromocytoma, Parathyroid hyperplasia; RET proto-oncogene. MEN2B: MTC, Phaeochromocytoma, mucosal neuromas, marfanoid habitus; most aggressive. Ix: Screen family; prophylactic thyroidectomy in MEN2 gene carriers. Ix: genetic testing.

conditions.name: Thyroid cancer
conditions.summary: Papillary (80%+): most common, excellent prognosis, BRAF/RET mutations, psammoma bodies. Follicular: haematogenous spread (bone, lung). Medullary (parafollicular C-cells, calcitonin): sporadic or MEN2. Anaplastic: rare, rapidly fatal. Ix: thyroid nodule workup - US, FNA. Mx: thyroidectomy (usually); RAI ablation post-surgery for papillary/follicular; TSH suppression; medullary: surgery + vandetanib/cabozantinib for metastatic.

conditions.name: Vitamin D deficiency
conditions.summary: Vitamin D deficiency → ↓Ca/phosphate absorption → rickets (children: bone pain, bowing, craniotabes, Harrison sulcus, dental enamel hypoplasia) or osteomalacia (adults: bone pain, proximal myopathy, Looser zones/pseudofractures on X-ray). Ix: ↓25-OH-D3, ↑PTH, ↑ALP, ↓Ca/phosphate. Causes: inadequate sun exposure, malabsorption, dark skin, obesity, CKD, anticonvulsants. Mx: high-dose vitamin D3 (colecalciferol) supplementation ± calcium.
utd: vitamin d deficiency adults clinical manifestations diagnosis

conditions.name: Obesity
conditions.summary: BMI ≥30. Adipose excess drives metabolic syndrome, T2DM, dyslipidaemia, HTN, OSA, NAFLD, GORD, OA, ↑cancer risk (colon, breast, endometrial), depression. Mx: Class III (BMI ≥40) or BMI ≥35 with comorbidities → bariatric surgery (gastric sleeve, RYGB - most effective long-term weight loss and T2DM remission). Pharmacotherapy: semaglutide/tirzepatide (GLP-1/GIP agonists) most effective agents; orlistat. Lifestyle: cornerstone.

conditions.name: Polycystic kidney disease
conditions.summary: Autosomal dominant (ADPKD, PKD1/PKD2 mutations) most common inherited kidney disease. Bilateral cortical cysts → progressive renal enlargement → ESRD (median age ~58). Extrarenal: hepatic cysts (most common), intracranial aneurysms (5-8%), mitral valve prolapse. Screen family members. Mx: HTN universal - aggressive BP control (ACE-i/ARB). Tolvaptan (V2R antagonist) slows progression in rapidly progressing disease. Ix: Annual BP, renal function; MRI/MRA for intracranial aneurysm screening if family history.
utd: autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease diagnosis
autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease management

conditions.name: Interstitial nephritis
conditions.summary: Tubulo-interstitial inflammation. Drug-induced most common: NSAIDs, penicillins, cephalosporins, PPIs, allopurinol (classic triad: fever + rash + eosinophilia in 10%). Also: infection (hantavirus, leptospirosis), autoimmune (Sjögren, sarcoid, IgG4-RD). AKI with urine eosinophils, WBC casts. Ix: clinical + renal biopsy. Mx: stop offending drug; corticosteroids if severe/persistent; recovery variable (incomplete if prolonged).
utd: acute interstitial nephritis clinical features diagnosis

conditions.name: Renal tubular acidosis
conditions.summary: Impaired tubular H+ secretion or HCO3 reabsorption → non-AG metabolic acidosis with normal AG. Type 1 (distal RTA): inability to acidify urine (urine pH >5.5 despite acidosis); nephrolithiasis (calcium phosphate stones), nephrocalcinosis; causes: Sjögren, SLE, amphotericin. Type 2 (proximal RTA): ↓HCO3 reabsorption; Fanconi syndrome. Mx: Type 4 (hyperkalaemic): ↓aldosterone or resistance; DM, CKD, ACE-i/ARBs. Mx: sodium bicarbonate; fludrocortisone for type 4.
utd: distal type 1 hypokalemic renal tubular acidosis

conditions.name: Testicular torsion
conditions.summary: Twisting of spermatic cord → ischaemia. Peak: adolescent males. Sx: sudden severe unilateral scrotal pain (can radiate to abdomen), nausea/vomiting, elevated testis, absent cremasteric reflex. Time-critical - viability: 6 h >90%, 24 h <10%. Do NOT delay surgery for Doppler US if clinical suspicion high. Mx: emergency surgical exploration (bilateral orchidopexy); if non-viable: orchiectomy. Manual detorsion temporising only.

conditions.name: Epididymitis
conditions.summary: Epididymal inflammation ± orchitis. <35 y: STI (Chlamydia, Gonorrhoea - treat empirically with ceftriaxone + doxycycline). >35 y: enteric organisms (E. coli) - UTI, urological instrumentation. Sx: gradual unilateral scrotal pain, swelling, tenderness; fever. US: epididymal enlargement + hyperaemia. Mx: analgesia, scrotal support; antibiotics guided by age/risk; exclude torsion (distinguish by onset - gradual vs acute).
utd: acute scrotal pain adults adolescents differential

conditions.name: Prostatitis
conditions.summary: Prostate inflammation. Acute bacterial: fever, dysuria, perineal pain, tender prostate (do NOT massage - bacteraemia risk); E. coli most common; Mx: fluoroquinolone 4 wk. Chronic bacterial: recurrent UTIs, same pathogens; Mx: prolonged fluoroquinolone/TMP-SMX. Chronic pelvic pain syndrome (CPPS/type III, most common): pelvic pain >3 mo, no infection identified; Mx: α-blocker, NSAIDs, amitriptyline, physiotherapy.
utd: chronic prostatitis chronic pelvic pain syndrome

conditions.name: Pancreatic cancer
conditions.summary: Ductal adenocarcinoma most common (90%). Risk: smoking, DM, chronic pancreatitis, hereditary (BRCA2, PALB2, Lynch). Sx: Late presentation: painless obstructive jaundice (head of pancreas), weight loss, new-onset DM, Courvoisier sign. Ix: CA 19-9 (monitoring, not screening). CT pancreatic protocol for staging. Resectable (~20%): Whipple procedure ± FOLFIRINOX adjuvant chemo. Locally advanced/metastatic: FOLFIRINOX or gemcitabine-nab-paclitaxel; prognosis poor (5-yr survival <10%).
utd: treatment locally advanced metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma

conditions.name: Oesophageal cancer
conditions.summary: Two main types: SCC (upper/mid: smoking, alcohol, hot beverages) and adenocarcinoma (lower: GORD/Barrett's oesophagus, obesity). Sx: Progressive dysphagia (solids → liquids), weight loss, odynophagia. Ix: OGD + biopsy; CT/PET staging. Resectable: oesophagectomy ± neoadjuvant chemoRT (FLOT/CROSS regimen). Mx: Palliative: stent, chemoRT. Prognosis poor unless early.

conditions.name: Gastric cancer
conditions.summary: Adenocarcinoma most common. Risk: H. pylori (most modifiable), salt-preserved food, smoking, gastric atrophy, pernicious anaemia, family history (CDH1 mutation in diffuse/signet-ring type). Late Sx: weight loss, epigastric pain, dysphagia, Virchow node, Sister Mary Joseph nodule. OGD + biopsy essential. Staging CT/PET. Resectable: gastrectomy + D2 lymphadenectomy; perioperative FLOT chemo. Mx: Advanced: platinum/fluoropyrimidine ± trastuzumab (HER2+) ± checkpoint inhibitors.
utd: gastric cancer clinical features diagnosis staging

conditions.name: Hepatocellular carcinoma
conditions.summary: Primary liver malignancy; most common worldwide. Risk: hepatitis B/C, cirrhosis (any cause), alcohol, NASH, aflatoxin, haemochromatosis. Ix: Screening with US ± AFP every 6 months in cirrhotic patients. ↑AFP (not always); arterial enhancement + washout on dynamic CT/MRI (LI-RADS 5 = HCC). Mx: early (Barcelona A): resection, ablation, or liver transplant (Milan criteria). Intermediate: TACE. Mx: Advanced: sorafenib or lenvatinib; atezolizumab + bevacizumab superior in first-line.

conditions.name: Anal fissure
conditions.summary: Linear tear in anoderm (distal anal canal below dentate line); posterior midline (90%) or anterior (10%); anterior fissures more common in women (obstetric trauma). Acute (<6 wk) or chronic (>6 wk - indurated margins, sentinel pile, hypertrophied anal papilla). Pathophysiology: internal anal sphincter hypertonicity → ↓anoderm blood supply → poor healing. Causes: hard stool/constipation (most common), Crohn disease (lateral/multiple/off-midline fissures - always biopsy). Sx: severe pain during and after defecation, fresh PR bleeding (on paper/stool surface - not mixed). Sx: visible fissure on gentle buttock retraction; digital rectal exam may not be possible (pain). Ix: clinical; exclude Crohn (if atypical). Mx: acute: laxatives (stool softening); topical lidocaine (short-term analgesia); chronic: topical GTN (glyceryl trinitrate 0.4% - ↓sphincter pressure, heals 50-80%; headache SE), diltiazem (topical, fewer headaches; equiv. efficacy), botulinum toxin injection (IAS - most effective single treatment ≈80%); lateral internal sphincterotomy (LIS - definitive surgical; ↑risk of incontinence in women/anterior fissures).

conditions.name: Haemorrhoids
conditions.summary: Abnormal enlargement/displacement of vascular cushions lining anal canal. Internal (above dentate line - covered by insensate mucosa; painless; classified I-IV): I prolapse on straining but reduce spontaneously; II reduce spontaneously; III require manual reduction; IV permanently prolapsed. External (below dentate line - covered by squamous epithelium; painful if thrombosed). Risk: constipation, straining, low-fibre diet, pregnancy, portal hypertension (rectal varices, not true haemorrhoids), pelvic tumours, prolonged sitting. Sx: painless bright red PR bleeding (on tissue/toilet bowl - fresh blood separate from stool surface), prolapse/discomfort, mucous discharge, pruritus ani; external thrombosed haemorrhoid: acute severe perianal pain + tender blue-black lump. Ix: proctoscopy; must exclude colorectal pathology (colonoscopy if ≥45 yr or unexplained blood). Mx: conservative - high-fibre diet, adequate hydration, sitz baths; rubber band ligation (RBL - most effective outpatient Mx for grade I-III); injection sclerotherapy; haemorrhoidectomy (grade III-IV or failed outpatient Mx); thrombosed external: excision within 72 hr (surgical) or conservative (resolves in 3-5 wk).

conditions.name: Meckel diverticulum
conditions.summary: Most common congenital GI anomaly. Remnant of vitello-intestinal duct. Rule of 2s: 2% incidence, 2 inches long, 2 feet from ileocaecal valve, 2:1 M:F, presents within first 2 years (though can present in adults). Complications: painless lower GI bleeding (ectopic gastric mucosa secretes acid → ulceration), obstruction, Meckel diverticulitis. Ix: Meckel scan (Tc-99m pertechnetate). Mx: symptomatic diverticulectomy; incidental removal controversial.

conditions.name: Volvulus
conditions.summary: Bowel twists on mesenteric axis → closed-loop obstruction. Sigmoid most common (elderly, institutionalised): 'coffee-bean' sign on AXR; Mx: rigid sigmoidoscopy detorsion, then elective sigmoid resection. Caecal volvulus: CT diagnosis; Mx: surgery (right hemicolectomy). Sx: Midgut volvulus in neonates (malrotation): bilious vomiting, emergency - Ladd procedure. Mx: Gastric volvulus (rare): nasogastric decompression then surgical repair.

conditions.name: Hiatal hernia
conditions.summary: Protrusion of stomach through diaphragmatic hiatus. Type I (sliding, 95%): GEJ slides above diaphragm - associated with GORD. Type II (para-oesophageal): fundus herniates alongside fixed GEJ. Type III (mixed). Type IV: other organs herniate. Sx: GORD symptoms; large PO hernia → early satiety, anaemia. Ix: OGD or barium swallow. Mx: PPI for GORD; laparoscopic fundoplication (Nissen) for symptomatic/large para-oesophageal hernias (risk of strangulation).

conditions.name: Zollinger-Ellison syndrome
conditions.summary: Gastrin-secreting tumour (gastrinoma) → massive acid hypersecretion → severe/refractory peptic ulcers (multiple, atypical sites). 60% malignant; 25% associated with MEN1. Sx: peptic ulcers resistant to PPI, diarrhoea/steatorrhoea (acid inactivates pancreatic lipase). Ix: fasting gastrin >1000 pg/mL + low gastric pH; secretin stimulation test; CT/68Ga-DOTATATE PET for localisation. Mx: high-dose PPI; surgical resection (curative in localised); octreotide, chemotherapy for metastatic.
utd: zollinger ellison syndrome clinical features diagnosis

conditions.name: Transient ischaemic attack
conditions.summary: Sudden focal neurological deficit from transient cerebral ischaemia, typically lasting <1 h with no infarction on DWI. HIGH-RISK for early stroke (ABCD2 score; 10% stroke within 48 h). Same mechanism as ischaemic stroke: thromboembolism (AF, carotid stenosis), lacunar. Ix: Urgent workup: MRI DWI, carotid Doppler, ECG/cardiac monitor, echo. Mx: antiplatelet (aspirin + clopidogrel short-term), statin, BP control; anticoagulation for AF; carotid endarterectomy if stenosis ≥70%.

long-term management of Transient ischemic attack

conditions.name: Encephalitis
conditions.summary: Brain parenchymal inflammation, usually infectious or autoimmune. Herpes simplex encephalitis: most common sporadic viral; temporal lobe involvement (amnesia, behavioural change, seizures); Ix (MRI): temporal hyperintensity; PCR CSF for HSV; Mx: IV aciclovir urgently. Autoimmune (NMDA-receptor, LGI1, CASPR2): psychiatric prodrome, seizures, movement disorders; CSF/serum antibodies; Mx: immunotherapy (steroids, IVIG, plasmapheresis). CSF: lymphocytic pleocytosis. Mortality significant if untreated.

conditions.name: Brain abscess
conditions.summary: Focal bacterial infection within brain parenchyma. Sources: contiguous (sinusitis, otitis, dental - most common), haematogenous (endocarditis, IVDU, cyanotic CHD), post-traumatic/surgical. Organisms: streptococci (most common), Staphylococcus, anaerobes, gram-negatives. Sx: fever, headache, focal deficits, seizures, ↑ICP. CT/Ix (MRI): ring-enhancing lesion with central low density. Mx: IV antibiotics (ceftriaxone + metronidazole); stereotactic aspiration for diagnosis and Mx; steroids if oedema/herniation.

conditions.name: Concussion
conditions.summary: Functional neurological disturbance (not structural) from head impact. Sx: headache, confusion, amnesia (anterograde/retrograde), dizziness, nausea; LOC in <10%. Ix: Neurological exam and CT usually normal (CT head: NICE/Canadian criteria to rule out intracranial haemorrhage). Rest then graduated return-to-play protocol. Most resolve in 7-10 d. Sx: Post-concussion syndrome: persistent symptoms >4 wk - amitriptyline (headache), rehabilitation. Second-impact syndrome: rare but catastrophic - avoid return to play until fully symptom-free.

conditions.name: Hydrocephalus
conditions.summary: Abnormal CSF accumulation in ventricles. Communicating: impaired CSF reabsorption (post-meningitis, SAH). Non-communicating (obstructive): CSF flow blocked (tumour, aqueduct stenosis). Sx: ↑ICP (headache worse supine, vomiting, papilloedema), Parinaud syndrome (dorsal midbrain compression: upgaze palsy). In neonates: macrocephaly. Ix: CT/MRI. Mx: treat cause; VP shunt or external ventricular drain; endoscopic third ventriculostomy (ETV) for aqueductal stenosis.

conditions.name: Cerebral venous thrombosis
conditions.summary: Thrombosis of dural venous sinuses or cortical veins. Causes: hypercoagulability (OCP, pregnancy, thrombophilia), dehydration, infection, post-partum. Sx: progressive headache (most common, often thunderclap), focal deficits, seizures, papilloedema; may mimic idiopathic intracranial hypertension. MRI + MRV (or CT venography) diagnostic. Mx: anticoagulation (heparin, then warfarin/DOAC ≥3-6 mo) - even with haemorrhagic infarct. Good prognosis with treatment.

long-term management of Cerebral venous thrombosis

conditions.name: Narcolepsy
conditions.summary: Chronic sleep disorder: excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) + cataplexy (sudden bilateral muscle weakness triggered by emotion - pathognomonic for type 1). Other features: hypnagogic/hypnopompic hallucinations, sleep paralysis. Type 1: ↓CSF hypocretin-1 (orexin deficiency from autoimmune destruction of lateral hypothalamus). Ix: polysomnography + MSLT (sleep onset REM in <8 min, ≥2 SOREMPS). Mx: modafinil/armodafinil (EDS); sodium oxybate (EDS + cataplexy); venlafaxine (cataplexy).

conditions.name: Restless legs syndrome
conditions.summary: Urge to move legs, especially at rest/evening, relieved by movement; ↓sleep quality. Primary (idiopathic, familial, onset <45 y) vs secondary (iron deficiency most important - check ferritin even if Hgb normal; also pregnancy, uraemia, peripheral neuropathy). Ix: IRLSSG criteria. Mx: iron supplementation if ferritin <75. Pharmacological: dopamine agonists (pramipexole, ropinirole); α2δ ligands (pregabalin/gabapentin); low-dose opioids for refractory (risk of augmentation with DA agonists).
utd: acute treatment of Restless legs syndrome
long-term management of Restless legs syndrome

conditions.name: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension
conditions.summary: ↑ICP without hydrocephalus or mass lesion. Predominantly obese women of childbearing age. Causes/associations: obesity, tetracyclines, vitamin A excess, steroids withdrawal, OCP, CVST. Sx: constant daily headache, pulsatile tinnitus, transient visual obscurations, diplopia (CN VI palsy), papilloedema → progressive visual field loss. LP: opening pressure >25 cmH2O, normal CSF. Mx: weight loss (most effective), acetazolamide, topiramate; LP-shunting or optic nerve sheath fenestration for visual loss.
utd: acute treatment of Idiopathic intracranial hypertension
long-term management of Idiopathic intracranial hypertension

conditions.name: Spinal cord compression
conditions.summary: Emergency when acute (metastatic, epidural abscess/haematoma). Causes: malignant (breast, lung, prostate, myeloma), disc herniation, epidural abscess/haematoma, fracture/dislocation. Sx: bilateral limb weakness (UMN signs), sensory level, bladder/bowel dysfunction (late = poor prognosis). Ix: MRI spine (whole spine in metastatic disease). Mx: high-dose dexamethasone immediately; urgent surgical decompression or radiotherapy depending on aetiology and surgical fitness.
utd: acute treatment of Spinal cord compression
long-term management of Spinal cord compression

conditions.name: Delirium
conditions.summary: Acute-onset fluctuating disturbance of attention, awareness, and cognition - NOT dementia (chronic). Hyperactive (agitated, hallucinations), hypoactive (withdrawn - often missed), mixed. Causes (PINCH ME): Pain, Infection, Nutrition, Constipation/dehydration, Hypoxia, Medication (anticholinergics, opioids, sedatives, polypharmacy), Environment/immobility. High mortality; independent predictor of dementia. Mx: treat underlying cause; non-pharmacological (reorientation, avoid restraints, light); low-dose haloperidol/quetiapine only if risk to self/others.

conditions.name: Autism spectrum disorder
conditions.summary: Neurodevelopmental disorder with heterogeneous presentation. Core features (DSM-5): persistent deficits in social communication/interaction + restricted/repetitive behaviours, present from early development. Severity levels 1-3. Associated: intellectual disability (50%), ADHD, anxiety, epilepsy, GI problems. Ix: clinical (ADOS-2, ADI-R). No pharmacological cure; Mx: early intensive behavioural intervention (ABA), speech/occupational therapy; SSRI for anxiety, antipsychotics for severe behaviour.

conditions.name: Panic disorder
conditions.summary: Recurrent unexpected panic attacks + persistent concern about future attacks OR maladaptive behavioural change (e.g. agoraphobia). Sx: Panic attack: surge of intense fear peaking in minutes with ≥4 of: palpitations, sweating, trembling, SOB, chest pain, dizziness, paraesthesia, depersonalisation, hot flushes, fear of dying/losing control. Rule out medical causes (hyperthyroidism, arrhythmia, phaeochromocytoma). Mx: CBT (most effective, long-term); SSRI/SNRI; short-term benzodiazepine (avoid long-term).

conditions.name: Social anxiety disorder
conditions.summary: Marked fear/anxiety about social situations where scrutiny by others is possible; fear of embarrassment/humiliation; avoided or endured with distress; ≥6 mo; significant impairment. Most common anxiety disorder. Mx: CBT (exposure therapy gold standard); SSRI/SNRI 1st-line pharmacotherapy; β-blocker (propranolol) for situational/performance anxiety.

conditions.name: Borderline personality disorder
conditions.summary: Pervasive pattern of instability in interpersonal relationships, self-image, and affect + marked impulsivity. Sx: Core features: frantic efforts to avoid abandonment, unstable intense relationships (idealisation/devaluation), identity disturbance, impulsivity (self-harm, risky sex, substance use), suicidal/self-harm behaviour, affective instability, chronic emptiness, anger, transient paranoia/dissociation. Mx: DBT (most evidence); MBT; schema therapy; no single approved drug - target symptoms (SSRI, mood stabiliser, low-dose antipsychotic).

conditions.name: Somatic symptom disorder
conditions.summary: One or more distressing somatic symptoms with excessive thoughts/feelings/behaviours about them (≥6 mo). Ix: Can overlap with genuine medical diagnosis. No conscious feigning (unlike factitious disorder/malingering). Related: illness anxiety disorder (health anxiety - minimal symptoms but excessive health worry), functional neurological symptom disorder (conversion - motor/sensory symptoms inconsistent with recognised neurological disease). Mx: regular scheduled appointments (avoid dismissal), CBT, low-dose TCA/SSRI, physiotherapy for functional motor symptoms.

conditions.name: Tourette syndrome
conditions.summary: Multiple motor tics + ≥1 vocal tic, present >1 yr, onset <18 y. Tics: sudden, rapid, repetitive, non-rhythmic; can be suppressed (with buildup of tension). Coprolalia/echolalia in minority (<15%). Associated: ADHD (60%), OCD (40%). Mx: psychoeducation; habit reversal therapy/CBIT (CBT-based, 1st-line non-pharma); pharmacological if impairing: alpha-2 agonists (guanfacine/clonidine), antipsychotics (fluphenazine, haloperidol, aripiprazole), topiramate.

conditions.name: Insomnia
conditions.summary: Difficulty initiating or maintaining sleep, or non-restorative sleep, ≥3 nights/wk for ≥3 mo, causing daytime impairment; despite adequate opportunity. Sx: Primary or comorbid (depression, anxiety, pain, sleep apnoea). Mx: CBT-I (sleep restriction, stimulus control, relaxation) is gold-standard first-line - more effective and durable than pharmacotherapy. Mx: melatonin (circadian); low-dose doxepin; suvorexant/lemborexant (orexin antagonists); Z-drugs (short-term only); avoid long-term benzodiazepines (dependence, falls risk).

conditions.name: Herpes zoster
conditions.summary: Reactivation of latent VZV from dorsal root ganglia. Risk: advancing age, immunosuppression. Sx: Prodrome: dermatomal pain/dysaesthesia → unilateral vesicular rash in dermatomal distribution (thoracic most common). Complications: post-herpetic neuralgia (PHN, most common), zoster ophthalmicus (CN V1, ↑risk keratitis/blindness), Ramsay Hunt syndrome (CN VII: facial palsy + ear vesicles + sensorineural hearing loss). Mx: aciclovir/valaciclovir within 72 h (reduces duration/severity); amitriptyline/gabapentin for PHN. Mx (prevention): recombinant zoster vaccine (Shingrix, 2 doses) in ≥50 y.

conditions.name: Varicella
conditions.summary: Primary VZV infection; highly contagious. Incubation 10-21 d; prodrome then crops of vesicles (dew-drops on rose petal) at different stages of evolution. Complications: secondary bacterial infection (GAS, S. aureus), pneumonia (adults, pregnant), encephalitis, cerebellar ataxia. Congenital varicella syndrome (1st-2nd trimester). Mx: aciclovir in high-risk (adults, immunocompromised, neonates, pregnant); VZIG for post-exposure prophylaxis in susceptible high-risk. Mx (prevention): VZV vaccine.

conditions.name: Candidiasis
conditions.summary: Candida spp. (most often C. albicans) infection. Mx: Superficial: oral thrush (white plaques, wipe off leaving erythema; immunosuppressed, inhaled steroids, ABx); oesophageal candidiasis (AIDS-defining); vaginal (vulvovaginal candidiasis - itching, curd-like discharge, pH <4.5; risk: ABx, diabetes, pregnancy). Invasive (candidaemia): critically ill, IV access, broad-spectrum ABx - high mortality. Mx: topical nystatin/azole (superficial); fluconazole oral for vaginal/oral; echinocandin (caspofungin) 1st-line for candidaemia.

conditions.name: Aspergillosis
conditions.summary: Aspergillus spp. Spectrum: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA - asthma/CF patients, eosinophilia, ↑IgE, central bronchiectasis; Mx: steroids + itraconazole); chronic pulmonary (aspergilloma - fungus ball in pre-existing cavity, haemoptysis; Mx: surgical or voriconazole); invasive (profoundly immunocompromised - neutropenia, HSCT; angioinvasion → haemoptysis, halo sign on CT; Mx: voriconazole 1st-line; isavuconazole alternative; high mortality).

conditions.name: Legionnaire's disease
conditions.summary: Legionella pneumophila; water-borne (cooling towers, hospital water systems, spa pools). Sx: Pontiac fever (mild, self-limited flu-like). Ix: Legionnaire's disease: severe CAP with relative bradycardia, GI Sx, hyponatraemia, ↑LFTs, ↑CK, confusion. Urinary Legionella antigen (L. pneumophila sg1 only; rapid, widely used). Intracellular organism → macrolide or fluoroquinolone (NOT β-lactam alone). Notifiable disease.

conditions.name: Tetanus
conditions.summary: Clostridium tetani neurotoxin (tetanospasmin) blocks GABA/glycine release → sustained muscle spasm. Generalised: trismus (lockjaw), risus sardonicus (grimace), opisthotonus, laryngospasm. Wounds: puncture, contaminated, devitalised tissue. Ix: clinical. Mx: human tetanus immunoglobulin (TIG), wound debridement, metronidazole, muscle relaxants/benzodiazepines, supportive (mechanical ventilation). Mx (prevention): tetanus toxoid immunisation (universal; booster every 10 y).

conditions.name: Botulism
conditions.summary: Clostridium botulinum neurotoxin blocks ACh release at NMJ → descending flaccid paralysis. Foodborne (canned/preserved food), wound (IVDU), infantile (honey, gut colonisation - most common in infants: constipation, hypotonia, poor feed). Sx: diplopia, dysarthria, dysphagia → limb weakness → respiratory failure; afebrile, alert, descending pattern. Mx: antitoxin (early); supportive ventilation; wound debridement. Do NOT give antibiotics for infantile (lyse bacteria releasing more toxin).

conditions.name: Dengue fever
conditions.summary: Flavivirus; Aedes mosquito. Endemic tropics/subtropics. Dengue fever: sudden fever, retro-orbital headache, severe myalgia/arthralgia ('breakbone fever'), maculopapular rash, leucopenia, thrombocytopenia. Dengue haemorrhagic fever/dengue shock syndrome: capillary leakage, haemorrhage, shock - warning signs: abdominal pain, vomiting, mucosal bleeding, rapid clinical deterioration. Ix: NS1 antigen (early) or IgM/IgG. Mx: supportive; careful IV fluid management; no aspirin/NSAIDs (↑bleeding). No specific antiviral.

conditions.name: Typhoid fever
conditions.summary: Salmonella typhi (or paratyphi) via faecal-oral route. Stepwise fever, relative bradycardia, rose spots (salmon-coloured macules on trunk), constipation then diarrhoea, hepatosplenomegaly, leucopenia. Complications: intestinal perforation/haemorrhage, encephalopathy. Ix: blood culture (gold standard weeks 1-2); bone marrow culture most sensitive. Mx: ceftriaxone or azithromycin (reduced fluoroquinolone sensitivity); dexamethasone for severe disease. Mx (prevention): typhoid vaccine + food/water hygiene.

conditions.name: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
conditions.summary: Pathological systemic thrombin activation → simultaneous microvascular thrombosis + consumption of clotting factors/platelets → haemorrhage. Triggers: sepsis (most common), obstetric emergencies (placental abruption, amniotic fluid embolism), trauma, malignancy, transfusion reactions. Ix: ↓platelets, ↑PT/aPTT, ↑D-dimer, ↓fibrinogen, schistocytes. Mx: treat underlying cause; component replacement (FFP, cryoprecipitate, platelets) for bleeding; LMWH/heparin for predominant thrombotic DIC.

conditions.name: Autoimmune haemolytic anaemia
conditions.summary: Immune-mediated RBC destruction. Warm AIHA (IgG, splenic destruction): most common; idiopathic, or secondary to CLL, SLE, drugs. Positive DAT (Coombs). Ix: Cold agglutinin disease (IgM, complement): cold exposure triggers; Mycoplasma, EBV, lymphoma. Sx: anaemia, jaundice, haemoglobinuria (if intravascular). Ix: ↑LDH, ↑bilirubin, ↓haptoglobin. Mx: Mx (warm): prednisolone 1st-line; rituximab, splenectomy for steroid-resistant. Cold: avoid cold, rituximab.

conditions.name: Myelodysplastic syndrome
conditions.summary: Clonal HSC disorder: cytopenias + dysplastic haematopoiesis, ↑risk of transformation to AML (~30%). Risk: prior chemotherapy/radiation, benzene, older age. Sx: fatigue (anaemia), infections (neutropenia), bleeding (thrombocytopenia). Ix: bone marrow biopsy (dysplastic cells, ↑blasts <20%). IPSS-R for risk stratification. Mx: low-risk: EPO, G-CSF, lenalidomide (del5q), azacitidine; high-risk: azacitidine ± venetoclax; allogeneic HSCT (potentially curative) for high-risk in fit patients.

conditions.name: Pemphigus vulgaris
conditions.summary: Life-threatening autoimmune intra-epidermal blistering disease; anti-desmoglein 1 and 3 IgG antibodies. Flaccid blisters that rupture easily → painful erosions on skin and mucous membranes (mouth often first). Nikolsky sign positive (skin slips off with lateral pressure). Ix: skin biopsy + immunofluorescence (IgG at cell surface). Mx: systemic steroids + rituximab (now preferred) or immunosuppressants (azathioprine, mycophenolate, cyclophosphamide); mortality significant pre-steroid era.
utd: clinical features and diagnosis of Pemphigus vulgaris

conditions.name: Bullous pemphigoid
conditions.summary: Most common autoimmune blistering disease; predominantly elderly. Anti-BP180 and anti-BP230 IgG against hemidesmosomal proteins. Mx: Tense (not flaccid) blisters - subepidermal; oral mucosa less commonly affected. Intense itch ± urticarial prodrome. Nikolsky sign negative. DIF: linear IgG and C3 at DEJ. Mx: potent topical steroids (clobetasol) for limited disease; systemic prednisolone ± doxycycline; rituximab or immunosuppressants for severe/refractory.
utd: clinical features and diagnosis of Bullous pemphigoid

conditions.name: Vitiligo
conditions.summary: Autoimmune destruction of melanocytes → depigmented macules/patches with clearly demarcated edges. Any skin site, often acral, periorificial; Koebner phenomenon. Associated: other autoimmune conditions (thyroid disease, T1DM, Addison, pernicious anaemia). Ix: clinical; Wood's lamp (cream-white fluorescence). Mx: topical corticosteroids (1st-line), tacrolimus, ruxolitinib cream; narrow-band UVB phototherapy; oral JAK inhibitors (ritlecitinib) for extensive disease; PUVA.
utd: clinical features and diagnosis of Vitiligo

conditions.name: Impetigo
conditions.summary: Superficial bacterial skin infection. Non-bullous (most common, golden honey-crust erosions, S. pyogenes ± S. aureus) and bullous (S. aureus toxin, large flaccid bullae → thin lacquer crust). Highly contagious; children > adults; warm humid conditions. Complications: post-streptococcal GN (non-bullous). Mx: localised: topical fusidic acid or mupirocin; widespread: oral flucloxacillin/cefalexin (cover S. aureus); no benefit for routine nasal swab in adults.
utd: clinical features and diagnosis of Impetigo

conditions.name: Seborrheic dermatitis
conditions.summary: Chronic relapsing inflammatory condition of sebum-rich areas (scalp, face - nasolabial folds, eyebrows, ears). Malassezia yeast implicated. Sx: erythematous patches with greasy yellowish scale, pruritus. Infantile: cradle cap (benign, resolves). Adult: dandruff (mild). Associated with Parkinson disease, HIV, immunosuppression. Mx: antifungal shampoo/cream (ketoconazole, selenium sulfide, zinc pyrithione) ± topical low-potency steroids; calcineurin inhibitors for face.
utd: clinical features and diagnosis of Seborrheic dermatitis

conditions.name: Dermatitis herpetiformis
conditions.summary: IgA-mediated dermatosis, pathognomonic extraintestinal manifestation of coeliac disease; virtually all patients have gluten-sensitive enteropathy. Intensely pruritic vesicles on extensor surfaces (elbows, knees, buttocks, back). Ix: skin biopsy (granular IgA deposits at dermoepidermal junction). Mx: strict gluten-free diet (eventually clears skin and gut lesion); dapsone for rapid itch relief while diet takes effect; monitor for haemolytic anaemia (dapsone SE).
utd: clinical features and diagnosis of Dermatitis herpetiformis

conditions.name: Hidradenitis suppurativa
conditions.summary: Chronic debilitating follicular disorder of apocrine gland-bearing skin (axillae, groin, inframammary, perianal). Painful nodules, abscesses, sinus tracts, scarring. Hurley staging (I-III). Associated: metabolic syndrome, IBD (Crohn), smoking. Mx: long-term antibiotics (tetracyclines, clindamycin-rifampicin); adalimumab or secukinumab (biologics); intralesional steroids for acute; surgical deroofing/wide excision for severe.
utd: clinical features and diagnosis of Hidradenitis suppurativa

conditions.name: Paget disease of bone
conditions.summary: Focal disorder of abnormal bone remodelling (↑osteoclast activity → disorganised woven bone). Axial skeleton, skull, femur. Usually asymptomatic; ↑↑ALP (most specific lab finding) with normal Ca/phosphate. Sx: bone pain, deformity (bowing tibia, enlarged skull), pathological fracture, hearing loss (skull involvement → CN VIII compression), high-output HF (hypervascular bone). ↑risk osteosarcoma (1%). Mx: bisphosphonate (zoledronate, single infusion) for symptomatic/active disease.

treatment of Paget disease of bone

conditions.name: Osteosarcoma
conditions.summary: Most common primary malignant bone tumour in adolescents; metaphysis of long bones (distal femur, proximal tibia, proximal humerus). Sunburst appearance + Codman triangle on X-ray. ↑ALP. Ix: MRI + CT chest (pulmonary mets) + biopsy. Mx: limb-sparing surgery + neoadjuvant + adjuvant chemotherapy (HDMTX, cisplatin, doxorubicin, ifosfamide); pulmonary metastasectomy. 5-yr survival: ~70% localised; <30% metastatic.

conditions.name: Spinal stenosis
conditions.summary: Narrowing of spinal canal → neural compression. Lumbar most common; degenerative (disc herniation, facet hypertrophy, ligamentum flavum hypertrophy, spondylolisthesis). Sx: Neurogenic claudication: bilateral leg pain/numbness/weakness worse with walking/extension, relieved by flexion (forward-lean, cycling). Unlike vascular claudication: pulses preserved, better with forward lean. MRI gold standard. Mx: physiotherapy, analgesics; epidural steroid injections; decompressive laminectomy for significant functional limitation.

conditions.name: Lumbar disc herniation
conditions.summary: Protrusion of nucleus pulposus through annulus fibrosus. Sx: L4-5 (L5 radiculopathy: dorsiflexion weakness, lateral foot sensory loss) and L5-S1 (S1 radiculopathy: plantarflexion weakness, lateral/plantar foot sensory loss, absent ankle reflex) most common. Straight leg raise test (sensitive for L4-5, L5-S1). MRI diagnostic. Mx: analgesia (NSAIDs), physiotherapy; most resolve in 6-12 wk. Sx: Epidural injection for radicular pain. Microdiscectomy if severe neurological deficit or cauda equina syndrome.

conditions.name: Plantar fasciitis
conditions.summary: Most common cause of heel pain; degeneration/inflammation of plantar fascia at calcaneal insertion. Risk: obesity, prolonged standing, tight Achilles, pes planus/cavus. Sx: worst in first steps in morning or after rest, improves with walking. Point tenderness over medial calcaneal tuberosity. Ix: clinical; US or MRI if diagnosis unclear. Mx: stretching exercises (Achilles + plantar fascia), orthotic insoles, NSAIDs; corticosteroid injection; extracorporeal shockwave therapy (refractory); PRP emerging.

conditions.name: Avascular necrosis
conditions.summary: Ischaemic death of bone tissue. Femoral head most common; also humeral head, femoral condyles, talus, scaphoid. Risk: corticosteroids (most common non-traumatic cause), alcohol, SLE, sickle cell, Gaucher, diving (decompression sickness), trauma. Sx: groin/hip pain, progressive if untreated → joint collapse. MRI (gold standard, earliest detection): subchondral signal changes. Mx: early: joint-preserving (core decompression, bisphosphonates controversial); established collapse: total hip replacement.

conditions.name: Dupuytren contracture
conditions.summary: Progressive fibroproliferative disease of palmar fascia → flexion contracture of fingers (ring and little finger most common). Risk: Northern European descent, male, age >40, diabetes, alcohol, anti-epileptics, HIV. Ix: clinical - pitting, nodules, cords in palm; table-top test positive (cannot flatten hand). Mx: observation if mild; collagenase clostridium histolyticum injection (Xiapex) for moderate contracture (MCP joint); needle aponeurotomy; surgical fasciectomy for severe.

conditions.name: Rotator cuff tear
conditions.summary: Tear of supraspinatus (most common), infraspinatus, teres minor, or subscapularis. Traumatic (acute, young patient) or degenerative (chronic, middle-aged+). Sx: shoulder pain, weakness with overhead activities, painful arc (60-120°). Hawkins, Neer tests. Empty can (supraspinatus), external rotation lag (infraspinatus), belly-press/lift-off (subscapularis). MRI diagnostic. Mx: physiotherapy + NSAIDs (partial tears); corticosteroid injection; surgical repair for full-thickness tears with significant dysfunction, especially in active/young.

conditions.name: Febrile seizures
conditions.summary: Seizures associated with fever (>38°C) in children 6 mo–5 y without CNS infection/prior afebrile seizure. Simple febrile seizure: generalised, <15 min, single in 24 h; benign, ↑recurrence risk (30%). Complex febrile seizure: focal, >15 min, >1 in 24 h; higher risk evaluation. LP if meningism or very young (<12 mo). Mx: acute: benzodiazepine if >5 min. Antipyretics don't prevent recurrence. No prophylactic AEDs routinely. 1-2% develop epilepsy.

conditions.name: Cerebral palsy
conditions.summary: Non-progressive disorder of movement/posture from early brain injury/malformation. Types: spastic (most common, upper motor neuron), dyskinetic/athetoid (basal ganglia), ataxic (cerebellum), mixed. Causes: periventricular leukomalacia (preterm), hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy, kernicterus, congenital infection. Associated: intellectual disability, epilepsy, visual/hearing impairment, communication difficulties. Mx: physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy; baclofen/botulinum toxin for spasticity; orthopaedic surgery for contractures.

conditions.name: Neural tube defect
conditions.summary: Failure of neural tube closure at 3-4 wk. Anencephaly (lethal, absent forebrain/skull vault). Sx: Spina bifida: spina bifida occulta (asymptomatic skin dimple, tufted hair) → meningocele (meninges herniate) → myelomeningocele (meninges + neural tissue herniate; cause of significant disability - lower limb paralysis, bladder/bowel dysfunction, hydrocephalus/Arnold-Chiari II). Mx (prevention): periconceptional folic acid (400 µg → 5 mg in high-risk). Mx: surgical closure within 24-48 h of birth; VP shunt.

conditions.name: Neonatal jaundice
conditions.summary: Visible jaundice in >50% term neonates. Physiological: peaks day 3-5, resolves by day 10 - immature hepatic conjugation. Pathological (first 24 h or prolonged >2 wk): haemolytic (Rh incompatibility, ABO incompatibility, G6PD, spherocytosis), infection, biliary atresia (conjugated - pale stools, dark urine, must exclude). Ix: Monitor bilirubin with transcutaneous/serum levels + plot on nomogram. Mx: phototherapy; exchange transfusion for very high levels. Ix: Kernicterus (unconjugated bilirubin penetrates BBB) → permanent neurological damage.

conditions.name: Developmental dysplasia of the hip
conditions.summary: Spectrum from dysplasia to frank dislocation; abnormal development of hip joint (acetabulum/femoral head). Risk: female, firstborn, breech, oligohydramnios, family history, left hip. Ix: Clinical screening: Barlow (posterior push → dislocatable hip) and Ortolani (abduction → reduces dislocated hip) in neonates (useful <3 months); Galeazzi (unequal knee height, shortened femur - unilateral DDH), limited abduction (older infant). USS hip (Grafen method): gold standard screening in high-risk infants; X-ray (>4-6 months when ossification occurs). Mx: Pavlik harness (6-9 months - early mild DDH, reduces hip into acetabulum); spica cast; closed reduction + arthrogram (failed harness); open reduction + osteotomy (older children/failed closed reduction). Untreated → osteoarthritis.
