conditions.name: Hirschsprung disease
conditions.summary: Congenital absence of Auerbach and Meissner plexus ganglia in distal colon (rectosigmoid 75%) → functional obstruction. Associated with Down syndrome. Sx: failure to pass meconium in first 48 h, progressive abdominal distension, bilious vomiting. Enterocolitis is a life-threatening complication. Ix: contrast enema (transition zone, rectosigmoid ratio >1:1 suggests Hirschsprung), rectal suction biopsy (absent ganglia, gold standard). Mx: surgical pull-through procedure.

conditions.name: Congenital hypothyroidism
conditions.summary: Most common preventable cause of intellectual disability. Thyroid dysgenesis (75%) or dyshormogenesis. Ix: Newborn screening (TSH/T4 heel-prick) essential - untreated leads to cretinism (profound ID, short stature, deafness). Sx: Subtle signs in neonate: prolonged jaundice, constipation, coarse cry, poor feeding, macroglossia, umbilical hernia, posterior fontanelle open. Mx: levothyroxine started within first 2 wk of life; dose guided by T4/TSH monitoring. Normal development with early treatment.

conditions.name: Hyperemesis gravidarum
conditions.summary: Severe nausea and vomiting in pregnancy causing dehydration, weight loss (>5% body weight), electrolyte imbalance, ketonuria; affects 0.3-2% pregnancies. Distinguished from common morning sickness by severity and complications. Risk: multiple pregnancy, hydatidiform mole, first pregnancy, ↑BMI, H. pylori infection, family/personal history. Pathophysiology: hCG + serotonin + oestrogen dysregulation; GDF15 (growth differentiation factor 15) recently identified as key mediator. Complications: Wernicke encephalopathy (thiamine deficiency - give IV thiamine/Pabrinex before glucose infusion), mallory-weiss tears, oesophageal rupture, Boerhaave, fetal growth restriction (prolonged HG), maternal weight loss, psychological distress (↑risk of depression/anxiety, PTSD, termination). PUQE score (pregnancy unique quantification of emesis). Ix: clinical + ketonuria; TFTs (transient gestational hyperthyroidism - treat HG not thyroid); USS (multiple/molar pregnancy). Mx: early outpatient: ginger, vitamin B6; antiemetics (domperidone, cyclizine, metoclopramide, ondansetron - all evidence of safety in pregnancy; prochlorperazine); IV rehydration + thiamine + antiemetics (hospital); steroids (prednisolone, methylprednisolone for refractory); nutritional support (enteral NG feeds if persistent); thalidomide NEVER.

conditions.name: Postpartum depression
conditions.summary: Depressive episode within 4 wk (DSM-5) to 12 mo post-delivery. Distinct from baby blues (days 2-5, self-limiting). Risk: prior MDD/PPD, lack of social support, poor marital relationship, stressful life events, unplanned pregnancy. Sx: persistent low mood, tearfulness, inability to bond, anxiety, guilt, suicidal ideation. Mx: psychotherapy (CBT, IPT) ± SSRI (sertraline/paroxetine safe in breastfeeding); brexanolone IV (neurosteroid) for severe. Screen all women with Edinburgh PND Scale.

conditions.name: Mastitis
conditions.summary: Breast inflammation; most common during breastfeeding (lactational mastitis). S. aureus most common organism (enters via nipple fissure). Sx: localised breast pain, erythema, induration, fever. May progress to breast abscess (fluctuant, requires US-guided aspiration ± surgical drainage). Mx: continue breastfeeding (empties breast); analgesia; antibiotics (flucloxacillin 10-14 d; erythromycin if PCN-allergic); ensure latch assessed; rule out inflammatory breast cancer if recurrent/non-lactational.

conditions.name: Vulvovaginal candidiasis
conditions.summary: Candida albicans most common; symptomatic in ~75% women at some point. Sx: vulval itching/soreness, non-offensive thick white curd-like discharge, superficial dyspareunia, dysuria. pH <4.5 (unlike BV). Risk: ABx, pregnancy, DM, immunosuppression, OCP. Ix: clinical; high-vaginal swab if recurrent or uncertain. Mx: single-dose oral fluconazole 150 mg (avoid in pregnancy) or topical clotrimazole; recurrent (≥4/yr): 6-month maintenance fluconazole weekly.

conditions.name: Preterm labor
conditions.summary: Labour with regular uterine contractions + cervical change between 20-37 wk. Risk: prior preterm birth (highest predictor), short cervix, infection/BV, multiple gestation, polyhydramnios, uterine anomaly, smoking. Ix: fetal fibronectin (high NPV if negative ≤22-34 wk) + cervical length US. Mx: if <34 wk: antenatal corticosteroids (fetal lung maturity), MgSO4 for neuroprotection if <32 wk, tocolysis (nifedipine, atosiban - short-term to allow corticosteroids), GBS prophylaxis.

conditions.name: Otitis externa
conditions.summary: Infection/inflammation of external auditory canal. Bacterial (Pseudomonas aeruginosa, S. aureus) most common; fungal (Aspergillus, Candida) in immunocompromised. Risk: water exposure (swimming), trauma (cotton buds), hearing aid use. Sx: otalgia (worse with pinna movement), discharge, canal oedema/erythema; aural fullness. Malignant (necrotising) OE: elderly/diabetic → bone/cartilage invasion, CN palsy, osteomyelitis. Mx: aural toilet, topical antibiotic-steroid drops (ciprofloxacin + dexamethasone); oral abx/IV for malignant OE.

conditions.name: Meniere disease
conditions.summary: Sx (triad): episodic true vertigo (>20 min), fluctuating low-frequency sensorineural hearing loss, tinnitus ± aural fullness. Cause: endolymphatic hydrops. Attacks can be frequent then enter remission. Audiogram: low-frequency SNHL. Ix: clinical (AAO criteria). Mx: dietary sodium restriction + diuretics (bendroflumethiazide/acetazolamide); acute attack: vestibular suppressants (prochlorperazine, benzodiazepines); gentamicin IT injections (ablative) or endolymphatic sac decompression for refractory.

conditions.name: Acoustic neuroma
conditions.summary: Benign Schwann-cell tumour of CN VIII (vestibulocochlear nerve), usually arising from superior vestibular branch. Association with NF2 (bilateral). Sx: unilateral progressive SNHL (commonest presentation), tinnitus, unsteadiness; large tumours: CN V (facial numbness), CN VII (facial palsy), ↑ICP, cerebellar signs. Ix: MRI with gadolinium (gold standard). Mx (options): observation with serial MRI; stereotactic radiosurgery (Gamma Knife); microsurgical excision.

conditions.name: Thyroid eye disease
conditions.summary: Autoimmune orbital inflammation associated with Graves disease (not exclusively); TSH receptor antibodies activate orbital fibroblasts. Sx: periorbital oedema, conjunctival injection, proptosis (exophthalmos), lid retraction, lid lag (von Graefe sign), diplopia (↑muscle oedema), corneal exposure, ↑IOP. Sight-threatening: optic neuropathy (↓VA, visual field defect, RAPD), corneal ulceration. CAS score. Mx: smoking cessation (modifiable risk), selenium; IV methylprednisolone (active moderate-severe); orbital decompression, squint surgery, lid surgery as needed.

conditions.name: Diabetic retinopathy
conditions.summary: Microvascular complication of DM; leading cause of blindness in working-age adults. Non-proliferative (NPDR): microaneurysms, dot-blot haemorrhages, hard exudates, cotton-wool spots. Proliferative (PDR): new vessel formation → vitreous haemorrhage, retinal detachment. Sx: Diabetic macular oedema (DMO): central vision loss. Risk: duration of DM, poor glycaemic control, HTN. Ix: Annual diabetic eye screening. Mx: optimise glycaemia/BP/lipids; intravitreal anti-VEGF (ranibizumab, aflibercept) for DMO and PDR; pan-retinal photocoagulation for PDR.

conditions.name: IgA nephropathy
conditions.summary: Most common primary glomerulonephritis worldwide. IgA immune complexes deposit in mesangium → activation. Sx: synpharyngitic macroscopic haematuria (haematuria concurrent with URTI - unlike post-strep which is 10-14 d later); persistent microscopic haematuria ± proteinuria. Ix: renal biopsy (mesangial IgA on immunofluorescence). Prognosis variable: 20-40% reach ESRD over 20 yr. Mx: ACE-i/ARB (proteinuria, BP control); steroids for significant proteinuria/proliferative pattern; SGLT2i emerging; fish oil.

conditions.name: Membranous nephropathy
conditions.summary: Most common cause of nephrotic syndrome in white adults. Ix: Primary: anti-PLA2R antibodies (70-80%); secondary: malignancy (lung, colon), SLE, hepatitis B, NSAIDs, gold. Sub-epithelial immune deposits → spike-and-dome pattern on EM. 1/3 remit spontaneously; 1/3 stable; 1/3 → ESRD. Mx: ACE-i/ARB for all; immunosuppression for persistent proteinuria (steroids + cyclophosphamide / rituximab for PLA2R+); treat secondary causes.

conditions.name: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis
conditions.summary: Most common cause of nephrotic syndrome in Black adults; leading cause of ESRD from GN in USA. Podocyte injury → segmental sclerosis. Primary (idiopathic, NPHS2/ACTN4 mutations); secondary: obesity (adaptive), HIV, heroin, reflux nephropathy, reduced nephron mass. Mx: High-dose steroids 1st-line; calcineurin inhibitors for steroid-resistant; rituximab; high recurrence rate post-transplant (circulating permeability factor).

conditions.name: Minimal change disease
conditions.summary: Most common nephrotic syndrome in children (<8 yr, >80%); also adults (15-25%). Effacement of podocyte foot processes on EM - light microscopy normal, no deposits on IF. Cause usually idiopathic; secondary: NSAIDs, lithium, lymphoma (Hodgkin). Sx: Presents as pure nephrotic syndrome with severe oedema. Steroid-responsive in >90% children; relapses common. Mx: prednisolone; cyclophosphamide/calcineurin inhibitors for frequent relapsers/steroid-dependent.
utd: minimal change disease nephrotic syndrome children

conditions.name: Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis
conditions.summary: Type III hypersensitivity 10-14 days after streptococcal pharyngitis or 3-6 wk after skin infection (impetigo). Children most commonly affected. Sx: Abrupt onset nephritic syndrome: haematuria (cola-coloured urine), oedema, HTN, oliguria, proteinuria. ↓C3, normal C4. Elevated ASO titre or anti-DNase B. Prognosis generally excellent in children; adults more risk of residual renal impairment. Mx: supportive (salt/fluid restriction, antihypertensives, diuretics); antibiotics for ongoing infection.

conditions.name: Goodpasture syndrome
conditions.summary: Anti-GBM antibodies (α3-chain of type IV collagen) → rapidly progressive GN ± pulmonary haemorrhage. Male predominance; bimodal age (20-30, 60-70). Sx: Pulmonary-renal syndrome: haemoptysis + nephritis. Ix: Anti-GBM antibodies in serum + linear IgG on IF (biopsy). ANCA positive in 30% (double-positive: worse prognosis). Mx: urgent plasmapheresis (remove antibodies) + cyclophosphamide + steroids. Sx: Outcome dependent on creatinine at presentation; dialysis-dependent at onset rarely recovers renal function.

conditions.name: Rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis
conditions.summary: Nephritic syndrome with rapid loss of renal function over days-weeks; crescents on biopsy (parietal epithelial cell proliferation). Three types: Type I (anti-GBM, 10-20%): Goodpasture; Type II (immune-complex, 40%): post-strep, lupus, IgA, cryoglobulin; Type III (pauci-immune, ANCA-associated, ~50%): GPA, MPA, EGPA. Emergency: early aggressive immunosuppression (steroids + cyclophosphamide ± plasmapheresis) to prevent irreversible dialysis dependence.

conditions.name: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
conditions.summary: ANCA-associated small-vessel vasculitis (c-ANCA/PR3-ANCA). Classic triad: upper respiratory tract (sinusitis, nasal septum perforation, saddle-nose deformity, otitis media), lower respiratory tract (pulmonary nodules, cavitating lesions, alveolar haemorrhage), rapidly progressive GN. Also: orbital pseudotumour, scleritis. CXR/CT: bilateral nodules ± cavitation. Ix: c-ANCA/PR3 + biopsy (granulomatous necrotising vasculitis). Mx: remission induction - rituximab or cyclophosphamide + high-dose steroids; maintenance: azathioprine/rituximab.
utd: initial treatment of Granulomatosis with polyangiitis

conditions.name: Microscopic polyangiitis
conditions.summary: ANCA-associated pauci-immune small-vessel vasculitis (p-ANCA/MPO-ANCA). No granulomas (distinguishes from GPA). Pulmonary-renal syndrome common; also cutaneous purpura, mononeuritis multiplex. Alveolar haemorrhage can be life-threatening. Ix: p-ANCA/MPO + biopsy. Mx: same as GPA - rituximab or cyclophosphamide + steroids; maintenance azathioprine/rituximab.

conditions.name: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis
conditions.summary: ANCA-associated vasculitis with three phases: allergic rhinitis/polyposis → asthma → eosinophilic tissue infiltration + vasculitis. p-ANCA/MPO in ~40%. Ix: Eosinophilia (>1.5×10⁹/L), asthma, and ≥2 of: eosinophilic infiltration on biopsy, neuropathy, migratory/transient pulmonary infiltrates, paranasal sinus abnormality, ≥10% eosinophils. Cardiac involvement (eosinophilic myocarditis) determines prognosis. Mx: steroids; cyclophosphamide for refractory/severe; mepolizumab for relapsing disease.

conditions.name: Takayasu arteritis
conditions.summary: Granulomatous large-vessel vasculitis of aorta and its major branches; young women of Asian descent (15-40 yr). Sx: constitutional (pre-pulseless phase), then limb claudication, bruits, absent/unequal pulses, BP differential between arms, hypertension (renovascular), angina. ↑ESR/CRP; imaging (MRA, CTA, PET-CT) shows wall thickening/stenosis/occlusion/aneurysm. Mx: high-dose steroids; methotrexate or azathioprine for steroid-sparing; tocilizumab; revascularisation in quiescent phase.

conditions.name: Behçet disease
conditions.summary: Systemic vasculitis of unknown aetiology; HLA-B51 association; young adults, Middle East/Asia. Mx: Recurrent oral ulcers (major criterion) + ≥2 of: genital ulcers, pathergy (skin hyperreactivity), eye lesions (posterior uveitis/retinal vasculitis - major cause of blindness), skin lesions (erythema nodosum, pseudofolliculitis). Also: GI ulcers, neurological (neuro-Behçet), venous thrombosis (DVT, cerebral venous sinus). Mx: colchicine (mucocutaneous); steroids; azathioprine/TNF inhibitors for severe disease.

conditions.name: Polyarteritis nodosa
conditions.summary: Necrotising vasculitis of medium-sized arteries; no glomerulonephritis, no ANCA. Associated with hepatitis B (30%). Sx: fever, weight loss, livedo reticularis, mononeuritis multiplex, renal artery involvement (HTN, infarcts), mesenteric infarction, testicular pain, skin nodules/ulcers. No pulmonary involvement. Ix: angiography (microaneurysms, beading) or biopsy of affected tissue. Mx: steroids ± cyclophosphamide; antiviral therapy (interferon + lamivudine) for HBV-associated.

conditions.name: Antiphospholipid syndrome
conditions.summary: Autoimmune hypercoagulable state; aPL antibodies (lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin IgG/IgM, anti-β2GPI). Sx: arterial/venous thrombosis (stroke, DVT, PE, retinal vein occlusion) ± obstetric morbidity (recurrent miscarriage, stillbirth, preeclampsia, IUGR). Secondary (with SLE most common) or primary. aPL must be positive on ≥2 occasions ≥12 wk apart (Sapporo criteria). Mx: warfarin (INR 2-3 for venous; 2.5-3.5 for arterial); low-dose aspirin; LMWH + aspirin for obstetric APS; avoid DOACs in thrombotic APS.

conditions.name: Mixed connective tissue disease
conditions.summary: Overlap syndrome with features of SLE, scleroderma, myositis, and RA; high-titre anti-U1-RNP antibodies. Sx: Raynaud phenomenon (hallmark, often first), hand swelling, arthritis, myositis, oesophageal dysmotility, serositis, pulmonary arterial hypertension (major cause of mortality). ANA positive; anti-dsDNA and anti-Sm usually negative. Mx: treat predominant manifestations; hydroxychloroquine (baseline); PAH monitoring and targeted treatment.

conditions.name: Adult-onset Still disease
conditions.summary: Rare systemic inflammatory disorder; diagnosis of exclusion. Sx: Quotidian fever (spiking ≥39°C, often evening, returning to normal), salmon-pink evanescent rash (coincides with fever), arthritis, and ≥2 of: lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, serositis, pharyngitis. ↑↑Ferritin (>10,000 diagnostic if other causes excluded). Rf and ANA usually negative. Complications: macrophage activation syndrome (MAS). Mx: NSAIDs; steroids; IL-1 inhibitors (anakinra, canakinumab) and IL-6 inhibitors (tocilizumab) for refractory.
utd: initial treatment of Adult-onset Still disease

conditions.name: Relapsing polychondritis
conditions.summary: Episodic inflammation and destruction of cartilaginous structures. Auricular chondritis (painful, swollen red pinna - spares non-cartilaginous lobe) most common; also nasal, tracheal, laryngeal chondritis (airway collapse - life-threatening), arthritis, eye (episcleritis, scleritis), cardiovascular (aortic regurgitation). Associated with MDS. Ix: clinical (McAdam criteria). Mx: NSAIDs for mild; steroids; dapsone; immunosuppressants for severe tracheal/cardiac involvement.

conditions.name: Mitral valve prolapse
conditions.summary: Billowing of mitral valve leaflet(s) into LA during systole; most common valvular abnormality. Most asymptomatic. Classic auscultatory finding: mid-systolic click ± late systolic murmur (MR). Complications: mitral regurgitation (significant in ~5%), infective endocarditis, arrhythmias (SVT, VT), rarely sudden cardiac death. Associated: Marfan, Ehlers-Danlos, hyperthyroidism. Sx: atypical chest pain, palpitations, anxiety. Mx: observation for most; β-blocker for symptomatic arrhythmias; surgery for severe MR.

conditions.name: Sick sinus syndrome
conditions.summary: Intrinsic sinus node dysfunction causing inappropriate bradycardia, sinoatrial block, sinus arrest, or alternating tachy-brady. Causes: fibrosis/ischaemia of SA node, drugs (digoxin, amiodarone, β-blocker, CCB). Sx: palpitations, presyncope, syncope, fatigue. Ix (ECG): sinus pauses, junctional escapes, AF/flutter alternating with sinus bradycardia. Mx: avoid bradycardic drugs; permanent pacemaker is definitive; anticoagulation if AF component.

conditions.name: Superior vena cava syndrome
conditions.summary: Obstruction of SVC → impaired venous return from head/neck/upper limbs. Causes: malignancy (lung cancer 60%, lymphoma 10%, other thoracic tumours) > thrombosis (central venous catheters, pacemaker leads). Sx: facial oedema, plethora, neck vein distension, arm oedema, headache, dyspnoea, visual changes; severe: ↑ICP, stridor. Ix: CT chest with contrast. Mx: treat underlying malignancy (radiotherapy, chemotherapy, stenting); endovascular stenting for rapid symptom relief; anticoagulation for thrombotic cause.
utd: superior vena cava syndrome clinical features diagnosis

conditions.name: Bradycardia
conditions.summary: Heart rate <60 bpm. Physiological (athletes, sleep, vagal tone). Pathological: AV block, sick sinus syndrome, hypothyroidism, hypothermia, ↑ICP (Cushing reflex), drugs (β-blockers, CCBs, digoxin, amiodarone). Sx: fatigue, presyncope, syncope, dyspnoea. Ix: Haemodynamically unstable: atropine 0.5 mg IV (repeat to 3 mg); transcutaneous then transvenous pacing if refractory; adrenaline/isoprenaline infusion as temporising measure. Permanent pacemaker if recurrent symptomatic bradycardia.

conditions.name: Graves disease
conditions.summary: Most common cause of hyperthyroidism; TSH-receptor stimulating IgG antibodies (TRAb/TSI). Diffuse goitre, ophthalmopathy (exophthalmos - see thyroid eye disease), pretibial myxoedema (rare). ↓TSH, ↑fT4/fT3, +TRAb. Mx: antithyroid drugs (methimazole/carbimazole 1st-line; PTU in pregnancy 1st trimester); radioiodine ablation (definitive, avoid in ophthalmopathy); thyroidectomy. Euthyroid 12-18 mo treatment; ~50% relapse on stopping antithyroids.

conditions.name: Hashimoto thyroiditis
conditions.summary: Most common cause of hypothyroidism in developed countries. Autoimmune lymphocytic destruction of thyroid. Ix: ↑TPO antibodies (>95%), ↑Tg antibodies. ↑TSH, ↓fT4. Firm, non-tender goitre (early) or small atrophic thyroid (late). Associated with other autoimmune disease (T1DM, vitiligo, Addison, coeliac, SLE). Transient hyperthyroidism possible ('Hashitoxicosis'). Mx: levothyroxine when overt hypothyroidism develops (TSH >10); marginal hypothyroidism (TSH 4.5-10): treat if symptomatic or pregnant.

conditions.name: Subacute thyroiditis
conditions.summary: Viral (or post-viral)-triggered painful granulomatous thyroiditis. Sx: painful tender thyroid, fever, malaise; triphasic: hyperthyroid (follicle destruction releases stored hormone) → hypothyroid → return to normal. ↑ESR/CRP, ↓TSH initially, ↑fT4. ↓uptake on radionuclide scan (unlike Graves). Mx: NSAIDs/aspirin for pain; steroids if severe; β-blocker for hyperthyroid symptoms; levothyroxine in prolonged hypothyroid phase; usually self-limiting over weeks-months.

conditions.name: Adrenal crisis
conditions.summary: Life-threatening acute adrenal insufficiency. Triggers: physiological stress (surgery, illness, trauma) in patient with known or undiagnosed adrenal insufficiency, or abrupt steroid withdrawal. Sx: hypotension (may be refractory to fluids/vasopressors alone), vomiting, abdominal pain, fever, confusion, hypoglycaemia, hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia. Mx: IV hydrocortisone 100 mg STAT (then 50-100 mg 6-8 hrly or continuous infusion); 0.9% NaCl ± dextrose; do not delay treatment for investigations. Life-saving - every patient on long-term steroids needs a sick-day rule and medical alert.

conditions.name: Neurofibromatosis
conditions.summary: NF1 (chromosome 17, neurofibromin): café-au-lait spots (≥6, >5 mm prepubertal), axillary/inguinal freckling, Lisch nodules (iris hamartomas), neurofibromas (cutaneous, plexiform), optic glioma, bone dysplasia; malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumour (MPNST). NF2 (chromosome 22, merlin): bilateral vestibular schwannomas (hallmark), multiple meningiomas, ependymomas, posterior subcapsular lens opacity. Ix: clinical criteria. Mx: surgical excision of symptomatic/malignant tumours; bevacizumab for hearing preservation in NF2; MEK inhibitors (selumetinib) for plexiform NF1.

conditions.name: von Willebrand disease
conditions.summary: Most common inherited bleeding disorder. Ix: Deficiency/dysfunction of von Willebrand factor (vWF) → impaired platelet adhesion + reduced factor VIII. Mx: Type 1 (70%, quantitative ↓, mild): mucocutaneous bleeding (epistaxis, menorrhagia, easy bruising, post-surgical bleed). Type 2 (qualitative defects): subtypes 2A, 2B, 2M, 2N. Type 3 (severe, near-absent vWF): may resemble haemophilia. ↑APTT, ↑bleeding time, ↓ristocetin cofactor. Mx: desmopressin (DDAVP - releases stored vWF, type 1); vWF/VIII concentrate; tranexamic acid for mucosal bleeding.

conditions.name: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia
conditions.summary: Immune-mediated thrombocytopenia paradoxically causing thrombosis, not bleeding. Ix: IgG antibodies against PF4-heparin complex → platelet and endothelial activation. Onset: 5-14 d after heparin start (or earlier if prior exposure). Thrombocytopenia (platelets drop >50% or <150×10⁹/L) + thrombosis (venous or arterial - 'white clot syndrome'). 4Ts score for clinical probability. Mx: Confirm: anti-PF4-heparin ELISA + functional assay (SRA). Mx: stop ALL heparin immediately; start non-heparin anticoagulant (argatroban, fondaparinux, danaparoid, rivaroxaban); NO platelet transfusion (worsens thrombosis).

conditions.name: Paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria
conditions.summary: Acquired clonal disorder of HSCs; PIGA mutation → lack GPI-anchored complement-regulatory proteins (CD55, CD59) → complement-mediated haemolysis. Sx (triad): haemolytic anaemia, thrombosis (hepatic/portal veins - Budd-Chiari, cerebral veins, unusual sites), cytopenias. Dark morning urine (haemoglobinuria - classic but not always present). Ix: flow cytometry (CD55/CD59 deficiency on RBCs and granulocytes). Mx: eculizumab (anti-C5 monoclonal) dramatically reduces haemolysis and thrombosis; anticoagulation; iron/folate; HSCT curative.

conditions.name: Folate deficiency
conditions.summary: Macrocytic megaloblastic anaemia. Causes: poor dietary intake (alcohol, elderly, overcooking vegetables), malabsorption (coeliac, jejunal disease), ↑demand (pregnancy, haemolytic anaemia, dialysis), drugs (methotrexate - DHFR inhibitor, trimethoprim, phenytoin, sulfasalazine). Identical blood picture to B12 deficiency - but no neurological manifestations. Essential to exclude B12 deficiency before giving folate (folate masks megaloblastic anaemia of B12 deficiency but neurological damage progresses). Mx: folic acid 5 mg daily; 5 mg periconceptional for neural tube defect prevention.

conditions.name: Anaemia of chronic disease
conditions.summary: Most common anaemia in hospitalised patients. Normocytic (usually) or mildly microcytic, normochromic anaemia. Causes: chronic infection, inflammatory disease (RA, IBD, SLE), malignancy. Mechanism: ↑hepcidin (blocks iron release from stores) + ↓EPO response. Ix: ↓serum iron, ↓TIBC (unlike iron deficiency: ↑TIBC), normal/↑ferritin. Mx: treat underlying disease; IV iron if coincident iron deficiency; EPO in selected patients (CKD, cancer on chemotherapy). Distinguish from iron deficiency: ferritin <30 = iron deficiency in chronic disease.

conditions.name: Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance
conditions.summary: Precursor to multiple myeloma; paraprotein <30 g/L + bone marrow plasma cells <10% + no CRAB criteria. Prevalence ~3-4% in adults >50. Risk of progression to MM: 1%/yr (IgG, low paraprotein, normal SFLC = low risk). Asymptomatic - found incidentally on SPEP. Monitoring: repeat SPEP/SFLC and clinical review every 6-12 mo. No treatment required. Sx: Educate about MM symptoms (bone pain, fatigue, renal failure) requiring prompt assessment.

conditions.name: Ascending cholangitis
conditions.summary: Bacterial infection of bile duct, usually from choledocholithiasis. Sx: Charcot's triad: fever/rigors, RUQ pain, jaundice. Reynolds pentad (severe): + hypotension + confusion. Organisms: E. coli, Klebsiella, Enterococcus. Ix: ↑WBC, ↑ALP/GGT/bilirubin, ± ↑amylase. US: bile duct dilation (>6 mm). Mx: IV antibiotics (piperacillin-tazobactam or ceftriaxone + metronidazole); urgent ERCP (sphincterotomy + stone removal) within 24-48 h; biliary drainage if ERCP fails.

conditions.name: Choledocholithiasis
conditions.summary: Gallstone in common bile duct. Sx: May be silent or cause biliary colic, jaundice, cholangitis, pancreatitis. Ix: ↑ALP, ↑GGT, ↑bilirubin (obstructive pattern). US: CBD dilation ± visible stone (only ~50% seen). MRCP (non-invasive) or EUS most accurate. Mx: ERCP + sphincterotomy + stone extraction; laparoscopic common bile duct exploration; cholecystectomy to prevent recurrence.

conditions.name: Budd-Chiari syndrome
conditions.summary: Hepatic venous outflow obstruction (hepatic veins ± IVC). Causes: thrombophilia (JAK2 mutation in PV most common), OCP, pregnancy, paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria, malignancy, membranous IVC obstruction (Asia). Sx: hepatomegaly, ascites (often painful), RUQ pain, jaundice; acute fulminant hepatic failure. Doppler US: absent hepatic vein flow; caudate lobe hypertrophy (has separate drainage). Mx: anticoagulation; TIPS (transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt) for refractory; liver transplant for fulminant.
utd: budd chiari syndrome clinical features diagnosis

conditions.name: Hepatic encephalopathy
conditions.summary: Neuropsychiatric complication of liver failure; ammonia + other toxins cross BBB. Grades: I (subtle cognitive changes) → IV (coma). Precipitants: GI bleed, infection (SBP), dehydration/diuretics, constipation, hepatotoxic drugs, TIPS. Asterixis (flapping tremor). Ix: clinical; EEG shows triphasic waves. Mx: identify and treat precipitants; lactulose (target 2-3 loose stools/day); rifaximin (reduces episodes in secondary prevention); avoid benzodiazepines and opioids; liver transplant.
utd: hepatic encephalopathy adults clinical manifestations diagnosis

conditions.name: Mesenteric ischaemia
conditions.summary: Inadequate blood flow to bowel. Acute mesenteric ischaemia: SMA embolus (AF, cardiac thrombus), SMA thrombosis, non-occlusive (cardiogenic shock), venous thrombosis. Sx: severe periumbilical pain out of proportion to physical findings (early); later peritonitis (bowel infarction). ↑WBC, ↑lactate, metabolic acidosis. CT angiography diagnostic. Mx: surgical revascularisation + bowel resection (necrotic bowel); endovascular approach emerging. High mortality. Chronic mesenteric ischaemia (intestinal angina): post-prandial pain + weight loss → angioplasty/stenting.
utd: acute mesenteric ischemia clinical features diagnosis

conditions.name: Short bowel syndrome
conditions.summary: Malabsorption following extensive small bowel resection (functional or anatomical < ~200 cm remaining). Causes: Crohn disease, mesenteric ischaemia/infarction, volvulus, necrotising enterocolitis (neonates), trauma, radiation enteritis. Critical factors: remaining bowel length, presence of ileocaecal valve (preserves transit, reduces bacterial overgrowth), residual colon (important for water/electrolyte absorption + SCFA production), continuity. Sx: diarrhoea/high output stoma, malabsorption (fat-soluble vitamins, B12, fat, protein, carbohydrate, water/electrolytes), dehydration, electrolyte imbalances (K⁺, Mg²⁺, PO₄), kidney stones (oxalate - hyperoxaluria), bacterial overgrowth, liver disease (PN-associated). Phases: acute (PN-dependent) → adaptive (bowel adaptation over 1-2 yr - hyperplasia, increased absorptive capacity) → stable. Mx: PN (total parenteral nutrition - essential early); fluid/electrolyte support; antidiarrhoeal agents (loperamide, codeine, cholestyramine - bile acid malabsorption); teduglutide (GLP-2 analogue - ↑intestinal adaptation, ↓PN requirements; major advance); small bowel transplant (last resort); nutritional rehabilitation; management of complications.
utd: short bowel syndrome adults clinical manifestations evaluation

conditions.name: Hepatorenal syndrome
conditions.summary: Functional renal failure in advanced cirrhosis; splanchnic vasodilation → renal vasoconstriction. Type 1 (HRS-AKI): rapid deterioration (creatinine doubles to >226 µmol/L in <2 wk) triggered by SBP, GI bleed, large-volume paracentesis; high short-term mortality. Type 2 (HRS-CKD): slower progression; resistant ascites. No response to IV fluids or stopping nephrotoxins (rules out other causes). Mx: noradrenaline (or terlipressin) + albumin infusion improves renal perfusion; TIPS as bridge; liver transplant definitive.

conditions.name: Glioblastoma
conditions.summary: Most common and most aggressive primary brain tumour (grade IV glioma); peak 55-65 yr. Sx: focal neurological deficits, seizures, ↑ICP (headache worse supine, nausea, vomiting). Ix (MRI): heterogeneous enhancing mass with central necrosis, surrounding oedema. IDH-wildtype; MGMT promoter methylation guides chemotherapy response. Mx: maximal safe surgical resection + radiotherapy + temozolomide (Stupp protocol) ± bevacizumab; median survival ~15 mo with treatment. TTFields (tumour-treating fields) for recurrence.

conditions.name: Meningioma
conditions.summary: Most common benign intracranial tumour; arises from arachnoid cap cells. F > M; peak 40-60 yr. Sphenoid ridge, parasagittal/falx, olfactory groove, posterior fossa common sites. Sx: often incidental; seizures, focal deficits, headache depending on location; olfactory groove → anosmia; parasagittal → leg weakness; sphenoid ridge → proptosis. CT/Ix (MRI): extra-axial homogeneous enhancing mass, dural tail. Ix: WHO grade I (90%), II, III (malignant). Mx: observation (small/incidental); surgery; stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) for <3 cm; radiotherapy for WHO II/III.

conditions.name: Lambert-Eaton syndrome
conditions.summary: Presynaptic NMJ disorder; antibodies against P/Q-type VGCC → ↓ACh release. 50-60% associated with small-cell lung cancer (paraneoplastic). Sx: proximal muscle weakness (worse early, briefly improves with repetition - opposite to MG), areflexia, autonomic dysfunction (dry mouth most common, constipation, impotence). Ix: VGCC antibodies; NCS: ↑CMAP amplitude on repetitive stimulation (post-tetanic potentiation). Mx: treat underlying malignancy; 3,4-DAP (amifampridine) 1st-line for symptoms; IVIG/plasmapheresis for immunosuppression.

conditions.name: Wernicke encephalopathy
conditions.summary: Thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency. Wernicke: classic triad - confusion/encephalopathy, ophthalmoplegia (lateral gaze palsy, nystagmus), ataxia (wide-based gait). Sx: Triad complete in <10% - any one feature warrants treatment. Risk: alcohol use disorder (most common in developed countries), prolonged vomiting (hyperemesis, post-bariatric surgery), malnutrition. Mx: IV thiamine (Pabrinex) BEFORE any glucose; 500 mg TDS for 3-5 days then maintenance. Korsakoff psychosis (anterograde amnesia, confabulation) from untreated Wernicke - often irreversible. Mx: Never give glucose before thiamine.

conditions.name: Cauda equina syndrome
conditions.summary: Compression of cauda equina nerve roots (below L1-L2) - surgical emergency. Causes: large central disc herniation (most common), spinal stenosis, malignancy, epidural abscess/haematoma. Sx: saddle anaesthesia, bilateral leg weakness/pain, bladder dysfunction (retention - 'painless retention' in acute - then overflow incontinence), bowel incontinence, sexual dysfunction. MRI spine urgently. Mx: emergency surgical decompression within 24-48 h (preferably ≤6 h) for best neurological recovery.

long-term management of Cauda equina syndrome

conditions.name: Syringomyelia
conditions.summary: Fluid-filled cavity within spinal cord parenchyma. Causes: Chiari malformation type I (most common), post-traumatic, post-inflammatory (meningitis, arachnoiditis), tethered cord, intramedullary tumour, idiopathic. Sx: cape distribution sensory loss (suspended dissociated sensory loss - pain/temp lost, light touch/proprioception spared), lower motor neurone weakness in arms, upper motor neurone signs in legs, scoliosis. MRI diagnostic. Mx: treat underlying cause (Chiari decompression - often stabilises/reverses syrinx); syringosubarachnoid shunting for persistent.

conditions.name: Neuromyelitis optica
conditions.summary: Autoimmune CNS demyelinating disease distinct from MS. Ix: AQP4-IgG (aquaporin-4) antibodies in ~70% (MOG-IgG in minority). Sx: Core features: optic neuritis (often bilateral/severe, poor recovery) + longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis (≥3 vertebral segments - distinguishes from MS). Area postrema involvement: intractable hiccups/nausea. Ix: Distinguish from MS: bilateral ON, severe attacks, poor recovery, AQP4+ serology, long cord lesions. Mx (attacks): high-dose IV methylprednisolone + plasmapheresis. Mx (prevention): azathioprine, mycophenolate, rituximab, or eculizumab.

conditions.name: POTS
conditions.summary: Dysautonomia characterised by ↑HR ≥30 bpm (or ≥120 bpm) within 10 min of standing, without orthostatic hypotension, with symptoms (palpitations, lightheadedness, presyncope, fatigue). Young women predominate; often post-viral (including post-COVID). Ix: 10-min standing test or tilt-table. Mx: education, ↑fluid/salt intake, compression garments, exercise rehabilitation (recumbent first); pharmacological: fludrocortisone, midodrine, β-blocker (low-dose), ivabradine.

conditions.name: Cryptococcal meningitis
conditions.summary: Cryptococcus neoformans (or C. gattii); soil/pigeon droppings. Predominantly in immunocompromised (HIV/AIDS most common - CD4 <100, defining illness). Sx: Subacute meningitis: insidious onset headache, fever, meningism; ↑ICP prominent (papilloedema, ↓consciousness). India ink stain (LP) + cryptococcal antigen (serum/CSF). Mx: induction - amphotericin B + flucytosine 2 wk; consolidation - fluconazole 8 wk; maintenance - fluconazole lifelong (until immune reconstitution with ART). Serial LPs or VP shunt to manage ↑ICP.

conditions.name: Pneumocystis pneumonia
conditions.summary: Fungal pneumonia by Pneumocystis jirovecii in immunocompromised (HIV CD4 <200, steroids, immunosuppressants, malignancy). Presents with subacute progressive dyspnoea, dry cough, fever, hypoxaemia. Ix (CXR): bilateral perihilar interstitial infiltrates (may be normal); CT: ground-glass opacification. Ix: bronchoscopy + BAL (GMS stain), or induced sputum. ↑LDH (non-specific). Mx: high-dose co-trimoxazole (TMP-SMX) 21 d (1st-line); adjunctive steroids if PaO2 <70 mmHg. Prophylaxis: TMP-SMX when CD4 <200.

conditions.name: Toxoplasmosis
conditions.summary: Toxoplasma gondii intracellular parasite; cats definitive host. Seroprevalence ~30% worldwide. Acquired: usually asymptomatic or mild mononucleosis-like illness. Congenital (primary infection in pregnancy): triad - hydrocephalus, chorioretinitis, intracranial calcifications; stillbirth or severe handicap. Mx: Immunocompromised reactivation (HIV, transplant): cerebral toxoplasmosis (ring-enhancing lesions on MRI, mass effect, seizures, fever, focal deficits). Mx: pyrimethamine + sulfadiazine + folinic acid; TMP-SMX (prophylaxis and alternative Mx).

conditions.name: Necrotizing fasciitis
conditions.summary: Rapidly progressive bacterial infection of fascia and subcutaneous tissue → widespread necrosis. Type I (polymicrobial - Fournier's gangrene): diabetics, immunocompromised, abdominal/perineal source. Type II (group A streptococcus ± S. aureus): healthy individuals; toxic shock. Sx: disproportionate pain, skin erythema → blistering/bullae → grey-blue/necrotic skin, crepitus; fever, septic shock; 'dishwater' fluid on incision. Ix: clinical + surgical exploration (gold standard); CT (gas tracking along fascial planes). Mx: immediate radical surgical debridement + IV antibiotics (piperacillin-tazobactam + clindamycin + vancomycin) + ICU.

conditions.name: Toxic shock syndrome
conditions.summary: S. aureus (TSST-1, SPEA) or S. pyogenes superantigens → massive T-cell activation → cytokine storm. Mx: Staphylococcal TSS: menstrual (retained tampon/contraceptive device), non-menstrual (post-surgical wound, burns). Streptococcal TSS: associated with necrotising fasciitis/invasive GAS infection. Ix: Criteria: fever, diffuse macular erythroderma (sunburn-like), desquamation (1-2 wk later), ↓BP + multi-organ involvement. Mx: aggressive fluid resuscitation; remove source (tampon, drain wound); anti-staphylococcal antibiotics + clindamycin (↓toxin production); IVIG for refractory streptococcal TSS.
utd: empiric treatment of Toxic shock syndrome

conditions.name: Measles
conditions.summary: Paramyxovirus; highly contagious (R0~15). Prodrome: 3 Cs (cough, coryza, conjunctivitis) + Koplik spots (pathognomonic enanthem: white spots on buccal mucosa). Then maculopapular rash (starts behind ears, spreads downwards). Complications: otitis media (most common), pneumonia (giant cell pneumonitis), encephalitis, SSPE (rare, fatal late complication). Ix: clinical; IgM serology; urine/nasopharyngeal PCR. Mx: supportive; vitamin A (reduces mortality, especially malnourished children). Mx (prevention): MMR vaccine.

conditions.name: Mumps
conditions.summary: Paramyxovirus; parotitis is hallmark (unilateral or bilateral painful parotid swelling, 'hamster-face'). Complications: orchitis (post-pubertal males, ~20-30%; unilateral usually; rarely infertility), oophoritis, aseptic meningitis (most common viral meningitis cause historically), encephalitis, pancreatitis, sensorineural hearing loss. Ix: serology (IgM), PCR saliva/urine. Mx: supportive; analgesia for orchitis; scrotal support. Mx (prevention): MMR vaccine; still occurs in vaccinated populations (waning immunity).

conditions.name: Rubella
conditions.summary: Togavirus; mild illness in children - low-grade fever, fine maculopapular rash (face → trunk → extremities), posterior cervical/suboccipital lymphadenopathy; arthralgia (adults, especially women). Congenital rubella syndrome (1st trimester most severe): deafness, cataracts, patent ductus arteriosus (triad), microcephaly, intellectual disability, blueberry muffin spots (extramedullary haematopoiesis). Ix: serology; PCR. Mx (prevention): MMR vaccine; screen pregnant women (vaccinate post-partum if non-immune).

conditions.name: Rocky Mountain spotted fever
conditions.summary: Rickettsia rickettsii; tick-borne (Dermacentor in USA). Sx (triad): fever, headache, rash (2-4 d after onset - petechial/purpuric rash starting on wrists/ankles, spreading centrally; involves palms and soles). Vasculitis → end-organ damage: AKI, pneumonitis, encephalopathy, ARDS. Ix: clinical; serology retrospective (Weil-Felix, IFA); skin biopsy PCR/IHC (acute diagnosis). Mx: doxycycline (start empirically, do NOT await confirmation); excellent prognosis if treated early; high mortality untreated.

conditions.name: Q fever
conditions.summary: Coxiella burnetii; zoonosis (cattle, sheep, goats via aerosol from parturient animals/their products). Acute: flu-like illness, atypical pneumonia, hepatitis. Chronic (1-5%): Q fever endocarditis (most common; pre-existing valvular disease or immunocompromised) - culture-negative endocarditis; PUO; ↑anti-phase I IgG. Ix: serology (phase I and II antibodies). Mx: acute - doxycycline 14 d; chronic endocarditis - doxycycline + hydroxychloroquine ≥18 mo.

conditions.name: Compartment syndrome
conditions.summary: ↑Pressure within an osteofascial compartment → ischaemia. Causes: fracture (tibial, distal radius most common), crush injury, reperfusion, circumferential burns, haematoma. Sx: the 5/6 Ps - Pain (out of proportion, especially with passive stretch), Pressure (firm compartment), Paraesthesia, Pallor, Pulselessness, Paralysis (late). Compartment pressure >30 mmHg or within 30 mmHg of diastolic BP is diagnostic threshold for fasciotomy. Mx: emergency decompressive fasciotomy - remove cast/bandages first; do NOT elevate limb.

conditions.name: Hip fracture
conditions.summary: Major cause of morbidity/mortality in elderly; 30-day mortality ~10%, 1-yr mortality ~30%. Risk: osteoporosis (BMD), female, age, falls, frailty. Types: intracapsular (displaced - disrupts blood supply to femoral head → avascular necrosis; Garden classification I-IV: undisplaced [I-II] → can fix with screws; displaced [III-IV] → hemiarthroplasty or THA); extracapsular (intertrochanteric/subtrochanteric - DHS, intramedullary nail). Sx: shortened, externally rotated leg; pain on movement/axial loading. X-ray pelvis + hip; CT if occult fracture suspected (MRI preferred). Mx: NHFD/Blue Book guidelines; orthopaedic emergency - target surgery within 36 hr (↓mortality, pressure sores, confusion, pain); anaemia/INR correction; early mobilisation + physiotherapy; bone protection (bisphosphonates, Ca/VitD); falls/fracture prevention; 4AT delirium assessment.

conditions.name: Adhesive capsulitis
conditions.summary: Progressive painful restriction of all shoulder movements (both active and passive), especially external rotation and abduction. Phases: freezing (pain, progressive restriction), frozen (less pain, marked restriction), thawing (gradual recovery). Risk: DM (5× more common), Parkinson, thyroid disease, immobility, rotator cuff injury. Ix: clinical. Mx: analgesia + physiotherapy (mainstay, recovery 1-3 yr); corticosteroid injection (speeds pain resolution); hydrodistension; manipulation under anaesthesia; arthroscopic capsular release.

conditions.name: Tennis elbow
conditions.summary: Tendinopathy/degeneration of the extensor carpi radialis brevis origin at lateral epicondyle. Common repetitive strain (racket sports, manual work). Sx: lateral elbow pain and tenderness, worsened by gripping and wrist extension; pain reproduced by resisted wrist/finger extension with elbow extended. Ix: clinical. Mx: activity modification, physiotherapy (eccentric exercises), NSAIDs; corticosteroid injection (short-term relief only, may worsen long-term); PRP; surgery for chronic refractory.

conditions.name: Scaphoid fracture
conditions.summary: Most commonly fractured carpal bone; fall on outstretched hand. Risk of missed diagnosis: X-ray may be negative initially in up to 25%. Anatomical snuffbox tenderness + scaphoid compression pain are key. Proximal pole fractures: ↑risk AVN (poor blood supply, retrograde from distal). Ix: MRI or CT if X-ray negative + strong clinical suspicion (X-ray may not show fracture for 10-14 d). Mx: undisplaced distal: thumb spica cast 8-12 wk; displaced/proximal/non-union: surgical fixation (headless compression screw).

conditions.name: Ewing sarcoma
conditions.summary: Malignant round-cell bone tumour; second most common primary bone malignancy in children/adolescents. EWS-FLI1 fusion (EWSR1 gene translocation). Diaphysis of long bones, pelvis, ribs, scapula. Sx: pain, swelling, fever, ↑ESR/CRP, ↑LDH - may mimic osteomyelitis. CXR/plain film: 'onion-skin' periosteal reaction + soft tissue mass. Ix: biopsy (small round blue cells, CD99+). Ix (staging): CT chest + bone scan/PET. Mx: neoadjuvant chemotherapy (VIDE/VDC-IE) + surgery ± radiotherapy; 5-yr survival ~70% localised, <30% metastatic.

conditions.name: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis
conditions.summary: Most common chronic arthritis in children (<16 yr, ≥6 wk). Subtypes: oligoarticular (≤4 joints, most common; ANA+, ↑uveitis risk), polyarticular RF− and RF+ (RA-like), systemic JIA (Still disease - quotidian fever, rash, hepatosplenomegaly), enthesitis-related, psoriatic. Complications: uveitis (asymptomatic in oligoarticular - regular slit-lamp screening), amyloidosis (systemic). Mx: NSAIDs; methotrexate; biologics (anti-TNF, abatacept, IL-1/IL-6 inhibitors for systemic); physiotherapy.

conditions.name: Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease
conditions.summary: Avascular necrosis of femoral head in children 4-8 yr; M:F 4:1; often bilateral (10-15%). Sx: insidious onset hip/knee pain, limp. Findings: ↓abduction/internal rotation. X-ray: subchondral lucency → collapse → revascularisation/remodelling (2-4 yr). MRI sensitive early. Prognosis depends on age at onset and extent of head involvement. Mx: conservative: activity restriction, physiotherapy; surgical (Salter osteotomy, femoral osteotomy) for severe/late presentation to contain femoral head within acetabulum.

conditions.name: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis
conditions.summary: Displacement of femoral head epiphysis at growth plate; obese adolescent males, 10-16 yr. Risk: obesity, hypothyroidism, GH deficiency, renal osteodystrophy. Sx: hip/groin/knee pain and limp; loss of internal rotation; leg externally rotated. X-ray (AP + frog-leg lateral): 'ice cream falling off cone' - displacement of epiphysis posteriorly. Stable (can bear weight) vs unstable (cannot). Mx: urgent surgical fixation (in-situ pinning); unstable SCFE: within 6-24 h to reduce AVN risk; bilateral fixation controversial.

conditions.name: Biliary atresia
conditions.summary: Progressive fibro-obliterative disease of extrahepatic bile ducts; most common cause of neonatal cholestasis requiring liver transplant. Presents weeks 2-8 of life: jaundice persisting beyond 14 d (conjugated), pale/white acholic stools, dark urine, hepatomegaly. Ix: US (absent/small gallbladder), HIDA scan (no bowel excretion), liver biopsy, intraoperative cholangiogram (gold standard). Mx: Kasai portoenterostomy (Roux-en-Y hepatoportoenterostomy) - before 8 wk for best outcome; if unsuccessful/delayed: liver transplant.

conditions.name: Phenylketonuria
conditions.summary: Autosomal recessive phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH) deficiency → phenylalanine accumulates → neurotoxicity. Ix: Detected by newborn screening (heel-prick blood spot). Sx: Untreated: progressive intellectual disability, seizures, microcephaly, mousy body odour, eczema-like rash, fair skin/hair (↓melanin). Maternal PKU: ↑phenylalanine teratogenic (microcephaly, CHD) in offspring if uncontrolled during pregnancy. Mx: lifelong low-phenylalanine diet; BH4 (sapropterin) for PAH-responsive variants; PEGylated phenylalanine ammonia lyase (pegvaliase) for poorly controlled.

conditions.name: Meconium aspiration syndrome
conditions.summary: Aspiration of meconium-stained amniotic fluid in neonate, usually term or post-term, from fetal distress. Chemical pneumonitis + mechanical obstruction + infection → respiratory distress at birth or shortly after. Sx: meconium-stained fluid, cyanosis, tachypnoea, barrel chest, crackles. Ix (CXR): patchy atelectasis + overinflation + air leak. Mx: resuscitation (avoid routine suctioning of non-vigorous infant first); supplemental O2; surfactant; inhaled nitric oxide for PPHN; ECMO in severe cases.

conditions.name: Transient tachypnea of the newborn
conditions.summary: Delayed clearance of fetal lung fluid → transient respiratory distress; most common neonatal respiratory condition. Risk: elective caesarean section (no thoracic squeeze), late preterm (34-36 wk). Sx: tachypnoea (RR >60), mild cyanosis, grunting; usually resolves within 12-48 h. Ix (CXR): perihilar streaking, fluid in horizontal fissure, hyperinflation. Mx: supportive - O2 (nasal cannula/CPAP), IV fluids if unable to feed; antibiotics if infection cannot be excluded; resolves spontaneously.

haemolysis elevated liver enzymes low platelets
conditions.name: HELLP syndrome
conditions.summary: Severe variant of preeclampsia: Haemolysis (microangiopathic), Elevated Liver enzymes, Low Platelets. Presents 27-36 wk or post-partum (30%). Sx: RUQ/epigastric pain, nausea/vomiting, malaise - may have minimal hypertension/proteinuria. ↑AST/ALT, ↓platelets (<100×10⁹/L), ↑LDH, ↑bilirubin, schistocytes. Complications: hepatic haematoma/rupture, DIC, ARF, placental abruption, pulmonary oedema. Mx: delivery (definitive) once >34 wk or earlier if unstable; MgSO4 for seizures; IV antihypertensives; steroids (↑platelet count temporarily).

conditions.name: Miscarriage
conditions.summary: Loss of pregnancy before 24 completed weeks. Frequency: 15-20% of recognised pregnancies (majority before 12 wk); ↑with maternal age. Types: threatened (PV bleeding + closed cervical os + viable USS); inevitable (PV bleeding + open os); incomplete (partial expulsion + retained products); complete (all products expelled); missed/silent (fetal demise without symptoms - empty sac / irregular sac / no cardiac activity). Recurrent miscarriage (RM): ≥3 consecutive losses (<24 wk). Causes RM: antiphospholipid syndrome (APS - most important treatable cause; lupus anticoagulant + anticardiolipin antibodies; Mx: aspirin + LMWH in pregnancy), chromosomal (parental karyotype; sporadic embryonic aneuploidy), uterine (septum, fibroids - submucosal), thyroid disease, diabetes. Ix: TVUSS (gestational sac, fetal pole, cardiac activity; confirms viability/non-viability). Mx: expectant (complete/inevitable - most pass spontaneously); medical (misoprostol - faster resolution); surgical (manual vacuum aspiration/ERPC - heavy bleeding, incomplete, clinical instability, patient preference); RhD immunoglobulin (if Rh-D negative ≥12 wk or sensitising event); counselling/psychological support.

conditions.name: Pelvic inflammatory disease
conditions.summary: Ascending infection of female upper genital tract (endometrium, fallopian tubes, ovaries, pelvic peritoneum). Causative organisms: Chlamydia trachomatis (most common), N. gonorrhoeae, endogenous flora. Sx: pelvic/lower abdominal pain, abnormal vaginal discharge, fever, dyspareunia, CMT (cervical motion tenderness - Chandelier sign), uterine and adnexal tenderness. Complications: tubo-ovarian abscess, chronic pelvic pain, ectopic pregnancy, infertility. Mx: ceftriaxone + doxycycline + metronidazole; IV if severe/abscess; drain abscess if non-responsive; treat partners.

conditions.name: Placenta accreta
conditions.summary: Abnormal placental invasion into (accreta), through (increta), or through full thickness of (percreta) uterine wall. Risk: prior caesarean section (↑with multiple CS), placenta previa, uterine surgery. Ix: prenatal US/MRI (loss of retroplacental clear space, myometrial lacunae). Major haemorrhage risk at delivery. Mx: planned delivery at 34-36 wk in centre with expert team; often requires caesarean hysterectomy; conservative management (delayed placental removal, methotrexate) in selected cases desiring future fertility.

conditions.name: Ovarian cyst
conditions.summary: Common incidental finding on pelvic US. Functional (most common in reproductive age): follicular cysts, corpus luteum cysts - resolve spontaneously. Benign: dermoid/mature teratoma (most common benign ovarian tumour in young women, may contain teeth/hair), serous/mucinous cystadenoma, endometrioma (chocolate cyst of endometriosis). Malignant: serous/mucinous cystadenocarcinoma. Risk: post-menopausal, large size, solid components, ascites, septations, ↑CA-125. IOTA classification/RMI for risk stratification. Ix: Simple cysts ≤5 cm in reproductive age: reassurance + repeat US.

conditions.name: Bartholin cyst
conditions.summary: Obstruction of Bartholin gland duct (posterolateral vaginal walls). Cyst: non-infected, often asymptomatic; may enlarge. Sx: Abscess: infected (mixed - E. coli, anaerobes; STI organisms - Chlamydia, GC, Staphylococcus), painful, fluctuant swelling at 4- or 8-o'clock position in labia majora; may prevent walking/sitting. Mx: cyst - Word catheter (marsupialization) or surgical marsupialization if symptomatic; abscess - I&D + Word catheter (prevents recurrence) + antibiotics; excision if recurrent in women >40 (exclude malignancy).

conditions.name: Adenomyosis
conditions.summary: Endometrial glands and stroma within myometrium → uterine enlargement and dysfunction. Distinguished from endometriosis (though commonly coexists). Sx: secondary dysmenorrhoea (characteristically worsening over years), menorrhagia (heavy menstrual bleeding), dyspareunia, pelvic pain; 'globular' enlarged tender uterus. Ix: MRI (junctional zone thickness >12 mm, high sensitivity); transvaginal US; definitive: hysterectomy specimen. Mx: medical (COCP, LNG-IUS, NSAIDs, GnRH analogues); hysterectomy (definitive).

conditions.name: Optic neuritis
conditions.summary: Inflammatory demyelination of optic nerve; strongest association with MS (15-20% present with optic neuritis; 50% of optic neuritis cases develop MS). Sx: unilateral visual loss (over hours-days), periorbital pain (worsened by eye movement), impaired colour vision (dyschromatopsia), RAPD (relative afferent pupillary defect - swinging flashlight test), central scotoma. Uhthoff phenomenon (↓vision with heat). MRI brain + orbits with gadolinium. Mx: IV methylprednisolone accelerates recovery; does not affect final visual outcome; high-risk lesions on MRI → disease-modifying therapy for MS.

conditions.name: Central retinal artery occlusion
conditions.summary: Ocular emergency (retina tolerates ischaemia <100 min). Embolic (carotid/cardiac, GCA) or thrombotic. Sx: sudden painless monocular visual loss (often total, pale fundus, cherry-red spot at fovea, RAPD). Treat as 'ocular stroke' - workup same as TIA. Mx: ocular massage + anterior chamber paracentesis (reduce IOP → dislodge embolus); inhale CO2 (vasodilation), sublingual GTN; thrombolysis in specialist centres (limited evidence). Long-term: control embolic risk factors; systemic anticoagulation if cardiac source.

conditions.name: Peritonsillar abscess
conditions.summary: Collection of pus in peritonsillar space between tonsil capsule and superior pharyngeal constrictor; most common deep neck space infection. Complication of tonsillitis (GAS, mixed flora). Sx: severe unilateral throat pain, dysphagia, odynophagia, hot-potato voice, trismus, drooling, uvular deviation to opposite side, bulging soft palate. Ix: clinical ± US/CT if uncertain. Mx: aspiration (preferred) or I&D + IV antibiotics (amoxicillin-clavulanate or ceftriaxone + metronidazole); steroids (↓oedema); tonsillectomy if recurrent.

conditions.name: Orbital cellulitis
conditions.summary: Infection posterior to orbital septum; most commonly from sinusitis (ethmoid) or periorbital skin source. Distinguish from preseptal (periorbital) cellulitis (anterior to septum, less serious). Sx: proptosis, ophthalmoplegia, pain with eye movement, ↓visual acuity, ↑IOP, chemosis, fever, ↑WBC. CT orbits/sinuses (ring-enhancing subperiosteal/orbital abscess). Complications: cavernous sinus thrombosis, intracranial extension (meningitis, brain abscess). Mx: hospital admission; IV antibiotics (ceftriaxone + metronidazole); surgical drainage if abscess/no clinical improvement.

conditions.name: Cholesteatoma
conditions.summary: Non-malignant keratinising squamous epithelium growing abnormally in middle ear (and/or mastoid). Congenital or acquired (retraction pocket from chronic Eustachian tube dysfunction, often with chronic otitis media with effusion). Sx: foul-smelling otorrhoea, conductive hearing loss; can expand to erode ossicles, mastoid, tegmen, facial canal (facial palsy), labyrinth (vertigo/SNHL), dura (meningitis, brain abscess). Ix: otoscopy (white pearly mass, attic crust), CT temporal bone. Mx: surgical excision (mastoidectomy); recurrence common - lifelong surveillance.

conditions.name: Nasal polyps
conditions.summary: Non-malignant oedematous outgrowths of nasal/sinus mucosa; bilateral usually (unilateral → exclude malignancy, inverted papilloma). Associations: chronic rhinosinusitis (most common), aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease (Samter's triad: asthma + aspirin intolerance + nasal polyps), cystic fibrosis (bilateral in children), primary ciliary dyskinesia. Sx: nasal obstruction, anosmia, post-nasal drip, chronic rhinosinusitis. Mx: intranasal corticosteroids (first-line); oral steroids (short course); dupilumab (IL-4/13 inhibitor) for severe; functional endoscopic sinus surgery (FESS) for refractory.

conditions.name: Corneal ulcer
conditions.summary: Corneal epithelial defect + stromal infiltrate; ocular emergency. Risk: contact lens wear (Pseudomonas most common), trauma, dry eye, immunosuppression. Sx: severe eye pain, redness, photophobia, discharge, ↓visual acuity, white opacity on cornea. Ix: slit-lamp + corneal scrape (micro/culture). Mx: intensive topical antibiotics (fluoroquinolone - ciprofloxacin, ofloxacin) every hour initially; modify based on culture; systemic treatment if scleral involvement; no steroids until response to antibiotics confirmed. Referral to ophthalmology.

conditions.name: Lichen planus
conditions.summary: Idiopathic inflammatory condition affecting skin, mucous membranes, nails, hair. Classic: 6 Ps - pruritic, planar, polygonal, purple, papules with Wickham striae (lacy white lines). Sites: flexor wrists, ankles, lower back. Oral LP: white reticular pattern (buccal mucosa), erosive form (painful); malignant potential. Nail LP: thinning, ridging, pterygium. Associations: hepatitis C, drugs (beta-blockers, NSAIDs, antimalarials), graft-vs-host. Ix: clinical ± biopsy (band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at dermal-epidermal junction). Mx: topical steroids; tacrolimus for oral; systemic steroids/retinoids/ciclosporin for severe.

conditions.name: Pityriasis rosea
conditions.summary: Self-limiting exanthem; likely HHV-6/7 reactivation. Herald patch (2-10 cm oval scaly plaque, often truncal) 1-2 wk before secondary eruption. Secondary: smaller oval scaly papules/plaques along Langer lines ('Christmas tree' pattern on back), mainly trunk/proximal limbs; spares palms/soles/face. Mild pruritus. Resolves 6-12 wk spontaneously. Mx: reassurance; topical steroids/antihistamines for itch; phototherapy (UVB) if severe.

conditions.name: Erythema multiforme
conditions.summary: Acute immune-mediated mucocutaneous condition. Target lesions (3 zones: central dusky/blistered, pale oedematous ring, outer erythema); acrally distributed (palms, soles, dorsa), symmetric. EM minor: no/minimal mucosal involvement. EM major: ≥2 mucosal sites. Triggers: HSV (most common - 50%), Mycoplasma, drugs (sulfonamides, penicillin). Distinguish from SJS (>10% BSA, extensive blistering, severe mucositis, systemic illness). Mx: treat trigger (aciclovir for HSV); symptomatic (antihistamines, topical steroids, mouthwash); systemic steroids controversial.

conditions.name: Stevens-Johnson syndrome
conditions.summary: Severe mucocutaneous drug hypersensitivity reaction; spectrum with TEN (SJS <10% BSA, SJS/TEN overlap 10-30%, TEN >30%). Culprits: sulfonamides, allopurinol, anticonvulsants (carbamazepine, lamotrigine, phenytoin), NSAIDs, antibiotics. Sx: prodrome (fever, malaise), then painful erythema → blisters → skin detachment (Nikolsky +), severe mucositis (oral, ocular, genital). Ocular complications: conjunctivitis → symblepharon → blindness. Mortality: SJS 5-15%, TEN 25-35% (SCORTEN score). Mx: stop offending drug; ICU/burns unit; fluid resuscitation; eye care; IVIG or ciclosporin.

conditions.name: Basal cell carcinoma
conditions.summary: Most common skin cancer (80%); arises from basal layer of epidermis; locally invasive but rarely metastasises (<0.1%). Risk: UV exposure, fair skin, Fitzpatrick I/II, ionising radiation, immunosuppression, Gorlin syndrome (PTCH1). Subtypes: nodular (pearly papule with rolled edge, telangiectasia, central ulceration - 'rodent ulcer'), superficial, morphoeic (ill-defined, scar-like). Sites: face (nose, inner canthus), ears, scalp. Ix: dermoscopy; biopsy. Mx: excision (first-line); Mohs surgery (high-risk/cosmetically sensitive); radiotherapy; imiquimod/PDT (superficial); vismodegib (hedgehog pathway inhibitor) for advanced.

conditions.name: Squamous cell carcinoma
conditions.summary: Second most common skin cancer; derived from keratinocytes; can metastasise (2-5%). Risk: cumulative UV, actinic keratoses (premalignant), fair skin, immunosuppression (transplant recipients - 100× risk), HPV (anogenital, oropharyngeal), Marjolin ulcer (chronic wounds). Sx: hyperkeratotic, crusted, or ulcerated plaque/nodule on sun-exposed skin; may arise from AK. High-risk features: >2 cm, >2 mm thick, poorly differentiated, perineural invasion, ear/lip, immunosuppressed host. Ix: biopsy. Mx: excision (4-6 mm margins); Mohs for high-risk; sentinel LN biopsy; radiotherapy; cemiplimab (PD-1 inhibitor) for metastatic.

conditions.name: Actinic keratosis
conditions.summary: Intraepidermal squamous cell dysplasia; premalignant lesion with risk of progression to SCC (1-8% per lesion over 10 yr). Risk: cumulative UV, fair skin, outdoor occupation, immunosuppression. Sx: rough, scaly, erythematous papule/plaque on sun-exposed skin (face, scalp, dorsal hands, forearms); may be more palpable than visible. Ix: clinical; biopsy if ulcerated/hyperkeratotic/in doubt. Mx: cryotherapy (single lesions); 5-FU or imiquimod cream (field treatment); diclofenac gel; photodynamic therapy (PDT); daylight PDT.

conditions.name: Alopecia areata
conditions.summary: Autoimmune patchy non-scarring hair loss; T-cell-mediated attack on hair follicle. Associations: thyroid disease, vitiligo, atopy, Down syndrome. Sx: smooth circular patches of hair loss (scalp most common); 'exclamation mark' hairs at margins; nail pitting/trachyonychia. Extent: alopecia totalis (whole scalp), alopecia universalis (all body hair). Ix: clinical; dermoscopy (yellow dots, black dots, exclamation mark hairs); biopsy if uncertain. Prognosis: 80% regrow within 1 yr in limited disease; poor prognosis if extensive/long-standing/prepubertal. Mx: intralesional steroids (limited disease); topical minoxidil; contact immunotherapy (DPCP); baricitinib/ritlecitinib (JAK inhibitors) for severe.

conditions.name: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
conditions.summary: Most common aggressive NHL (30-35% of all lymphomas). Ix: excision biopsy; CD20+, BCL6, MUM1; cell of origin: GCB vs non-GCB (Hans classifier) by IHC; MYC/BCL2 double-hit (HGBCL) - worse prognosis. Sx: rapidly enlarging nodal mass; B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss); extranodal in 40%. Ann Arbor staging + IPI (International Prognostic Index: age, LDH, PS, stage, extranodal sites). Mx: R-CHOP × 6 cycles ± RT for localised (standard); R-EPOCH for MYC-rearranged/double-hit; polatuzumab vedotin + R-CHP for high risk; ASCT for relapsed/refractory; CAR-T (axicabtagene, lisocabtagene) for R/R.

conditions.name: Follicular lymphoma
conditions.summary: Most common indolent NHL (20-25%); t(14;18) BCL2 translocation (BCL2 overexpression → anti-apoptosis). Median age 60; predominantly nodal. Ix: biopsy; CD10+, BCL2+, CD20+, germinal centre origin; Follicular Lymphoma International Prognostic Index (FLIPI). Sx: waxing/waning painless lymphadenopathy; often incidental. Transformation to DLBCL in ~3% per year (PET-CT suspicious). Watch-and-wait (asymptomatic limited disease) vs. R-bendamustine or R-CHOP (symptomatic/bulky); rituximab maintenance; lenalidomide-rituximab. Incurable with conventional Mx but prolonged survival.

conditions.name: Mantle cell lymphoma
conditions.summary: Aggressive B-cell NHL; t(11;14) → cyclin D1 overexpression; CD5+, CD20+, cyclin D1+. Predominantly older men. Sx: lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, peripheral blood involvement (leukaemic phase), GI involvement (lymphomatous polyposis - colonoscopy). Blastoid variant (aggressive, poor prognosis). Ki67 >30% - high proliferative index. Mx: intensive regimen (R-CHOP alternating R-DHAP) + ASCT for fit patients; ibrutinib (BTK inhibitor) ± rituximab/venetoclax; bendamustine-rituximab for elderly/unfit; currently incurable (median survival 5-7 yr, improving).

conditions.name: Burkitt lymphoma
conditions.summary: Highly aggressive B-cell NHL; t(8;14) c-MYC translocation. Three types: endemic (African - EBV-associated, jaw/facial mass in children), sporadic (abdominal mass, ileocaecal, most common in West), immunodeficiency-associated (HIV). 'Starry sky' histology (tingible-body macrophages). Ix: biopsy; CD20+, CD10+, BCL6+, BCL2−, Ki67 ~100%. Mx: intensive regimen (R-CODOX-M/R-IVAC or R-Hyper-CVAD); CNS prophylaxis; tumour lysis syndrome prophylaxis (allopurinol, rasburicase, hydration). Potentially curable in 70-90% with modern protocols.

conditions.name: Waldenström macroglobulinaemia
conditions.summary: Indolent B-cell lymphoma/plasma cell dyscrasia characterised by IgM paraprotein (monoclonal IgM) and bone marrow infiltration with lymphoplasmacytic cells. MYD88 L265P mutation (>90%). Sx: hyperviscosity syndrome (headache, visual disturbance, epistaxis, retinal 'sausage-link' veins), peripheral neuropathy (IgM-associated demyelinating), cryoglobulinaemia type I (Raynaud, purpura), haemolytic anaemia (cold agglutinins), lymphadenopathy/splenomegaly. Serum protein electrophoresis: IgM spike. Mx: watch-and-wait if asymptomatic; ibrutinib ± rituximab (first-line); bendamustine + rituximab; plasmapheresis for hyperviscosity emergency.

conditions.name: Progressive supranuclear palsy
conditions.summary: Atypical parkinsonian syndrome; tau accumulation (4R tauopathy) in subthalamic nucleus, globus pallidus, substantia nigra, brainstem. Sx: vertical gaze palsy (downgaze paresis earliest - 'cannot look at buttons'), axial rigidity > limb, early falls (backward), pseudobulbar palsy (dysarthria, dysphagia, emotional lability), frontal dementia (executive dysfunction), square-wave jerks. PSP-RS (Richardson syndrome) most common. No tremor at rest (unlike PD). Poor response to levodopa. Ix: clinical + MRI ('hummingbird sign' - midbrain atrophy, 'morning glory' on axial). Median survival 7 yr.

long-term management of Progressive supranuclear palsy

conditions.name: Multiple system atrophy
conditions.summary: Atypical parkinsonian syndrome; alpha-synuclein glial cytoplasmic inclusions (oligodendrocytes). Two subtypes: MSA-P (parkinsonism-predominant; striatonigral degeneration) and MSA-C (cerebellar-predominant; olivopontocerebellar atrophy). Early severe autonomic dysfunction: orthostatic hypotension, urogenital dysfunction (early urinary incontinence in women, erectile dysfunction in men), REM sleep behaviour disorder. Poor response to levodopa (but partial initial response). MSA-C: ataxic gait, dysarthria, nystagmus. Ix (MRI): putaminal atrophy + lateral rim (hot cross bun sign - pontine cruciform), pontine/cerebellar atrophy. Rapid progression, median survival 9 yr.
