conditions.name: Corticobasal degeneration
conditions.summary: 4R tauopathy affecting frontoparietal cortex and basal ganglia. Corticobasal syndrome (CBS) = clinical presentation (other causes possible). Sx: asymmetric limb rigidity + dystonia, apraxia, alien limb phenomenon (limb moves involuntarily), myoclonus, cortical sensory loss, executive dysfunction, aphasia. No resting tremor; rare falls. Ix (MRI): asymmetric frontoparietal cortical atrophy. Poor levodopa response. Overlap with PSP (CBS-PSP overlap). Prognosis: median 6-8 yr.

conditions.name: Frontotemporal dementia
conditions.summary: Degenerative dementia affecting frontal/temporal lobes; younger onset (50-70 yr). Subtypes: behavioural variant FTD (bvFTD - disinhibition, apathy, loss of empathy, hyperorality, perseveration, executive dysfunction, early preserved memory), semantic dementia (SD - fluent aphasia, word/face/object knowledge loss), non-fluent/agrammatic PPA (nfPPA - effortful speech, agrammatism). Tau (Pick disease - Pick bodies; CBD; PSP) or TDP-43 or FUS pathology. Genetic: C9orf72 (FTD-ALS), MAPT, GRN, VCP. Ix: clinical + FDG-PET (frontal/temporal hypometabolism) + atrophy. No disease-modifying Mx.

conditions.name: Histoplasmosis
conditions.summary: Endemic mycosis; Histoplasma capsulatum; Ohio and Mississippi River valleys (USA); bird/bat droppings. Primary pulmonary: usually asymptomatic or flu-like (fever, headache, myalgia, cough); calcified granulomas. Complications in immunocompromised: disseminated histoplasmosis (fever, hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia, adrenal insufficiency, mucosal ulcers, CNS). Ix: urine/serum Histoplasma antigen (most sensitive in disseminated); culture (gold standard but slow); serology. Mx: mild-moderate: itraconazole; severe/disseminated: amphotericin B then itraconazole step-down.

conditions.name: Coccidioidomycosis
conditions.summary: Endemic mycosis; Coccidioides immitis/posadasii; SW United States (California, Arizona), Mexico/Central America. Inhaled arthrospores. Primary pulmonary: self-limiting fever, cough, chest pain, eosinophilia; 'desert rheumatism' (erythema nodosum + arthralgias). Disseminated (rare, risk: immunosuppression, African/Filipino descent, 3rd trimester pregnancy): meningitis (chronic basilar), skin lesions, osteomyelitis. Serology: IgM (early), IgG (IFA/CF - disease activity). Ix: culture (biosafety level 3); spherules on biopsy. Mx: mild: fluconazole or itraconazole; severe/CNS: fluconazole (life-long for meningitis) or amphotericin B.

conditions.name: Blastomycosis
conditions.summary: Endemic mycosis; Blastomyces dermatitidis; Great Lakes/Mississippi-Ohio River basin; moist soil/decaying wood. Primary pulmonary: fever, cough, pleuritis (often misdiagnosed as bacterial pneumonia or malignancy). Disseminated: skin (verrucous/ulcerative lesions - classic), bone (osteolytic), genitourinary (prostatitis, epididymo-orchitis), CNS. Ix: culture (gold standard); direct KOH mount (broad-based budding yeast); urinary antigen (cross-reacts with Histoplasma). Mx: mild-moderate pulmonary: itraconazole; severe/disseminated: amphotericin B → itraconazole step-down.

conditions.name: Brucellosis
conditions.summary: Zoonosis; Brucella spp. (B. melitensis most common/virulent - goats/sheep; B. abortus - cattle; B. suis - swine); unpasteurised dairy, raw meat, occupational (farmers, vets, lab workers). Sx: undulant fever (fluctuating), night sweats, myalgia, arthralgia, hepatosplenomegaly, lymphadenopathy. Focal complications: spondylodiscitis (most common), sacroiliitis, epididymo-orchitis, neurobrucellosis (meningitis), endocarditis (rare but fatal). Ix: blood culture (slow); serology (SATAg ≥1:160); PCR. Mx: doxycycline 6 wk + rifampicin 6 wk (or streptomycin 2-3 wk); combination essential to prevent relapse.

conditions.name: Leptospirosis
conditions.summary: Zoonotic spirochaetosis; Leptospira interrogans; contact with rat urine-contaminated water (flooding, fresh water activities). Biphasic illness: Leptospiraemic phase (4-7 d): abrupt fever, myalgia (severe calf pain), headache, conjunctival suffusion, rash; then brief improvement → Immune phase: Weil disease (severe leptospirosis, 5-10%): jaundice, acute kidney injury (non-oliguric), pulmonary haemorrhage, uveitis, myocarditis, aseptic meningitis. Ix: serology (MAT - gold standard, available from wk 1-2); PCR (early). Mx: mild: doxycycline or amoxicillin; severe: IV penicillin G or ceftriaxone.

conditions.name: Scrub typhus
conditions.summary: Rickettsia-like infection; Orientia tsutsugamushi; transmitted by trombiculid mite larvae (chiggers); Asia-Pacific. Sx: fever, headache, myalgia, lymphadenopathy; pathognomonic eschar (painless black crust with erythematous halo at bite site); maculopapular rash (day 5-7). Complications: meningoencephalitis, myocarditis, AKI, ARDS, multi-organ failure. Ix: clinical (eschar); serology (Weil-Felix - low sensitivity; IIF - gold standard); PCR. Mx: doxycycline (200 mg daily × 7 d); chloramphenicol alternative; azithromycin in pregnancy/children. High mortality if untreated.

conditions.name: Visceral leishmaniasis
conditions.summary: Systemic infection by Leishmania donovani (Indian subcontinent, E. Africa) or L. infantum (Mediterranean, S. America); transmitted by sandfly bite. Sx: prolonged fever (>2 wk), progressive splenomegaly (massive), hepatomegaly, pancytopenia (anaemia, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia), cachexia, darkening of skin (kala-azar = black sickness). Untreated: >95% mortality. Ix: rK39 antigen test (rapid, high sensitivity in Indian VL); bone marrow/spleen aspirate (Leishman-Donovan bodies); PCR. Mx: liposomal amphotericin B (first-line globally); sodium stibogluconate (antimonial) in E. Africa; miltefosine (oral, teratogenic).

conditions.name: Schistosomiasis
conditions.summary: Helminth infection; Schistosoma spp.; cercariae penetrate intact skin in fresh water (sub-Saharan Africa, Middle East, SE Asia, S. America). Acute: Katayama fever (swimmer's itch → serum-sickness-like: urticaria, fever, eosinophilia, hepatosplenomegaly, 4-8 wk after heavy exposure). Chronic S. mansoni/S. japonicum: hepatic periportal fibrosis (pipestem fibrosis), portal hypertension, oesophageal varices, cor pulmonale. Chronic S. haematobium: urogenital schistosomiasis - haematuria, hydronephrosis, bladder SCC (major risk). Ix: stool/urine microscopy (ova); serology; rectal biopsy. Mx: praziquantel (drug of choice, single dose or 2-day course).

conditions.name: ACL tear
conditions.summary: Most common significant knee ligament injury; non-contact deceleration/pivot mechanism or contact valgus. Sx: 'pop', haemarthrosis within 2 hr, instability (giving way). Sx: Lachman test (best - anterior tibial translation with knee at 20°, most sensitive in acute), anterior drawer test, pivot shift. Associated injuries: 'unhappy triad' (ACL + MCL + medial meniscus, now ACL + lateral meniscus more common in clinical practice); medial meniscus more commonly torn with chronic ACL deficiency. Ix (MRI): gold standard for complete assessment. Mx: conservative (bracing + physio, for lower-demand patients); ACL reconstruction (BPTB or hamstring autograft) for active patients with instability.

conditions.name: Meniscal tear
conditions.summary: Very common knee injury; medial > lateral. Acute (twisting injury - young athletes) or degenerative (older, minimal trauma). Sx: medial/lateral joint line pain, swelling, locking (bucket-handle tear - knee stuck in 20-30° flexion), clicking. Sx: joint line tenderness, McMurray test (click/pain on rotation), Thessaly test. Ix (MRI): gold standard. Mx: acute locked knee → urgent meniscectomy; young patients with peripheral tears (red zone vascular) → repair; degenerative tears → conservative (physio); partial meniscectomy if conservative fails.

conditions.name: De Quervain tenosynovitis
conditions.summary: Stenosing tenosynovitis of 1st dorsal compartment (APL and EPB tendons). Common in new mothers (lifting baby) and racket sports. Sx: radial wrist pain, tenderness over radial styloid process. Finkelstein test: positive (pain on ulnar deviation with thumb held in fist) - pathognomonic. Ddx: first CMC joint OA (tenderness more distal, grind test), Wartenberg syndrome, radial nerve neuritis. Mx: activity modification, thumb spica splint; corticosteroid injection (highly effective); surgical decompression (first dorsal compartment release) if refractory.

conditions.name: Trigger finger
conditions.summary: Stenosing tenosynovitis of digital flexor tendon at A1 pulley; ring finger most common, then middle, little, thumb. Causes: idiopathic, diabetes, RA, hypothyroidism, amyloidosis. Stages: 0 (no locking) → 4 (locked in flexion). Sx: pain at A1 pulley, clicking/triggering on flexion-extension, nodule, locking in flexion (must passively extend - 'trigger' releases). Mx: splinting; corticosteroid injection at A1 pulley (effective, especially in non-diabetics); surgical A1 pulley release (definitive, percutaneous or open).

conditions.name: Golfer's elbow
conditions.summary: Tendinopathy of common flexor-pronator origin at medial epicondyle; overuse injury. Sports (golf, baseball, throwing) and occupational (gripping, repetitive pronation). Sx: medial epicondyle pain, worse with resisted wrist flexion and pronation, gripping. Sx: tenderness directly over medial epicondyle, pain on resisted wrist flexion (medial epicondyle) - compare to lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow). Ddx: cubital tunnel syndrome (ulnar nerve entrapment - check Tinel's, sensory loss 4th/5th finger), medial collateral ligament injury. Mx: rest, NSAIDs, physiotherapy (eccentric exercises); corticosteroid injection; PRP; surgical debridement if refractory (rarely needed).

conditions.name: Galactosaemia
conditions.summary: Autosomal recessive inborn error of galactose metabolism. Classic: GALT deficiency (galactose-1-phosphate uridylyltransferase). Sx: Presents in neonate on breast milk/formula (contains lactose): jaundice (conjugated + unconjugated), hepatomegaly, vomiting, poor feeding, hypoglycaemia, E. coli sepsis (galactose → impaired leucocyte killing), cataracts (galactitol). Ix: Newborn screening (blood spot). Long-term complications even on galactose-free diet: ovarian insufficiency (premature in females), intellectual disability, speech problems. Mx: galactose-free diet (eliminate milk, dairy).

conditions.name: MCAD deficiency
conditions.summary: Most common fatty acid oxidation disorder; ACADM gene mutation; autosomal recessive. Impaired medium-chain fatty acid oxidation → hypoketotic hypoglycaemia during fasting/illness. Presentations: 3-24 months; vomiting, lethargy → coma; Reye-like syndrome (vomiting, encephalopathy, raised transaminases, hyperammonaemia); sudden death (may mimic SIDS). Acylcarnitine profile: ↑C8 (octanoylcarnitine) - detected on newborn screening. Ix: newborn bloodspot screen (incl. UK); urinary organic acids (dicarboxylic aciduria); acylcarnitine profile; DNA genotyping. Mx: avoid prolonged fasting; emergency glucose during illness; carnitine if deficient; excellent prognosis if diagnosed before crisis.

conditions.name: Fragile X syndrome
conditions.summary: Most common inherited cause of intellectual disability; CGG trinucleotide repeat expansion in FMR1 gene (Xq27.3) - full mutation >200 repeats → gene silencing via hypermethylation → absent FMRP. X-linked dominant (males more severely affected). Sx: intellectual disability (mild-severe), autism spectrum features (gaze aversion, hand flapping), macroorchidism (post-pubertal), facial features (long narrow face, large ears, prominent jaw), behavioural (ADHD, anxiety, perseveration). Carrier females (55-200 repeats = premutation): FMR1 premutation-associated disorders: FXTAS (tremor/ataxia syndrome in elderly males), premature ovarian insufficiency. Ix: FMR1 CGG repeat analysis (DNA).

conditions.name: Williams syndrome
conditions.summary: Microdeletion 7q11.23 (elastin gene ELN + others); 1 in 7,500. Sx: supravalvular aortic stenosis (SVAS - pathognomonic; due to ELN deletion), peripheral pulmonary stenosis, hypercalcaemia (infancy), elfin facies (periorbital fullness, stellate iris, broad nasal tip, wide mouth, full lips), intellectual disability (mild-moderate), 'cocktail party personality' (overly friendly, loquacious, hypersocial), visuospatial deficit (blocks task failed), relative strengths in language/music, joint laxity, renal anomalies. FISH/SNP array for del 7q11.23. Mx: cardiology follow-up (progressive SVAS); calcium restriction if hypercalcaemic; developmental support.

conditions.name: Prader-Willi syndrome
conditions.summary: Genomic imprinting disorder; loss of paternally expressed genes on 15q11-q13. Causes: paternal deletion (70%), maternal uniparental disomy 15 (25%), imprinting defect (5%). Phases: infancy - hypotonia, poor suck, feeding difficulties, hypogonadism (cryptorchidism in males), short stature (GH deficiency); childhood onwards - hyperphagia (uncontrollable) → obesity (leading cause of morbidity), short stature, intellectual disability (mild), behavioural problems (stubbornness, skin picking, temper tantrums), sleep disturbance (sleep-disordered breathing, excessive daytime somnolence). Facial: narrow forehead, almond eyes, triangular mouth. Ix: methylation analysis (detects all types). Mx: GH therapy (improves height, body composition, cognition); strict dietary control; behaviour management.

conditions.name: Renal artery stenosis
conditions.summary: Narrowing of renal artery → reduced perfusion → RAAS activation → renovascular hypertension. Two causes: atherosclerosis (>90% - older patients, CV risk factors, bilateral in 30%, progressive renal impairment, flash pulmonary oedema) and fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD - young women, string-of-beads appearance on CTA, amenable to angioplasty). Sx: hypertension resistant to ≥3 agents, accelerated hypertension, renal impairment after starting ACEi/ARB, asymmetric kidneys on US, abdominal bruit. Ix: renal artery duplex ultrasound (screen); CT/MR angiography (confirm). Mx: atherosclerotic: aggressive medical Mx (ACEi/ARB, statins, aspirin) - renal artery stenting does not improve outcomes (ASTRAL, CORAL trials); FMD: percutaneous transluminal angioplasty.

conditions.name: Alport syndrome
conditions.summary: Hereditary nephritis due to mutations in type IV collagen genes (COL4A3/A4/A5). X-linked dominant (COL4A5 - most common, males severely affected): progressive nephritis (haematuria → proteinuria → ESRD by 20-30 yr); sensorineural hearing loss; anterior lenticonus (bilateral, pathognomonic - lens cone into anterior chamber); macular flecks. Autosomal recessive (COL4A3/A4 - similar severity to X-linked males). Autosomal dominant (COL4A3/A4 - milder). Ix: electron microscopy of kidney biopsy (irregular thinning/thickening of GBM, lamellation); genetic testing. Mx: ACEi (slows progression); dialysis/transplant (donor should be screened for Alport - risk of anti-GBM nephritis in transplant).

conditions.name: Bartter syndrome
conditions.summary: Rare autosomal recessive renal tubular disorder; defective Na-K-2Cl transporter in thick ascending limb (TAL) of loop of Henle (or associated channels). Phenotype: salt wasting → hypovolaemia → secondary hyperaldosteronism → hypokalaemia, metabolic alkalosis, hypomagnesaemia, hypercalciuria. Normotension (despite hyperaldosteronism - volume depletion + vasodilation). Type I-V by gene. Presents in infancy (polyhydramnios, salt wasting, failure to thrive, nephrocalcinosis) or milder in older children/adults. Ix: electrolytes (hypokalaemia + alkalosis + high urine chloride), normal BP, high renin/aldosterone. Mx: potassium/magnesium supplements; NSAIDs (indometacin); potassium-sparing diuretics (spironolactone, amiloride).

conditions.name: Gitelman syndrome
conditions.summary: Autosomal recessive renal tubular disorder; SLC12A3 (NCC transporter) mutation; defective Na-Cl reabsorption in distal convoluted tubule. Less severe than Bartter. Adult/adolescent presentation. Electrolytes: hypokalaemia, metabolic alkalosis, hypomagnesaemia, hypocalciuria (distinguishes from Bartter). Usually normotensive. Sx: often incidental; muscle cramps/weakness, fatigue, palpitations (hypokalaemia), paraesthesia (hypomagnesaemia), chondrocalcinosis. Ix: electrolytes + spot urine Ca/Cr ratio (low). Mx: oral KCl + MgCl supplements; NSAIDs if symptoms persist; amiloride; spironolactone.

conditions.name: Restrictive cardiomyopathy
conditions.summary: Least common cardiomyopathy; impaired ventricular filling (diastolic dysfunction) with normal/near-normal LV size and systolic function. Causes: amyloidosis (most common in developed world - AL or ATTR), sarcoidosis, haemochromatosis, endomyocardial fibrosis (tropical - Löffler endocarditis, eosinophilia), radiation. Sx: right-sided HF predominant (raised JVP, ascites, peripheral oedema, hepatomegaly), fatigue, exertional dyspnoea; Kussmaul sign. Ix (ECG): low voltage in amyloid; conduction blocks in sarcoid/haemochromatosis. Ix (echo): biventricular hypertrophy, granular sparkling (amyloid), biatrial enlargement, diastolic dysfunction. MRI with gadolinium: LGE pattern (diffuse subendocardial in amyloid; patchy in sarcoid). Mx: treat underlying cause; diuretics (cautiously); avoid digoxin in amyloid; tafamidis (ATTR amyloid).

conditions.name: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy
conditions.summary: Inherited cardiomyopathy (desmosomal proteins - PKP2 most common, DSG2, DSC2, DSP, JUP); fibrofatty replacement of RV myocardium → RV dilatation, dysfunction, arrhythmias. LV involvement in ~50%. Autosomal dominant, incomplete penetrance. Sx: palpitations, syncope, SCD in young adults (exercise-triggered); RV failure (late). Ix (ECG): epsilon wave (pathognomonic - notch after QRS in V1-V3), T-wave inversion V1-V3, LBBB morphology VT. Ix (MRI): RV dilatation/dysfunction, wall motion abnormality, fibrofatty infiltration (LGE). Task Force Criteria (2010) for diagnosis. SCD risk especially with exercise → restrict competitive sports; ICD; beta-blockers; sotalol/amiodarone; catheter ablation; transplant late-stage.

conditions.name: Brugada syndrome
conditions.summary: Inherited (SCN5A mutation in ~25%) or sporadic; Na⁺ channel dysfunction → coved-type ST elevation in V1-V3 (type 1 pattern - spontaneous or provoked by sodium channel blocker). Risk of VF/SCD during rest/sleep, especially males, SE Asian ethnicity ('sudden unexplained nocturnal death'). Fever can unmask/worsen. Ix: Schwartz-like diagnostic criteria (Brugada criteria). Mx: quinidine (Ito blocker - for VT/VF storms and asymptomatic with inducible VF); ICD (resuscitated SCD, symptomatic VT/VF); avoid Na⁺ channel blockers, tricyclics, cocaine, excessive alcohol, fever.

conditions.name: Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome
conditions.summary: Accessory pathway (bundle of Kent) bypasses AVN → pre-excitation on Ix (ECG): short PR + delta wave + wide QRS. Risk of SVT (AVRT - orthodromic most common: narrow QRS; antidromic: wide QRS), AF with rapid ventricular response (delta waves, irregular wide-complex tachycardia → VF risk). SCD risk from AF with rapid conduction over accessory pathway. Ix: ECG (delta waves); electrophysiology study (EPS). Mx: symptomatic/high-risk: catheter ablation of accessory pathway (curative, >95%); acute AF in WPW: DC cardioversion or procainamide - AVOID AVN blockers (digoxin, verapamil, adenosine → accelerate accessory pathway → VF).

conditions.name: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
conditions.summary: Transient LV dysfunction (apical ballooning); emotional/physical stress triggers (catecholamine surge). Predominantly post-menopausal women. Mimics ACS: chest pain, ECG changes (ST elevation → T-wave inversion, QTc prolongation), troponin rise (mild relative to wall motion abnormality extent). Echo/ventriculography: apical/mid-ventricular ballooning, hyperkinetic base. Coronary angiography: no obstructive CAD. Complications: LV outflow obstruction (dynamic), cardiogenic shock, acute MR, LV thrombus, VT/VF (rare). Ix: modified Mayo criteria. Mx: supportive (ACEi, beta-blockers; avoid dobutamine if LVOT obstruction); typically resolves in 4-8 wk; recurrence ~5%/yr.

conditions.name: Eisenmenger syndrome
conditions.summary: Pulmonary arterial hypertension with reversed (Eisenmenger physiology) or bidirectional shunt from originally left-to-right shunt (VSD, ASD, PDA, AVSD). Pathophysiology: chronic ↑pulmonary flow → vascular remodelling → ↑PVR → shunt reversal → cyanosis. Sx: progressive dyspnoea, cyanosis, clubbing, polycythaemia, haemoptysis, syncope; paradoxical emboli (stroke). Sx: cyanosis, clubbing, polycythaemia; RV heave; ↑P2; EDM (PR) or PSM (TR). Complications: haemoptysis, stroke, brain abscess, endocarditis, SCD, iron deficiency (iron-restricted erythropoiesis). Mx: targeted PAH therapy (sildenafil, bosentan, prostacyclins); heart-lung transplant; avoid pregnancy (very high maternal mortality); phlebotomy only if Hct >65% + symptoms (dehydrate with caution).

conditions.name: Occupational asthma
conditions.summary: Asthma caused or worsened by workplace exposures. Sensitiser-induced (most common): develops after latency period; persists after removal from exposure (isocyanates - painters/spray, latex, flour/grain dust, animal proteins, colophony). Irritant-induced (RADS): high-level exposure without latency. Classic: symptoms worse at work, improve on weekends/holidays; serial PEF monitoring (≥4 readings/day). Ix: serial PEF charts; specific inhalation challenge (gold standard); specific IgE/skin prick testing. Mx: complete removal from causative exposure (best outcome); treat like non-occupational asthma; compensation/medicolegal implications.

conditions.name: Pneumoconiosis
conditions.summary: Group of lung diseases from inhalation of mineral/organic dusts. Silicosis (crystalline silica - mining, quarrying, sandblasting): simple (nodular opacities upper lobes) → progressive massive fibrosis (PMF); acute silicosis if heavy exposure; ↑risk TB (silicatuberculosis). Coal workers' pneumoconiosis (coal dust): simple CWP (round opacities) → PMF (Caplan syndrome if RA). Asbestosis (asbestos fibres): bilateral lower lobe fibrosis, pleural plaques (bilateral, calcified, pathognomonic of asbestos exposure - not asbestosis per se); ↑risk lung carcinoma + mesothelioma. Berylliosis (chronic): granulomatous lung disease resembling sarcoidosis; LPT (lymphocyte proliferation test). Ix: All: history of occupational exposure + compatible HRCT + spirometry (restrictive). Mx: supportive; remove from exposure; surveillance.

conditions.name: Respiratory failure
conditions.summary: Type 1 (hypoxaemic): PaO₂ <8 kPa, PaCO₂ normal/low. Causes: V/Q mismatch (pneumonia, PE, ARDS, pulmonary oedema), shunt (ASD, hepatopulmonary). Type 2 (hypercapnic + hypoxaemic): PaO₂ <8 kPa, PaCO₂ >6 kPa. Causes: ↓respiratory drive (opiates, CNS), pump failure (COPD, NMD, chest wall, obesity hypoventilation). Ix: A-a gradient (elevated = parenchymal cause; normal = hypoventilation). Mx: Type 1 - high-flow O₂ (target SpO₂ 94-98%); treat cause; CPAP/intubation if severe. Type 2 - controlled O₂ (target 88-92% in COPD); NIV (BiPAP - reduces intubation/mortality in COPD and cardiogenic pulmonary oedema); treat cause; invasive ventilation if NIV fails.

conditions.name: Obesity hypoventilation syndrome
conditions.summary: Obesity (BMI>30) + daytime hypercapnia (PaCO₂ >6 kPa) not explained by other cause; 90% have OSA. Pathophysiology: reduced chest wall compliance, ↑work of breathing, blunted hypercapnic response. Sx: severe daytime somnolence (worse than OSA alone), dyspnoea, oedema (cor pulmonale). ABG: hypercapnic, hypoxaemic, compensated respiratory acidosis (↑bicarbonate). Polycythaemia. Ix (CXR): cardiomegaly, pleural effusions. Mx: CPAP (OSA-predominant) or NIV/BiPAP (hypercapnia-predominant); weight loss (bariatric surgery); respiratory stimulants (medroxyprogesterone, acetazolamide); acute hypercapnic decompensation: NIV.

conditions.name: Ménière's disease
conditions.summary: Recurrent episodes of vertigo + tinnitus + fluctuating sensorineural hearing loss (SNHL) + aural fullness; endolymphatic hydrops (idiopathic). Attacks last 20 min to 12 hr (average 2-3 hr); SNHL affects low frequencies initially. Diagnostic criteria: ≥2 definite episodes vertigo 20 min-12 hr + documented SNHL + tinnitus/fullness + not better explained by other diagnosis. Ix: clinical; audiogram (low-frequency SNHL). Mx: acute attack: prochlorperazine/betahistine; prophylaxis: betahistine (high-dose: 48 mg tds), low-salt diet, diuretics (bendroflumethiazide); intratympanic gentamicin (chemical ablation - controls vertigo, risk SNHL); endolymphatic sac surgery; labyrinthectomy (deafened ear, intractable vertigo).

conditions.name: Vestibular neuritis
conditions.summary: Acute unilateral vestibular dysfunction; presumed viral/post-viral (HSV-1). Vestibular neuritis: vertigo only (cochlear nerve spared). Labyrinthitis: vertigo + hearing loss/tinnitus (cochlea affected). Sx: sudden severe vertigo, nausea/vomiting, unsteady; lasts days-weeks; no auditory symptoms (neuritis). Head impulse test (HIT): positive (catch-up saccade - reduced VOR). No nystagmus with gaze change (unlike central cause). HINTS exam in acute vestibular syndrome: HIT normal (absent), nystagmus direction-changing, skew deviation = central (stroke) - emergency MRI; HIT abnormal (present), unidirectional nystagmus, no skew = peripheral (neuritis). Mx: vestibular sedatives (prochlorperazine, cyclizine - first 48 hr only); corticosteroids (prednisolone ↑vestibular recovery); vestibular rehabilitation (key - Cawthorne-Cooksey exercises); resolves 6-12 wk.

conditions.name: Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome
conditions.summary: Paraneoplastic (SCLC - 50-60%) or autoimmune; VGCC (voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channel) antibodies → ↓acetylcholine release from presynaptic terminal. Sx: proximal limb weakness (worse initially, improves with repeated activity - facilitation, opposite to MG), hyporeflexia (reflexes return after repeated contraction), autonomic dysfunction (dry mouth, constipation, erectile dysfunction, orthostatic hypotension, ocular, absent sweating). Ptosis/diplopia less prominent than MG. NCS/EMG: low CMAP amplitude, incremental response on rapid repetitive stimulation (>100 Hz or after voluntary contraction - key difference from MG). Ix: VGCC antibodies; screen for malignancy (CT/PET). Mx: treat underlying malignancy; 3,4-diaminopyridine (DAP - enhances ACh release, first-line symptomatic); pyridostigmine; IVIG; immunosuppression.

conditions.name: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease
conditions.summary: Most common hereditary peripheral neuropathy. CMT1 (demyelinating): CMT1A - PMP22 duplication (17p11.2), AD; most common. CMT1X: GJB1 (connexin 32), X-linked dominant. CMT2 (axonal): various. Sx: childhood/young adult onset; distal muscle wasting (peroneal atrophy - 'inverted champagne bottle' legs), foot deformity (pes cavus, hammer toes), distal sensory loss, absent reflexes, slow nerve conduction velocities (CMT1), steppage gait, scoliosis. Ix: NCS/EMG; genetic testing (panel). Mx: no disease-modifying therapy; physiotherapy; orthotics (AFO); foot surgery; avoid neurotoxic drugs (vincristine - severely worsens CMT).

conditions.name: Hyperprolactinaemia
conditions.summary: ↑serum prolactin. Causes: physiological (pregnancy, lactation, stress, exercise, sleep); drugs (dopamine antagonists - metoclopramide, antipsychotics, domperidone; opioids; oestrogens; methyldopa; verapamil); hypothyroidism (TRH stimulates prolactin); pituitary stalk effect (any large pituitary/hypothalamic mass compressing stalk - blocks dopamine); prolactinoma (most common pituitary tumour; micro <10 mm, macro ≥10 mm). Sx: hypogonadism (amenorrhoea, oligomenorrhoea, infertility, ↓libido, erectile dysfunction), galactorrhoea (non-puerperal lactation; absent in ~50%); macroadenoma: headache, visual field defect. Ix: serum prolactin; MRI pituitary; TFTs. Mx: prolactinoma: dopamine agonists (cabergoline first-line - best efficacy/tolerability; bromocriptine - cheaper, used in pregnancy); surgery (transsphenoidal) if intolerant/resistant or large macro with mass effect; drug-induced: review medication.

conditions.name: Hypoparathyroidism
conditions.summary: ↓PTH → hypocalcaemia + hyperphosphataemia. Causes: post-surgical (thyroidectomy, parathyroidectomy - most common), autoimmune (APS type 1, isolated), DiGeorge syndrome (22q11.2 deletion), hypomagnesaemia (functional hypoparathyroidism). Sx: hypocalcaemia - perioral tingling, paraesthesia (fingertips), muscle cramps, tetany (carpopedal spasm), Chvostek sign (facial muscle twitch on tapping facial nerve), Trousseau sign (carpal spasm on BP cuff inflation), prolonged QTc, seizures, cataracts, basal ganglia calcification (chronic). Ix: ↓Ca²⁺, ↑PO₄, ↓PTH; check Mg (correct first). Mx: acute hypocalcaemia: IV calcium gluconate (10 mL 10% slowly); chronic: oral calcium carbonate + calcitriol (active vitamin D); recombinant PTH 1-34 (teriparatide) for chronic hypoparathyroidism if conventional Mx inadequate.

conditions.name: Pseudohypoparathyroidism
conditions.summary: PTH resistance (not PTH deficiency); GNAS1 mutation (imprinting - maternal allele affected in PHP Ia). Biochemistry same as hypoparathyroidism (↓Ca²⁺, ↑PO₄) but ↑PTH. Ix: PHP Ia (Albright hereditary osteodystrophy, AHO): short stature, rounded face, short 4th/5th metacarpals, obesity, cognitive impairment; also TSH/gonadotrophin resistance. Sx: PHP Ib: isolated PTH resistance, no AHO features. PHP II: post-receptor defect. Mx: same as hypoparathyroidism (calcium + calcitriol).

conditions.name: Necrotising enterocolitis
conditions.summary: Serious inflammatory/ischaemic injury of neonatal intestine; predominantly premature infants (inversely related to gestational age). Risk: prematurity, formula feeding (breast milk protective), perinatal hypoxia, infection. Sx: feed intolerance, bilious vomiting, abdominal distension, bloody stools, systemic illness (temperature instability, apnoea, lethargy, shock). X-ray: pneumatosis intestinalis (pathognomonic - intramural gas), portal venous gas, free air (perforation). Ix: clinical + AXR. Bell staging I-III. Mx: bowel rest (nil by mouth), NG decompression, IV antibiotics (gram-negative + anaerobe coverage), total parenteral nutrition; surgical (resection ± stoma) for perforation, peritonitis, full-thickness necrosis - short bowel syndrome complication.

conditions.name: Paracetamol overdose
conditions.summary: Most common cause of acute liver failure in UK/USA. Mechanism: NAPQI (toxic metabolite) saturates glutathione → hepatocyte necrosis. Risk: staggered/therapeutic excess doses, malnutrition/anorexia (↓glutathione), chronic alcohol, hepatic enzyme inducers (carbamazepine, rifampicin, phenytoin - ↑NAPQI). Phase I (0-24 hr): nausea, vomiting, malaise (or asymptomatic). Phase II (24-72 hr): hepatic tenderness, ↑ALT/AST (can reach >10,000 IU/L), ↑bilirubin, coagulopathy. Phase III (72-96 hr): fulminant hepatic failure, renal failure, encephalopathy, death. Phase IV: recovery. Ix: paracetamol level (4-hr post-ingestion plotted on treatment nomogram; not applicable for staggered OD). Mx: activated charcoal (within 1-2 hr); N-acetylcysteine (NAC) IV (antidote - replenishes glutathione; effective up to 24 hr, benefit up to 72 hr in some); transplant listing (King's criteria - MELD or pH <7.3, PT>100/INR>6.5, creatinine >300, grade III-IV encephalopathy).

conditions.name: Opioid overdose
conditions.summary: Opioid toxidrome: miosis (pinpoint pupils - classic), respiratory depression (key - respiratory rate <12, ↑PaCO₂), decreased consciousness; may have hypothermia, bradycardia, hypotension, pulmonary oedema, rhabdomyolysis. Drugs: heroin, morphine, fentanyl (and analogues - carfentanil 100× fentanyl potency, mass casualty risk), codeine, tramadol, oxycodone, methadone (long half-life - prolonged toxicity). Mx: immediate naloxone (IV/IM/IN - 0.4 mg IV, repeated every 2-3 min; titrate to breathing, not full reversal - precipitates withdrawal/agitation); airway support; naloxone infusion for long-acting opioids (methadone half-life 36-60 hr - observation and repeat doses needed); monitor for re-narcotisation. Harm reduction: naloxone take-home kits; opioid substitution therapy (methadone, buprenorphine).

conditions.name: Benzodiazepine overdose
conditions.summary: Benzodiazepines act on GABA-A receptor (Cl⁻ influx). Sx: Toxidrome: sedation, slurred speech, ataxia, amnesia; respiratory depression (mild compared to opioids); miosis (less marked than opioids). Rarely fatal in isolation; dangerous combined with alcohol/opioids (synergistic CNS/respiratory depression - most overdose deaths). Mx: Supportive care (airway, breathing, IV access). Flumazenil (competitive GABA-A antagonist - antidote): use with caution - precipitates seizures in chronic users/epileptics, benzodiazepine dependence, and TCA co-ingestion; short-acting (30-60 min) → re-sedation with long-acting BZDs; NOT routinely recommended.

conditions.name: Carbon monoxide poisoning
conditions.summary: CO binds Hb (240× greater affinity than O₂) → carboxyhaemoglobin (COHb) → impaired O₂ delivery + cellular toxicity (cytochrome c oxidase). Sources: faulty boilers/gas heaters, car exhaust, fire smoke. Classic: multiple people affected in enclosed space; cherry-red skin (not always present, often cyanosis). Sx: mild (headache, nausea, dizziness); moderate (confusion, visual disturbance, ataxia, tachycardia); severe (syncope, seizures, coma, cardiac arrhythmias, pulmonary oedema). SpO₂ unreliable (co-oximeter overestimates). Ix: co-oximetry (arterial or venous blood gas); COHb level (>3% non-smoker, >10% smoker = significant). Mx: 100% O₂ via non-rebreather mask (reduces COHb half-life from 5 hr to 60-90 min); hyperbaric oxygen (HBO - indications: COHb >25%, loss of consciousness, cardiac/neurological complications, pregnancy; reduces delayed neurological sequelae); assess for cyanide (fire victims) - give hydroxocobalamin.

conditions.name: Anorexia nervosa
conditions.summary: Eating disorder; distorted body image + persistent food restriction + intense fear of weight gain; underweight (BMI <17.5 or <85% expected). Subtypes: restricting and binge-purge. Medical complications: amenorrhoea/anovulation (hypothalamic), lanugo, bradycardia, hypotension, hypothermia, ↓bone density (osteoporosis), ↓K⁺ (purging), ↓phosphate (refeeding syndrome risk), ↓oestrogen, prolonged QTc, dental erosion (purging). Highest mortality of any psychiatric disorder (5-10% - anorexia + suicide). Ix: DSM-5 criteria; exclude organic causes of weight loss. Mx: restore nutrition/weight (inpatient if BMI <13-14 or medically compromised); refeeding syndrome prevention (thiamine, phosphate monitoring, gradual increase); SSRI not effective for weight restoration; CBT-E (cognitive behavioural therapy for eating disorders); MANTRA/SSCM; olanzapine (weight gain adjunct); family-based therapy (adolescents).

conditions.name: Bulimia nervosa
conditions.summary: Eating disorder; binge eating + compensatory behaviour (purging - self-induced vomiting, laxatives, diuretics; non-purging - exercise, fasting); normal or overweight (BMI 18.5-25). Binge: objectively large amount of food in discrete time + loss of control. At least 1×/wk × 3 months (DSM-5). Medical complications: parotid hypertrophy (Russell's sign - calluses on dorsal hand from vomiting), dental erosion (enamel loss from acid), ↓K⁺ (hypokalaemia - life-threatening arrhythmias, Mallory-Weiss tears), aspiration, peripheral oedema (laxative abuse). Ix: DSM-5; exclude purging disorder, BED. Mx: CBT (gold standard - most evidence); SSRI (fluoxetine 60 mg/d - licensed for BN, reduces binge frequency); guided self-help; nutritional rehabilitation.

conditions.name: Binge eating disorder
conditions.summary: Most common eating disorder; recurrent binge eating without regular compensatory behaviour (distinguishes from BN). Binge episodes ≥1×/wk × 3 months; marked distress. Often associated with obesity, depression, anxiety. Ix: DSM-5. Mx: CBT (first-line for binge behaviour + distress); IPT; SSRI (less evidence than in BN); lisdexamfetamine (licensed for moderate-severe BED in adults - ADHD medication that ↓binge frequency); dialectical behaviour therapy (DBT); address obesity separately (GLP-1 agonists, bariatric surgery).

conditions.name: Generalised anxiety disorder
conditions.summary: Excessive, difficult-to-control anxiety about multiple activities/events on most days for ≥6 months. Associated: muscle tension, fatigue, difficulty concentrating, irritability, sleep disturbance, restlessness. Significant impairment. Distinguish from: depression (often comorbid), panic disorder (discrete attacks), PTSD (related to specific trauma), OCD (obsessions/compulsions). GAD-7 screening tool. Mx: low-intensity first (NICE step 2): self-help/psychoeducation, bibliotherapy; high-intensity: CBT or applied relaxation; pharmacological: SSRI/SNRI (first-line - sertraline, venlafaxine; 8-12 wk adequate trial); pregabalin (second-line); buspirone; avoid long-term benzodiazepines (dependence, does not treat underlying GAD).

conditions.name: Eating disorder not otherwise specified
conditions.summary: ARFID (avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder): avoidance/restriction of food intake not driven by body image concerns; may be sensory sensitivity, fear of choking/vomiting, or lack of interest. Common in autism, ADHD, anxiety. Can cause malnutrition, growth failure, social impairment. Ix: OSFED: clinically significant eating disorders not meeting full criteria for AN, BN, BED (e.g., atypical AN - full syndrome at normal weight; sub-threshold BN/BED; purging disorder; night eating syndrome). Mx: ARFID - CBT (food exposure hierarchy), dietetics; feeding support; OSFED - treat as the most similar full disorder.

conditions.name: Insomnia disorder
conditions.summary: Difficulty initiating/maintaining sleep or early waking, ≥3 nights/wk for ≥3 months with daytime impairment; not explained by other sleep disorder or substance. Causes: psychophysiological (conditioned arousal - most common chronic insomnia), comorbid psychiatric (depression, anxiety, PTSD), medical (pain, nocturia, OSA, restless legs), substance (alcohol, caffeine, stimulants), circadian (shift work, jet lag). Sx: daytime fatigue, cognitive impairment, mood disruption, poor performance. Ix: sleep diary/actigraphy; exclude OSA (Epworth Sleepiness Scale, sleep study). Mx: CBT-I (CBT for insomnia - first-line; sleep restriction therapy, stimulus control, sleep hygiene, relaxation, cognitive restructuring; superior to medication long-term); sleep hygiene; pharmacological: z-drugs (zolpidem, zopiclone - short-term only), melatonin (CRD-pattern, ≥55 yr in EU; jet lag), doxepin (low dose), suvorexant/lemborexant (orexin receptor antagonists - emerging); avoid long-term hypnotics.

conditions.name: Substance use disorder
conditions.summary: Pattern of substance use causing significant impairment/distress: ≥2 of 11 DSM-5 criteria within 12 months (tolerance, withdrawal, larger amounts, inability to cut down, time spent using, craving, failure to fulfil obligations, social problems, recreational activities given up, hazardous use, continued despite harm). Mx: Substances: alcohol, opioids, cannabis, stimulants (cocaine, amfetamine), sedatives, hallucinogens, nicotine. Opioid use disorder (OUD): OST (opioid substitution therapy) - methadone (full agonist, closely monitored, once-daily, risk of QTc prolongation and OD) or buprenorphine (partial agonist, safer, sublingual; buprenorphine-naloxone [Suboxone] reduces diversion/injection); naltrexone (extended-release IM - maintenance for high-motivated abstinent patients); needle exchange; naloxone distribution. Cannabis use disorder: no pharmacological treatment; CBT; motivational interviewing. Nicotine: NRT, varenicline (most effective), bupropion; combination NRT.

conditions.name: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome
conditions.summary: Potentially fatal idiosyncratic reaction to antipsychotics (typical > atypical) or dopamine agonist withdrawal; dopamine D2 receptor blockade in striatum + hypothalamus. Sx (tetrad): hyperthermia (>38°C, often >40°C), rigidity ('lead pipe'), altered consciousness (confusion → coma), autonomic instability (diaphoresis, tachycardia, labile BP, tachypnoea). ↑CK (often >1000, can be >100,000), leukocytosis, ↑LFTs, metabolic acidosis, myoglobinuria → AKI. Onset: hours to days after starting/increasing antipsychotic or stopping dopaminergic. Ddx: serotonin syndrome (hyperthermia + clonus/hyperreflexia + agitation/diarrhoea; onset faster, <24 hr), malignant hyperthermia (inhalational anaesthetic/succinylcholine), anticholinergic toxidrome. Mx: stop causative drug; supportive - IV fluids, cooling, respiratory support; bromocriptine or dantrolene (↓rigidity); benzodiazepines (agitation/rigidity); ECT (refractory/catatonic); recovery days-weeks; restart antipsychotics cautiously after 2 wk.

conditions.name: Serotonin syndrome
conditions.summary: Excess serotonergic activity at 5-HT1A/2A receptors; triad (Hunter criteria): neuromuscular abnormalities (clonus - most discriminating, hyperreflexia, agitation, tremor), autonomic instability (hyperthermia, tachycardia, ↑BP, diaphoresis), altered mental status. Onset: rapid (<24 hr, often within 6 hr). Mx: Caused by serotonergic drugs alone or combination: SSRIs/SNRIs + MAOIs (most dangerous), linezolid (MAOI properties), tramadol, fentanyl, pethidine, triptans, lithium, St John's Wort, cocaine, MDMA/ecstasy. Sx: Distinguish from NMS (rigidity vs clonus; slower onset). Ix: Hunter criteria: clonus + agitation or diaphoresis, OR tremor + hyperreflexia, OR hypertonia + hyperthermia + clonus OR ocular clonus. Mx: discontinue serotonergic drugs; supportive - benzodiazepines (agitation, seizures, BP), cooling (hyperthermia); cyproheptadine (5-HT2A antagonist - ↓serotonergic activity); severe: intubation, paralysis; usually resolves 24-72 hr.

conditions.name: Malignant hyperthermia
conditions.summary: Pharmacogenetic disorder of skeletal muscle; mutations in ryanodine receptor 1 (RYR1, 70%) or DHPR (CACNA1S); autosomal dominant, incomplete penetrance. Triggered by: volatile inhalational anaesthetics (halothane, isoflurane, desflurane, sevoflurane) and depolarising neuromuscular blocker (succinylcholine). Mechanism: uncontrolled SR Ca²⁺ release → sustained muscle contraction → hyperthermia, acidosis. Sx: masseter muscle rigidity (early - after succinylcholine), ↑ETCO₂ (earliest metabolic sign), tachycardia, muscle rigidity (generalised), hyperthermia (>38.8°C → can reach 45°C), rhabdomyolysis, metabolic/respiratory acidosis, DIC, death if untreated. Ix: clinical; ↑CK, ↑K⁺, ↑lactate; CHCT (caffeine halothane contracture test - diagnostic gold standard, muscle biopsy). Mx: STOP trigger agents immediately; dantrolene (skeletal muscle relaxant - inhibits RYR1-mediated Ca²⁺ release; 2.5 mg/kg IV bolus, repeat to max 10 mg/kg; life-saving); 100% O₂; active cooling; correct acidosis/K⁺; avoid succinylcholine/volatiles in known cases (use TIVA).

conditions.name: Heat stroke
conditions.summary: Core temperature >40°C + CNS dysfunction (confusion, seizures, coma) + anhidrosis (classic) or diaphoresis (exertional). Classic heat stroke: elderly/chronically ill; hot humid environment; impaired thermoregulation (anticholinergics, diuretics, CCBs); dry skin. Exertional: young athletes/military recruits; extreme exercise + environmental heat; wet skin. Complications: multi-organ failure (AKI, hepatic failure, ARDS, DIC, rhabdomyolysis, coagulopathy). Ix: rectal temperature (most accurate - oesophageal/bladder); ABG, FBC, metabolic panel, CK, coagulation, troponin. Mx: immediate aggressive cooling (core temp to <39°C within 30 min - ↑survival): ice water immersion (most rapid/effective for exertional), evaporative cooling (spray + fan), ice packs (axilla, groin, neck - less efficient); IV fluids; monitor and treat complications; NO antipyretics (not effective - different mechanism from pyrexia).

conditions.name: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma
conditions.summary: Heterogeneous group of lymphoid malignancies. B-cell (85%): DLBCL, follicular, MCL, Burkitt, marginal zone, CLL/SLL. T-cell (15%): PTCL-NOS, ALCL (ALK+/−), AITL, CTCL/mycosis fungoides. Sx: lymphadenopathy (painless, rubbery - unlike painful in infection), constitutional B symptoms (fever >38°C, night sweats, weight loss >10%), extranodal disease (GI, skin, CNS, bone marrow). PET-CT staging (Ann Arbor I-IV + A/B), FDG-avid for most NHL. Bone marrow biopsy (stage IV if marrow involved). IPI (International Prognostic Index) for aggressive NHL. Mx: type and stage dependent; generally: anti-CD20 therapy (rituximab) backbone for B-cell lymphomas; CHOP-based chemotherapy; novel agents (BTK inhibitors, BCL-2 inhibitors, CAR-T for relapsed/refractory).

conditions.name: Hodgkin lymphoma
conditions.summary: B-cell malignancy; Reed-Sternberg cells (CD30+, CD15+, CD20−, characteristic owl-eye appearance - pathognomonic). Bimodal age distribution (young adults 20-30 yr; second peak >50 yr). EBV association (especially mixed cellularity). Subtypes: classical HL (95%) - nodular sclerosis (most common, young women, mediastinal), mixed cellularity (EBV+), lymphocyte-rich, lymphocyte-depleted; nodular lymphocyte-predominant HL (NLPHL, 5% - LP/'popcorn' cells, CD20+, indolent, better prognosis). Sx: painless cervical/supraclavicular lymphadenopathy; mediastinal mass (dyspnoea); B symptoms; alcohol-induced nodal pain (classic - not always present). PET-CT staging. Mx: early-stage (I-IIA): ABVD × 2-4 + radiotherapy (or ABVD × 4-6 without RT); advanced (III-IV): ABVD × 6 or esc-BEACOPP; relapsed/refractory: salvage chemo + ASCT; brentuximab vedotin (anti-CD30) + pembrolizumab; cure rate >85% early-stage.

conditions.name: Chronic lymphocytic leukaemia
conditions.summary: Most common adult leukaemia in Western world; clonal B-cell (CD5+, CD23+, CD20dim, CD19+); IGHV mutational status (mutated = better prognosis). Median age 70 yr; males > females. Sx: usually asymptomatic (incidental lymphocytosis); progressive lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, anaemia (normocytic or autoimmune haemolytic - AIHA), thrombocytopenia (ITP or marrow infiltration); infections (hypogammaglobulinaemia). Rai/Binet staging. High-risk molecular markers: del 17p (TP53 mutation), del 11q, unmutated IGHV. Ix: persistent lymphocytosis >5 × 10⁹/L + immunophenotyping. Mx: watch-and-wait (early, asymptomatic); chemoimmunotherapy (FCR - fludarabine, cyclophosphamide, rituximab; fit, mutated IGHV, young); targeted: ibrutinib (BTK inhibitor), acalabrutinib (less CV SE), venetoclax + obinutuzumab (BCL-2 inhibitor); richter transformation → aggressive NHL management.

conditions.name: Acute myeloid leukaemia
conditions.summary: Clonal expansion of myeloid blasts (≥20% in marrow/blood); most common acute leukaemia in adults. Risk: prior haematological disorder (MDS → secondary AML), radiation, cytotoxic therapy (alkylating agents, topoisomerase II inhibitors), Down syndrome (AML-M7), Fanconi anaemia. WHO classification: by genetics (NPM1, FLT3-ITD, CEBPA, IDH1/2, t(15;17)/PML-RARA, t(8;21)/RUNX1-RUNX1T1, inv(16)/CBFβ). Sx: cytopenias (fatigue, haemorrhage - DIC especially APL, infection), leukostasis (>100×10⁹/L blasts → hypoxia, CNS), gum hypertrophy (M5 - monocytic). APL (M3, PML-RARA): DIC, highly sensitive to ATRA + arsenic trioxide (excellent prognosis if survive initial DIC). Mx: induction 7+3 (cytarabine + anthracycline) → consolidation; HSCT (standard/poor risk, ≥CR1); FLT3 inhibitors (midostaurin, quizartinib for FLT3-ITD+); IDH inhibitors (enasidenib, ivosidenib); venetoclax + azacitidine (elderly/unfit - now standard).

conditions.name: Acute lymphoblastic leukaemia
conditions.summary: Clonal proliferation of lymphoid precursor cells (B-cell 85%, T-cell 15%); most common childhood cancer; bimodal: peak 3-5 yr + adults >50 yr. Philadelphia chromosome (t(9;22)/BCR-ABL1 - Ph+ ALL) worse prognosis; now treated with TKI. MLL rearrangements (infants - worst prognosis). T-ALL: adolescent males, mediastinal mass (superior mediastinal syndrome). Sx: bone marrow failure (anaemia, infection, bleeding); bone pain (periosteal infiltration), hepatosplenomegaly, lymphadenopathy, CNS (headache, cranial nerve palsy - prophylaxis mandatory), testicular infiltration. Ix: blood film (lymphoblasts), immunophenotyping, cytogenetics, FISH, RT-PCR for BCR-ABL1. Mx: multi-agent induction (vincristine, anthracycline, steroid, asparaginase) → CNS prophylaxis (intrathecal methotrexate) → consolidation → maintenance (2-3 yr); TKI (imatinib/dasatinib for Ph+); HSCT (high risk/relapse); blinatumomab (BiTE antibody), inotuzumab ozogamicin, CAR-T (tisagenlecleucel in children/young adults with R/R B-ALL).

conditions.name: Chronic myeloid leukaemia
conditions.summary: Clonal myeloproliferative neoplasm; t(9;22) BCR-ABL1 (Philadelphia chromosome) → constitutively active tyrosine kinase. Three phases: chronic (years - best response to TKI), accelerated (blasts 10-19%, clonal evolution), blast crisis (blasts ≥20% - AML-like or ALL-like phenotype; poor prognosis). Sx: chronic phase: fatigue, splenomegaly (massive - characteristic, left-sided pain); hyperviscosity. Blood film: characteristic spectrum of myeloid cells at all stages of maturation ('left shift'); ↑basophils (pathognomonic); ↑platelets. ↓NAP (neutrophil alkaline phosphatase - distinguishes from leukaemoid reaction). BCR-ABL1 (FISH, RT-PCR). Mx: TKI (tyrosine kinase inhibitor) first-line: imatinib (1st gen), dasatinib/nilotinib (2nd gen - deeper/faster remission), asciminib (3rd gen - STAMP inhibitor, for T315I resistant/intolerant); monitor BCR-ABL1 PCR response (major molecular response MR3, deep MR4/5); HSCT (accelerated/blast crisis or TKI-resistant); TKI discontinuation possible in sustained deep molecular response (~40%).

conditions.name: Myelofibrosis
conditions.summary: Myeloproliferative neoplasm; progressive BM fibrosis → extramedullary haematopoiesis. Driver mutations: JAK2 V617F (60%), CALR (25%), MPL (8%); 'high-molecular risk': ASXL1, SRSF2, EZH2, IDH1/2 mutations (worse prognosis). Pre-fibrotic phase (pre-PMF) → overt fibrotic phase. Sx: progressive splenomegaly (massive), anaemia (leukoerythroblastic - immature WBC + nucleated RBC, teardrops on film), constitutional symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss, fatigue), portal hypertension, bone pain. ↑LDH; ↑uric acid. Blood film: leukoerythroblastic anaemia, teardrop cells (dacrocytes). BM biopsy: reticulin/collagen fibrosis (grade MF-0 to MF-3). IPSS/DIPSS scoring. Mx: ruxolitinib (JAK1/2 inhibitor - ↓spleen, ↑QoL, modest OS benefit); fedratinib, pacritinib (alternatives for low platelets); HSCT (only curative - high-risk young patients); transfusions; hydroxycarbamide; luspatercept (anaemia); danazol (steroids for anaemia in pre-fibrotic).

conditions.name: Nephritic syndrome
conditions.summary: Inflammation of glomeruli → haematuria (dysmorphic RBCs, RBC casts - specific for glomerulonephritis), proteinuria (non-nephrotic range, usually), hypertension, oedema, ↓GFR/oliguria. Causes: IgA nephropathy (most common worldwide), post-streptococcal GN (2-4 wk after URTI/impetigo; ↓C3, normal C4; resolves spontaneously), lupus nephritis (↓C3/C4 - hypocomplementaemia; ANA/anti-dsDNA), MPGN (↓C3 ± C4; secondary: hep C, chronic infection; C3 glomerulopathy), Goodpasture (anti-GBM - linear IgG; haemoptysis/pulmonary haemorrhage), ANCA-associated GN (pauci-immune, no immune deposits). Rapidly progressive GN (RPGN) = crescentic GN - acute deterioration in GFR, crescents on biopsy; emergency. Ix: urinalysis, renal biopsy, complement, ANCA, anti-GBM, ANA, anti-dsDNA, ASOT/ASO titre, hepatitis serology. Mx: treat underlying cause; immunosuppression (steroids ± cyclophosphamide for crescentic GN, ANCA, lupus); plasma exchange (anti-GBM, severe ANCA).

conditions.name: IgA vasculitis
conditions.summary: IgA-mediated small vessel vasculitis; most common childhood vasculitis (peak 4-7 yr). Sx (tetrad): palpable purpura (non-blanching, lower limbs/buttocks), arthritis/arthralgia (ankles/knees), abdominal pain (colicky, gut vasculitis → intussusception in 2%, GI bleed), renal involvement (IgA nephropathy - haematuria ± proteinuria; in 20-50%). Often post-infection trigger (URTI, GAS). Skin biopsy: IgA deposits (perivascular). Adults have more severe renal disease than children. Ix: clinical; urinalysis (renal monitoring × 3-6 months); skin biopsy. Mx: mostly self-limiting; NSAIDs (arthralgia); prednisolone (abdominal pain - may prevent intussusception; no proven benefit for renal disease); ACEi/ARB (established nephritis + proteinuria); immunosuppression for severe renal disease.
