conditions.name: Lupus nephritis
conditions.summary: Renal involvement in SLE (affects 50-60%); major cause of morbidity/mortality. ISN/RPS classification: Class I (minimal mesangial), II (mesangial proliferative), III (focal proliferative - <50% glomeruli), IV (diffuse proliferative - ≥50% glomeruli; worst prognosis, most aggressive), V (membranous - nephrotic syndrome), VI (advanced sclerosing - >90% global sclerosis). Sx: haematuria, proteinuria, nephrotic syndrome (class V), nephritic (class III/IV), hypertension, ↓GFR, renal failure. Hypocomplementaemia (↓C3, ↓C4 - class III/IV); ↑anti-dsDNA (active disease marker); 'wire loop' lesion on biopsy (subendothelial deposits). Mx: class III/IV: induction - MMF (mycophenolate mofetil) or cyclophosphamide (EURO-LUPUS) + steroids + hydroxychloroquine; belimumab (BLyS inhibitor) + MMF; voclosporin (calcineurin inhibitor) + MMF (↓proteinuria in class III-V); maintenance: MMF ± hydroxychloroquine; renal replacement if failure.

conditions.name: Acute pancreatitis
conditions.summary: Acute inflammation of pancreas; autodigestion by activated enzymes. Causes (I GET SMASHED): Idiopathic, Gallstones (most common, 40%), Ethanol (second most common), Trauma, Steroids, Mumps/autoimmune, Autoimmune, Scorpion sting, Hyperlipidaemia/Hypothermia, ERCP, Drugs (azathioprine, thiazides, valproate). Sx: severe epigastric pain radiating to back, nausea/vomiting, tenderness (guarding), Grey-Turner sign (flank bruising - haemorrhagic), Cullen sign (periumbilical bruising). ↑amylase (>3× ULN; or lipase - more specific). Severity scoring: Atlanta revised criteria (mild, moderate, severe); APACHE-II; Glasgow (Imrie) score; CRP >150 at 48 hr = severe. CT (contrast-enhanced) at 48-72 hr for: uncertain diagnosis, suspected complications (necrotising pancreatitis). Mx: aggressive IV fluid resuscitation; analgesia; nutritional support (early oral/NG - superior to TPN); ERCP (within 72 hr for biliary pancreatitis with cholangitis/persistent obstruction); surgical debridement of infected pancreatic necrosis; cholecystectomy during same admission or early after for gallstone pancreatitis.

conditions.name: Chronic pancreatitis
conditions.summary: Chronic fibro-inflammatory disease; irreversible parenchymal damage → exocrine/endocrine insufficiency. Causes: alcohol (most common in developed world - 70-80%), genetic (PRSS1 trypsinogen mutation - hereditary pancreatitis; CFTR - CF-related; SPINK1, CTRC), autoimmune (IgG4-related - swollen, sausage-shaped pancreas; ↑IgG4; responds to steroids), tropical, idiopathic. Sx: severe chronic abdominal/back pain (most disabling), exocrine insufficiency (steatorrhoea, malabsorption, fat-soluble vitamin deficiencies - A, D, E, K), endocrine insufficiency (diabetes mellitus - brittle), weight loss. Complications: pseudocyst, biliary/duodenal obstruction, portal vein thrombosis, pancreatic carcinoma (↑risk). CT/MRI/MRCP: pancreatic calcification, ductal dilation ('chain of lakes'). Mx: abstinence from alcohol/smoking; analgesia (NSAIDs, opioids; coeliac plexus block); pancreatic enzyme replacement (Creon); ADEK vitamins; diabetes management; endoscopic (ERCP, pancreatic duct decompression, pseudocyst drainage); surgical (Beger, Frey, Whipple - for pain/complications).

conditions.name: Diverticular disease
conditions.summary: Diverticula (pulsion pseudodiverticula - mucosa/submucosa herniate through colonic wall at weak points adjacent to taeniae where blood vessels penetrate); sigmoid colon (90%); low-fibre diet, obesity, increasing age. Diverticulosis: asymptomatic or intermittent LLQ pain (coexistent IBS-like symptoms); incidental on imaging/colonoscopy. Diverticular bleeding: painless PR bleeding (often large volume), often resolves spontaneously; can be massive. Diverticulitis: microperforation → pericolonic inflammation; Sx: LLQ pain, fever, ↑WBC; CT (investigation of choice - confirms diagnosis, stagings Hinchey classification). Complications (Hinchey): pericolic phlegmon (I), pericolic abscess (II), purulent peritonitis (III), faecal peritonitis (IV - highest mortality). Mx: uncomplicated: oral antibiotics (co-amoxiclav) + liquid diet + analgesia; abscess: CT-guided drainage; peritonitis: emergency surgery (Hartmann or primary anastomosis - laparoscopic lavage/drainage for Hinchey III); elective sigmoidectomy (recurrent episodes, persistent fistula).

conditions.name: Status epilepticus
conditions.summary: Seizure lasting ≥5 min or ≥2 seizures without recovery between; medical emergency (prolonged → neuronal injury). Causes: poor drug compliance (most common), alcohol withdrawal, CNS infection, metabolic (Na⁺, glucose, Ca²⁺, uraemia), stroke, hypoxia, drug toxicity, structural (tumour). Operational definition (time T1 = 5 min → treat; T2 = 30 min → irreversible neuronal injury, lorazepam best). Ix: Algorithm (ABCDE + glucose check): Phase 1 (0-5 min) - benzodiazepine: lorazepam IV 0.1 mg/kg (preferred) OR diazepam IV/PR OR midazolam buccal/IM; Phase 2 (5-30 min, if not terminated) - levetiracetam 60 mg/kg IV, or sodium valproate 40 mg/kg IV, or phenytoin/fosphenytoin; Phase 3 (>30 min - RSE) - phenobarbitone, or general anaesthesia (propofol/thiopental/midazolam infusion) in ICU with EEG monitoring. Mx: Treat cause; correct glucose/electrolytes; consider pyridoxine (infants - B6 deficiency); LP if meningitis/encephalitis suspected.

conditions.name: Transverse myelitis
conditions.summary: Acute spinal cord inflammation; bilateral sensory/motor deficits below lesion level, bowel/bladder dysfunction, sensory level. Causes: idiopathic, MS (partial, asymmetric, short segment <2 vertebral levels - RAPD; enhancing lesion), NMOSD (extensive longitudinal transverse myelitis LETM ≥3 vertebral segments - AQP4/MOG antibody), SLE/antiphospholipid, Sjögren, sarcoidosis, paraneoplastic, post-viral/vaccination, vascular (spinal cord infarction - abrupt onset, anterior cord syndrome). MRI spine: cord signal change, swelling, enhancement (active). Ix: MRI spine + brain; CSF (inflammatory); AQP4/MOG-IgG; ANA, anti-Ro/La. Mx: high-dose IV methylprednisolone 1 g/d × 3-5 d (acute); plasma exchange (IVIG less evidence) for severe/unresponsive; treat cause; rehabilitation (physio/OT/bladder management).

conditions.name: Autonomic neuropathy
conditions.summary: Disorder of autonomic nervous system (sympathetic/parasympathetic). Causes: diabetes (most common - diabetic autonomic neuropathy); Parkinson disease/MSA; amyloidosis; Guillain-Barré; paraneoplastic (anti-Hu, anti-Yo); hereditary (HSAN, Fabry); autoimmune (autoimmune autonomic ganglionopathy - anti-ganglionic AChR). Sx: cardiovascular - orthostatic hypotension (symptomatic drop ≥20 systolic or ≥10 diastolic 3 min after standing; dizziness, syncope, falls, fatigue); anhidrosis/hyperhidrosis; GI - gastroparesis (early satiety, nausea, vomiting, bloating), constipation, diarrhoea; genitourinary - erectile dysfunction, neurogenic bladder (overflow incontinence); pupillary (impaired light response); sudomotor (dry skin). Ix: orthostatic BP (tilt table test for complex cases); QSART (quantitative sudomotor axon reflex); heart rate variability; urea breath test (H. pylori if gastroparesis); gastric emptying study. Mx: treat cause; orthostatic hypotension: fludrocortisone, midodrine, droxidopa (noradrenaline precursor), compression stockings; gastroparesis: domperidone, metoclopramide, erythromycin, gastric stimulator.

conditions.name: Spinal muscular atrophy
conditions.summary: Autosomal recessive; SMN1 deletion (chromosome 5q) → loss of SMN protein → degeneration of alpha motor neurons. Types: SMA I (Werdnig-Hoffmann - onset <6 months, never sit, death by 2 yr without Mx), SMA II (onset 6-18 months, sit independently, never walk), SMA III (Kugelberg-Welander - walk independently, onset >18 months), SMA IV (adult onset). Ix: SMN1 copy number; NBS in many countries. Mx (transformative in last decade): nusinersen (antisense oligonucleotide - intrathecal, monthly → 4-monthly; splicing of SMN2 pre-mRNA to ↑full-length SMN); onasemnogene abeparvovec (AAV9 gene therapy - IV, single dose, most effective when given before symptom onset); risdiplam (oral SMN2 splicing modifier); supportive - ventilatory support, physiotherapy, nutrition, orthopaedic management.

conditions.name: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
conditions.summary: Progressive degeneration of upper (UMN) and lower (LMN) motor neurons; most common adult-onset MND (90%). Familial in 10% (SOD1, C9orf72 most common - also FTD-ALS). Sporadic: largely unknown. Sx: combined UMN (spasticity, brisk reflexes, Babinski) + LMN (fasciculations, wasting, weakness, ↓reflexes) signs in multiple regions (bulbar, cervical, thoracic, lumbar). Bulbar onset (dysarthria, dysphagia) worse prognosis. No sensory/autonomic/sphincter/eye movement involvement (until late, if at all). Ix: El Escorial criteria; NCS/EMG (widespread denervation); MRI brain/spine (exclude other causes). Mx: riluzole (glutamate antagonist - modest survival benefit ~3 months); edaravone/tofersen (SOD1 - targeted for SOD1-ALS); supportive: NIV (prolongs survival - most important intervention), PEG (gastrostomy), saliva management (glycopyrronium), MDT (ALS clinic - neurologist, physio, OT, SALT, dietician, palliative care). Median survival 3-5 yr.

conditions.name: Male infertility
conditions.summary: Affects ~50% of infertile couples; semen analysis (WHO criteria: count ≥16 million/mL, motility ≥42%, morphology ≥4% Kruger). Causes: Pre-testicular (endocrine - hypothalamic/pituitary: Kallmann syndrome, hyperprolactinaemia, hypogonadism); Testicular (most common - primary testicular failure: idiopathic oligospermia, Klinefelter syndrome 47XXY, orchitis, previous chemo/radiotherapy, undescended testis, varicocele - most common correctable cause); Post-testicular (obstructive azoospermia - bilateral absence vas deferens/CF, previous vasectomy, epididymal obstruction). Ix: semen analysis × 2; FSH/LH/testosterone/prolactin; USS testes; karyotype (if azoospermia); Y-chromosome microdeletion (AZF region). Mx: varicocele surgery (controversial); obstructive azoospermia: surgical sperm extraction (TESE/PESA) + ICSI; non-obstructive: micro-TESE + ICSI; hormonal (hypogonadotrophic hypogonadism - FSH + HCG); lifestyle modification.

conditions.name: Female infertility
conditions.summary: Defined as failure to conceive after 12 months unprotected intercourse (6 months if female >35 yr); affects 1 in 7 couples. Causes: ovulatory dysfunction (30-40%: PCOS most common, hypothalamic amenorrhoea, hyperprolactinaemia, thyroid disease, ↑FSH/premature ovarian insufficiency); tubal/peritoneal (30-35%: previous PID/chlamydia, endometriosis, adhesions); unexplained (25%); uterine (fibroids, polyps, septum, Asherman syndrome); cervical (mucus hostility). Ix: Investigation: cycle day 2-3 FSH/LH/AMH/AFC (ovarian reserve), mid-luteal progesterone (confirm ovulation), thyroid, prolactin, rubella immunity; hysterosalpingography (HSG) or laparoscopy with dye (tubal patency); USS (ovarian/uterine pathology). Mx: anovulation: metformin, letrozole (first-line - PCOS), clomiphene, FSH injections, IUI; tubal: IVF or surgical repair; unexplained: IVF; donor oocytes (premature ovarian insufficiency).

conditions.name: Kidney cancer
conditions.summary: Clear cell RCC most common (75% - VHL mutation/deletion); papillary (15%), chromophobe (5%), oncocytoma (benign). Risk: smoking, obesity, HTN, VHL syndrome (bilateral multifocal clear cell RCC), hereditary papillary RCC (MET), Birt-Hogg-Dubé (FLCN - chromophobe/oncocytoma + skin fibrofolliculomas + spontaneous pneumothorax), tuberous sclerosis (angiomyolipoma + RCC). Classic triad (10%): haematuria + loin pain + palpable flank mass. 'Internist's tumour': paraneoplastic syndromes - polycythaemia (↑EPO), hypercalcaemia (PTHrP), Stauffer syndrome (non-metastatic hepatic dysfunction). Ix: CT chest/abdomen/pelvis (staging Fuhrman/ISUP grade); bone scan if bone pain; MRI (inferior vena cava thrombus - surgical planning). Mx: localised: partial/radical nephrectomy (laparoscopic); locally advanced (IVC thrombus): radical nephrectomy; metastatic: VEGF-targeted Mx (sunitinib, pazopanib, cabozantinib) ± nivolumab + ipilimumab (immunotherapy combination - first-line in IMDC intermediate/poor risk); pembrolizumab + axitinib (favourable risk); ablative therapy (RFA/cryotherapy, surveillance for small incidental lesions).

conditions.name: Acute appendicitis
conditions.summary: Most common surgical emergency (lifetime risk ~8%); obstruction of appendix lumen → bacterial overgrowth → inflammation → perforation. Sx: periumbilical pain migrating to RIF (McBurney point - 2/3 way from umbilicus to ASIS), anorexia, nausea, low-grade fever. Sx: RIF tenderness, guarding, Rovsing sign (LIF pressure → RIF pain), Psoas sign (leg extension), Obturator sign (hip flexion/internal rotation - pelvic appendix). Atypical: retrocaecal (less localised tenderness, no anterior peritonism), pelvic (bladder/vaginal symptoms), pregnancy (appendix displaced superiorly). Alvarado score (MANTRELS) or Appendicitis Inflammatory Response (AIR) score. USS (children/young women - exclude ovarian pathology), CT (adult, equivocal USS, elderly - ↑sensitivity/specificity). CRP, WBC. Mx: laparoscopic appendicectomy (standard); antibiotic-only treatment (selected uncomplicated, ongoing trials); drainage/interval appendicectomy for appendix mass (phlegmon).

conditions.name: Inguinal hernia
conditions.summary: Most common hernia overall; males 10× females. Indirect (most common - passes through deep inguinal ring into inguinal canal → external ring → scrotum/labia): patent processus vaginalis; lateral to inferior epigastric vessels. Direct (Hesselbach's triangle - medial to IEV, through posterior inguinal wall): acquired weakness from raised intra-abdominal pressure; older men. Sx: groin swelling, dragging/aching pain (worse on standing/straining, relieved supine), reducible (can push back into abdomen). Complications: incarceration (irreducible), strangulation (ischaemia - tense, tender, non-reducible → emergency). Ix: clinical; USS if uncertain. Mx: repair if symptomatic or complications (elective hernia repair → prevent strangulation, improve QoL); Lichtenstein (open mesh - tension-free, gold standard); laparoscopic TEP/TAPP (bilateral, recurrent, earlier return to work); strangulation → emergency surgery + bowel resection if necrotic.

conditions.name: Femoral hernia
conditions.summary: Protrudes through femoral canal (below and lateral to pubic tubercle - below inguinal ligament, medial to femoral vein); females > males (3:1) - but inguinal still more common in both sexes. Below and lateral to pubic tubercle (vs inguinal = above and medial). High risk of strangulation (>50% present as emergency) due to narrow femoral ring. Usually small, often missed. Sx: groin lump (below inguinal ligament, medial to femoral pulse), often painful, not always clearly reducible. Ix: clinical; USS. Mx: surgical repair recommended even if asymptomatic (high strangulation risk): open (McEvedy/lockwood approaches), laparoscopic; emergency if strangulated → repair + bowel resection if ischaemic.

conditions.name: Acute angle-closure glaucoma
conditions.summary: Ophthalmological emergency; sudden rise in IOP due to closure of iridocorneal angle → obstruction of aqueous outflow. Risk: hypermetropia (shallow anterior chamber), female, East Asian, anticholinergics (dilate pupil → angle closure). Precipitants: dim light, reading, anticholinergic drugs, mydriatic drops. Sx: sudden onset severe eye pain, frontal headache, nausea/vomiting, halos around lights, rapidly ↓visual acuity; red eye (circumcorneal - 'ciliary flush'). Sx: ↑IOP (>21 mmHg, often >40 mmHg), mid-dilated fixed pupil (oval, sluggish), corneal oedema (hazy, steamy), shallow anterior chamber, conjunctival injection. Ix: slit lamp + tonometry. Mx: immediate eye drops (pilocarpine 2% - pupil constriction, opens angle; timolol - ↓aqueous production; acetazolamide IV/oral - carbonic anhydrase inhibitor); IV mannitol (severe); definitive: laser peripheral iridotomy (LPI - both eyes, prevent recurrence); protect fellow eye prophylactically.

conditions.name: Open angle glaucoma
conditions.summary: Chronic progressive optic neuropathy; open iridocorneal angle (trabecular meshwork dysfunctional); raised or normal IOP → optic nerve damage (cupping) → visual field loss (peripheral first → tunnel vision → total blindness). Insidious, painless; often diagnosed late. Risk: ↑IOP (>21 mmHg), age >60, family history, myopia, diabetes, HTN (vascular), afro-Caribbean. Optic disc: ↑cup:disc ratio (>0.7), asymmetry, disc haemorrhage (flag). Visual field: nasal step, arcuate scotoma, altitudinal defect. Ix: tonometry, disc examination, visual fields, OCT (RNFL/GCL thinning). Mx: IOP lowering (each 1 mmHg reduction ↓progression ~10%): prostaglandin analogues (latanoprost - first-line, once daily; ↑uveal outflow; SE: iris pigmentation, hypertrichosis), beta-blockers (timolol), carbonic anhydrase inhibitors (dorzolamide, brinzolamide), alpha-2 agonists (brimonidine), netarsudil (ROCK inhibitor); laser trabeculoplasty (SLT); trabeculectomy (bleb surgery); tube shunts (advanced).

conditions.name: Colles fracture
conditions.summary: Most common fracture in adults <75 yr; fracture of distal radius (within 2 cm of wrist) with dorsal displacement and angulation of distal fragment (dinner fork deformity); typically FOOSH (fall on outstretched hand) in osteoporotic post-menopausal women. Smith fracture: volar displacement (reverse Colles). Barton fracture: intra-articular fracture-dislocation. Ix: AP + lateral wrist X-ray; CT if intra-articular. Complications: median nerve injury (acute carpal tunnel - check thenar sensation/motor), extensor pollicis longus rupture, malunion, CRPS. Mx: undisplaced: below-elbow cast 6 wk; displaced: closed reduction ± cast or surgical fixation (volar locking plate - ORIF for intra-articular, unstable, dorsal angulation >20°); elderly/osteoporotic: DEXA scan + bone protection.

conditions.name: Ankle fracture
conditions.summary: Common fractures of lateral malleolus, medial malleolus, posterior malleolus. Sx: Ottawa rules: X-ray indicated if tenderness over posterior 6 cm/tip of medial/lateral malleolus OR unable to weight-bear × 4 steps. Weber classification (fibula fracture level relative to syndesmosis): Weber A (below syndesmosis - stable, ligament usually intact → conservative); Weber B (at level - usually stable, may be unstable with medial injury → assess stability); Weber C (above syndesmosis - syndesmotic injury, unstable → ORIF). Lauge-Hansen classification (mechanism). Bimalleolar (both malleoli) and trimalleolar (both + posterior) fractures → unstable → ORIF with screws/plates + syndesmosis repair if disrupted. Maisonneuve: proximal fibula fracture + medial ankle/syndesmosis injury - must check full fibula; unstable → ORIF.

conditions.name: Spinal fracture
conditions.summary: Vertebral fractures range from osteoporotic compression fractures to high-energy burst fractures with cord injury. Sx: Stable compression fracture (wedge): anterior collapse, posterior wall intact; often osteoporotic/minor trauma; back pain (thoracic/lumbar); bracing or conservative; vertebroplasty/kyphoplasty (pain relief, controversial). Burst fracture: axial loading → comminution, posterior wall breach → retropulsion → cord compression (unstable). Chance fracture: flexion-distraction (lap belt injury - posterior ligamentous/bony failure, chance of visceral injury). Hangman fracture: C2 bilateral pedicle fractures (hyperextension). Jefferson fracture: C1 ring burst (axial load). Odontoid fractures: Type II most common, unstable. Mx: ABCDE + spinal immobilisation; CT spine (gold standard for bony injury); MRI (cord, soft tissue, epidural haematoma); neurosurgical involvement; surgical stabilisation (unstable/neurological deficit); MDT rehabilitation (SCI: spinal cord injury centres; bladder/bowel/pressure care; Stoke Mandeville model).

conditions.name: Akathisia
conditions.summary: Subjective inner restlessness + objective motor restlessness (inability to sit/stand still, rocking, pacing); adverse effect of dopamine antagonists (antipsychotics, metoclopramide, prochlorperazine). Onset: hours to weeks after starting/dose increase. Inner tension/dysphoria drives suicidality (akathisia-related agitation). Sx: Distinguish: restless legs syndrome (RLS - nocturnal, limb specific, relieved by movement), anxiety, agitation from psychiatric illness, tardive dyskinesia (late-onset, involuntary). Mx: dose reduction (best); propranolol (evidence for antipsychotic-induced - first-line), mirtazapine, lorazepam; switch to lower-D2-affinity antipsychotic (clozapine, quetiapine); anticholinergics (less evidence for akathisia than for dystonia/parkinsonism).

conditions.name: Tardive dyskinesia
conditions.summary: Involuntary repetitive movements from prolonged dopamine receptor blockade (antipsychotics, metoclopramide). Predominantly orofacial: lip smacking, tongue protrusion, chewing movements, grimacing; also limb choreiform movements, trunk rocking, respiratory dyskinesia. Onset: ≥3 months of exposure (earlier in elderly). Risk: older age, female, affective disorder, longer/higher exposure, typical > atypical antipsychotics. Ix: Abnormal Involuntary Movement Scale (AIMS). Irreversible in many cases; may persist or worsen after drug cessation. Ix: clinical (AIMS, DISCUS scale); exclude other causes of dyskinesia. Mx: VMAT2 inhibitors (valbenazine, deutetrabenazine - US-approved; most effective); switch to clozapine or quetiapine (low D2); reduce/discontinue offending drug cautiously; tetrabenazine (older); clonazepam.

conditions.name: Lithium toxicity
conditions.summary: Narrow therapeutic index (0.6-1.2 mmol/L for maintenance; 0.8-1.0 mmol/L for treatment). Toxicity types: acute (deliberate overdose - GI dominant), chronic (accumulation - neurological dominant, more dangerous), acute-on-chronic. Precipitants of chronic toxicity: dehydration (diarrhoea, vomiting, sweating), NSAIDs (↑reabsorption), ACEi/ARBs (↑levels), low sodium diet, diuretics. Sx: GI (nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea); neurotoxicity (tremor [coarse], ataxia, confusion, slurred speech, drowsiness, seizures, coma); cardiac (bradycardia, QTc prolongation, T-wave changes). Severe toxicity (>2.5 mmol/L or symptomatic): ICU-level care. Ix: lithium level (>1.5 mmol/L = toxic; >2.0 = serious; >3.0 = life-threatening); ECG; U&E (renal function). Mx: stop lithium; IV 0.9% NaCl (↑renal clearance; large volumes); haemodialysis (severe toxicity/level >3.5 or severe neurological/renal failure); monitoring; SILENT syndrome (lithium-induced irreversible neurotoxicity).

conditions.name: Tricyclic antidepressant overdose
conditions.summary: Highly dangerous in overdose; narrow margin between therapeutic and toxic dose. Mechanism: Na⁺ channel blockade (cardiac + CNS toxicity), anticholinergic effects (antimuscarinic), antihistamine, alpha-1 blockade. Sx: anticholinergic (dry mouth, urinary retention, ↓bowel sounds, ↑HR, dilated pupils, flushed skin, fever, delirium); cardiac (wide QRS > 100 ms - Na⁺ channel block, ↑QTc, ventricular arrhythmia, torsades, VF); CNS depression (seizures, coma); hypotension (alpha-blockade). Ix (ECG): broad QRS (>100 ms in overdose = serious risk of arrhythmia; >160 ms = very high risk VF/asystole); right axis deviation; terminal R wave in aVR (>3 mm/R:S ratio >0.7 in aVR). Mx: activated charcoal (if within 1 hr, airway protected); IV sodium bicarbonate (for QRS >100 ms or hypotension - alkalinisation narrows QRS, improves haemodynamics); AVOID physostigmine; intubation + ventilation (acidosis → worse toxicity); magnesium (torsades); ECMO if refractory cardiac arrest.

conditions.name: Gender dysphoria
conditions.summary: Distress arising from incongruence between one's experienced/expressed gender and assigned sex at birth (DSM-5: gender dysphoria; ICD-11: gender incongruence - removed from mental disorder chapter to sexual health). Not pathological in itself; clinically significant when distress/impairment present. Ix: multidisciplinary specialist gender services (psychiatrist, endocrinologist, psychologist); psychosocial assessment; rule out differential (dissociative disorders, psychosis, severe depression). Medical Mx (after thorough assessment + persistent documented incongruence): puberty blockers (GnRH analogues - reversible pause - adolescents; effects on bone density, height, fertility); gender-affirming hormone therapy (oestrogen for trans women, testosterone for trans men - significant changes in secondary sexual characteristics); surgical options (various, threshold: legal adult, on hormones ≥1 yr). Mental health support (comorbid depression, anxiety, self-harm, suicidality - high rates); social transition; legal name/gender change.

conditions.name: Cord prolapse
conditions.summary: Obstetric emergency; umbilical cord descends below presenting part after membranes rupture → cord compression by presenting part → fetal hypoxia → death. Risk: abnormal fetal lie (transverse/oblique), malpresentation (footling/shoulder), prematurity, polyhydramnios, multiple pregnancy, long cord, artificial ROM (AROM - risk if head not engaged). Ix: palpable cord in vagina (VE), cord visible at vulva, fetal bradycardia after ROM. Immediate management: relieve cord compression (push presenting part up vaginally with fingers - do NOT remove fingers until delivery), knee-chest/exaggerated Sims position, fill bladder (100-300 mL saline → elevates head), tocolysis; emergency CS (immediate - Category 1 if fetal heart present); cord kept warm and moist; call for help/activate emergency team.

conditions.name: Shoulder dystocia
conditions.summary: Obstetric emergency; head delivered but anterior shoulder impacted behind symphysis pubis. Mx: Risk factors: macrosomia (most significant, though 50% occur in normal-weight babies), previous shoulder dystocia, diabetes, obesity, prolonged 2nd stage, operative vaginal delivery. Unpredictable. Recognition: 'turtle neck' sign (head retracts against perineum), failure of restitution/external rotation. Mx: Management - HELPERR (mnemonic): Help (call team), Episiotomy (if needed for manoeuvres, not itself releases bony obstruction), Legs (McRoberts - thigh hyperflexion onto abdomen - widens pelvic outlet; first-line), Pressure (suprapubic - Rubin's angle; never fundal), Enter (internal rotation manoeuvres - Rubin II, Woods screw, Barlow), Remove posterior arm, Roll to all-fours. Zavanelli (head replacement + CS) if all fail. Neonatal complications: brachial plexus injury (Erb palsy, Klumpke); hypoxia; fractures (humerus, clavicle).

conditions.name: Postpartum haemorrhage
conditions.summary: Primary PPH: blood loss ≥500 mL within 24 hr of delivery (≥1000 mL for major). 4 Ts - Tone (uterine atony - 70-80%; most common cause), Trauma (cervical/vaginal/perineal tears, uterine rupture), Tissue (retained placenta/clots), Thrombin (coagulopathy). Secondary PPH: >24 hr to 12 wk; usually endometritis ± retained products. Risk factors: prolonged labour, oxytocin augmentation, multiple pregnancy, polyhydramnios, grande multiparity, fibroids, antepartum haemorrhage, previous PPH. Mx: Mx primary PPH: uterotonic drugs (oxytocin IV bolus → infusion, ergometrine, Syntocinon, carboprost - watch for bronchospasm in asthmatics, misoprostol); bimanual uterine compression; tranexamic acid (within 3 hr); Bakri balloon tamponade; B-Lynch suture; interventional radiology (uterine artery embolisation); hysterectomy (last resort); correct coagulopathy (cryoprecipitate, FFP, platelets - 'major haemorrhage protocol').

conditions.name: Urinary incontinence
conditions.summary: Involuntary urine leakage. Types: stress urinary incontinence (SUI): leakage with cough/laugh/exertion; ↓urethral sphincter support (urethral hypermobility - intrinsic sphincter deficiency after childbirth, menopause); urodynamics: no detrusor overactivity, leak on stress. Urge urinary incontinence (UUI): sudden urge + inability to defer voiding; overactive bladder (OAB); detrusor overactivity on urodynamics; urgency with/without incontinence, nocturia. Mixed: both components. Overflow incontinence: chronic retention → dribbling (BPH, neuropathic bladder). Risk: multiparity, menopause, obesity, pelvic surgery, UTI, caffeine. Ix: symptom assessment (ICIQ questionnaire), bladder diary, MSU, urodynamics (if mixed/surgery planned). Mx: Mx (SUI): pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT - first-line, 3 months); pessary; duloxetine (SNRI - second-line medical); TVT/TOT (midurethral sling - surgical, gold standard); colposuspension (Burch). Mx OAB/UUI: PFMT + bladder training; antimuscarinic (oxybutynin, tolterodine, solifenacin); beta-3 agonist (mirabegron - better SE profile); botulinum toxin A injection into detrusor (refractory); sacral neuromodulation.

conditions.name: Pelvic organ prolapse
conditions.summary: Descent of pelvic organs into/beyond vaginal introitus. Types: cystocele (anterior wall - bladder), rectocele (posterior wall - rectum), enterocele (apical - small bowel/peritoneum herniation), uterine prolapse, vault prolapse (post-hysterectomy). POP-Q staging (0-IV). Risk: multiparity, vaginal delivery, menopause (oestrogen deficiency), obesity, chronic straining (constipation, COPD), connective tissue disorders. Sx: vaginal bulge ('something coming down'), pelvic pressure, incomplete bladder/bowel emptying, urinary symptoms (incontinence, urgency, incomplete emptying - 'splinting' to empty rectocele), dyspareunia. Ix: clinical (pelvic examination, POP-Q). Mx: conservative (pelvic floor exercises, weight loss); ring/shelf pessary (highly effective for suitable anatomy; requires follow-up); surgical repair (colporrhaphy anterior/posterior, sacrocolpopexy for apical/vault - mesh complications: erosion, pain, regulatory restrictions on vaginal mesh in UK/US).

conditions.name: Amenorrhoea
conditions.summary: Primary: no menarche by age 15 (presence of secondary sexual characteristics) or by 13 (absence). Secondary: cessation of menses ≥3-6 months in previously menstruating woman. Primary causes: gonadal dysgenesis (Turner syndrome - 45,X - most common), mullerian agenesis (MRKH syndrome - absent uterus/upper vagina, normal ovaries/XX karyotype), imperforate hymen, androgen insensitivity (complete AIS - 46,XY, testes, absent uterus, female phenotype, tall), Kallmann syndrome (GnRH deficiency + anosmia). Secondary causes: pregnancy (first exclude), hypothalamic (functional hypothalamic amenorrhoea - weight loss, excessive exercise, stress: ↓FSH/LH, ↓oestrogen, ↓BMD → osteoporosis risk), hyperprolactinaemia, thyroid disease (hypo/hyperthyroidism), premature ovarian insufficiency (POI - FSH >25 twice, <40 yr), PCOS, Asherman syndrome (intrauterine adhesions post-curettage). Ix: pregnancy test; FSH/LH/oestradiol (↑FSH = ovarian cause; ↓FSH+LH = hypothalamic/pituitary); prolactin; TFTs; progesterone challenge test; USS pelvis; MRI pituitary; karyotype (if ↑FSH <30 yr). Mx: treat cause; oestrogen replacement (POI, Turner); weight restoration; dopamine agonist (prolactinoma).

conditions.name: Puerperal sepsis
conditions.summary: Sepsis originating from genital tract in the 28 days following childbirth, miscarriage, or abortion; leading cause of maternal mortality. Causative organisms: GAS (group A Streptococcus - most dangerous, rapid deterioration, toxic shock syndrome), E. coli (most common), Staphylococcus aureus, anaerobes (Bacteroides), Clostridium. Risk: caesarean section (most significant), prolonged ROM, retained products of conception, obesity, anaemia, immunosuppression, GAS contact. Sx: fever (>38°C) or hypothermia (<36°C), uterine/lower abdominal tenderness, offensive lochia, rigors, tachycardia, septic shock (late). Ix: blood cultures (before antibiotics), HVS, MSU, FBC, CRP, lactate (organ dysfunction). Mx: immediate broad-spectrum IV antibiotics (co-amoxiclav or cephalosporin + metronidazole; add clindamycin if GAS suspected/toxic shock); surgical (evacuation of retained products - hysteroscopy/ERPC); source control; sepsis 6 bundle; IVIG (group A strep toxic shock).

conditions.name: Acute rheumatic fever
conditions.summary: Inflammatory complication of group A streptococcal pharyngitis (Streptococcus pyogenes); immune-mediated (molecular mimicry - anti-streptococcal antibodies cross-react with cardiac, joint, skin, neural antigens). Affects children 5-15 yr. Jones criteria (major): Joints (migratory polyarthritis - most common; knees/ankles), heart (carditis - pan, ↑PR, mitral/aortic murmurs, HF; most serious), Nodules (subcutaneous - firm, painless, over bony prominences), Erythema marginatum (ring-shaped rash - trunk/proximal limbs; evanescent), Sydenham's chorea (involuntary movements, emotional lability; late, post-infectious). Minor criteria: fever, ↑ESR/CRP, ↑PR. Evidence of preceding GAS infection (ASOT↑, positive throat culture/rapid antigen). Ix: 2 major or 1 major + 2 minor + evidence GAS. Mx: penicillin V (eradicate GAS); aspirin (arthritis + fever - high dose); steroids (severe carditis/HF); long-term secondary prophylaxis (benzathine penicillin G IM monthly × years - prevents recurrences, prevents rheumatic heart disease progression; duration depends on cardiac involvement).

conditions.name: Enuresis
conditions.summary: Involuntary voiding of urine; nocturnal (bedwetting - most common): primary (never dry, normal development) or secondary (recurrence after 6+ months dry - UTI, stress, diabetes insipidus/mellitus, constipation, OSA, sexual abuse). Prevalence: 15% at age 5 yr, decreasing ~15% per year spontaneously. Associations: family history, developmental delay, ADHD, constipation. Exclude UTI, structural anomaly, neurological cause, T1DM (polydipsia). Daytime enuresis (diurnal): more concerning - overactive bladder, giggle incontinence, dysfunctional voiding. Mx: Mx (nocturnal): reassurance (most self-resolve); fluid management (↑daytime, ↓evening); bladder training; enuresis alarm (first-line effective treatment - conditioning); desmopressin (DDAVP - nasal spray/oral; works while taking; hyponatraemia risk - restrict evening fluids, check electrolytes if polyuria/polydipsia); treat constipation; antimuscarinic (if detrusor overactivity).

conditions.name: Immune thrombocytopenic purpura
conditions.summary: Autoimmune thrombocytopenia; anti-platelet antibodies (anti-GP IIb/IIIa) → platelet destruction by spleen. Acute ITP: children (post-viral - often 1-2 wk after URTI/varicella; typically self-limiting, resolves in weeks-months; petechiae/purpura, mucous membrane bleeding but rarely life-threatening). Chronic ITP: adults; >12 months; spontaneous or after infection/vaccination; treatment often required. Ix: isolated thrombocytopenia (platelets <100 × 10⁹/L), no splenomegaly, normal WBC/Hb; blood film (no fragmentation - excludes TTP/HUS, no blast cells - excludes leukaemia); exclude secondary causes (SLE, hepatitis, HIV, H. pylori, drugs - heparin→HIT). Mx: children - watch-and-wait if no major bleeding (majority resolve); IVIG or steroids (if <20 × 10⁹/L + bleeding or pre-procedure). Adults: corticosteroids (first-line); IVIG (rapid rise, pre-surgery); TPO receptor agonists (eltrombopag, romiplostim - second-line, ↑platelet production); rituximab; splenectomy (durable remission in 60-70% - deferred ≥12 months); fostamatinib; emergency: platelet transfusion + IVIG + methylprednisolone (intracranial haemorrhage).

conditions.name: Fetal alcohol spectrum disorder
conditions.summary: Spectrum of conditions caused by prenatal alcohol exposure (no safe level in pregnancy). Fetal Alcohol Syndrome (FAS - most severe): characteristic facial features (smooth philtrum, thin upper lip, small palpebral fissures), growth restriction (weight/height <10th centile), CNS abnormalities (structural, functional - IQ <70). Partial FAS: 2 facial features + neurodevelopmental impairment. ARND (alcohol-related neurodevelopmental disorder): neurodevelopmental impairment without full facial/growth criteria. ARBD: structural anomalies (cardiac, renal, skeletal). Effects: intellectual disability, executive dysfunction, ADHD, memory impairment, learning difficulties, behavioural problems, speech/language delay, psychiatric comorbidities (depression, PTSD, substance use). No safe level of alcohol in pregnancy. Ix: confirmed prenatal alcohol exposure + diagnostic criteria (facial features, growth, CNS). Mx: no specific treatment; educational support, behavioural management, treat ADHD/psychiatric comorbidities; carer/family support.

conditions.name: Gastroenteritis
conditions.summary: Infection causing diarrhoea (≥3 loose stools/24 hr) ± vomiting; usually self-limiting. Mx: Viral (80%): rotavirus (most common globally in children - <5 yr; vaccine-preventable), norovirus (all ages; epidemic; vomiting-dominant; contaminated food/water/surfaces; cruise ships), adenovirus. Sx: Bacterial: Salmonella (poultry, eggs), Campylobacter (most common bacterial in UK - undercooked poultry; can cause reactive arthritis, GBS), E. coli O157:H7 (STEC - haemorrhagic colitis → HUS), Shigella (dysentery - bloody diarrhoea, fever, tenesmus), Clostridium perfringens (rice/meat - short incubation), C. difficile (post-antibiotics; pseudomembranous colitis). Stool culture: if bloody, prolonged (>7 d), immunocompromised, travel, systemic illness. Mx: oral rehydration therapy (ORS - main treatment; WHO formula; children especially); IV fluids (unable to tolerate oral, severe dehydration, shock); antibiotics only for: invasive bacterial (Campylobacter - azithromycin if severe; Shigella - azithromycin; Salmonella typhi/paratyphi - ceftriaxone/azithromycin; Clostridioides difficile - vancomycin/fidaxomicin).

conditions.name: Dehydration
conditions.summary: Deficit of body water (and often electrolytes). Ix: history (fluid intake/losses - vomiting, diarrhoea, polyuria, sweating), clinical features, fluid balance. Sx: mild (<5% - thirst, dry mouth, ↑HR), moderate (5-10%: sunken eyes, ↓skin turgor, dry mucous membranes, oliguria, cool peripheries, ↓capillary refill), severe (>10%: lethargic/obtunded, mottled skin, very sunken fontanelle in infants, anuric, shock - hypotension). Useful markers: blood urea (↑), ↑urine specific gravity, capillary refill, FAST Hug. In children (NICE traffic light): features alerting to dehydration (altered responsiveness, sunken eyes, dry mucous membranes, tachycardia, ↓skin turgor, ↑CRT, oliguria - 'amber/red'). Mx: mild: oral rehydration therapy (ORT - ORS solution); moderate: ORS in supervised setting; severe/shock: IV fluid resuscitation (isotonic saline 20 mL/kg bolus, reassess, repeat; replace deficit + maintenance; correct electrolytes - Na⁺, K⁺ especially); nasogastric rehydration (when ORT fails/IV not available); monitor urine output.

conditions.name: Tricuspid stenosis
conditions.summary: Rare valvular lesion; obstruction of tricuspid valve orifice → ↑right atrial pressure. Almost always rheumatic (almost always coexistent with MS in rheumatic heart disease); also carcinoid syndrome (right-sided valve disease from circulating vasoactive substances), congenital. Sx: fatigue, peripheral oedema, ascites, hepatic congestion; similar to right HF. Sx: low-pitched mid-diastolic murmur at lower left sternal edge (louder on inspiration - Carvallo's sign), giant 'a' wave in JVP, hepatomegaly. Ix (ECG): ↑P wave (tall, pointed - 'P pulmonale'). Ix (echo): thickened/restricted tricuspid leaflets, pressure gradient. Mx: treat underlying cause; diuretics (oedema); percutaneous balloon valvuloplasty; valve repair/replacement (combined with MVR for rheumatic heart disease; tissue valve preferred for tricuspid - mechanical valves prone to thrombosis at low-flow right side).

conditions.name: Tricuspid regurgitation
conditions.summary: Systolic backflow from RV into RA through incompetent tricuspid valve. Functional (most common - annular dilation from RV dilation/failure secondary to PAH, left HF) or primary (rheumatic, carcinoid, infective endocarditis - IV drug users/pacemaker lead, Ebstein anomaly, trauma). Sx: right-sided HF - peripheral oedema, ascites, hepatomegaly, pulsatile liver; fatigue. Sx: pansystolic murmur at lower left sternal edge (louder on inspiration - Carvallo's sign), elevated pulsatile JVP (large 'v' wave/cv wave), systolic hepatic pulsation. Ix (echo): dilated RA/RV, tricuspid regurgitation on Doppler, ↑PAP. Mx: diuretics; treat underlying cause (HF, PAH); surgical repair (annuloplasty - preferred, better outcomes than replacement) or replacement (bioprosthesis) if severe + valve repair surgery indicated.

conditions.name: Pulmonary stenosis
conditions.summary: Obstruction to RV outflow (subvalvular, valvular, supravalvular). Congenital (most common - isolated valvular, Williams syndrome, Noonan syndrome, congenital rubella, Alagille syndrome) or acquired (carcinoid - right-sided). Haemodynamics: RV pressure overload → RV hypertrophy → RV failure (severe). Sx: usually asymptomatic; exertional dyspnoea, fatigue, right HF (severe). Sx: harsh systolic ejection murmur (upper left sternal edge, radiates to left clavicle), ejection click (mobile valve), ↑P2 absent (in severe), RV heave, widely split S2 (↑RV ejection time). Ix (echo): ↑gradient across pulmonary valve; RV hypertrophy; post-stenotic dilation of PA. Mx: percutaneous balloon pulmonary valvuloplasty (peak gradient >40 mmHg or symptomatic - excellent results, first-line); surgical valvotomy/repair (if unsuitable for balloon); pulmonary valve replacement (PR after valvotomy - Ross procedure, homograft, transcatheter PVR).

conditions.name: Empyema
conditions.summary: Pus in pleural space; complication of pneumonia (parapneumonic empyema - most common), lung abscess, oesophageal perforation, haematogenous seeding, post-surgical/procedural. Stages: exudative (clear fluid, low LDH) → fibrinopurulent (cloudy/turbid, fibrin, loculations, pH<7.2) → organising (thick peel, trapped lung, restricted expansion). Common organisms: Streptococcus pneumoniae, S. milleri, S. aureus (MRSA - hospital-acquired), Gram-negative rods (hospital), anaerobes (aspiration). Sx: fever, pleuritic chest pain, dyspnoea, weight loss; may be blunted by antibiotic treatment. CXR/USS/CT: pleural fluid with loculations. Ix: pleural fluid analysis (turbid/pus, pH <7.2, glucose <2.2 mmol/L, LDH >1000, Gram stain + culture). Mx: antibiotics (IV - cover S. milleri, anaerobes, MRSA if hospital-acquired); chest drain (intercostal drain for free-flowing; imaging-guided small-bore for loculated); intrapleural fibrinolytics + DNase (alteplase + dornase alfa - ↑drainage of loculated); surgical (VATS decortication - thick peel/failed drain); nutritional support.

conditions.name: Haemothorax
conditions.summary: Blood in pleural space. Causes: trauma (rib fractures, penetrating chest injury - most common), iatrogenic (central venous catheter, thoracic surgery, biopsy), spontaneous (coagulopathy, malignancy, bullous lung disease, AVM). Sx: dyspnoea, chest pain, tachycardia, haemoptysis (if bronchial communication). Sx: dullness at base, ↓breath sounds, haemodynamic instability (massive haemothorax = shock). Ix (CXR): opacification (>200 mL to be visible - upright); USS (faster, bedside, sensitive). Mx: intercostal drain (large-bore - 28-32 Fr - dependent position; evacuates blood, ↓risk empyema, ↓risk fibrothorax/trapped lung); VATS (video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery) for: retained haemothorax >1 wk, clotted haemothorax, failure to re-expand; autotransfusion (cell saver); surgery for massive/ongoing haemorrhage (>1.5 L initial drain, >200 mL/hr × 4 hr, continuing instability); prophylactic antibiotics (traumatic haemothorax).

conditions.name: Haemolytic uraemic syndrome
conditions.summary: Thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA): microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia (MAHA) + thrombocytopenia + acute kidney injury (triad). Typical HUS (D+): Shiga toxin-producing E. coli (STEC O157:H7 most common; also O111, O26, O145) after bloody diarrhoea - affects children; self-limiting in ~90%; Mx: supportive (fluids, dialysis); AVOID antibiotics (may ↑Shiga toxin release) and anti-motility agents. Atypical HUS (aHUS): complement dysregulation (mutations in CFH, CFI, MCP/CD46, C3, CFB, thrombomodulin); recurrent/renal failure; Mx: eculizumab (C5 complement inhibitor - transformative; meningococcal vaccination before starting). Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP - see TTP entry): ADAMTS13 deficiency (congenital or acquired anti-ADAMTS13 antibodies); neurological features dominant; Mx: plasma exchange + steroids + rituximab.

conditions.name: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
conditions.summary: Thrombotic microangiopathy caused by severe ADAMTS13 deficiency (<10%) - the metalloprotease that cleaves ultra-large von Willebrand factor (ULvWF) multimers → ULvWF → platelet thrombi in microvasculature. Acquired TTP (most common): anti-ADAMTS13 antibodies (autoimmune, often with SLE, pregnancy, drugs - quinine, ticlopidine). Congenital TTP (Upshaw-Schulman): rare, recurrent. PLASMIC score (risk stratification for ADAMTS13 <10%). Pentad (classic, now recognised as TTP when TMA + ADAMTS13 deficiency): MAHA, thrombocytopenia, neurological symptoms (confusion, stroke, headache - fluctuating), fever, acute kidney injury. Ix: ADAMTS13 activity + inhibitor level (< 10% confirms TTP); blood film (schistocytes, helmet cells); FBC, LDH, haptoglobin (↓). Mx: plasma exchange (PEX - removes inhibitor + replaces ADAMTS13; daily until remission; life-saving); corticosteroids + rituximab (↑remission, ↓relapse); caplacizumab (anti-vWF nanobody - ↓platelet thrombi rapidly; reduces TMA and organ damage); avoid platelet transfusion (fuels thrombosis).

aliases: chronic kidney disease mineral bone disorder
conditions.name: Renal osteodystrophy
conditions.summary: Spectrum of bone and mineral disorders in CKD: hyperphosphataemia (↓renal phosphate excretion) → ↑FGF-23 (early) → ↓calcitriol (active vitamin D) → hypocalcaemia → ↑PTH (secondary hyperparathyroidism) → skeletal changes. Types: osteitis fibrosa cystica (high PTH - subperiosteal resorption, 'rugger-jersey spine', 'salt and pepper' skull, brown tumours), osteomalacia (↓calcitriol - accumulation of unmineralised osteoid; bone pain, fractures), adynamic bone disease (over-suppressed PTH with oversuppressive treatments), mixed uraemic osteodystrophy. Calciphylaxis: vascular/soft tissue calcification → skin necrosis (rare, high mortality). Ix: Ca²⁺, PO₄, PTH, ALP, calcitriol; bone density (DEXA); bone biopsy (tetracycline labelling - gold standard but rarely done). Mx: dietary phosphate restriction; phosphate binders (calcium carbonate → active/non-calcium binders: lanthanum, sevelamer for ↑Ca²⁺); active vitamin D analogues (alfacalcidol, calcitriol - stimulate Ca/PO₄ absorption; ↓PTH); cinacalcet (calcimimetic - ↓PTH secretion, ↓Ca²⁺ absorption); parathyroidectomy (severe refractory 3° HPT).

conditions.name: Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis
conditions.summary: Infection of pre-existing ascites without an intra-abdominal source; occurs in ~15% of hospitalised cirrhotics with ascites. Pathogenesis: bacterial translocation from gut (E. coli, Klebsiella, S. pneumoniae, Streptococcus - monomicrobial in true SBP). Sx: fever, abdominal pain/tenderness, deteriorating hepatic encephalopathy, new-onset ascites; may be asymptomatic. Ix: diagnostic paracentesis in all new ascites or deteriorating cirrhotics - ascitic PMN >250 cells/mm³ = SBP (culture may be negative - 'culture-negative neutrocytic ascites' = treat same). Mx: IV antibiotics (3rd gen cephalosporin - ceftriaxone/cefotaxime × 5 d; oral fluoroquinolone for mild if no prior exposure); IV albumin 1.5 g/kg on day 1, 1 g/kg on day 3 (↓renal failure + mortality by 38%, NEJM 1999); secondary prophylaxis (long-term norfloxacin or TMP-SMX); primary prophylaxis (norfloxacin for high-risk: ascites protein <1.5 g/dL + renal/liver dysfunction).

conditions.name: Horner syndrome
conditions.summary: Interruption of oculosympathetic chain at any level: 1st order (hypothalamus → C8/T1 - stroke, syringomyelia, MS, tumour), 2nd order (preganglionic - lung apex Pancoast tumour, cervical rib, brachial plexus injury, subclavian artery aneurysm, aortic dissection), 3rd order (postganglionic - carotid artery dissection/aneurysm, cavernous sinus, otitis media - painful 3rd order Horner). Sx (triad): ptosis (partial - tarsal muscle only), miosis (small pupil - anhidrosis if central/preganglionic but not postganglionic), enophthalmos (apparent). Anhidrosis: ipsilateral face (central/preganglionic); absent (postganglionic - past superior cervical ganglion). Pharmacological testing: cocaine eyedrops (dilate normal, not Horner's pupil; confirms diagnosis); apraclonidine (reverses anisocoria - diagnostic); hydroxyamphetamine (differentiates pre vs postganglionic). Ix: MRI brain/neck/chest (depending on suspected level) + CXR/CT chest (Pancoast). Mx: treat underlying cause.

conditions.name: Ramsay Hunt syndrome
conditions.summary: Varicella-zoster virus (VZV) reactivation in geniculate ganglion of facial nerve (CN VII). Sx (triad): peripheral facial palsy (LMN - same as Bell's palsy but more severe), otalgia (severe ear pain), vesicular eruption in ear (herpes zoster oticus - pinna, external auditory canal, tympanic membrane) or oral mucosa (palate). May also affect CN VIII → vertigo, hearing loss, tinnitus. Ix: clinical (vesicles + facial palsy + otalgia pathognomonic); VZV PCR from vesicles/saliva. Differentiate from Bell's palsy: vesicles present + worse prognosis. Mx: early antiviral (aciclovir 800 mg 5×/d or valaciclovir 1 g tds × 7 d - start within 72 hr ideally) + prednisolone (2 wk course); eye lubrication (same as Bell's palsy). Prognosis: 50-70% complete facial recovery (worse than Bell's - 90%); risk of post-herpetic neuralgia.

conditions.name: Internuclear ophthalmoplegia
conditions.summary: Lesion of medial longitudinal fasciculus (MLF) between CN VI nucleus and contralateral CN III nucleus → inability to adduct ipsilateral eye on conjugate gaze + nystagmus in abducting eye. Bilateral INO = strong suggestion of MS (most common cause in young adults). Unilateral INO: brainstem stroke (older patients), MS, tumour, Wernicke, Lyme, vasculitis. One-and-a-half syndrome: INO + ipsilateral gaze palsy (PPRF + MLF lesion on same side) → only contralateral eye abducts (WEMINO - wrong eye moves in, nystagmus oscillates). Sx: ask patient to follow finger side to side; ipsilateral eye fails to adduct, contralateral abducting eye has nystagmus. Convergence intact (distinguishes from 3rd nerve palsy). Ix: MRI brain (brainstem). Mx: treat underlying cause (MS: optic neuritis protocols; stroke: thrombolysis/secondary prevention).

conditions.name: Friedreich ataxia
conditions.summary: Most common hereditary ataxia; autosomal recessive; GAA trinucleotide repeat expansion in frataxin gene (FXN, chromosome 9q); frataxin deficiency → mitochondrial iron accumulation → oxidative damage. Onset: childhood/adolescence (typically <25 yr). Sx: progressive gait ataxia, limb ataxia (dysmetria), dysarthria, dysphagia; areflexia (↓/absent tendon reflexes - spinocerebellar tracts + posterior columns + peripheral nerve); extensor plantar responses (UMN); scoliosis, pes cavus; cardiomyopathy (HCM - most common cause of death in 60-80%; arrhythmias; cardiac failure); optic atrophy; SNHL; diabetes mellitus (30%). NCS: sensory axonal neuropathy. Ix (MRI): spinal cord atrophy. Ix: GAA repeat expansion (>66 repeats - pathological); frataxin levels. Mx: omaveloxolone (NRF2 activator - first approved treatment, US 2023; modest benefit); cardiomyopathy (beta-blockers, ACEi; avoid digoxin + CCBs in HCM); physiotherapy; orthotics; cardiac monitoring + ICD if arrhythmia.

conditions.name: CIDP
conditions.summary: Acquired immune-mediated demyelinating neuropathy; chronic counterpart of GBS. Onset >8 wk (GBS ≤4 wk). Sx: progressive or relapsing proximal and distal weakness (symmetric), sensory loss, areflexia, ataxia (sensory). Subtypes: typical CIDP (bilateral, proximal + distal), multifocal (MADSAM - Lewis-Sumner), distal (DADS - predominantly sensory, often with anti-MAG antibodies). Associated: diabetes, HIV, haematological malignancy, POEMS (anti-CNTN1, anti-NF155, anti-NF140/186 - nodal/paranodal antibodies). Ix: NCS/EMG (demyelination: ↓NCVs, ↑DML, ↑F-wave, conduction block); CSF (↑protein, normal WBC); nerve biopsy (onion bulbs - only if diagnostic uncertainty); anti-CNTN1/NF155 antibodies. Mx: IVIG (high-dose, monthly maintenance); corticosteroids; plasma exchange; immunosuppression (azathioprine, MMF, ciclosporin) as steroid-sparing; rituximab (nodopathy with antibodies); subcutaneous Ig (home administration).

conditions.name: Muscular dystrophy
conditions.summary: X-linked recessive (Duchenne/Becker) or other inheritance; dystrophin gene (Xp21 - largest human gene) mutation. Duchenne (DMD): frameshift/large deletion → absent dystrophin; onset 2-5 yr. Becker (BMD): in-frame mutation → truncated/reduced dystrophin; milder/later onset. DMD features: progressive proximal weakness (Gowers' sign - climbing up legs to stand), calf pseudohypertrophy (fibrofatty infiltration), Trendelenburg gait, ↑CK (very high - >10,000 IU/L), eventual loss of ambulation (by age 12 with steroids, earlier without), respiratory failure (scoliosis, ↓FVC), cardiomyopathy (DCM - Ix (ECG): tall R in V1, deep Q in lateral leads). Ix: genetic testing (deletion/duplication array, sequencing); CK (very high); muscle biopsy + dystrophin staining/WB. Mx: glucocorticoids (deflazacort - delays ambulation loss ~2-3 yr, respiratory decline); exon-skipping therapies (eteplirsen, golodirsen - exon 51, 53 skipping; restore reading frame → shorter functional dystrophin); gene therapy (delandistrogene moxeparvovec - micro-dystrophin AAV9); ACEi + beta-blockers (cardiomyopathy); ventilatory support (NIV → tracheostomy); physiotherapy, orthotics; scoliosis surgery.

conditions.name: Phaeochromocytoma
conditions.summary: Catecholamine-secreting tumour of adrenal medulla (phaeochromocytoma) or extra-adrenal chromaffin cells (paraganglioma). Rule of 10s (historical, less accurate now): 10% malignant, 10% bilateral, 10% extra-adrenal, 10% familial. Genetic syndromes: MEN2A/2B (RET), VHL (VHL), NF1 (NF1), SDH mutations (SDHB/C/D - most common hereditary, ↑malignancy in SDHB). Sx: paroxysmal 'spells' - headache (80%), palpitations (70%), sweating/diaphoresis (70%), hypertension (paroxysmal or sustained), pallor, anxiety, chest/abdominal pain; hypertensive crisis precipitated by surgery, drugs (tricyclics, metoclopramide, decongestants, tyramine). Ix: 24-hr urine fractionated metanephrines/catecholamines OR plasma metanephrines (most sensitive/specific); CT/MRI abdomen (localisation); 123I-MIBG scan or DOTATATE PET-CT (functional imaging; extra-adrenal, metastatic). Mx: alpha-blockade first (phenoxybenzamine or doxazosin × 10-14 d - essential before surgery to prevent hypertensive crisis intraoperatively); then beta-blocker ONLY AFTER adequate alpha-blockade; laparoscopic adrenalectomy; malignant PPGL: MIBG therapy, sunitinib, temozolomide.

conditions.name: Insulinoma
conditions.summary: Rare pancreatic neuroendocrine tumour; beta-cell tumour secreting insulin (endogenous). 90% benign, solitary, sporadic; ~10% MEN1 (multiple/malignant). Whipple triad: (1) neuroglycopenic symptoms (confusion, seizures, coma - brain glucose-deprived), (2) documented hypoglycaemia (blood glucose <2.5 mmol/L during symptoms), (3) relief with glucose administration. Sx: neuroglycopenia (diplopia, confusion, behaviour change, seizures, coma); adrenergic (palpitations, tremor, sweating) - often absent/blunted. Patients eat excessively to prevent attacks → weight gain. Fasting hypoglycaemia (prolonged 72-hr fast - monitored). Ix: 72-hr supervised fast → hypoglycaemia with paradoxically elevated insulin (>3 mU/L), ↑C-peptide (endogenous), ↑proinsulin, ↓glucose, negative exogenous insulin screen (factitious Münchausen). Localisation: MRI/CT (>2 cm); EUS (best - detects <1 cm, 80-90% sensitive). Mx: surgical enucleation (curative); diazoxide (inhibits insulin secretion - pre-op/unresectable); octreotide (SST analogue - ↓insulin secretion in some); sunitinib, everolimus (malignant).

conditions.name: Erythema nodosum
conditions.summary: Panniculitis (inflammation of subcutaneous fat); most common form of reactive panniculitis. Tender, erythematous, nodular lesions (1-10 cm) on anterior shins bilaterally; also ankles, forearms (rare). Usually self-limiting (2-8 wk); lesions evolve from red/bright → bruise-like (no ulceration - distinguishes from vasculitis/NL). Causes (SORE mnemonic or 'remember STRIPE'): Streptococcal pharyngitis (most common in children), Sarcoidosis (Löfgren syndrome - EN + hilar adenopathy + arthritis + uveitis - good prognosis), Tuberculosis, Oral contraceptive pill, Pregnancy, IBD (Crohn > UC), Behçet disease, drugs (sulfonamides, antibiotics). 50% idiopathic. Ix: clinical (skin biopsy if atypical - septal panniculitis without vasculitis); investigations for cause: ASOT, CXR, ANA, ACE, TSH, culture, HIV. Mx: treat underlying cause; NSAIDs (first-line symptomatic); potassium iodide (refractory); bed rest/elevation.

conditions.name: Psittacosis
conditions.summary: Zoonotic infection; Chlamydophila (Chlamydia) psittaci; transmitted from psittacine birds (parrots, budgerigars, cockatiels) or poultry/pigeons - inhalation of dried bird excreta. Atypical pneumonia: prolonged fever, severe headache, myalgia, dry cough; can cause severe pneumonia, hepatitis, endocarditis, meningitis. Relative bradycardia (temperature-pulse dissociation - like typhoid). Ix (CXR): consolidation (unilateral). Ix: serology (complement fixation test - titre ≥1:64 diagnostic; PCR on respiratory secretions). Notifiable disease. Mx: doxycycline (14 d, first-line); azithromycin (if doxycycline intolerant, or in pregnancy/children); fluoroquinolone; treatment usually required 10-14 d (avoid short courses - risk of relapse).

conditions.name: Hepatitis A
conditions.summary: Picornavirus (enterovirus family); faecal-oral transmission (contaminated water/food - shellfish, raw produce, travel to endemic areas); commonest viral hepatitis worldwide. Incubation 15-50 d. Sx: prodrome (malaise, fever, anorexia, nausea, RUQ discomfort) → jaundice (often mild, resolving 2-8 wk); cholestatic variant (prolonged jaundice, pruritus); no chronic infection; rare fulminant hepatic failure (<1% but ↑risk in pre-existing liver disease). ↑AST/ALT (markedly, >1000 IU/L), ↑bilirubin, ↑INR (severe); anti-HAV IgM (acute infection); anti-HAV IgG (past infection/immunity). Mx: supportive; avoid hepatotoxins (paracetamol caution, alcohol); liver transplant (fulminant hepatic failure). Mx (prevention): HAV vaccine (highly effective, 2-dose; recommended for travellers, MSM, CLD, IVDU, food workers); post-exposure immunoglobulin; hygiene.

conditions.name: Acanthosis nigricans
conditions.summary: Velvety, hyperpigmented, hyperkeratotic skin thickening at flexures (axillae, back of neck, groin, antecubital fossa). Associated conditions: insulin resistance/T2DM (most common - obesity-associated; also PCOS, metabolic syndrome, Cushing syndrome); malignancy (paraneoplastic - especially GI adenocarcinoma, most commonly gastric cancer - acanthosis nigricans maligna: rapid onset, severe, oral mucosa/widespread involvement, de novo in adult without obesity); endocrine (acromegaly, hypothyroidism, Addison disease); drugs (nicotinic acid, glucocorticoids, combined OCP, protease inhibitors). Ix: clinical; investigate for underlying cause (fasting glucose/insulin, BMI; if non-obese adult: screen for malignancy - FOBT, OGD, CT abdomen). Mx: treat underlying cause; weight loss (obesity-related - improves/resolves); topical keratolytics; dermabrasion (cosmetic).

conditions.name: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome
conditions.summary: Autosomal dominant; STK11/LKB1 mutation. Hamartomatous polyps (small bowel > colon > stomach); non-malignant polyps per se but ↑cancer risk. Characteristic feature: mucocutaneous pigmentation (melanin spots - perioral/buccal mucosa, lips, fingers; present in infancy/childhood, may fade at puberty except buccal). Complications: small bowel intussusception (polyps act as lead point - recurrent abdominal pain, obstruction), GI bleeding, ↑cancer risk - GI (gastric, small intestinal, colonic - lifetime risk 39-66%), pancreatic cancer (132× relative risk!), gynaecological (sex cord tumour with annular tubules - SCTAT of ovary - ↑oestrogen → menstrual irregularity; cervical adenoma malignum; breast cancer 50× risk), testicular SCST. Ix: clinical criteria (characteristic pigmentation + polyp histology or family history); STK11 mutation. Mx: regular surveillance endoscopy (gastroscopy/colonoscopy every 3 yr from age 8); capsule endoscopy/MRI enterography (small bowel polyps); balloon-assisted enteroscopy/laparotomy for large polyps; cancer screening (breast, pancreas, gynaecological).

conditions.name: Factor V Leiden
conditions.summary: Most common inherited thrombophilia in Caucasians (5% prevalence, up to 50% of thrombophilia patients); missense mutation (R506Q) in factor V gene → resistance to inactivation by activated protein C (APC resistance) → ↑thrombin generation → hypercoagulability. Autosomal dominant; heterozygous: 5-8× ↑VTE risk; homozygous: 50-80× ↑VTE risk. Risk: VTE (DVT, PE), obstetric complications (recurrent miscarriage, pre-eclampsia, placental abruption - heterozygous association modest; stronger for homozygous). Combined risks: OCP + FV Leiden = 35× risk DVT vs general population (OCP alone = 3-4×). Ix: activated protein C (APC) resistance assay (functional screen) → DNA testing (R506Q). Mx: VTE: anticoagulation (DOAC/warfarin); prophylactic LMWH (high-risk situations - surgery, immobility, pregnancy/postpartum in homozygous or prior VTE heterozygous); OCP risks (discuss alternatives); family screening.

conditions.name: Protein C deficiency
conditions.summary: Inherited thrombophilias from deficiency of natural anticoagulant proteins. Protein C (PROC gene): serine protease activated by thrombomodulin-thrombin complex → inactivates FVa + FVIIIa with protein S as cofactor. Protein S (PROS1 gene): cofactor for protein C. Both autosomal dominant; heterozygous: 5-10× ↑VTE risk; homozygous: severe neonatal purpura fulminans (fatal without immediate protein C concentrate/fresh frozen plasma). Acquired causes: vitamin K deficiency (warfarin → proteins C/S deplete faster than thrombin), liver disease, DIC, nephrotic syndrome. Warfarin skin necrosis: warfarin initiates a paradoxical hypercoagulable state (fast ↓protein C before factor X falls) → skin infarction - use heparin bridge when initiating warfarin. Ix: protein C/S functional levels + antigenic levels; genotyping. Mx: VTE treatment (DOAC preferred over warfarin in protein C/S deficiency); LMWH thromboprophylaxis (high-risk situations); family screening.

conditions.name: Haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
conditions.summary: Severe life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome; uncontrolled activation of cytotoxic T lymphocytes, NK cells, macrophages → cytokine storm → multi-organ failure. Primary (familial) HLH: mutations in perforin pathway (PRF1, UNC13D, STXBP2, RAB27A, STX11) - autosomal recessive, often infants. Sx: Secondary (reactive/acquired) HLH: EBV (most common trigger), HIV, CMV, other infections, malignancy (lymphoma - haematological trigger), autoimmune (Macrophage Activation Syndrome/MAS - in sJIA/systemic JIA and adult-onset Still disease). Ix: HScore (clinical scoring). HLH-2004 criteria: ≥5 of 8 - fever, splenomegaly, cytopenias (≥2 lineages), hypertriglyceridaemia, low/absent NK cell activity, ↑ferritin (>500, often >10,000), haemophagocytosis on bone marrow/LN/spleen biopsy, ↑soluble CD25 (IL-2Rα - very elevated). Mx: treat trigger; HLH-2004 protocol (etoposide + dexamethasone ± ciclosporin); HSCT (primary/refractory); ruxolitinib (JAK inhibitor for secondary/MAS); IVIG; emapalumab (anti-IFNγ - primary/refractory HLH).

conditions.name: Hypogonadism
conditions.summary: Deficiency of sex steroids. Male hypogonadism: Primary (hypergonadotrophic - ↑LH/FSH, ↓testosterone): Klinefelter, mumps orchitis, chemotherapy/radiation, undescended testis. Secondary (hypogonadotrophic - ↓LH/FSH): Kallmann syndrome (GnRH deficiency + anosmia), constitutional delay, hyperprolactinaemia, hypothalamic/pituitary disease, anabolic steroid use. Sx: prepubertal onset - delayed puberty, small testes, eunuchoidal proportions (arm span > height); adult onset - low libido, erectile dysfunction, infertility, loss of muscle/bone mass, fatigue, mood changes, anaemia, hot flushes, gynaecomastia. Ix: morning serum testosterone × 2 (8-10 am, fasting; <8 nmol/L = deficiency; 8-12 nmol/L = grey zone); LH/FSH (↑primary, ↓secondary); prolactin; TFTs; MRI pituitary (if secondary). Mx: testosterone replacement (IM, transdermal gel, implant, intranasal); HCG + FSH (fertility); cabergoline (hyperprolactinaemia); treat underlying cause.

conditions.name: Acute tubular necrosis
conditions.summary: Most common cause of intrinsic acute kidney injury (AKI); ischaemic or nephrotoxic injury to tubular epithelial cells. Mx: Ischaemic ATN: prolonged prerenal hypoperfusion (septic shock, haemorrhage, major surgery, cardiogenic shock - when autoregulation fails); tubular cells most vulnerable in S3 segment of PT and mTAL. Nephrotoxic ATN: aminoglycosides (trough monitoring essential), contrast (CIN - ↓risk with hydration; avoid high-osmolar contrast; NAC controversial), cisplatin, amphotericin B, myoglobin (rhabdomyolysis), haemoglobin (haemolysis), pigment nephropathy, heavy metals. Urinalysis: muddy brown granular/epithelial cell casts (pathognomonic), +protein (mild). Phases: oliguric (<400 mL/day, 1-3 wk) → polyuric (tubule recovers before concentrating ability → up to 3-10 L/day - watch electrolytes) → recovery (weeks-months). FeNa >1% (vs prerenal <1%); FeUN <35% (if diuretics given). Mx: treat precipitant; haemodynamic optimisation; discontinue nephrotoxins; fluid management; dialysis (severe uraemia, fluid overload, ↑K⁺, acidosis); majority recover (unlike CKD).

conditions.name: Cardio-renal syndrome
conditions.summary: Bidirectional heart-kidney dysfunction where primary dysfunction of one organ causes secondary dysfunction of the other. Type 1 (acute CRS): acute cardiac event → AKI (acute HF decompensation, cardiogenic shock → ↓renal perfusion; ↑venous pressure → renal congestion). Type 2 (chronic CRS): chronic HF → CKD. Sx: Type 3 (acute renocardiac): AKI → acute cardiac dysfunction (hyperkalaemia → arrhythmia, fluid overload → pulmonary oedema, uraemia → myocarditis). Type 4 (chronic renocardiac): CKD → chronic cardiac dysfunction (renovascular HTN, anaemia, uraemia → LVH, accelerated CAD). Type 5 (secondary CRS): systemic disease causing both (sepsis, amyloidosis, diabetes, lupus). Mx: optimise haemodynamics; diuresis (IV loop diuretics + monitor renal function - balance decongestion vs AKI); ultrafiltration; SGLT2 inhibitors (benefit both heart and kidney); address underlying cause; RRT if severe AKI/CKD.

conditions.name: Medication overuse headache
conditions.summary: Headache on ≥15 days/month developing or worsening during regular use of acute headache medication for >3 months. Most common in migraineurs who overuse acute treatments. Drugs: triptans, opioids, NSAIDs, paracetamol, ergotamine (different thresholds - opioids/triptans after 10 days/month; NSAIDs/paracetamol after 15 days/month). Headache character: typically morning, bilateral, dull/pressing, aggravated by exertion; overlaid on pre-existing migraine pattern. Paradox: more analgesic use → more frequent headache → more analgesic use. Ix: ICHD-3 criteria; headache diary (frequency, acute medication use). Mx: withdrawal of overused medication (key - abrupt preferred for triptans/NSAIDs; gradual for opioids/barbiturates; warn of worsening x 2-4 wk); bridge therapy (naproxen, prednisone, dihydroergotamine); preventive migraine therapy (topiramate, amitriptyline, propranolol, CGRP antibodies - particularly effective in MOH); psychological support; relapse rate 30-40%.

conditions.name: Cerebral artery dissection
conditions.summary: Tear in the intima of carotid or vertebral arteries → intramural haematoma → lumen compromise (ischaemia) or aneurysmal dilation → thromboembolism → stroke/TIA. Young adults; most common cause of stroke in <45 yr. Causes: spontaneous (connective tissue disorders - Marfan, EDS type IV, FMD), trauma (minor neck manipulation, whiplash, chiropractic), forceful activity. Carotid dissection: ipsilateral neck/face pain, partial Horner syndrome (ptosis + miosis, no anhidrosis - postganglionic), carotid bruit, TIA/stroke (ipsilateral hemisphere); pulsatile tinnitus. Vertebral dissection: occipital/posterior neck pain, lateral medullary syndrome (Wallenberg), cerebellar stroke. Ix: CTA or MRA (lumen narrowing ± intramural haematoma - 'string sign'; crescent sign on MRI T1 fat-sat); DWI for ischaemic stroke. Mx: anticoagulation (heparin → warfarin × 3-6 months) or antiplatelet therapy (aspirin + clopidogrel; randomised trials show no significant difference - CADISS trial); endovascular stenting (occlusion/persistent symptoms); FMD: angioplasty.

conditions.name: Cavernous sinus syndrome
conditions.summary: Cavernous sinus contains: CN III, IV, VI, V1/V2, ICA, sympathetic fibres. Cavernous sinus thrombosis (CST - septic): most common cause - skin/soft tissue infection of face (boils, carbuncles - danger triangle of face → angular vein → ophthalmic vein → CS), dental abscess, sinusitis (ethmoid/sphenoid). Sx: periorbital oedema/chemosis, proptosis (bilateral - pathognomonic), headache, fever, diplopia (CN VI most susceptible), ptosis, reduced corneal reflex (V1), papilloedema. Ix: contrast CT/MRI (filling defect in cavernous sinus, venous engorgement). Mx: IV antibiotics (IV ceftriaxone + metronidazole + vancomycin for MRSA); anticoagulation (unfractionated heparin - reduces mortality/morbidity, even in septic CST; controversial but most guidelines recommend); surgical drainage (causal sinus infection if needed). Cavernous sinus tumours (pituitary adenoma, meningioma, metastasis) or non-infectious thrombosis (hypercoagulable states): surgical/radiation or anticoagulation.

conditions.name: Ophthalmoplegia
conditions.summary: CN III palsy (oculomotor): complete - ptosis (complete), eye 'down and out' (SO and LR intact), pupil dilation (mydriasis - if surgical/compressive cause: aneurysm of posterior communicating artery [PCOM] is classic emergency - 'blown pupil' + painful). Medical (ischaemic/diabetic): pupil sparing (vasa nervorum occlusion; fascicular fibres - pupil sympathetic - run peripherally). Surgical: pupil involved (compression - PCOM aneurysm; tentorial herniation - uncal herniation). CN IV palsy (trochlear): mildest; vertical diplopia (worse looking down); head tilt (away from affected side); cause - closed head trauma (most common), microvascular. CN VI palsy (abducens): most common CN palsy; failure of abduction; horizontal diplopia; false localising sign (↑ICP); microvascular (DM, HTN) most common in adults; must exclude raised ICP (LP, imaging). Ix: CT/MRI brain; angiography (if PCOM aneurysm suspected). Mx: treat cause; eye patching for diplopia; prism glasses.

conditions.name: LADA
conditions.summary: Latent Autoimmune Diabetes in Adults; adult-onset autoimmune diabetes, often misdiagnosed as T2DM initially. GAD (glutamic acid decarboxylase) antibodies positive (most common); ZnT8, IA-2 less commonly. Sx: typically >30 yr, normal/low BMI, acute onset + initially responds to oral agents, accelerated progression to insulin dependence (usually within 6 years). Distinguish from T2DM: younger, slimmer, stronger family/personal history of autoimmunity, rapidly requires insulin, lower C-peptide. Classic features: not obese, no metabolic syndrome, poor response to oral agents, gradual total beta-cell loss. Ix: positive GAD65 antibody + adult onset diabetes; C-peptide (↓over time); HbA1c. Mx: insulin (earlier better - evidence for islet preservation with early insulin vs sulphonylureas which may accelerate beta-cell loss); islet preservation strategies; tight glycaemic control.

conditions.name: Mallory-Weiss tear
conditions.summary: Mucosal laceration at gastro-oesophageal junction from forceful/repeated vomiting, retching, coughing, or any ↑intra-abdominal pressure. Common in heavy alcohol users (not exclusive). Sx: haematemesis (fresh blood) after forceful episode of vomiting; typically preceded by episode of non-bloody vomiting, then bloody vomiting (Mallory-Weiss sequence); usually self-limiting. Ix: upper GI endoscopy (OGD) - longitudinal mucosal tear at GEJ, typically on the gastric side; no scope needed if mild/self-limited but required for significant bleeding. Complications: active arterial bleeding (uncommon), haematoma, perforation (very rare). Mx: majority stop bleeding spontaneously (supportive - IV access, fluid resuscitation, PPI, antiemetics); endoscopic haemostasis if active bleeding (injection adrenaline, thermal coagulation, haemoclips); rarely surgical (oversewing - very rare). Distinguish from Boerhaave syndrome (full-thickness oesophageal perforation - surgical emergency, pneumomediastinum on CXR/CT).

conditions.name: Oesophageal varices
conditions.summary: Dilated submucosal veins in oesophagus due to portal hypertension → portosystemic collateralisation. Portal hypertension threshold for variceal formation: HVPG >10 mmHg (threshold for varices >12 mmHg). Ix (grading): F1 (small, flat), F2 (medium, protrude into lumen), F3 (large, coil). Sx: High-risk features: large F3 varices, red wale signs (cherry-red spots - endoscopic), Child-Pugh C. Variceal haemorrhage: acute upper GI bleeding (haematemesis, melaena - often massive), high mortality (15-20% per episode). Ix: OGD (diagnostic and therapeutic); CT angiography (localise, show portal system). Mx: Mx - acute haemorrhage: terlipressin (splanchnic vasoconstrictor - ↓portal pressure, reduces mortality; give before/on way to endoscopy); IV antibiotics (norfloxacin/ceftriaxone - prevent SBP, improves survival); TIPS/balloon tamponade (Sengstaken-Blakemore - rescue); endoscopic band ligation (EVL - preferred over sclerotherapy). Secondary prophylaxis: non-selective beta-blockers (propranolol/carvedilol - ↓portal pressure; start 5 d after acute bleed) + EVL (combination → most effective). Primary prophylaxis (large varices or small + red signs): NSBB alone (carvedilol preferred - ↓portal pressure, anti-cardiac output).

conditions.name: Menopause
conditions.summary: Permanent cessation of menstruation (retrospectively, after 12 consecutive months without periods) from ovarian follicular depletion; average age 51 yr (UK). Premature ovarian insufficiency (POI): <40 yr. Perimenopause: variable cycle length, symptoms, irregular periods preceding FMP. Vasomotor sx: hot flushes (72%), night sweats (most common, most bothersome). Other sx: sleep disturbance, mood changes (depression, anxiety, irritability), cognitive symptoms ('brain fog'), urogenital atrophy (GSM - genitourinary syndrome of menopause: vaginal dryness, dyspareunia, urinary urgency/frequency/UTIs), sexual dysfunction, joint/muscle aches. Long-term: cardiovascular risk ↑ (oestrogen cardioprotective), osteoporosis. Ix: clinical (>45 yr; serum FSH generally NOT needed); FSH >40 IU/L × 2 (>6 wk apart) if <45 yr or diagnostic uncertainty. Mx: HRT (hormone replacement therapy - most effective; oestrogen ± progestogen [if uterus present - prevents endometrial cancer]; systemic/local; benefits > risks in healthy women <60 yr or <10 yr from menopause; ↓bone fractures, hot flushes, GSM); local oestrogen (GSM - very safe, minimal systemic absorption); non-hormonal: SSRIs/SNRIs, clonidine, gabapentin (vasomotor sx); lifestyle (exercise, weight); tibolone.

conditions.name: Ovarian mass
conditions.summary: Ovarian/adnexal mass with broad differential: functional cysts (follicular, corpus luteum - most common, young women; resolves spontaneously), endometrioma ('chocolate cyst'), benign neoplastic (dermoid/mature teratoma - most common in young women; serous/mucinous cystadenoma - most common benign epithelial), malignant (epithelial ovarian cancer - postmenopausal), borderline tumours, sex cord stromal (granulosa cell tumour, fibroma - Meigs syndrome). Risk assessment: IOTA (International Ovarian Tumour Analysis) criteria; RMI (risk of malignancy index - USS score × menopausal status × CA-125); ADNEX model. Ix: USS (first-line) - unilocular cyst (almost certainly benign), complex/mixed echogenicity/bilateral/solid components (risk malignancy ↑); CA-125 + HE4; CT (staging if suspicious/suspected malignant). Mx: premenopausal simple cyst <5 cm → observe (repeat USS 3-6 months); persistent/growing/complex → surgery; postmenopausal: lower threshold for surgical management; dermoid/endometrioma: laparoscopic cystectomy.

conditions.name: Anal cancer
conditions.summary: 85% squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) arising from anal canal epithelium; 15% adenocarcinoma (from anal glands/rectal extension). HPV infection (HPV 16, 18) causative in >90% anal SCC (same molecular pathway as cervical cancer); anal Pap smear screening in high-risk populations. Risk: HIV/immunosuppression (× 25-30↑ in HIV), MSM, multiple sexual partners, smoking, HPV infection, cervical/vulval/vaginal CIN history. Sx: bleeding per rectum, anal pain, mass/ulcer, pruritus, incontinence, change in bowel habit. Ix: examination under anaesthesia (EUA) + biopsy; MRI pelvis (local staging - T/N staging); CT chest/abdomen/pelvis (distant staging); PET-CT (nodal/distant). FIGO/AJCC staging. Mx: concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CRT) is standard of care for localised/locoregionally advanced (not surgery as primary Mx): mitomycin C + 5-FU + RT (Nigro protocol - modified) achieves CR in ~80%; APR (abdominoperineal resection) reserved for residual/recurrent disease after CRT; pembrolizumab (metastatic/refractory).

conditions.name: Rheumatic heart disease
conditions.summary: Cardiac sequela of acute rheumatic fever; valvular damage from repeated streptococcal infections + immune-mediated inflammation. Most common in developing countries; leading cause of mitral/aortic valve disease in young people in Asia/Africa/Middle East. Valve involvement: mitral valve most commonly affected (MR > MS); aortic (AR > AS); tricuspid (rare, right-sided); pulmonary (very rare). Characteristic pathology: Aschoff nodules (granulomatous lesion); fibrin deposition → leaflet thickening/fusion → fibrosis/calcification → stenosis; chordal fusion/shortening → regurgitation. Ix (severity): mild RHD (subclinical - echo only) to severe stenosis/regurgitation. Complications: AF (mitral stenosis → ↑LA pressure → LA dilation → AF → embolic stroke), infective endocarditis, heart failure, mitral facies (malar flush). Mx: secondary prophylaxis (benzathine penicillin - prevent recurrent GAS → prevent further valve damage); treat valve disease (balloon valvuloplasty for suitable MS; surgical repair or replacement for MS/MR/AR/AS; anticoagulation for AF/mechanical valves).

conditions.name: Prosthetic valve disease
conditions.summary: Complications of prosthetic heart valves. Types: mechanical (tilting disc - Björk-Shiley; bileaflet - St Jude/ATS; ball-and-cage - Starr-Edwards) vs bioprosthetic (tissue - bovine pericardium/porcine aortic valve; homograft).
